acceptance_criteria.Then: The account details fetch state flag must be set to NOT FETCHED (ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED set to TRUE), indicating that no account data has been loaded and the user must first enter and submit a valid account number before any account or customer details can be displayed or edited

rules.rule_name: Restore Shared CardDemo Communication Area for Returning Session
rules.rule_description: When the program is re-entered from a prior interaction (not a fresh start), the shared CardDemo communication area must be restored from the passed communication area data so that cross-program context such as account ID, customer ID, card number, and navigation routing are preserved from the previous interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Restore CardDemo
Communication Area
Reload shared program data
from previous session

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has determined this is a returning session — prior session data exists (EIBCALEN is greater than zero) AND the entry is not a first-time arrival from the Main Menu
acceptance_criteria.When: The returning session restoration path is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The CardDemo shared communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) must be populated by copying the first portion of the passed communication area (DFHCOMMAREA) with a length equal to the size of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, restoring all shared cross-program data fields to their values from the previous interaction

rules.rule_name: Restore Program-Specific Communication Area for Returning Session
rules.rule_description: When the program is re-entered from a prior interaction, the program-specific communication area must be restored from the passed communication area data so that the account update state, previously fetched account details, and any pending changes are preserved exactly as they were at the end of the previous interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Restore Program-Specific
Communication Area
Reload local program data
from previous session

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has determined this is a returning session and the shared CardDemo communication area has been restored from the passed communication area
acceptance_criteria.When: The returning session restoration path continues
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) must be populated by copying the second portion of the passed communication area (DFHCOMMAREA), starting at the position immediately after the CardDemo communication area (offset = LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1) and with a length equal to the size of WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, restoring all local account update state flags, previously fetched account data, and pending change information

key_functionalities.title: PF Key Validation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([User Presses a Key])
    CAPTUREKEY[Identify Which Key Was Pressed\nCapture the function key or Enter key\nfrom the user's terminal input]
    ISPF03{PF03\nPressed?}
    ISENTER{Enter\nPressed?}
    ISPF05{PF05\nPressed?}
    ISPF12{PF12\nPressed?}
    CHECKPF05STATE{Are changes validated\nbut not yet confirmed?}
    CHECKPF12STATE{Have account details\nalready been fetched\nand displayed?}
    OTHERINVALIDKEY[Any Other Key Pressed\nPF01, PF02, PF04, PF06-PF11,\nPF13-PF24, CLEAR, PA1, PA2, etc.]
    PF03VALID([PF03 Valid\nProceed to Exit Program])
    ENTERVALID([Enter Valid\nProceed to Process Input])
    PF05VALID([PF05 Valid\nProceed to Save Confirmation])
    PF12VALID([PF12 Valid\nProceed to Cancel and Refresh])
    PF05INVALID[PF05 Not Valid in Current Context\nUser has not yet made and\nvalidated changes to confirm]
    PF12INVALID[PF12 Not Valid in Current Context\nNo account details are currently\ndisplayed to cancel]
    TREATENTER[Treat as Enter Key\nInvalid key is overridden\nand processed as Enter]

    START --> CAPTUREKEY
    CAPTUREKEY --> ISPF03
    ISPF03 -->|Yes| PF03VALID
    ISPF03 -->|No| ISENTER
    ISENTER -->|Yes| ENTERVALID
    ISENTER -->|No| ISPF05
    ISPF05 -->|Yes| CHECKPF05STATE
    CHECKPF05STATE -->|Yes - Changes validated,\nawaiting confirmation| PF05VALID
    CHECKPF05STATE -->|No - Not in correct\nstate for save confirmation| PF05INVALID
    ISPF05 -->|No| ISPF12
    ISPF12 -->|Yes| CHECKPF12STATE
    CHECKPF12STATE -->|Yes - Account details\nare currently displayed| PF12VALID
    CHECKPF12STATE -->|No - No account details\nhave been fetched yet| PF12INVALID
    ISPF12 -->|No| OTHERINVALIDKEY
    PF05INVALID --> TREATENTER
    PF12INVALID --> TREATENTER
    OTHERINVALIDKEY --> TREATENTER

rules.rule_name: Capture and Identify User Key Press
rules.rule_description: When a user presses any key on the terminal, the system must identify and record which specific key was pressed so that subsequent processing can determine the appropriate action. Extended PF keys (PF13-PF24) are treated as their base equivalents (PF01-PF12).
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Identify Which Key Was Pressed
Capture the function key or Enter key
from the user's terminal input

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and presses any key on the terminal
acceptance_criteria.When: The system receives the key press input from the terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies and records the key pressed as one of the following logical key indicators: Enter key, Clear key, PA1 key, PA2 key, PF01 through PF12. Extended keys PF13 through PF24 are mapped to their base equivalents: PF13 maps to PF01, PF14 maps to PF02, PF15 maps to PF03, PF16 maps to PF04, PF17 maps to PF05, PF18 maps to PF06, PF19 maps to PF07, PF20 maps to PF08, PF21 maps to PF09, PF22 maps to PF10, PF23 maps to PF11, PF24 maps to PF12. Exactly one key indicator is set to active for use in subsequent processing.

rules.rule_name: Determine Overall Key Validity in Current Context
rules.rule_description: After identifying which key was pressed, the system evaluates whether that key is valid given the current state of the Account Update screen. Only specific keys are permitted under specific conditions; all others are considered invalid.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Identify Which Key Was Pressed
Capture the function key or Enter key
from the user's terminal input

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has pressed a key on the Account Update screen and the key has been identified
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the key against the current screen state
acceptance_criteria.Then: The key is marked as valid if it is the Enter key (always valid), OR it is PF03 (always valid), OR it is PF05 AND the current state is 'Changes Validated but Not Yet Confirmed', OR it is PF12 AND the current state is NOT 'Account Details Not Yet Fetched' (i.e., account details have already been loaded and displayed). If none of these conditions are met, the key is marked as invalid.

rules.rule_name: Enter Key Is Always a Valid Action
rules.rule_description: The Enter key is unconditionally valid on the Account Update screen regardless of the current screen state. Pressing Enter always triggers standard input processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Enter
Pressed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen in any state
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The key is recognized as valid and the system proceeds to process the user's screen input without any state-based restriction

rules.rule_name: PF03 Key Is Always Valid for Exit
rules.rule_description: The PF03 key (Exit) is unconditionally valid on the Account Update screen regardless of the current screen state. Pressing PF03 always initiates the exit and return-to-menu process.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
PF03
Pressed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen in any state
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF03 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The key is recognized as valid and the system proceeds to exit the Account Update screen and return control to the calling program or main menu, without any state-based restriction

rules.rule_name: PF05 Key Valid Only When Changes Are Validated and Awaiting Confirmation
rules.rule_description: The PF05 key (Save/Confirm) is a context-sensitive key that is only valid when the user has made changes to account or customer data, those changes have passed all validations, and the system is waiting for the user to explicitly confirm the save. PF05 is not valid at any other point in the workflow.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Are changes validated
but not yet confirmed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and presses PF05
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the current screen state is 'Changes Validated but Not Yet Confirmed' (i.e., all field-level validations have passed and the system is prompting the user to confirm the update)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the current state IS 'Changes Validated but Not Yet Confirmed', PF05 is marked as valid and the system proceeds to execute the save and update process. If the current state is NOT 'Changes Validated but Not Yet Confirmed' (for example, no account has been fetched, details are just being displayed, or changes have validation errors), PF05 is marked as invalid and is overridden to be treated as the Enter key.

rules.rule_name: PF05 Not Valid Outside of Confirmation State
rules.rule_description: When PF05 is pressed but the screen is not in the 'Changes Validated but Not Yet Confirmed' state, the key press is considered invalid because there are no confirmed-valid changes ready to be saved.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
PF05 Not Valid in Current Context
User has not yet made and
validated changes to confirm

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and the current state is NOT 'Changes Validated but Not Yet Confirmed' (e.g., no account has been fetched, account details are displayed but no changes made, or changes have failed validation)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF05
acceptance_criteria.Then: PF05 is treated as an invalid key press. The system overrides the PF05 action and processes the interaction as if the Enter key had been pressed, continuing with standard input processing.

rules.rule_name: PF12 Key Valid Only When Account Details Have Been Fetched
rules.rule_description: The PF12 key (Refresh/Cancel Changes) is a context-sensitive key that is only valid when account and customer details have already been retrieved and are currently displayed on the screen. PF12 is not valid when the screen is in its initial state with no account data loaded.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Have account details
already been fetched
and displayed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and presses PF12
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the current screen state indicates that account details have already been fetched and displayed (i.e., the state is NOT 'Account Details Not Yet Fetched')
acceptance_criteria.Then: If account details HAVE been fetched and are displayed, PF12 is marked as valid and the system proceeds to refresh the screen with the original fetched data, cancelling any unsaved changes. If account details have NOT yet been fetched (the screen is in initial/search state), PF12 is marked as invalid and is overridden to be treated as the Enter key.

rules.rule_name: PF12 Not Valid When No Account Details Are Displayed
rules.rule_description: When PF12 is pressed but no account details have been fetched and displayed yet, the key press is considered invalid because there is no loaded account data to refresh or cancel changes against.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
PF12 Not Valid in Current Context
No account details are currently
displayed to cancel

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and the current state is 'Account Details Not Yet Fetched' (the screen is in its initial state, waiting for the user to enter an account number)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF12
acceptance_criteria.Then: PF12 is treated as an invalid key press. The system overrides the PF12 action and processes the interaction as if the Enter key had been pressed, continuing with standard input processing.

rules.rule_name: Any Unrecognized or Unsupported Key Is Treated as Enter
rules.rule_description: Any key press that is not explicitly supported by the Account Update screen (including PF01, PF02, PF04, PF06 through PF11, CLEAR, PA1, PA2, and any other unsupported keys) is treated as an invalid action and automatically overridden to behave as the Enter key, ensuring the screen continues to process normally.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Any Other Key Pressed
PF01, PF02, PF04, PF06-PF11,
PF13-PF24, CLEAR, PA1, PA2, etc.

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen in any state
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key that is not Enter, PF03, a contextually valid PF05, or a contextually valid PF12 — including but not limited to PF01, PF02, PF04, PF06, PF07, PF08, PF09, PF10, PF11, CLEAR, PA1, or PA2
acceptance_criteria.Then: The key is marked as invalid. The system overrides the key action and substitutes it with the Enter key action, so that the screen input is processed as a standard Enter key submission. No error message is displayed to the user for the invalid key — processing continues silently as Enter.

rules.rule_name: Invalid Key Override to Enter Key Processing
rules.rule_description: When any key is determined to be invalid in the current context, the system enforces a fallback mechanism that substitutes the invalid key with the Enter key, ensuring uninterrupted screen processing flow.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Treat as Enter Key
Invalid key is overridden
and processed as Enter

acceptance_criteria.Given: A key has been pressed on the Account Update screen and has been evaluated as invalid (either an unsupported key type, or a context-sensitive key pressed outside its valid state)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines the key is invalid (the invalid key flag is active)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the active key indicator to Enter key, effectively replacing the invalid key action with Enter key processing. All subsequent processing proceeds as if the user had pressed the Enter key. This override applies to: unsupported keys (PF01, PF02, PF04, PF06-PF11, CLEAR, PA1, PA2), PF05 pressed when changes are not in 'validated but unconfirmed' state, and PF12 pressed when account details have not yet been fetched.

key_functionalities.title: Exit and Return to Calling Program
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([User Presses PF03 - Exit])
    B{Was this program\ncalled from another\nprogram or transaction?}
    C[Set Destination to\nCalling Transaction ID\nand Calling Program]
    D[Set Destination to\nMain Menu Transaction\nand Main Menu Program]
    E[Update Communication Area:\nRecord current program\nas the originating program]
    F[Set User Context:\nMark as Standard User,\nSet Entry Mode to Fresh Entry]
    G[Transfer Control to\nDestination Program\npassing updated\nCommunication Area]
    H([Destination Program\nReceives Control])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - Calling program details exist| C
    B -->|No - Entered directly or from main menu| D
    C --> E
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G --> H

rules.rule_name: Determine Return Destination Transaction When Calling Transaction Exists
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF03 to exit, the system checks whether a calling transaction ID was recorded in the communication area. If a valid calling transaction ID exists, it is used as the return destination; otherwise, the system defaults to the main menu transaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was this program called from another program or transaction?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Account Update screen and the communication area contains a previously recorded calling transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) that is not blank and not empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF03 to exit the Account Update screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination transaction ID (CDEMO-TO-TRANID) to the calling transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) that was stored in the communication area, so control will be returned to the originating transaction

rules.rule_name: Default Return Destination to Main Menu When No Calling Transaction Exists
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF03 to exit and no calling transaction ID is recorded in the communication area (the program was entered directly or from the main menu), the system defaults the return destination to the main menu transaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No - Entered directly or from main menu

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Account Update screen and the communication area does not contain a valid calling transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID is blank or empty)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF03 to exit the Account Update screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination transaction ID (CDEMO-TO-TRANID) to the predefined main menu transaction ID (LIT-MENUTRANID), so control will be returned to the main menu

rules.rule_name: Determine Return Destination Program When Calling Program Exists
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF03 to exit, the system checks whether a calling program name was recorded in the communication area. If a valid calling program name exists, it is used as the return destination program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Destination to Calling Transaction ID and Calling Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Account Update screen and the communication area contains a previously recorded calling program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) that is not blank and not empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF03 to exit the Account Update screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program name (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) to the calling program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) that was stored in the communication area, so control will be returned to the originating program

rules.rule_name: Default Return Destination to Main Menu Program When No Calling Program Exists
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF03 to exit and no calling program name is recorded in the communication area, the system defaults the return destination to the main menu program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Destination to Main Menu Transaction and Main Menu Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Account Update screen and the communication area does not contain a valid calling program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is blank or empty)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF03 to exit the Account Update screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program name (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) to the predefined main menu program name (LIT-MENUPGM), so control will be returned to the main menu program

rules.rule_name: Record Current Program as Originator in Communication Area
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control, the system updates the communication area to record the Account Update program and its transaction as the originating source, so the destination program knows where it was called from.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Update Communication Area: Record current program as the originating program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF03 and the destination program and transaction have been determined
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the communication area for the transfer of control
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current Account Update transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) into the 'from transaction' field (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) and the current Account Update program name (LIT-THISPGM) into the 'from program' field (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the communication area, and also records the current map set name (LIT-THISMAPSET) into CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET and the current map name (LIT-THISMAP) into CDEMO-LAST-MAP

rules.rule_name: Set User Type to Standard User on Exit
rules.rule_description: When exiting via PF03, the system sets the user type context to standard user (non-administrative) in the communication area, ensuring the destination program receives the correct user role context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set User Context: Mark as Standard User, Set Entry Mode to Fresh Entry

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF03 and the communication area is being prepared for transfer
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the user context before transferring control
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the user type indicator (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER) to 'Standard User' in the communication area, indicating the receiving program should treat this as a regular user session

rules.rule_name: Set Program Entry Mode to Fresh Entry on Exit
rules.rule_description: When exiting via PF03, the system sets the program entry mode to 'fresh entry' in the communication area, ensuring the destination program initializes itself as if being entered for the first time rather than as a re-entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set User Context: Mark as Standard User, Set Entry Mode to Fresh Entry

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF03 and the communication area is being prepared for transfer
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the entry mode context before transferring control
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the program entry mode flag (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) to 'Enter' (fresh entry) in the communication area, so the destination program will initialize itself as a new entry rather than treating it as a screen re-entry

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Destination Program with Communication Area
rules.rule_description: After all context has been set, the system transfers control directly to the determined destination program, passing the fully updated communication area so the destination program has all necessary session context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer Control to Destination Program passing updated Communication Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination program name (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) has been determined (either the calling program or the main menu program), the user type is set to Standard User, the entry mode is set to Fresh Entry, and the communication area has been updated with the current program as the originator
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the transfer of control
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system transfers control directly to the destination program identified by CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, passing the complete updated communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) to that program, and the destination program begins execution with the provided context

key_functionalities.title: Fresh Entry Screen Display
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Fresh Entry into Program\nFirst time or from Main Menu]) 
    B[Reset Program Working Area\nClear all previous session data]
    C[Initialize Screen Header\nSet screen titles, transaction ID,\nprogram name, current date and time]
    D{Is this a\nFresh Entry?}
    E[Skip Data Population\nDo not populate any\naccount or customer fields]
    F[Set All Data Fields to Blank\nAccount details, customer details,\nbalances, dates, names, address,\nphone numbers all shown empty]

    I[No Action Keys Highlighted\nPF05 Save and PF12 Cancel\nare not activated as no\ndata has been loaded yet]
    J[Send Blank Screen to User\nDisplay the empty account update screen\nwith cursor positioned on\nAccount Number entry field]
    K([User Sees Blank Screen\nReady to Enter Account Number])

    A --> B

rules.rule_name: Detect Fresh Program Entry
rules.rule_description: Determine whether the current invocation is a fresh entry into the Account Update program — either the very first time it is launched (no prior session data exists) or when the user navigates to it directly from the Main Menu without having previously re-entered the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Fresh Entry into Program
First time or from Main Menu

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Update program is invoked
acceptance_criteria.When: Either (a) there is no existing session communication area (first-time launch), OR (b) the calling program is the Main Menu program AND the program re-entry flag is NOT set
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program is treated as a fresh entry: all communication area data and program working storage are fully reset to empty/initial values, the program state is set to 'Enter' mode, and the account details state is set to 'Details Not Fetched'

rules.rule_name: Reset All Session Data on Fresh Entry
rules.rule_description: When a fresh entry is detected, all previously held session data — including the shared communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) and the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) — must be completely cleared to prevent stale data from a prior session from appearing on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Reset Program Working Area
Clear all previous session data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has been identified as a fresh entry (first launch or navigation from Main Menu without re-entry)
acceptance_criteria.When: The fresh entry initialization logic executes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The shared communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is fully initialized to empty values, the program-specific working area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is fully initialized to empty values, the program state flag is set to 'Program Enter', and the account details availability flag is set to 'Details Not Fetched'

rules.rule_name: Initialize Screen Header with Current Date and Time
rules.rule_description: Before displaying any screen, the screen header area must be populated with static identification information (screen titles, transaction ID, program name) and dynamic runtime information (current system date and current system time) so the user can identify the screen context and when it was rendered.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Initialize Screen Header
Set screen titles, transaction ID,
program name, current date and time

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Update screen is about to be sent to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen initialization routine (3100-SCREEN-INIT) executes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen output area is cleared to low values; Screen Title Line 1 is populated from the standard title definition (CCDA-TITLE01); Screen Title Line 2 is populated from the standard title definition (CCDA-TITLE02); the Transaction Name field is set to the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID); the Program Name field is set to the current program name (LIT-THISPGM); the Current Date field is formatted as MM/DD/YY using the system current date; and the Current Time field is formatted as HH:MM:SS using the system current time

rules.rule_name: Skip Account and Customer Data Population on Fresh Entry
rules.rule_description: When the program is in 'Enter' mode (fresh entry), the screen variable setup routine must skip all account and customer data field population entirely. No account details, customer details, balances, dates, names, or address information should be moved to the screen output area during a fresh entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is this a
Fresh Entry?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen variable setup routine (3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS) is executing
acceptance_criteria.When: The program state flag is set to 'Program Enter' (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: All account and customer data field population steps are bypassed entirely — no account number, no account details, no customer details are moved to the screen output fields; the routine exits without populating any data fields

rules.rule_name: Display All Account and Customer Fields as Blank
rules.rule_description: When account details have not yet been fetched (initial state), all account and customer detail fields on the screen must be set to blank (low values) so the user sees a completely empty form. This covers all data fields including account status, all financial limits and balances, all date fields, group ID, customer number, SSN parts, FICO score, date of birth, customer name fields, all address fields, both phone numbers, government ID, EFT account ID, and primary cardholder flag.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set All Data Fields to Blank
Account details, customer details,
balances, dates, names, address,
phone numbers all shown empty

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen variable setup routine is determining what values to display
acceptance_criteria.When: The account details state is 'Details Not Fetched' OR the account number is zero/empty
acceptance_criteria.Then: All of the following screen output fields are set to blank (low values): Account Status, Credit Limit, Current Balance, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date Year/Month/Day, Expiry Date Year/Month/Day, Reissue Date Year/Month/Day, Group ID, Customer Number, SSN Part 1/Part 2/Part 3, FICO Score, Date of Birth Year/Month/Day, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City, State, Zip Code, Country, Phone 1 Area Code/Prefix/Line Number, Phone 2 Area Code/Prefix/Line Number, Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, and Primary Cardholder Flag

rules.rule_name: Display Search Key Prompt Message on Fresh Entry
rules.rule_description: When the program is in fresh entry mode or account details have not yet been fetched, the informational message area on the screen must display a prompt instructing the user to enter an Account Number to begin a search. This guides the user on the required first action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Informational Message
Display prompt asking user
to enter an Account Number to search

acceptance_criteria.Given: The informational message setup routine (3250-SETUP-INFOMSG) is executing
acceptance_criteria.When: The program state is 'Program Enter' (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) OR the account details state is 'Details Not Fetched' (ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED) OR there is no informational message currently set (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message flag is set to 'Prompt for Search Keys' (PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS), and the corresponding search key prompt message text is moved to the informational message output field (INFOMSGO) on the screen

rules.rule_name: Protect All Screen Fields by Default
rules.rule_description: As the first step in setting screen field protection attributes, all input fields on the Account Update screen must be set to protected (read-only) mode. This is the default baseline protection applied before selectively unprotecting specific fields based on the current program state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Screen Field Protection
Protect ALL fields except
Account Number entry field
Only Account Number is editable

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen attribute setup routine (3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS) is executing and calls the protect-all routine (3310-PROTECT-ALL-ATTRS)
acceptance_criteria.When: The protect-all-attributes routine executes
acceptance_criteria.Then: All of the following screen input fields are set to protected (read-only) mode using the DFHBMPRF attribute: Account Number, Account Status, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Balance, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date Year/Month/Day, Expiry Date Year/Month/Day, Reissue Date Year/Month/Day, Group ID, Customer Number, SSN Part 1/Part 2/Part 3, FICO Score, Date of Birth Year/Month/Day, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City, State, Zip Code, Country, Phone 1 Area Code/Prefix/Line Number, Phone 2 Area Code/Prefix/Line Number, Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, Primary Cardholder Flag, and the Informational Message field

rules.rule_name: Make Only Account Number Field Editable on Fresh Entry
rules.rule_description: When account details have not yet been fetched (fresh entry state), only the Account Number entry field should be made editable so the user can enter a search value. All other fields remain protected. The Account Number field is unprotected by setting it to 'field select enabled' (DFHBMFSE) attribute.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Screen Field Protection
Protect ALL fields except
Account Number entry field
Only Account Number is editable

acceptance_criteria.Given: All screen fields have been set to protected mode and the screen attribute setup routine is evaluating the current program state
acceptance_criteria.When: The account details state is 'Details Not Fetched' (ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account Number input field attribute (ACCTSIDA) is set to 'field select enabled' (DFHBMFSE), making it the only editable field on the screen; all other fields remain protected

rules.rule_name: Position Cursor on Account Number Field for Fresh Entry
rules.rule_description: When no account data has been fetched and the screen is in fresh entry state, the cursor must be automatically positioned on the Account Number field so the user can immediately begin typing the account number without manually navigating to the field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Screen Field Protection
Protect ALL fields except
Account Number entry field
Only Account Number is editable

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen attribute setup routine is setting cursor position based on the current state and validation flags
acceptance_criteria.When: The account filter flag is 'Not OK' (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK) OR the account filter flag is 'Blank' (FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK) OR no other specific field error flag is set (falls to OTHERWISE condition)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor length attribute for the Account Number field (ACCTSIDL) is set to -1, which instructs the terminal to position the cursor on the Account Number input field when the screen is displayed

rules.rule_name: Suppress Action Key Highlighting When No Data is Loaded
rules.rule_description: When the screen is in fresh entry state with no account data loaded, the PF5 (Confirm/Save) and PF12 (Re-fetch) action keys must not be visually highlighted or activated. These keys are only highlighted when there is data to act upon — PF5 when changes are pending confirmation, and PF12 when changes have been made.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
No Action Keys Highlighted
PF05 Save and PF12 Cancel
are not activated as no
data has been loaded yet

acceptance_criteria.Given: The informational message attribute setup routine (3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS) is executing
acceptance_criteria.When: The account update state is NOT 'Changes Made' (ACUP-CHANGES-MADE is FALSE) AND the informational message state is NOT 'Prompt for Confirmation' (PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION is FALSE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: Neither the PF5 key attribute (FKEY05A) nor the PF12 key attribute (FKEY12A) is set to the highlighted/bright attribute (DFHBMASB); both action keys remain in their default non-highlighted display state, indicating they are not currently active

rules.rule_name: Send Blank Account Update Screen to User
rules.rule_description: After all screen fields, messages, and attributes have been prepared for a fresh entry, the completed blank screen must be transmitted to the user's terminal. The screen is sent with cursor positioning enabled, the terminal screen is erased before display, and the keyboard is unlocked so the user can immediately begin entering data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Send Blank Screen to User
Display the empty account update screen
with cursor positioned on
Account Number entry field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen output area (CACTUPAO) has been fully prepared with blank data fields, the search key prompt message, all fields protected except Account Number, and no action keys highlighted
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen send routine (3400-SEND-SCREEN) executes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen map (LIT-THISMAP) from the map set (LIT-THISMAPSET) is sent to the terminal using the prepared output area (CACTUPAO) with the following settings: cursor is automatically positioned on the designated field (CURSOR option active), the terminal screen is fully erased before the new screen is displayed (ERASE option), and the keyboard is freed/unlocked so the user can immediately type (FREEKB option); the next map and mapset are recorded in the session navigation fields (CCARD-NEXT-MAP and CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET)

key_functionalities.title: Post
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Update Outcome Detected]) --> B{Was the Update
Successful or Failed?}
    B -->|Successful Update
OR Failed Update| C[Clear Program Working Area
Reset all intermediate processing
data and flags]
    C --> D[Clear Account ID
Remove previously searched
account number from context]
    D --> E[Set Program State to
Fresh Entry Mode
Mark as entering program anew]
    E --> F[Display Blank Account
Update Screen
Show empty search screen
ready for new account number entry]
    F --> G[Set Program State to
Re-Entry Mode
Mark that screen has been displayed]

Status to Not Fetched
Indicate no account data
is currently loaded]

New Account Search
User can enter a new
account number to search])

rules.rule_name: Detect Post-Update Outcome to Trigger Screen Reset
rules.rule_description: After the update processing completes, the system evaluates whether the outcome was a successful update or a failed update attempt, and in both cases triggers the same screen reset workflow to allow a new account search.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was the Update Successful or Failed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account update process has completed and the program state is either 'Changes Okayed and Done' (successful update) or 'Changes Failed' (failed update attempt)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the current program state in the main processing decision block
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system proceeds with the post-update screen reset workflow for both successful and failed update outcomes, treating both outcomes identically for the purpose of resetting the screen

rules.rule_name: Clear Program Working Area After Update Outcome
rules.rule_description: After a successful or failed update, all intermediate program working data, processing flags, and the program-specific communication area are cleared to remove any residual state from the previous account update session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear Program Working Area - Reset all intermediate processing data and flags

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account update process has completed with either a successful update (ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE) or a failed update (ACUP-CHANGES-FAILED)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates the post-update reset sequence
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program-specific working area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is fully initialized to remove all intermediate processing data, flags, and state information from the previous update session; and the miscellaneous storage area (WS-MISC-STORAGE) is also fully initialized to clear any temporary working values

rules.rule_name: Clear Previously Searched Account ID from Context
rules.rule_description: After a successful or failed update, the account number that was previously searched and used in the update session is removed from the shared session context so that no stale account reference persists into the next user interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear Account ID - Remove previously searched account number from context

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account update process has completed with either a successful or failed update outcome, and the shared session context (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) still holds the account number from the previous search
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the post-update reset sequence
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account ID stored in the shared session communication area (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) is set to zeroes, effectively removing the previously searched account number from the active session context

rules.rule_name: Set Program State to Fresh Entry Mode Before Displaying Blank Screen
rules.rule_description: Before sending the blank reset screen, the program state is temporarily set to 'fresh entry' mode so that the screen rendering logic treats the upcoming display as an initial program entry, resulting in a fully blank and unprotected account search screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Program State to Fresh Entry Mode - Mark as entering program anew

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program working area and account ID have been cleared following a successful or failed update
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to display the blank account update screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program entry state flag (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) is set to TRUE, marking the program as being in fresh entry mode so that the screen setup routines render an initial blank screen with only the account number field available for input

rules.rule_name: Display Blank Account Update Screen for New Search
rules.rule_description: After resetting the program state to fresh entry mode, a blank account update screen is sent to the user. All account and customer detail fields are empty and protected, and only the account number search field is available for input, prompting the user to begin a new account search.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Blank Account Update Screen - Show empty search screen ready for new account number entry

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program state has been set to fresh entry mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is TRUE) and all working areas have been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the send-map routine (3000-SEND-MAP)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen is initialized with current date and time; all account and customer detail fields (Account Status, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Balance, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date, Group ID, Customer Number, SSN parts, FICO Score, Date of Birth, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Lines 1 and 2, City, State, Zip, Country, Phone Numbers 1 and 2, Government ID, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder flag) are set to blank/empty; the information message area displays a prompt for the user to enter a search key (account number); all fields except the account number entry field are protected from input; and the screen is sent to the terminal with the keyboard unlocked and the screen erased

rules.rule_name: Set Program State to Re-Entry Mode After Blank Screen is Sent
rules.rule_description: After the blank account update screen has been sent to the user, the program state is updated to re-entry mode to indicate that the screen has already been displayed once. This ensures that on the next user interaction, the system correctly identifies this as a re-entry rather than a first-time entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Program State to Re-Entry Mode - Mark that screen has been displayed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The blank account update screen has been successfully sent to the user following a post-update reset
acceptance_criteria.When: The system completes the screen send operation and prepares to return control to await the next user input
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is set to TRUE, marking that the screen has been displayed and the next interaction will be treated as a re-entry to the program

rules.rule_name: Mark Account Details as Not Fetched After Screen Reset
rules.rule_description: After the blank screen is sent and the program is placed in re-entry mode, the account details status is explicitly set to 'not fetched' to indicate that no account data is currently loaded in the session. This ensures the next user interaction correctly routes to the account search flow rather than the account edit flow.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Account Details Status to Not Fetched - Indicate no account data is currently loaded

acceptance_criteria.Given: The blank account update screen has been sent and the program state has been set to re-entry mode
acceptance_criteria.When: The system finalizes the post-update reset sequence before returning control to await the next user input
acceptance_criteria.Then: The account details status flag (ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED) is set to TRUE, indicating that no account data is currently loaded; on the next user interaction, the system will treat any input as a new account search request rather than an attempt to edit previously loaded account details

rules.rule_name: Return Control to Await Next User Input After Reset
rules.rule_description: After all reset steps are complete, the system saves the current session state and returns control to the terminal, waiting for the user to enter a new account number. The session state is preserved in the communication area so it can be restored on the next interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Screen Ready for New Account Search - User can enter a new account number to search

acceptance_criteria.Given: The post-update reset sequence is complete: working areas cleared, account ID cleared, program state set to re-entry mode, account details marked as not fetched, and blank screen sent to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the common return routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: Any pending return message is moved to the screen error message area; the current shared session state (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) and program-specific state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) are saved together into the return communication area; control is returned to the CICS environment specifying the same transaction ID to be re-invoked when the user next presses a key, with the saved communication area passed along so the session state is fully restored on the next interaction

rules.rule_name: Initialize New Input Data Area Before Capturing Screen Input
rules.rule_description: Before capturing any user-entered data from the account update screen, all previously held new/pending input values must be cleared to ensure no stale data from a prior interaction contaminates the current input capture cycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Receive all data entered by user from the account update screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account update screen has been submitted by the user and the system is about to capture the entered data
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins the screen input receive process
acceptance_criteria.Then: All fields in the new account and customer details working area (ACUP-NEW-DETAILS) are initialized to empty/default values before any screen field values are read, ensuring a clean slate for the current input

rules.rule_name: Capture Account ID from Screen Input
rules.rule_description: The Account ID entered by the user on the account update screen must be captured and stored. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank (spaces), the Account ID is treated as not provided and cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored as the working Account ID for subsequent processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Account ID field blank or asterisk?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the account update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads the Account ID field (ACCTSIDI) from the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Account ID field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, both the working Account ID (CC-ACCT-ID) and the new Account ID input field (ACUP-NEW-ACCT-ID-X) are cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered Account ID value is stored in both CC-ACCT-ID and ACUP-NEW-ACCT-ID-X

rules.rule_name: Restrict Full Field Capture to Edit Mode Only
rules.rule_description: When the screen is in Search Mode (no account details have been fetched and displayed yet), only the Account ID field is relevant. All other account and customer detail fields on the screen are ignored and not captured, because the user has not yet retrieved an account to edit.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is screen in Search Mode? No account details displayed yet

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the account update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines that the screen is currently in Search Mode, meaning account details have not yet been fetched (ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is true)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system stops capturing screen input immediately after reading the Account ID field and exits the input capture process; no account status, financial limits, balances, dates, customer details, or any other fields are read from the screen

rules.rule_name: Capture Account Active Status from Screen Input
rules.rule_description: The Account Active Status field entered by the user must be captured. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the status is treated as not provided and cleared. Otherwise, the entered value (expected to be Y or N) is stored for subsequent validation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Account Status field blank or asterisk?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads the Account Status field (ACSTTUSI) from the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Account Status field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new Account Active Status (ACUP-NEW-ACTIVE-STATUS) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in ACUP-NEW-ACTIVE-STATUS

rules.rule_name: Capture Credit Limit from Screen Input with Numeric Conversion
rules.rule_description: The Credit Limit entered by the user must be captured as text. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the Credit Limit is cleared. If a value is entered, it is stored as text and, if it is a valid signed numeric value, it is also converted to a numeric form for subsequent financial calculations and comparisons.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Credit Limit field blank or asterisk?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads the Credit Limit field (ACRDLIMI) from the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Credit Limit field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new Credit Limit text field (ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-X) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); if a value is entered, it is stored in ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-X, and additionally, if the entered text passes a signed numeric format check (TEST-NUMVAL-C returns 0), the numeric equivalent is computed using NUMVAL-C and stored in ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-N; if the text is not a valid signed number, the numeric field is left unchanged

key_functionalities.title: Account Number Validation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Account Number Validation Start])
    CHECKBLANK{Is Account Number\nBlank or Empty?}
    BLANKERROR[Mark Account Number as Blank\nPrompt user to enter\nan account number\nSet Account ID to Zero]
    CHECKNUMERIC{Is Account Number\nNumeric?}
    CHECKZERO{Is Account Number\nEqual to Zero?}
    NUMERROR[Mark Account Number as Invalid\nDisplay Message:\n'Account Number if supplied must be\na 11 digit Non-Zero Number'\nSet Account ID to Zero]
    VALID[Mark Account Number as Valid\nStore Account Number\nfor further processing]
    END([Account Number Validation End])

    START --> CHECKBLANK
    CHECKBLANK -->|Yes - Blank or Empty| BLANKERROR
    CHECKBLANK -->|No - Has a Value| CHECKNUMERIC
    CHECKNUMERIC -->|No - Contains Non-Numeric Characters| NUMERROR
    CHECKNUMERIC -->|Yes - All Numeric| CHECKZERO
    CHECKZERO -->|Yes - Value is Zero| NUMERROR
    CHECKZERO -->|No - Non-Zero Value| VALID
    BLANKERROR --> END
    NUMERROR --> END
    VALID --> END

rules.rule_name: Account Number Blank or Empty Check
rules.rule_description: Validates that the user has entered an account number before any further processing. If the account number field is left blank or empty, the system must prompt the user to provide one and reset the account identifier to zero.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Account Number Blank or Empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has submitted the form with the Account Number field left blank, containing only spaces, or containing no value (empty/low-values)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs account number validation on the submitted Account Number field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) mark the account number filter status as 'Blank' (invalid), (2) set the overall input status to 'Error', (3) display a prompt message asking the user to enter an account number, (4) reset both the session Account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) and the new Account ID working field (ACUP-NEW-ACCT-ID) to zero, and (5) stop further account number validation

rules.rule_name: Account Number Must Be Numeric
rules.rule_description: Validates that the account number entered by the user contains only numeric digits. If the account number contains any non-numeric characters, it is rejected with a specific error message indicating the required format.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Account Number Numeric?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a non-blank value in the Account Number field on the Account Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the entered Account Number consists entirely of numeric digits
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Account Number contains any non-numeric characters, the system must: (1) set the overall input status to 'Error', (2) display the error message 'Account Number if supplied must be a 11 digit Non-Zero Number', (3) reset the session Account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) to zero, and (4) stop further account number validation. If the Account Number is fully numeric, processing continues to the zero-value check

rules.rule_name: Account Number Must Be Non-Zero
rules.rule_description: Validates that the account number entered by the user is not zero. An account number of all zeros is not a valid account identifier and must be rejected with the same format error message as a non-numeric entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Account Number Equal to Zero?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a numeric value in the Account Number field on the Account Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the numeric Account Number has a value equal to zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Account Number equals zero, the system must: (1) set the overall input status to 'Error', (2) display the error message 'Account Number if supplied must be a 11 digit Non-Zero Number', (3) reset the session Account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) to zero, and (4) stop further account number validation. If the Account Number is non-zero, processing continues to mark the account number as valid

rules.rule_name: Account Number Valid - Store for Further Processing
rules.rule_description: When the account number passes all validation checks (non-blank, numeric, and non-zero), it is accepted as a valid 11-digit account number and stored in the session context for subsequent account lookup and processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Account Number as Valid
Store Account Number
for further processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered an Account Number that is non-blank, fully numeric, and non-zero on the Account Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The account number successfully passes all validation checks (blank check, numeric check, and zero check)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) copy the validated Account Number into the session Account ID field (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) for use in subsequent account lookup operations, (2) mark the account number filter status as 'Valid' (FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID), and (3) allow processing to continue to the account data retrieval step

key_functionalities.title: Account Data Lookup
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Account Data Lookup])
    READ[Read Card Cross-Reference File\nusing Account ID as search key]
    CXACAIX[(CXACAIX\nCard Cross-Reference File)]
    FOUND{Account Found\nin Cross-Reference?}
    EXTRACT[Extract Associated Details\nRetrieve Customer ID\nRetrieve Card Number\nStore in communication area]
    NOTFOUND[Account Not Found\nMark account as invalid\nSet error message:\n'Account not found in Cross Reference file']
    OTHERERROR[Lookup Unsuccessful\nMark account as invalid\nSet error message]
    SUCCESS([End: Customer ID and\nCard Number Retrieved\nProceed to Account\nMaster Data Retrieval])
    FAIL([End: Account Lookup Failed\nReturn to Screen\nwith Error Message])

    START --> READ
    CXACAIX -.->|Search by Account ID| READ
    READ --> FOUND
    FOUND -->|Account Found| EXTRACT
    FOUND -->|Account Not Found| NOTFOUND
    FOUND -->|Unexpected Issue| OTHERERROR
    EXTRACT --> SUCCESS
    NOTFOUND --> FAIL
    OTHERERROR --> FAIL

rules.rule_name: Initiate Card Cross-Reference Lookup by Account ID
rules.rule_description: When an account data lookup is triggered, the system must search the Card Cross-Reference file using the provided Account ID as the search key to locate the associated customer and card details.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Card Cross-Reference File using Account ID as search key

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid 11-digit non-zero Account ID has been entered and confirmed as the search key for account data retrieval
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates the account data lookup process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system searches the Card Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX) using the Account ID as the unique search key to locate the associated customer ID and card number

rules.rule_name: Successful Cross-Reference Lookup - Extract Customer ID and Card Number
rules.rule_description: When the Account ID is found in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system must extract and store the associated Customer ID and Card Number for use in subsequent lookups.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Extract Associated Details - Retrieve Customer ID, Retrieve Card Number, Store in communication area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has searched the Card Cross-Reference file using the Account ID as the search key
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID is found in the Card Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system extracts the Customer ID (XREF-CUST-ID) and stores it in the session communication area (CDEMO-CUST-ID), and extracts the Card Number (XREF-CARD-NUM) and stores it in the session communication area (CDEMO-CARD-NUM), making both values available for subsequent account and customer master data retrieval

rules.rule_name: Account Not Found in Card Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: When the provided Account ID does not exist in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system must mark the account search as invalid and display a descriptive error message identifying the account number and the file where it was not found.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Account Not Found - Mark account as invalid, Set error message: 'Account not found in Cross Reference file'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has searched the Card Cross-Reference file using the provided Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the account filter as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK), sets an input error condition, and if no prior error message has been set, constructs and displays the error message: 'Account: [Account ID] not found in Cross ref file. Resp: [response code] Reas: [reason code]', and the account data lookup process is terminated without proceeding to the Account Master or Customer Master lookups

rules.rule_name: Unexpected Failure During Cross-Reference Lookup
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected issue occurs during the Card Cross-Reference file lookup (neither a successful read nor a 'not found' response), the system must mark the account as invalid and record a system-level error message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Lookup Unsuccessful - Mark account as invalid, Set error message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to search the Card Cross-Reference file using the Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The lookup results in an unexpected outcome that is neither a successful find nor a standard 'not found' response
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the account filter as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK), sets an input error condition, records the operation name as 'READ', records the file name (LIT-CARDXREFNAME-ACCT-PATH), captures the response and reason codes, and sets the standard file error message; the account data lookup process is terminated without proceeding to further lookups

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Account Master Retrieval After Successful Cross-Reference
rules.rule_description: After successfully retrieving the Customer ID and Card Number from the Card Cross-Reference file, the system must continue the account data lookup by proceeding to retrieve account details from the Account Master file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End: Customer ID and Card Number Retrieved - Proceed to Account Master Data Retrieval

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card Cross-Reference lookup has completed successfully and both Customer ID and Card Number have been stored in the session communication area
acceptance_criteria.When: The cross-reference lookup step ends with a successful outcome
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system proceeds to the next step in the account data lookup sequence, which is reading the Account Master file (9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT) using the same Account ID to retrieve full account details

rules.rule_name: Terminate Account Lookup and Return Error to Screen
rules.rule_description: When the Card Cross-Reference lookup fails for any reason (account not found or unexpected issue), the account data lookup process must be terminated immediately and the user must be returned to the screen with an appropriate error message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End: Account Lookup Failed - Return to Screen with Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card Cross-Reference file lookup has failed, either because the account was not found or due to an unexpected issue, and the account filter flag has been set to invalid
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks the account filter validity flag after the cross-reference lookup
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system exits the account data lookup process immediately (GO TO 9000-READ-ACCT-EXIT) without performing any further lookups (Account Master or Customer Master), and the error message previously set is displayed to the user on the account update screen

rules.rule_name: Read Account Master File by Account ID
rules.rule_description: When an account lookup is initiated, the system retrieves the full account record from the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) using the Account ID as the unique search key. This is the primary data retrieval step to obtain all account-level details.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Account Master File using Account ID as search key

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid Account ID has been provided and the Cross-Reference lookup has already succeeded in the prior step
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a lookup of the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) using the Account ID as the search key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the full account record containing Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date, and Group ID

rules.rule_name: Account Successfully Found in Account Master File
rules.rule_description: When the Account Master File lookup returns a successful result, the system marks the account as found and makes all retrieved account details available for display and further processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Account as Found
Account details now available:
- Active Status
- Current Balance
- Credit Limit
- Cash Credit Limit
- Current Cycle Credit
- Current Cycle Debit
- Open Date
- Expiry Date
- Reissue Date
- Group ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup of the Account Master File using the Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The account record is found successfully in the Account Master File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the account as found (FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER = TRUE) and the following account details become available for use: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date (Year/Month/Day), Expiry Date (Year/Month/Day), Reissue Date (Year/Month/Day), and Group ID

rules.rule_name: Account Not Found in Account Master File
rules.rule_description: When the Account Master File lookup finds no matching record for the provided Account ID, the system flags an input error and prepares a descriptive error message to inform the user that the account does not exist in the Account Master File.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Account Not Found Error
Prepare message:
'Account not found in
Account Master File'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup of the Account Master File using the Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: No account record matching the provided Account ID is found in the Account Master File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag (INPUT-ERROR = TRUE), marks the account filter as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK = TRUE), and if no prior error message has been set, prepares the error message: 'Account: [Account ID] not found in Acct Master file'

rules.rule_name: Account Master File Lookup Failure
rules.rule_description: When the Account Master File lookup encounters an unexpected failure (other than a simple not-found condition), the system flags an input error and prepares a generic file error message to inform the user that the account lookup could not be completed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Account Lookup Error
Prepare error message
for user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup of the Account Master File using the Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account Master File lookup fails due to an unexpected error (not a not-found condition)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag (INPUT-ERROR = TRUE), marks the account filter as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK = TRUE), and prepares a standard file error message indicating the operation was a READ on the Account Master File

rules.rule_name: Stop Processing and Return Error When Account Not Retrieved
rules.rule_description: When the Account Master File lookup fails for any reason (not found or unexpected error), the system immediately stops the account data retrieval process and returns control to the screen display with the error message, without proceeding to Customer Data Retrieval.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Stop: Return Error
to Screen Display

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Master File lookup has resulted in either a not-found condition or an unexpected error
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the result of the Account Master File lookup and determines the account was not successfully retrieved
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system immediately halts the account data retrieval process (exits 9000-READ-ACCT), does not proceed to Customer Data Retrieval, and returns the error condition and message to the screen display for the user

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Customer Data Retrieval After Successful Account Lookup
rules.rule_description: When the Account Master File lookup succeeds, the system continues the data retrieval sequence by proceeding to retrieve the associated customer details using the Customer ID obtained from the earlier Cross-Reference lookup.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Proceed to
Customer Data Retrieval

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Master File lookup has completed successfully and the account record has been marked as found
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the account lookup result and confirms the account was found
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system proceeds to the next step in the retrieval sequence — Customer Data Retrieval — using the Customer ID (CDEMO-CUST-ID) that was obtained from the Card Cross-Reference lookup

rules.rule_name: Store Retrieved Account Details as Original Reference Values
rules.rule_description: After all three lookups (Cross-Reference, Account Master, Customer Master) succeed, the system stores all retrieved account field values as the original 'old' reference values. These stored values are later used to detect whether the user has made any changes and to detect concurrent modifications by other users before saving updates.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Account as Found
Account details now available:
- Active Status
- Current Balance
- Credit Limit
- Cash Credit Limit
- Current Cycle Credit
- Current Cycle Debit
- Open Date
- Expiry Date
- Reissue Date
- Group ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Master File lookup has succeeded and the account record is available
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched account data as original reference values
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system saves the following account fields as original 'old' values for change-detection purposes: Account ID (ACUP-OLD-ACCT-ID), Active Status (ACUP-OLD-ACTIVE-STATUS), Current Balance (ACUP-OLD-CURR-BAL-N), Credit Limit (ACUP-OLD-CREDIT-LIMIT-N), Cash Credit Limit (ACUP-OLD-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-N), Current Cycle Credit (ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-N), Current Cycle Debit (ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-N), Open Date split into Year (ACUP-OLD-OPEN-YEAR), Month (ACUP-OLD-OPEN-MON), Day (ACUP-OLD-OPEN-DAY), Expiry Date split into Year (ACUP-OLD-EXP-YEAR), Month (ACUP-OLD-EXP-MON), Day (ACUP-OLD-EXP-DAY), Reissue Date split into Year (ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-YEAR), Month (ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-MON), Day (ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-DAY), and Group ID (ACUP-OLD-GROUP-ID)

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Customer Record from Customer Master File
rules.rule_description: The system uses the Customer ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference lookup to read the Customer Master file and retrieve the full customer profile.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use Customer ID retrieved from Card Cross-Reference to search Customer Master File

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid Customer ID has been retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference file during the account lookup process
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to read the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT) using the Customer ID as the search key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Customer Master file is accessed using the Customer ID to locate the matching customer record

rules.rule_name: Customer Record Successfully Found in Customer Master
rules.rule_description: When the Customer Master file contains a record matching the provided Customer ID, the system marks the customer as found and makes the full customer profile available for display and editing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Customer as Found - Record contains: Full Name First, Middle, Last - Address Line 1, Line 2, City - State, Zip, Country - Primary and Secondary Phone Numbers - Social Security Number - Date of Birth - FICO Credit Score - EFT Account ID - Primary Card Holder Indicator - Government Issued ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has submitted a read request to the Customer Master file using a Customer ID
acceptance_criteria.When: A matching customer record is found in the Customer Master file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the customer as successfully found, and the following customer data fields become available: First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City (Address Line 3), State Code, Zip Code, Country Code, Primary Phone Number, Secondary Phone Number, Social Security Number, Date of Birth, FICO Credit Score, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator, and Government Issued ID

rules.rule_name: Customer Record Not Found in Customer Master
rules.rule_description: When no customer record exists in the Customer Master file for the given Customer ID, the system sets an error condition and generates an appropriate error message to be displayed to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Customer Not Found - Set Error Flag - Display message: Customer ID not found in Customer Master

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has submitted a read request to the Customer Master file using a Customer ID
acceptance_criteria.When: No matching customer record is found in the Customer Master file for the provided Customer ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag, sets the customer filter status to 'not found', and displays the error message: 'CustId: [Customer ID] not found in customer master' along with the response and reason codes from the file system

rules.rule_name: Store Customer Personal Identity Data as Original Values

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Store Fetched Data as Original Values

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched customer data as original values
acceptance_criteria.Then: The following customer identity fields are stored as original values: Customer ID, Social Security Number (full), Date of Birth Year, Date of Birth Month, Date of Birth Day, FICO Credit Score, First Name, Middle Name, and Last Name

rules.rule_name: Store Customer Address Data as Original Values
rules.rule_description: After successfully retrieving the customer record, the system stores the customer's full address information as the original baseline values to enable change detection when the user submits edits.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Store Fetched Data as Original Values

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched customer address data as original values
acceptance_criteria.Then: The following customer address fields are stored as original values: Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City (Address Line 3), State Code, Country Code, and Zip Code

rules.rule_name: Store Customer Contact and Financial Data as Original Values
rules.rule_description: After successfully retrieving the customer record, the system stores the customer's contact details and financial profile data as the original baseline values to enable change detection when the user submits edits.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Store Fetched Data as Original Values

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched customer contact and financial data as original values

rules.rule_name: Propagate Customer Name to Session Context

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched data into the session context

rules.rule_name: Exit Account Retrieval Process on Customer Not Found

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Exit: Return Error to Screen Display

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system attempted to read the Customer Master file and the customer record was not found
acceptance_criteria.When: The customer not-found error condition is detected
acceptance_criteria.Then: The account data retrieval process exits immediately without storing any fetched data, and the error message is passed back to the screen display for the user to see; no account or customer data is presented for editing
