rules.rule_name: Initialize Original Details Storage Before Saving Fetched Data
rules.rule_description: Before storing any retrieved account or customer data as original values, the original details storage area must be fully cleared to ensure no stale data from a previous session or lookup contaminates the new comparison baseline.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear and Initialize Original Details Storage Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully retrieved account and customer data from the Account Master, Customer Master, and Card Cross-Reference files for a given Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The process to store fetched data as original values begins
acceptance_criteria.Then: The entire original details storage area (ACUP-OLD-DETAILS) is cleared and initialized to its default empty state before any new values are written into it, ensuring a clean baseline for subsequent change detection

rules.rule_name: Save Account Identity and Status as Original Values
rules.rule_description: The Account ID retrieved from the Account Master file and the Account Active Status must be preserved as the original (baseline) values so that any user modifications to these fields can be detected during the change comparison step.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save Account ID as Original Account ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Master file record has been successfully read for the requested Account ID, providing the Account ID and Account Active Status
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched account data as original values
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account ID from the Account Master record is saved as the Original Account ID (ACUP-OLD-ACCT-ID), and the Account Active Status from the Account Master record is saved as the Original Account Active Status (ACUP-OLD-ACTIVE-STATUS)

rules.rule_name: Save Account Financial Values as Original Values
rules.rule_description: All five account financial values retrieved from the Account Master file must be preserved as original (baseline) numeric values so that any user modifications to these financial fields can be accurately detected during the change comparison step.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save Account Financial Values as Original Values: Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Master file record has been successfully read, providing the five financial values: Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit amount, and Current Cycle Debit amount
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched account financial data as original values
acceptance_criteria.Then: Each financial value is saved individually as its corresponding original numeric value: Current Balance is saved as ACUP-OLD-CURR-BAL-N, Credit Limit is saved as ACUP-OLD-CREDIT-LIMIT-N, Cash Credit Limit is saved as ACUP-OLD-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-N, Current Cycle Credit is saved as ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-N, and Current Cycle Debit is saved as ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-N

rules.rule_name: Save Account Dates as Original Values by Splitting into Year, Month, and Day Components
rules.rule_description: The three account dates stored in the Account Master file in YYYY-MM-DD format must each be decomposed into separate Year, Month, and Day components and stored individually as original values. This decomposition enables field-level change detection and screen display of individual date parts.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save Account Dates as Original Dates by splitting into Year / Month / Day parts: Account Open Date, Account Expiry Date, Account Reissue Date

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Master file record has been successfully read, providing three dates in YYYY-MM-DD format: Account Open Date (ACCT-OPEN-DATE), Account Expiry Date (ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE), and Account Reissue Date (ACCT-REISSUE-DATE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched account date data as original values
acceptance_criteria.Then: Each date is split into three components using fixed character positions: positions 1-4 (Year), positions 6-7 (Month), and positions 9-10 (Day). Account Open Date Year is saved to ACUP-OLD-OPEN-YEAR, Month to ACUP-OLD-OPEN-MON, Day to ACUP-OLD-OPEN-DAY. Account Expiry Date Year is saved to ACUP-OLD-EXP-YEAR, Month to ACUP-OLD-EXP-MON, Day to ACUP-OLD-EXP-DAY. Account Reissue Date Year is saved to ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-YEAR, Month to ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-MON, Day to ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-DAY

rules.rule_name: Save Account Group ID as Original Value
rules.rule_description: The Account Group ID retrieved from the Account Master file must be preserved as the original (baseline) value so that any user modification to this field can be detected during the change comparison step.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save Account Group ID as Original Group ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Master file record has been successfully read, providing the Account Group ID (ACCT-GROUP-ID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched account group data as original values
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account Group ID from the Account Master record is saved as the Original Group ID (ACUP-OLD-GROUP-ID)

rules.rule_name: Save Customer ID as Original Value
rules.rule_description: The Customer ID retrieved from the Customer Master file must be preserved as the original (baseline) value to establish the customer identity link for the account being updated and to support change detection.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save Customer ID as Original Customer ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer Master file record has been successfully read using the Customer ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference lookup, providing the Customer ID (CUST-ID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched customer identity data as original values
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Customer ID from the Customer Master record is saved as the Original Customer ID (ACUP-OLD-CUST-ID)

rules.rule_name: Save Customer Personal Details as Original Values
rules.rule_description: The customer's Social Security Number, Date of Birth, and FICO Credit Score retrieved from the Customer Master file must be preserved as original values. The Date of Birth is decomposed into separate Year, Month, and Day components. These values serve as the baseline for detecting any user modifications during the change comparison step.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save Customer Personal Details as Original Values: SSN, Date of Birth Year / Month / Day, FICO Credit Score

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer Master file record has been successfully read, providing the customer's SSN (CUST-SSN), Date of Birth in YYYY-MM-DD format (CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD), and FICO Credit Score (CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched customer personal data as original values
acceptance_criteria.Then: The SSN is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-SSN. The Date of Birth is split using fixed character positions: positions 1-4 (Year) saved to ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-YEAR, positions 6-7 (Month) saved to ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-MON, and positions 9-10 (Day) saved to ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-DAY. The FICO Credit Score is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-FICO-SCORE

rules.rule_name: Save Customer Name Details as Original Values
rules.rule_description: The customer's full name components — First Name, Middle Name, and Last Name — retrieved from the Customer Master file must be preserved as original (baseline) values so that any user modifications to name fields can be detected during the change comparison step.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save Customer Name Details as Original Values: First Name, Middle Name, Last Name

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer Master file record has been successfully read, providing the customer's First Name (CUST-FIRST-NAME), Middle Name (CUST-MIDDLE-NAME), and Last Name (CUST-LAST-NAME)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched customer name data as original values
acceptance_criteria.Then: The First Name is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-FIRST-NAME, the Middle Name is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-MIDDLE-NAME, and the Last Name is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-LAST-NAME

rules.rule_name: Save Customer Address Details as Original Values
rules.rule_description: All six components of the customer's mailing address retrieved from the Customer Master file must be preserved as original (baseline) values so that any user modifications to address fields can be detected during the change comparison step.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save Customer Address Details as Original Values: Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City, State Code, Country Code, Zip Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer Master file record has been successfully read, providing the customer's Address Line 1 (CUST-ADDR-LINE-1), Address Line 2 (CUST-ADDR-LINE-2), City stored as Address Line 3 (CUST-ADDR-LINE-3), State Code (CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD), Country Code (CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD), and Zip Code (CUST-ADDR-ZIP)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched customer address data as original values
acceptance_criteria.Then: Address Line 1 is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-1, Address Line 2 is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-2, City (Address Line 3) is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-3, State Code is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD, Country Code is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD, and Zip Code is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-ZIP

rules.rule_name: Save Customer Contact and Identity Details as Original Values
rules.rule_description: The customer's contact and identity details — Primary Phone Number, Secondary Phone Number, Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, and Primary Card Holder Indicator — retrieved from the Customer Master file must be preserved as original (baseline) values so that any user modifications to these fields can be detected during the change comparison step.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save Customer Contact Details as Original Values: Primary Phone Number, Secondary Phone Number, Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer Master file record has been successfully read, providing the customer's Primary Phone Number (CUST-PHONE-NUM-1), Secondary Phone Number (CUST-PHONE-NUM-2), Government Issued ID (CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID), EFT Account ID (CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID), and Primary Card Holder Indicator (CUST-PRI-CARD-HOLDER-IND)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched customer contact and identity data as original values
acceptance_criteria.Then: Primary Phone Number is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1, Secondary Phone Number is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2, Government Issued ID is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID, EFT Account ID is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID, and Primary Card Holder Indicator is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-PRI-HOLDER-IND

rules.rule_name: Update Session Communication Area with Account and Customer Context
rules.rule_description: After all original values are stored, the shared session communication area must be updated with key account and customer identifiers so that other programs and screens in the session can access the current account context without re-reading the files.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Update Communication Area with Account ID, Customer ID, Customer Name, Account Status and Card Number for Session Context

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Master, Customer Master, and Card Cross-Reference records have all been successfully read and their data stored as original values
acceptance_criteria.When: The system finalizes the storage of fetched data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The session communication area (CDEMO) is updated with the following values: Account ID (ACCT-ID) is stored in CDEMO-ACCT-ID, Customer ID (CUST-ID) is stored in CDEMO-CUST-ID, Customer First Name (CUST-FIRST-NAME) is stored in CDEMO-CUST-FNAME, Customer Middle Name (CUST-MIDDLE-NAME) is stored in CDEMO-CUST-MNAME, Customer Last Name (CUST-LAST-NAME) is stored in CDEMO-CUST-LNAME, Account Active Status (ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS) is stored in CDEMO-ACCT-STATUS, and the Card Number from the Cross-Reference record (XREF-CARD-NUM) is stored in CDEMO-CARD-NUM

key_functionalities.title: Change Detection
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    CD_START([Begin Change Detection])
    CD_INIT[Set Initial State:\nNo Changes Found]

    CD_ACCT_GRP{Compare Account Fields:\nAccount ID, Active Status,\nCurrent Balance, Credit Limit,\nCash Credit Limit}
    CD_ACCT_DATES{Compare Account Dates:\nOpen Date, Expiry Date,\nReissue Date}
    CD_ACCT_OTHER{Compare Other Account Fields:\nCurrent Cycle Credit,\nCurrent Cycle Debit,\nGroup ID}

    CD_CUST_NAME{Compare Customer Name Fields:\nFirst Name, Middle Name,\nLast Name}
    CD_CUST_ADDR{Compare Customer Address Fields:\nAddress Line 1, Address Line 2,\nCity, State, Country, Zip Code}
    CD_CUST_PHONE{Compare Customer Phone Numbers:\nPhone Number 1\nPhone Number 2\nAll three parts of each}
    CD_CUST_OTHER{Compare Other Customer Fields:\nSSN, Government Issued ID,\nDate of Birth, EFT Account ID,\nPrimary Card Holder Indicator,\nFICO Score}

    CD_CHANGED[Flag: Change Has Occurred\nUser Has Modified Data -\nProceed to Validate Changes]
    CD_NOCHANGE[Flag: No Changes Detected\nUser Has Not Modified Any Data -\nNo Update Required]

    CD_END([End Change Detection])

    CD_START --> CD_INIT
    CD_INIT --> CD_ACCT_GRP

    CD_ACCT_GRP -->|Difference Found| CD_CHANGED
    CD_ACCT_GRP -->|All Match| CD_ACCT_DATES

    CD_ACCT_DATES -->|Difference Found| CD_CHANGED
    CD_ACCT_DATES -->|All Match| CD_ACCT_OTHER

    CD_ACCT_OTHER -->|Difference Found| CD_CHANGED
    CD_ACCT_OTHER -->|All Match| CD_CUST_NAME

    CD_CUST_NAME -->|Difference Found| CD_CHANGED
    CD_CUST_NAME -->|All Match| CD_CUST_ADDR

    CD_CUST_ADDR -->|Difference Found| CD_CHANGED
    CD_CUST_ADDR -->|All Match| CD_CUST_PHONE

    CD_CUST_PHONE -->|Difference Found| CD_CHANGED
    CD_CUST_PHONE -->|All Match| CD_CUST_OTHER

    CD_CUST_OTHER -->|Difference Found| CD_CHANGED
    CD_CUST_OTHER -->|All Fields Match| CD_NOCHANGE

    CD_CHANGED --> CD_END
    CD_NOCHANGE --> CD_END

rules.rule_name: Initialize Change Detection State
rules.rule_description: Before comparing any field values, the change detection process initializes its state to indicate that no changes have been found. This baseline state is updated if any field comparison reveals a difference.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Initial State: No Changes Found

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the account update screen after account details have already been fetched and displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The change detection process begins
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the internal state to 'No Changes Found' as the starting baseline before any field comparisons are performed

rules.rule_name: Compare Core Account Fields for Changes
rules.rule_description: The system compares the user-entered values for core account fields against the originally fetched values. Active Status comparison is case-insensitive. Numeric fields are compared by value. If any difference is found, the process immediately flags a change and stops further comparison.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Compare Account Fields: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account details have been fetched and displayed, and the user has submitted the screen with entered values for Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, and Cash Credit Limit
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the new (user-entered) values against the original fetched values for: Account ID (exact match), Active Status (case-insensitive match), Current Balance (numeric value match), Credit Limit (numeric value match), and Cash Credit Limit (numeric value match)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If any of these five fields differ between the new and original values, the system immediately flags the state as 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process; if all five fields match, the system proceeds to compare account date fields

rules.rule_name: Compare Account Date Fields for Changes
rules.rule_description: The system compares the user-entered date values for Open Date, Expiry Date, and Reissue Date against the originally fetched values. Each date is compared as a complete date value. If any difference is found, the process immediately flags a change.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Compare Account Dates: Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date

acceptance_criteria.Given: The core account fields (Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit) have all matched between new and original values
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the new (user-entered) values against the original fetched values for: Open Date (exact match), Expiry Date (exact match), and Reissue Date (exact match)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If any of these three date fields differ between the new and original values, the system immediately flags the state as 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process; if all three date fields match, the system proceeds to compare other account fields

rules.rule_name: Compare Other Account Fields for Changes
rules.rule_description: The system compares the user-entered values for Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, and Group ID against the originally fetched values. Group ID comparison is case-insensitive and ignores leading/trailing spaces. If any difference is found, the process immediately flags a change.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Compare Other Account Fields: Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Group ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The core account fields and account date fields have all matched between new and original values
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the new (user-entered) values against the original fetched values for: Current Cycle Credit (numeric value match), Current Cycle Debit (numeric value match), and Group ID (case-insensitive match after trimming leading and trailing spaces)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If any of these three fields differ between the new and original values, the system immediately flags the state as 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process; if all three fields match, the system proceeds to compare customer name fields

rules.rule_name: Compare Customer Name Fields for Changes
rules.rule_description: The system compares the user-entered customer name values and Customer ID against the originally fetched values. All comparisons are case-insensitive and ignore leading/trailing spaces. Customer ID is also included in this comparison group. If any difference is found, the process immediately flags a change.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Compare Customer Name Fields: First Name, Middle Name, Last Name

acceptance_criteria.Given: All account-level fields (core fields, dates, and other account fields) have matched between new and original values
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the new (user-entered) values against the original fetched values for: Customer ID (case-insensitive, trimmed), First Name (case-insensitive, trimmed), Middle Name (case-insensitive, trimmed), and Last Name (case-insensitive, trimmed)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If any of these four fields differ between the new and original values, the system immediately flags the state as 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process; if all four fields match, the system proceeds to compare customer address fields

rules.rule_name: Compare Customer Address Fields for Changes
rules.rule_description: The system compares the user-entered customer address values against the originally fetched values. All text field comparisons are case-insensitive and ignore leading/trailing spaces. Zip Code is compared case-insensitively and trimmed. If any difference is found, the process immediately flags a change.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Compare Customer Address Fields: Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City, State, Country, Zip Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: All account-level fields and customer name fields have matched between new and original values
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the new (user-entered) values against the original fetched values for: Address Line 1 (case-insensitive, trimmed), Address Line 2 (case-insensitive, trimmed), City/Address Line 3 (case-insensitive, trimmed), State Code (case-insensitive, trimmed), Country Code (case-insensitive, trimmed), and Zip Code (case-insensitive, trimmed)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If any of these six address fields differ between the new and original values, the system immediately flags the state as 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process; if all six address fields match, the system proceeds to compare customer phone number fields

rules.rule_name: Compare Customer Phone Number Fields for Changes
rules.rule_description: The system compares the user-entered phone number values against the originally fetched values. Each phone number is stored in three separate parts (Area Code, Prefix, Line Number) and each part is compared individually using an exact match. If any part of either phone number differs, the process immediately flags a change.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Compare Customer Phone Numbers: Phone Number 1, Phone Number 2, All three parts of each

acceptance_criteria.Given: All account-level fields, customer name fields, and customer address fields have matched between new and original values
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the new (user-entered) values against the original fetched values for all six phone number parts: Phone Number 1 Area Code (exact match), Phone Number 1 Prefix (exact match), Phone Number 1 Line Number (exact match), Phone Number 2 Area Code (exact match), Phone Number 2 Prefix (exact match), and Phone Number 2 Line Number (exact match)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If any of these six phone number parts differ between the new and original values, the system immediately flags the state as 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process; if all six phone number parts match, the system proceeds to compare other customer fields

rules.rule_name: Compare Other Customer Fields for Changes
rules.rule_description: The system compares the remaining user-entered customer fields against the originally fetched values. Government Issued ID and Primary Card Holder Indicator comparisons are case-insensitive and trimmed. SSN, Date of Birth, EFT Account ID, and FICO Score are compared by exact value. This is the final comparison group — if all match, no changes are detected.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Compare Other Customer Fields: SSN, Government Issued ID, Date of Birth, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator, FICO Score

acceptance_criteria.Given: All account-level fields, customer name fields, customer address fields, and customer phone number fields have matched between new and original values
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the new (user-entered) values against the original fetched values for: SSN (exact match of full SSN value), Government Issued ID (case-insensitive, trimmed), Date of Birth (exact match), EFT Account ID (exact match), Primary Card Holder Indicator (case-insensitive, trimmed), and FICO Score (exact match)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If any of these six fields differ between the new and original values, the system flags the state as 'Change Has Occurred'; if all six fields match, the system flags the state as 'No Changes Detected', indicating the user has not modified any data and no update is required

rules.rule_name: Flag Change Has Occurred - Proceed to Validation
rules.rule_description: When any field comparison during change detection reveals a difference between the user-entered value and the originally fetched value, the system immediately flags that a change has occurred and exits the comparison process. This flag triggers the full field-by-field validation process to run on the submitted data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Flag: Change Has Occurred - User Has Modified Data - Proceed to Validate Changes

acceptance_criteria.Given: The change detection process is comparing new (user-entered) values against original fetched values across account and customer fields
acceptance_criteria.When: A difference is detected in any compared field at any point during the comparison sequence
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system immediately sets the state to 'Change Has Occurred', exits the change detection process without performing any further comparisons, and the subsequent action is to proceed with full input validation of all submitted field values

rules.rule_name: Flag No Changes Detected - Skip Update
rules.rule_description: When all field comparisons across all account and customer fields show that the user-entered values match the originally fetched values, the system flags that no changes have been detected. This means no update to the account or customer records is required, and the screen is redisplayed with the original values without triggering any validation or update processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Flag: No Changes Detected - User Has Not Modified Any Data - No Update Required

acceptance_criteria.Given: The change detection process has completed comparisons across all account fields (Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Group ID) and all customer fields (Customer ID, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Lines 1-3, State, Country, Zip, Phone 1 all parts, Phone 2 all parts, SSN, Government Issued ID, Date of Birth, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator, FICO Score)
acceptance_criteria.When: Every single field comparison shows that the new (user-entered) value matches the original fetched value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the state to 'No Changes Detected', no field validation is performed, no update to account or customer records is initiated, and the screen is redisplayed showing the original values with a message indicating no changes were found

key_functionalities.title: Account Status Validation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start Account Status Validation])
    GETVAL[Retrieve Account Active Status\nValue entered by user on screen]
    CHECKBLANK{Is Account Status\nBlank or Empty?}
    BLANKERROR[Mark as Invalid\nSet Error: 'Account Status\nmust be supplied']
    CHECKYN{Does Account Status\nContain Y or N?}
    INVALIDERROR[Mark as Invalid\nSet Error: 'Account Status\nmust be Y or N']
    VALID[Mark Account Status\nas Valid\nProceed to next validation]
    END([End Account Status Validation])

    START --> GETVAL
    GETVAL --> CHECKBLANK
    CHECKBLANK -->|Yes - Blank or Empty| BLANKERROR
    CHECKBLANK -->|No - Value Provided| CHECKYN
    CHECKYN -->|No - Invalid Value| INVALIDERROR
    CHECKYN -->|Yes - Y or N| VALID
    BLANKERROR --> END
    INVALIDERROR --> END
    VALID --> END

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Account Active Status for Validation
rules.rule_description: Before validating the account active status, the system retrieves the value entered by the user on the account update screen and prepares it for the Y/N validation routine. This rule ensures the correct field value and field label ('Account Status') are loaded into the validation working area prior to any checks being performed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Account Active Status Value entered by user on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted the account update screen with a value entered (or left blank) in the Account Status field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to validate the Account Status field by loading the user-entered value from the screen input area (ACUP-NEW-ACTIVE-STATUS) into the Yes/No validation working field, and sets the field label to 'Account Status'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account Status value entered by the user is available in the validation working area, the field label 'Account Status' is set for use in any error messages, and the Y/N validation routine is invoked to perform the actual checks

rules.rule_name: Account Status Mandatory Presence Check
rules.rule_description: The Account Active Status field is mandatory on the account update screen. If the user leaves the field blank, empty, or submits a zero value, the system must reject the input and inform the user that the field must be supplied. Only the first error message encountered during the entire screen validation is displayed to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Account Status Blank or Empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted the account update screen and the Account Status field has been loaded into the validation working area
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account Status value is blank (spaces), empty (low-values), or zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: The overall input is marked as invalid (INPUT-ERROR), the Account Status field is specifically flagged as blank (FLG-YES-NO-BLANK), and if no prior error message has already been set, the error message 'Account Status must be supplied.' is recorded; validation of the Account Status field ends immediately without checking the Y/N value

rules.rule_name: Account Status Y or N Value Check
rules.rule_description: When the Account Active Status field is not blank, the system must verify that the value entered is either 'Y' (Yes/Active) or 'N' (No/Inactive). Any other value is considered invalid. This enforces the business rule that an account's active status can only be one of two defined states.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Does Account Status Contain Y or N?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted the account update screen, the Account Status field is not blank, and the value has been loaded into the validation working area
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account Status value is evaluated and it does NOT equal 'Y' or 'N' (i.e., FLG-YES-NO-ISVALID is not set, meaning the value is not a valid Y/N indicator)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The overall input is marked as invalid (INPUT-ERROR), the Account Status field is specifically flagged as containing an invalid value (FLG-YES-NO-NOT-OK), and if no prior error message has already been set, the error message 'Account Status must be Y or N.' is recorded; validation of the Account Status field ends immediately

rules.rule_name: Account Status Successfully Validated
rules.rule_description: When the Account Active Status field passes both the mandatory presence check and the Y/N value check, it is marked as valid and the validation result is stored. Processing continues to the next field validation in the account update workflow.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Account Status as Valid Proceed to next validation

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted the account update screen with a value in the Account Status field that is not blank and equals either 'Y' or 'N'
acceptance_criteria.When: Both the blank check and the Y/N value check pass successfully (FLG-YES-NO-ISVALID is confirmed as true)
acceptance_criteria.Then: No error is raised for the Account Status field, the validated Account Status value is stored in the account status edit result area (WS-EDIT-ACCT-STATUS), and the validation process proceeds to the next field (Open Date validation)

rules.rule_name: Single Error Message Display Policy for Account Status
rules.rule_description: When the Account Status field fails validation (either blank or invalid value), an error message is only recorded if no other error message has already been captured during the current screen validation pass. This ensures that only the first error encountered across all fields is shown to the user at one time, preventing message overwriting.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark as Invalid Set Error: 'Account Status must be supplied' / 'Account Status must be Y or N'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Status field has failed validation (either blank or contains a value other than Y or N) during the account update screen submission
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to record the Account Status error message ('Account Status must be supplied.' or 'Account Status must be Y or N.')
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error message is written to the screen error message area ONLY IF no prior error message has already been set (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is true); if a prior error message already exists, the Account Status error message is suppressed and the existing message is preserved

key_functionalities.title: Date Field Validation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Date Field Validation])

    OPENDATE[Validate Account Open Date\nExtract Year, Month, Day\nfrom CCYYMMDD format]
    EXPIRYDATE[Validate Account Expiry Date\nExtract Year, Month, Day\nfrom CCYYMMDD format]
    REISSUEDATE[Validate Account Reissue Date\nExtract Year, Month, Day\nfrom CCYYMMDD format]
    DOBDATE[Validate Customer Date of Birth\nExtract Year, Month, Day\nfrom CCYYMMDD format]

    subgraph DATECHECK[_Date Validation Steps 'applied to each date field'_]
        YEARBLANK{Year\nSupplied?}
        YEARBLANK_ERR[Mark Year as Missing\nSet Error Message:\nYear must be supplied]
        YEARNUMERIC{Year is\n4-digit Numeric?}
        YEARNUMERIC_ERR[Mark Year as Invalid\nSet Error Message:\nMust be 4 digit number]
        YEARCENTURY{Year is\n1900s or 2000s?}
        YEARCENTURY_ERR[Mark Year as Invalid\nSet Error Message:\nCentury is not valid]
        YEAROK[Year is Valid]

        MONTHBLANK{Month\nSupplied?}
        MONTHBLANK_ERR[Mark Month as Missing\nSet Error Message:\nMonth must be supplied]
        MONTHRANGE{Month is\nbetween 1 and 12?}
        MONTHRANGE_ERR[Mark Month as Invalid\nSet Error Message:\nMonth must be between 1 and 12]
        MONTHOK[Month is Valid]

        DAYBLANK{Day\nSupplied?}
        DAYBLANK_ERR[Mark Day as Missing\nSet Error Message:\nDay must be supplied]
        DAYNUMERIC{Day is\nNumeric?}
        DAYNUMERIC_ERR[Mark Day as Invalid\nSet Error Message:\nDay must be between 1 and 31]
        DAYRANGE{Day is\nbetween 1 and 31?}
        DAYRANGE_ERR[Mark Day as Invalid\nSet Error Message:\nDay must be between 1 and 31]
        DAYOK[Day is Valid]

        DAY31CHECK{Month allows\n31 days?}
        DAY31_ERR[Mark Day and Month Invalid\nSet Error Message:\nCannot have 31 days in this month]
        FEB30CHECK{Is February\nwith 30 days?}
        FEB30_ERR[Mark Day and Month Invalid\nSet Error Message:\nCannot have 30 days in this month]
        FEB29CHECK{Is February\nwith 29 days?}
        LEAPCHECK{Is it a\nLeap Year?\nYear divisible by 4\nor 400 for century years}

        DATEVALID([Date is Valid])
    end

    DOBFUTURECHECK{Date of Birth\nAdditional Check:\nIs DOB in the past?}

    END([End: All Date Fields Validated])

    START --> OPENDATE
    OPENDATE --> YEARBLANK
    EXPIRYDATE --> YEARBLANK
    REISSUEDATE --> YEARBLANK
    DOBDATE --> YEARBLANK

    YEARBLANK -->|No - Blank| YEARBLANK_ERR
    YEARBLANK -->|Yes - Supplied| YEARNUMERIC
    YEARBLANK_ERR --> MONTHBLANK

    YEARNUMERIC -->|No - Not Numeric| YEARNUMERIC_ERR
    YEARNUMERIC -->|Yes - Numeric| YEARCENTURY
    YEARNUMERIC_ERR --> MONTHBLANK

    YEARCENTURY -->|No - Invalid Century| YEARCENTURY_ERR
    YEARCENTURY -->|Yes - Valid Century| YEAROK
    YEARCENTURY_ERR --> MONTHBLANK
    YEAROK --> MONTHBLANK

    MONTHBLANK -->|No - Blank| MONTHBLANK_ERR
    MONTHBLANK -->|Yes - Supplied| MONTHRANGE
    MONTHBLANK_ERR --> DAYBLANK

    MONTHRANGE -->|No - Out of Range| MONTHRANGE_ERR
    MONTHRANGE -->|Yes - Valid Range| MONTHOK
    MONTHRANGE_ERR --> DAYBLANK
    MONTHOK --> DAYBLANK

    DAYBLANK -->|No - Blank| DAYBLANK_ERR
    DAYBLANK -->|Yes - Supplied| DAYNUMERIC
    DAYBLANK_ERR --> DAY31CHECK

    DAYNUMERIC -->|No - Not Numeric| DAYNUMERIC_ERR
    DAYNUMERIC -->|Yes - Numeric| DAYRANGE
    DAYNUMERIC_ERR --> DAY31CHECK

    DAYRANGE -->|No - Out of Range| DAYRANGE_ERR
    DAYRANGE -->|Yes - Valid Range| DAYOK
    DAYRANGE_ERR --> DAY31CHECK
    DAYOK --> DAY31CHECK

    DAY31CHECK -->|Day is 31 but Month\ndoes not allow 31 days| DAY31_ERR
    DAY31CHECK -->|Day and Month\nare Compatible| FEB30CHECK
    DAY31_ERR --> DATEVALID

    FEB30CHECK -->|February with 30 days| FEB30_ERR
    FEB30CHECK -->|Not February or\nDay is not 30| FEB29CHECK
    FEB30_ERR --> DATEVALID

    FEB29CHECK -->|February with 29 days| LEAPCHECK
    FEB29CHECK -->|Not February 29| DATEVALID
    LEAPCHECK -->|Not a Leap Year| LEAP_ERR
    LEAPCHECK -->|Is a Leap Year| DATEVALID
    LEAP_ERR --> DATEVALID

    OPENDATE -.->|After date check| EXPIRYDATE
    EXPIRYDATE -.->|After date check| REISSUEDATE

    DOBVALID --> END

rules.rule_name: Date Field Validation Invocation for Account and Customer Dates
rules.rule_description: The system applies date validation to four specific date fields on the account update screen: Account Open Date, Account Expiry Date, Account Reissue Date, and Customer Date of Birth. Each date is validated in sequence using a common date validation routine. Date of Birth has an additional future-date check applied only after it passes the common validation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Validate Account Open Date, Validate Account Expiry Date, Validate Account Reissue Date, Validate Customer Date of Birth - Extract Year, Month, Day from CCYYMMDD format

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted the account update screen with values entered for Account Open Date, Account Expiry Date, Account Reissue Date, and Customer Date of Birth, and changes have been detected compared to the originally fetched values
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the submitted input fields for date validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must validate Account Open Date first, then Account Expiry Date, then Account Reissue Date, and finally Customer Date of Birth — each using the common CCYYMMDD date validation routine; for Customer Date of Birth only, if the date passes common validation, an additional check is performed to ensure the date is in the past; validation results (pass/fail flags) are stored separately for each date field as Open Date flags, Expiry Date flags, Reissue Date flags, and Date of Birth flags respectively

rules.rule_name: Year Must Be Supplied for Date Fields
rules.rule_description: When validating any date field (Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date, or Date of Birth), the year component is mandatory and must not be blank or empty.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: YEARBLANK: Year Supplied? → No - Blank → Mark Year as Missing, Set Error Message: Year must be supplied

acceptance_criteria.Given: A date field (Account Open Date, Account Expiry Date, Account Reissue Date, or Customer Date of Birth) is being validated and the year portion of the date has been submitted
acceptance_criteria.When: The year value is blank (spaces) or contains no data (low-values)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must mark the year as missing by setting the Year-Blank error flag, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name] : Year must be supplied'; the system then proceeds to validate the month component without further year checks

rules.rule_name: Year Must Be a 4-Digit Numeric Value
rules.rule_description: When a year value has been supplied for any date field, it must be a valid 4-digit numeric value to be accepted.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: YEARNUMERIC: Year is 4-digit Numeric? → No - Not Numeric → Mark Year as Invalid, Set Error Message: Must be 4 digit number

acceptance_criteria.Given: A date field year component has been supplied (is not blank) and is being validated
acceptance_criteria.When: The year value is not numeric (contains non-numeric characters)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must mark the year as invalid by setting the Year-Not-OK error flag, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name] must be 4 digit number'; the system then proceeds to validate the month component without further year checks

rules.rule_name: Year Century Must Be 1900s or 2000s
rules.rule_description: When a year value is numeric, it must belong to either the 20th century (1900–1999) or the 21st century (2000–2099). Years outside these two centuries are not accepted.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: YEARCENTURY: Year is 1900s or 2000s? → No - Invalid Century → Mark Year as Invalid, Set Error Message: Century is not valid

acceptance_criteria.Given: A date field year component has been supplied and confirmed to be numeric
acceptance_criteria.When: The year value does not fall within the 1900s (last century) or the 2000s (current century)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must mark the year as invalid by setting the Year-Not-OK error flag, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name] : Century is not valid'; the system then proceeds to validate the month component; if the year is within the 1900s or 2000s, the year is marked as valid and month validation proceeds

rules.rule_name: Month Must Be Supplied for Date Fields
rules.rule_description: When validating any date field, the month component is mandatory and must not be blank or empty, regardless of whether the year was valid or not.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: MONTHBLANK: Month Supplied? → No - Blank → Mark Month as Missing, Set Error Message: Month must be supplied

acceptance_criteria.Given: A date field (Account Open Date, Account Expiry Date, Account Reissue Date, or Customer Date of Birth) is being validated and the month portion has been submitted
acceptance_criteria.When: The month value is blank (spaces) or contains no data (low-values)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must mark the month as missing by setting the Month-Blank error flag, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name] : Month must be supplied'; the system then proceeds to validate the day component without further month checks

rules.rule_name: Month Must Be a Number Between 1 and 12
rules.rule_description: When a month value has been supplied for any date field, it must represent a valid calendar month — a number between 1 (January) and 12 (December).
rules.sub_graph_node_text: MONTHRANGE: Month is between 1 and 12? → No - Out of Range → Mark Month as Invalid, Set Error Message: Month must be between 1 and 12

acceptance_criteria.Given: A date field month component has been supplied (is not blank) and is being validated
acceptance_criteria.When: The month value is not a valid calendar month number (not between 1 and 12 inclusive, or is not numeric)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must mark the month as invalid by setting the Month-Not-OK error flag, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name]: Month must be a number between 1 and 12'; the system then proceeds to validate the day component; if the month is valid (1–12), the month is marked as valid and day validation proceeds

rules.rule_name: Day Must Be Supplied for Date Fields
rules.rule_description: When validating any date field, the day component is mandatory and must not be blank or empty, regardless of whether the year or month were valid.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: DAYBLANK: Day Supplied? → No - Blank → Mark Day as Missing, Set Error Message: Day must be supplied

acceptance_criteria.Given: A date field (Account Open Date, Account Expiry Date, Account Reissue Date, or Customer Date of Birth) is being validated and the day portion has been submitted
acceptance_criteria.When: The day value is blank (spaces) or contains no data (low-values)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must mark the day as missing by setting the Day-Blank error flag, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name] : Day must be supplied'; the system then proceeds to the month-day cross-validation checks without further day checks

rules.rule_name: Day Must Be a Numeric Value
rules.rule_description: When a day value has been supplied for any date field, it must be a numeric value before range checking can be applied.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: DAYNUMERIC: Day is Numeric? → No - Not Numeric → Mark Day as Invalid, Set Error Message: Day must be between 1 and 31

acceptance_criteria.Given: A date field day component has been supplied (is not blank) and is being validated
acceptance_criteria.When: The day value is not numeric (contains non-numeric characters)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must mark the day as invalid by setting the Day-Not-OK error flag, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name]:day must be a number between 1 and 31'; the system then proceeds to the month-day cross-validation checks without further day range checks

rules.rule_name: Day Must Be Between 1 and 31
rules.rule_description: When a day value is confirmed to be numeric, it must fall within the general calendar day range of 1 to 31 inclusive.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: DAYRANGE: Day is between 1 and 31? → No - Out of Range → Mark Day as Invalid, Set Error Message: Day must be between 1 and 31

acceptance_criteria.Given: A date field day component has been supplied and confirmed to be numeric
acceptance_criteria.When: The numeric day value is less than 1 or greater than 31
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must mark the day as invalid by setting the Day-Not-OK error flag, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name]:day must be a number between 1 and 31'; the system then proceeds to the month-day cross-validation checks; if the day is between 1 and 31 inclusive, the day is marked as valid

rules.rule_name: Day 31 Is Not Valid for Months That Have Fewer Than 31 Days
rules.rule_description: Not all calendar months have 31 days. When a user enters day 31, the system must verify that the specified month actually has 31 days. Months with only 28, 29, or 30 days cannot have a 31st day.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: DAY31CHECK: Month allows 31 days? → Day is 31 but Month does not allow 31 days → Mark Day and Month Invalid, Set Error Message: Cannot have 31 days in this month

acceptance_criteria.Given: A date field has passed individual year, month, and day format checks and is undergoing month-day cross-validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The entered day value is 31 AND the entered month is one that does not allow 31 days (i.e., the month is not January, March, May, July, August, October, or December)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must mark both the day and the month as invalid by setting the Day-Not-OK and Month-Not-OK error flags, set the overall input as invalid, set the error message to '[Date Field Name]:Cannot have 31 days in this month', and stop further cross-validation for this date field

rules.rule_name: February Cannot Have 30 Days
rules.rule_description: February never has 30 days regardless of whether it is a leap year or not. When a user enters February (month 2) with day 30, this is always invalid.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: FEB30CHECK: Is February with 30 days? → February with 30 days → Mark Day and Month Invalid, Set Error Message: Cannot have 30 days in this month

acceptance_criteria.Given: A date field has passed the 31-day month check and is undergoing further month-day cross-validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The entered month is February (month 2) AND the entered day value is 30
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must mark both the day and the month as invalid by setting the Day-Not-OK and Month-Not-OK error flags, set the overall input as invalid, set the error message to '[Date Field Name]:Cannot have 30 days in this month', and stop further cross-validation for this date field

rules.rule_name: February 29 Is Only Valid in a Leap Year
rules.rule_description: February 29 (the leap day) only exists in leap years. A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, except for century years (years ending in 00) which must be divisible by 400. If the year is not a leap year, February 29 is an invalid date.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: FEB29CHECK: Is February with 29 days? → LEAPCHECK: Is it a Leap Year? Year divisible by 4 or 400 for century years → Not a Leap Year → Mark Day, Month, Year Invalid, Set Error Message: Not a leap year - Cannot have 29 days in this month

acceptance_criteria.Given: A date field has passed the February-30 check and is undergoing further month-day cross-validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The entered month is February (month 2) AND the entered day value is 29, and the leap year check is performed: if the year ends in '00' (century year), the year must be divisible by 400; otherwise the year must be divisible by 4; if the year does not satisfy the applicable divisibility rule, it is not a leap year
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the year is NOT a leap year: the system must mark the day, month, and year all as invalid by setting Day-Not-OK, Month-Not-OK, and Year-Not-OK error flags, set the overall input as invalid, set the error message to '[Date Field Name]:Not a leap year.Cannot have 29 days in this month', and stop further cross-validation for this date field; if the year IS a leap year (remainder is zero after division), the date February 29 is accepted as valid

rules.rule_name: Customer Date of Birth Must Not Be a Future Date
rules.rule_description: A customer's date of birth must represent a date that has already occurred. A date of birth that is today's date or any future date is not a valid birth date. This check is applied exclusively to the Date of Birth field after it has passed all standard date format validations.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: DOBFUTURECHECK: Date of Birth Additional Check: Is DOB in the past? → DOB is today or in the future → Mark Day, Month, Year Invalid, Set Error Message: Date of Birth cannot be in the future

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer Date of Birth field has passed all standard date format validations (year, month, day, and calendar cross-checks) and is undergoing the additional birth date check
acceptance_criteria.When: The entered Date of Birth, when converted to an integer date value, is greater than or equal to today's current system date converted to an integer date value (i.e., the date is today or in the future)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must mark the day, month, and year all as invalid by setting Day-Not-OK, Month-Not-OK, and Year-Not-OK error flags, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name]:cannot be in the future'; if the Date of Birth is strictly before today's date, the date of birth is accepted as valid

key_functionalities.title: Date of Birth Age Validation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Date of Birth Age Validation
Triggered only when basic date format
validation has already passed])
    GETTODAY[Get Today's Date
Capture the current system date
as the reference point]
    CONVERTDOB[Convert Date of Birth
to a numeric integer value
for date comparison]
    CONVERTTODAY[Convert Today's Date
to a numeric integer value
for date comparison]
    COMPARE{Is Date of Birth
strictly before
Today's Date?}
    VALID[Date of Birth is Valid
DOB represents a past date
and is accepted]
    INVALID[Date of Birth is Invalid
Mark Day, Month, and Year fields
as all in error]
    ERRMSG[Set Error Message
'Date of Birth cannot be
in the future']
    HIGHLIGHTRED[Highlight DOB Fields in Red
Day, Month, and Year fields
are highlighted red on screen]
    END_VALID([End: DOB Age Validation Passed
Proceed with remaining
field validations])
    END_INVALID([End: DOB Age Validation Failed
User must correct the
Date of Birth])

    START --> GETTODAY
    GETTODAY --> CONVERTDOB
    CONVERTDOB --> CONVERTTODAY
    CONVERTTODAY --> COMPARE
    COMPARE -->|Yes - DOB is in the past
Valid birth date| VALID
    COMPARE -->|No - DOB is today or
in the future| INVALID
    VALID --> END_VALID
    INVALID --> ERRMSG
    ERRMSG --> HIGHLIGHTRED
    HIGHLIGHTRED --> END_INVALID

rules.rule_name: Conditional Trigger of DOB Age Validation Based on Prior Format Validation
rules.rule_description: The Date of Birth age validation (checking whether the date is in the past) is only invoked when the basic date format validation has already passed successfully. If the basic format check failed, the age check is skipped entirely.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Start: Date of Birth Age Validation
Triggered only when basic date format
validation has already passed

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a Date of Birth on the account update screen and the basic date format validation (year, month, day structure, leap year checks) has been performed
acceptance_criteria.When: The basic date format validation result flag (WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-ISVALID) indicates the date format is valid
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system proceeds to invoke the Date of Birth age validation routine (EDIT-DATE-OF-BIRTH) to check whether the date represents a past date, and the resulting date validation flags (WS-EDIT-DATE-FLGS) are stored as the Date of Birth validation outcome (WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-FLGS); if the basic format validation did not pass, the age validation is skipped entirely

rules.rule_name: Capture Current System Date as Reference Point for DOB Validation
rules.rule_description: Before comparing the entered Date of Birth against today's date, the system retrieves the current system date to use as the reference point for determining whether the date of birth is in the past.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Get Today's Date
Capture the current system date
as the reference point

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Date of Birth age validation routine has been triggered because the basic date format validation passed
acceptance_criteria.When: The age validation routine begins execution
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system captures the current system date (WS-CURRENT-DATE-YYYYMMDD) using the system's current date function, which will serve as the reference point for all subsequent date comparison logic

rules.rule_name: Convert Date of Birth to Numeric Integer for Date Comparison
rules.rule_description: The entered Date of Birth (in CCYYMMDD format) is converted to a numeric integer representation so that it can be arithmetically compared against today's date to determine whether it falls before the current date.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Convert Date of Birth
to a numeric integer value
for date comparison

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current system date has been captured and the Date of Birth (WS-EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD-N) has passed basic format validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares for the date comparison
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system computes a numeric integer value (WS-EDIT-DATE-BINARY) from the Date of Birth using the INTEGER-OF-DATE function applied to the date value (WS-EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD-N), producing a single comparable integer that represents the absolute day count of the Date of Birth

rules.rule_name: Convert Today's Date to Numeric Integer for Date Comparison
rules.rule_description: The current system date is converted to a numeric integer representation so that it can be arithmetically compared against the entered Date of Birth to determine whether the Date of Birth falls strictly before today.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Convert Today's Date
to a numeric integer value
for date comparison

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current system date (WS-CURRENT-DATE-YYYYMMDD) has been captured and the Date of Birth integer (WS-EDIT-DATE-BINARY) has been computed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares for the date comparison
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system computes a numeric integer value (WS-CURRENT-DATE-BINARY) from today's date using the INTEGER-OF-DATE function applied to the current date value (WS-CURRENT-DATE-YYYYMMDD-N), producing a single comparable integer that represents the absolute day count of today's date

rules.rule_name: Date of Birth Must Be Strictly Before Today's Date
rules.rule_description: The core age validation rule: the Date of Birth must represent a date that is strictly in the past — it cannot be today's date or any future date. The comparison is performed using the integer representations of both dates.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is Date of Birth
strictly before
Today's Date?

acceptance_criteria.Given: Both the Date of Birth (WS-EDIT-DATE-BINARY) and today's date (WS-CURRENT-DATE-BINARY) have been converted to numeric integer values for comparison
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the two integer date values
acceptance_criteria.Then: If today's date integer (WS-CURRENT-DATE-BINARY) is strictly greater than the Date of Birth integer (WS-EDIT-DATE-BINARY), the Date of Birth is considered valid and the validation passes; if today's date integer is equal to or less than the Date of Birth integer (meaning the DOB is today or in the future), the Date of Birth is considered invalid and the validation fails

rules.rule_name: Date of Birth Accepted as Valid When It Represents a Past Date
rules.rule_description: When the Date of Birth is confirmed to be strictly before today's date, the date is accepted as a valid birth date and no error is raised for the age check. Processing continues to any remaining field validations.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Date of Birth is Valid
DOB represents a past date
and is accepted

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Date of Birth integer value (WS-EDIT-DATE-BINARY) and today's date integer value (WS-CURRENT-DATE-BINARY) have been computed
acceptance_criteria.When: Today's date integer (WS-CURRENT-DATE-BINARY) is strictly greater than the Date of Birth integer (WS-EDIT-DATE-BINARY)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system takes no error action (CONTINUE), the Date of Birth age validation passes, no error flags are set for Day, Month, or Year, no error message is generated, and processing proceeds normally to the end of the Date of Birth validation routine

rules.rule_name: Mark All Date of Birth Component Fields as Invalid When DOB Is Not in the Past
rules.rule_description: When the Date of Birth is today or in the future, all three date component fields (Day, Month, and Year) are simultaneously marked as invalid. This ensures the user is clearly directed to correct the entire date entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Date of Birth is Invalid
Mark Day, Month, and Year fields
as all in error

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Date of Birth integer value (WS-EDIT-DATE-BINARY) has been compared against today's date integer value (WS-CURRENT-DATE-BINARY)
acceptance_criteria.When: Today's date integer (WS-CURRENT-DATE-BINARY) is NOT strictly greater than the Date of Birth integer (WS-EDIT-DATE-BINARY), meaning the Date of Birth is today or in the future
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the overall input error indicator (INPUT-ERROR) to TRUE, sets the Day field error flag (FLG-DAY-NOT-OK) to TRUE, sets the Month field error flag (FLG-MONTH-NOT-OK) to TRUE, and sets the Year field error flag (FLG-YEAR-NOT-OK) to TRUE, marking all three date components as invalid

rules.rule_name: Set Error Message When Date of Birth Is in the Future
rules.rule_description: When the Date of Birth fails the age validation because it is today or in the future, a specific error message is generated to inform the user that the date of birth cannot be a future date. The message is only set if no prior error message has already been recorded.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Error Message
'Date of Birth cannot be
in the future'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Date of Birth has been determined to be invalid because it is today or in the future, and all three date component error flags (Day, Month, Year) have been set to TRUE
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether an error message has already been set (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is TRUE, meaning no prior message exists)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system constructs and stores an error message by concatenating the field name label (from WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME, trimmed of trailing spaces) with the text ':cannot be in the future', and stores this combined message in the error message area (WS-RETURN-MSG); if a prior error message already exists (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is FALSE), the existing message is preserved and no new message is written

rules.rule_name: Highlight Date of Birth Fields in Red on Screen When Validation Fails
rules.rule_description: When any Date of Birth component field (Year, Month, or Day) has a validation error or is blank, that field is highlighted in red on the screen to visually direct the user to the fields requiring correction. Additionally, if a mandatory date component was left blank, an asterisk placeholder is displayed in that field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Highlight DOB Fields in Red
Day, Month, and Year fields
are highlighted red on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account update screen is being prepared for display after a Date of Birth validation failure, and the program is in re-entry mode (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen attributes are being set up (3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS) and any of the following conditions are true: the Year field is invalid (FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-YEAR-NOT-OK) or blank (FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-YEAR-BLANK); the Month field is invalid (FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-MONTH-NOT-OK) or blank (FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-MONTH-BLANK); the Day field is invalid (FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-DAY-NOT-OK) or blank (FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-DAY-BLANK)
acceptance_criteria.Then: For each Date of Birth component field that is in error or blank: the field's color attribute is set to RED (DFHRED) on the screen output map (CACTUPAO); additionally, if the specific component field was blank (FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-YEAR-BLANK, FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-MONTH-BLANK, or FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-DAY-BLANK respectively), an asterisk character '*' is placed in that field's output value (DOBYEARO, DOBMONO, or DOBDAYO) as a visual placeholder indicating the field was left empty

key_functionalities.title: Credit Limit Validation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Credit Limit Validation Start])

    CHECK_SUPPLIED{Is Credit Limit\nSupplied?\nNot blank or empty}

    ERROR_BLANK[Mark Credit Limit as Missing\nSet error message:\n'Credit Limit must be supplied']

    CHECK_NUMERIC{Is Credit Limit\na Valid Signed\nNumeric Value?\neg. 1234.56 or -500.00}

    ERROR_INVALID[Mark Credit Limit as Invalid\nSet error message:\n'Credit Limit is not valid']

    VALID[Credit Limit is Valid\nMark field as successfully validated]

    END_ERROR([Validation Failed\nField highlighted in red on screen])
    END_OK([Validation Passed\nProceed to next field validation])

    START --> CHECK_SUPPLIED
    CHECK_SUPPLIED -->|No - Blank or Empty| ERROR_BLANK
    CHECK_SUPPLIED -->|Yes - Value Entered| CHECK_NUMERIC
    CHECK_NUMERIC -->|No - Not a Valid Signed Number| ERROR_INVALID
    CHECK_NUMERIC -->|Yes - Valid Signed Numeric| VALID
    ERROR_BLANK --> END_ERROR
    ERROR_INVALID --> END_ERROR
    VALID --> END_OK

rules.rule_name: Credit Limit Field Must Be Supplied
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Credit Limit field has been entered by the user and is not left blank or empty before any further validation is performed. This is a mandatory field on the account update screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Credit Limit Supplied? Not blank or empty

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has made changes to account details, and the Credit Limit field (ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-X) is part of the update form
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the form and the Credit Limit field contains only blank spaces or is completely empty (LOW-VALUES or SPACES)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the overall input as invalid (INPUT-ERROR), sets the Credit Limit field status to 'Blank/Missing' (FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-BLANK), records the error message 'Credit Limit must be supplied.' as the first error message (only if no prior error message has been set), the Credit Limit field is highlighted in red on the screen, an asterisk '*' is displayed in the Credit Limit field to indicate it is missing, and the cursor is positioned on the Credit Limit field

rules.rule_name: Credit Limit Must Be a Valid Signed Numeric Value
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Credit Limit value entered by the user is a properly formatted signed numeric value (e.g., 1234.56 or -500.00), allowing for currency-style input including signs and decimal points. This check is only performed after confirming the field is not blank.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Credit Limit a Valid Signed Numeric Value? eg. 1234.56 or -500.00

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, has made changes to account details, and the Credit Limit field (ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-X) has been supplied with a non-blank value
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the entered Credit Limit value passes the signed numeric currency validation (NUMVAL-C test, which accepts values like 1234.56, -500.00, or currency-formatted numbers) and the value fails this check
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the overall input as invalid (INPUT-ERROR), sets the Credit Limit field status to 'Invalid' (FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-NOT-OK), records the error message 'Credit Limit is not valid' as the first error message (only if no prior error message has been set), the Credit Limit field is highlighted in red on the screen, and the cursor is positioned on the Credit Limit field

rules.rule_name: Credit Limit Successfully Validated
rules.rule_description: When the Credit Limit field passes both the mandatory presence check and the signed numeric format check, it is marked as successfully validated, allowing the update process to proceed to the next field validation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Credit Limit is Valid
Mark field as successfully validated

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has entered a value in the Credit Limit field (ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-X)
acceptance_criteria.When: The Credit Limit value is non-blank AND passes the signed numeric currency format validation (NUMVAL-C test returns 0, confirming it is a valid signed numeric value such as 1234.56 or -500.00)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the Credit Limit field status as valid (FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-ISVALID), the validated numeric value is computed and stored internally (ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-N) using NUMVAL-C conversion, no error message is generated for this field, the field result flag (WS-EDIT-CREDIT-LIMIT) is updated to reflect successful validation, and processing continues to the next field validation

rules.rule_name: Credit Limit Error Field Screen Highlighting
rules.rule_description: When the Credit Limit field fails validation (either missing or invalid), the screen display is updated to visually indicate the error to the user by highlighting the field in red and placing the cursor on it, and showing an asterisk if the field was left blank.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Validation Failed
Field highlighted in red on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Credit Limit field has failed validation — either it was not supplied (FLG-CRED-LIMIT-BLANK) or it contained an invalid value (FLG-CRED-LIMIT-NOT-OK), and the program is in re-entry mode (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen attributes for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Credit Limit field (ACRDLIMC) is highlighted in red (DFHRED) on the screen; if the field was blank (FLG-CRED-LIMIT-BLANK), an asterisk '*' is placed in the Credit Limit output field (ACRDLIMO) to indicate the missing value; the cursor is positioned on the Credit Limit field (ACRDLIML set to -1) to direct the user's attention to the error

key_functionalities.title: Cash Credit Limit Validation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Cash Credit Limit Validation])
    CHECK_BLANK{Is Cash Credit\nLimit blank or\nnot supplied?}
    ERROR_BLANK[Mark as Invalid\nError: 'Cash Credit Limit\nmust be supplied']
    CHECK_NUMERIC{Is value a valid\nsigned numeric\nnumber?}
    ERROR_NUMERIC[Mark as Invalid\nError: 'Cash Credit Limit\nis not valid']
    MARK_VALID[Mark Cash Credit\nLimit as Valid]
    END_INVALID([End: Validation Failed\nField highlighted red on screen])
    END_VALID([End: Validation Passed\nProceed to next field validation])

    START --> CHECK_BLANK
    CHECK_BLANK -->|Yes - Missing| ERROR_BLANK
    CHECK_BLANK -->|No - Value Supplied| CHECK_NUMERIC
    CHECK_NUMERIC -->|No - Not Valid Signed Numeric| ERROR_NUMERIC
    CHECK_NUMERIC -->|Yes - Valid Signed Numeric| MARK_VALID
    ERROR_BLANK --> END_INVALID
    ERROR_NUMERIC --> END_INVALID
    MARK_VALID --> END_VALID

rules.rule_name: Cash Credit Limit - Mandatory Field Presence Check
rules.rule_description: Ensures that the Cash Credit Limit field is not left empty when a user submits account update details. The field is mandatory and must contain a value before any further validation is performed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Cash Credit Limit blank or not supplied?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has fetched account details, and changes have been detected between the original and newly entered values
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the screen and the Cash Credit Limit field is blank, empty, or contains only spaces or low-values (i.e., no value has been entered)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Cash Credit Limit field is marked as invalid with a blank indicator, the overall input is flagged as containing an error, the error message 'Cash Credit Limit must be supplied.' is set (only if no prior error message has already been recorded), and validation for this field stops immediately without proceeding to the numeric format check

rules.rule_name: Cash Credit Limit - Signed Numeric Format Validation
rules.rule_description: Ensures that the Cash Credit Limit value entered by the user is a properly formatted signed numeric value (e.g., may include currency signs or positive/negative indicators). This check only runs when a value has been supplied.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is value a valid signed numeric number?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, has fetched account details, changes have been detected, and the Cash Credit Limit field has been supplied with a non-blank value
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the supplied Cash Credit Limit value is a valid signed numeric number (using currency-aware numeric validation that accepts signs and decimal points)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the value is NOT a valid signed numeric number, the Cash Credit Limit field is marked as invalid, the overall input is flagged as containing an error, and the error message 'Cash Credit Limit is not valid' is set (only if no prior error message has already been recorded), and validation for this field stops; if the value IS a valid signed numeric number, processing continues to mark the field as valid

rules.rule_name: Cash Credit Limit - Mark Field as Successfully Validated
rules.rule_description: Records the successful outcome of Cash Credit Limit validation so that downstream processing (such as update confirmation and screen display) can correctly identify this field as having passed all validation checks.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Cash Credit Limit as Valid

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, has fetched account details, changes have been detected, the Cash Credit Limit field has been supplied with a non-blank value, and the value has passed the signed numeric format check
acceptance_criteria.When: All validation checks for the Cash Credit Limit field have been completed without any errors
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Cash Credit Limit field validation flag is set to valid, indicating the field has passed all checks, and processing proceeds to the next field validation (Reissue Date)

key_functionalities.title: Current Balance Validation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Current Balance Validation]) --> B[Receive Current Balance\nfrom Screen Input]
    B --> C{Is Current Balance\nBlank or Missing?}
    C -->|Yes - Not Supplied| D[Mark Current Balance\nas Blank Error\nSet Input Error Flag]
    D --> E[Display Error Message:\n'Current Balance must be supplied']
    E --> Z
    C -->|No - Value Entered| F{Is Current Balance\na Valid Signed\nNumeric Value?}
    F -->|No - Invalid Format| G[Mark Current Balance\nas Invalid Error\nSet Input Error Flag]
    G --> H[Display Error Message:\n'Current Balance is not valid']
    H --> Z
    F -->|Yes - Valid Signed Numeric| I[Store Numeric Value\nof Current Balance\nfor Further Processing]

    Z([End: Current Balance Validation Complete])

rules.rule_name: Current Balance Input Capture and Blank Handling
rules.rule_description: When the user enters a value in the Current Balance field on the account update screen, the system captures the input. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank (spaces), the Current Balance is treated as not supplied and cleared internally.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Receive Current Balance from Screen Input

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account update screen is displayed and the user has interacted with the Current Balance field
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen input is received and the Current Balance field contains either an asterisk '*' or spaces
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Current Balance value is cleared (set to empty/low-values) internally, indicating no value was supplied by the user; otherwise, the entered value is captured as-is for further validation

rules.rule_name: Current Balance Mandatory Field Check
rules.rule_description: The Current Balance field is mandatory on the account update screen. If the user does not supply a value, the system must flag the field as blank, set an input error, and display an appropriate error message. Only the first error message encountered during the session is displayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Current Balance Blank or Missing?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account update screen has been submitted with account details already fetched, and changes have been detected between the original and newly entered values
acceptance_criteria.When: The Current Balance field is empty, blank (spaces), or was not supplied by the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the Current Balance field with a 'blank' error status, sets the overall input error flag to true, and displays the error message 'Current Balance must be supplied.' — provided no prior error message has already been set in the session

rules.rule_name: Current Balance Signed Numeric Format Validation
rules.rule_description: When a value is supplied for Current Balance, it must be a valid signed numeric value (i.e., it may include a sign indicator such as '+' or '-' and decimal notation). Values that cannot be interpreted as a signed numeric amount are rejected.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Current Balance a Valid Signed Numeric Value?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Current Balance field has been supplied with a non-blank value on the account update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The entered Current Balance value fails the signed numeric format check (i.e., it cannot be interpreted as a valid signed currency/numeric amount)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the Current Balance field with an 'invalid' error status, sets the overall input error flag to true, and displays the error message 'Current Balance is not valid' — provided no prior error message has already been set in the session

rules.rule_name: Current Balance Numeric Value Storage on Successful Validation
rules.rule_description: When the Current Balance passes the signed numeric format check, the system converts the text representation of the balance into its internal numeric form for use in subsequent processing such as change detection, update record preparation, and screen display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store Numeric Value of Current Balance for Further Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Current Balance field has been supplied with a non-blank value on the account update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The entered Current Balance value passes the signed numeric format validation (i.e., it is a valid signed numeric amount)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system converts the text value of Current Balance into its numeric equivalent and stores it as the new Current Balance numeric value for further processing; the Current Balance field is marked as valid

rules.rule_name: Current Balance Validation Orchestration
rules.rule_description: The Current Balance validation is invoked as part of the full field-by-field edit process, which occurs only when account details have already been fetched and actual changes have been detected between the original and newly entered values. The validation result flag is stored for use in screen attribute setup and error highlighting.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Current Balance as Valid

acceptance_criteria.Given: Account details have been fetched and displayed on screen, and the user has submitted changes where at least one field differs from the originally fetched values
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs the full input validation sequence for all editable fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Current Balance validation routine is invoked with the entered Current Balance value; upon completion, the resulting validation status flag (valid, blank, or invalid) is stored against the Current Balance field and used to control error highlighting and cursor positioning on the screen

key_functionalities.title: Current Cycle Credit Validation
