Set error: 'Primary Card Holder
must be supplied']
    C -->|No - Value Present| E{Does the value
contain only
'Y' or 'N'?}
    E -->|Yes - Valid Value| F[Mark Primary Card
Holder Indicator
as Valid]
    E -->|No - Invalid Value| G[Mark field as invalid
Set error: 'Primary Card Holder
must be Y or N']
    D --> H([End: Validation
Failed - Field Blank])
    G --> I([End: Validation
Failed - Invalid Value])
    F --> J([End: Validation
Passed])

rules.rule_name: Primary Card Holder Indicator - Mandatory Field Check
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Primary Card Holder Indicator field has been supplied by the user before any value check is performed. This is a mandatory field and cannot be left blank, empty, or zero.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is the value blank or not supplied?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer details on the Account Update screen, and the Primary Card Holder Indicator field is available for input
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the screen without entering a value in the Primary Card Holder Indicator field, leaving it blank, empty (spaces), or as zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the Primary Card Holder Indicator field as blank/missing, sets an overall input error condition on the screen, and displays the error message 'Primary Card Holder must be supplied.' The validation stops immediately for this field and no further value checks are performed

rules.rule_name: Primary Card Holder Indicator - Allowed Value Check
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Primary Card Holder Indicator field contains only an accepted value of 'Y' (Yes) or 'N' (No). Any other non-blank value is considered invalid.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Does the value contain only 'Y' or 'N'?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer details on the Account Update screen, and the Primary Card Holder Indicator field has been supplied with a non-blank value
acceptance_criteria.When: The user enters a value in the Primary Card Holder Indicator field that is neither 'Y' nor 'N'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the Primary Card Holder Indicator field as invalid, sets an overall input error condition on the screen, and displays the error message 'Primary Card Holder must be Y or N.' The validation fails for this field

rules.rule_name: Primary Card Holder Indicator - Successful Validation
rules.rule_description: Confirms that the Primary Card Holder Indicator field has passed all validation checks — it was supplied and contains a valid value of 'Y' or 'N'. The field is marked as valid and no error is raised.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Primary Card Holder Indicator as Valid

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer details on the Account Update screen, and the Primary Card Holder Indicator field has been supplied with a value
acceptance_criteria.When: The entered value is either 'Y' or 'N'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the Primary Card Holder Indicator field as valid, no error condition is set for this field, and no error message is generated. Processing continues to the next validation step

rules.rule_name: Primary Card Holder Indicator - Retrieve and Prepare for Validation
rules.rule_description: Defines the process of retrieving the Primary Card Holder Indicator value entered by the user from the screen input and preparing it for validation. The field label 'Primary Card Holder' is set as the context for any error messages generated during validation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Primary Card Holder Indicator value entered by user

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Account Update screen with changes to account and customer details, and the system has determined that changes have been made and full field validation is required
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins validation of the Primary Card Holder Indicator field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the Primary Card Holder Indicator value entered by the user from the screen input, sets the field context name to 'Primary Card Holder' for use in any error messages, and invokes the Yes/No validation routine to check the value. The validated result is stored back as the Primary Card Holder field status

key_functionalities.title: Determine Next Action After Input Processing
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Determine Next Action\nAfter Input Processing])

    EVALSTATE{What is the\nCurrent Screen State?}

    %% Branch 1: Details Not Fetched or PF12 Cancel
    NOTFETCHED[Details Not Yet Fetched\nor PF12 Cancel Requested]
    ACCTVALID{Is Account Number\nValid?}
    FETCHDATA[Fetch Account, Customer\nand Card Data from Database]
    CUSTFOUND{Was Customer\nData Found?}
    SHOWDETAILS_1[Set State: Show Account\nand Customer Details on Screen]
    STAYBLANK[Stay on Search Screen\nNo Data to Display]

    %% Branch 2: Details Already Shown
    DETAILSSHOWN[Details Currently\nDisplayed on Screen]
    INPUTERROR{Are There Input\nValidation Errors?}
    NOCHANGES{Were Any Changes\nDetected?}
    SETCHANGESCONFIRMED[Set State: Changes Validated\nPrompt User for Confirmation]
    STAYDETAILS[Stay on Details Screen\nNo Action Needed]

    %% Branch 3: Changes Have Validation Errors
    CHANGESBAD[Changes Have\nValidation Errors]
    REDISPLAYERRORS[Re-display Screen\nwith Validation Error Messages]

    %% Branch 4: Changes Validated, Awaiting PF05
    CHANGESOK_NOPF05[Changes Validated\nPF05 Not Yet Pressed]
    WAITCONFIRM[Stay on Confirmation Prompt\nAwaiting User to Press PF05]

    %% Branch 5: Changes Validated AND PF05 Pressed
    CHANGESOK_PF05[Changes Validated\nand PF05 Save Pressed]
    SAVEPROCESS[Attempt to Save\nAccount and Customer Changes]
    SAVERESULT{What Was the\nSave Outcome?}
    LOCKERROR[Set State: Lock Error\nCould Not Lock Record for Update]
    UPDATEFAILED[Set State: Update Failed\nChanges Could Not Be Saved]
    DATACHANGED[Set State: Show Details\nRecord Was Changed by Another User\nRefresh with Latest Data]
    SAVESUCCESS[Set State: Update Successful\nChanges Saved Successfully]

    %% Branch 6: Changes Already Done
    CHANGESDONE[Previous Update\nCompleted Successfully]
    SHOWDETAILS_2[Set State: Show Updated\nAccount and Customer Details]
    CLEARCONTEXT{Was Program Called\nfrom Another Transaction?}
    CLEARIDS[Clear Account ID, Card Number\nand Account Status from Context]
    KEEPCONTEXT[Keep Existing\nTransaction Context]

    START --> EVALSTATE

    EVALSTATE -->|Details Not Fetched\nor PF12 Cancel| NOTFETCHED
    EVALSTATE -->|Details Shown on Screen| DETAILSSHOWN
    EVALSTATE -->|Changes Have Errors| CHANGESBAD
    EVALSTATE -->|Changes Validated,\nPF05 Not Pressed| CHANGESOK_NOPF05
    EVALSTATE -->|Changes Validated\nand PF05 Pressed| CHANGESOK_PF05
    EVALSTATE -->|Previous Update Done| CHANGESDONE

    NOTFETCHED --> ACCTVALID
    ACCTVALID -->|Invalid Account| STAYBLANK
    ACCTVALID -->|Valid Account| FETCHDATA
    FETCHDATA --> CUSTFOUND
    CUSTFOUND -->|Yes| SHOWDETAILS_1
    CUSTFOUND -->|No| STAYBLANK

    DETAILSSHOWN --> INPUTERROR
    INPUTERROR -->|Yes - Errors Present| STAYDETAILS
    INPUTERROR -->|No Errors| NOCHANGES
    NOCHANGES -->|No Changes Made| STAYDETAILS
    NOCHANGES -->|Changes Detected| SETCHANGESCONFIRMED

    CHANGESBAD --> REDISPLAYERRORS

    CHANGESOK_NOPF05 --> WAITCONFIRM

    CHANGESOK_PF05 --> SAVEPROCESS
    SAVEPROCESS --> SAVERESULT
    SAVERESULT -->|Could Not Lock\nAccount Record| LOCKERROR
    SAVERESULT -->|Locked But\nSave Failed| UPDATEFAILED
    SAVERESULT -->|Record Changed\nby Another User| DATACHANGED
    SAVERESULT -->|Save Completed\nSuccessfully| SAVESUCCESS

    CHANGESDONE --> SHOWDETAILS_2
    SHOWDETAILS_2 --> CLEARCONTEXT
    CLEARCONTEXT -->|No Prior Transaction| CLEARIDS
    CLEARCONTEXT -->|Has Prior Transaction| KEEPCONTEXT

    STAYBLANK --> END([End: Proceed to\nDisplay Screen])
    SHOWDETAILS_1 --> END
    STAYDETAILS --> END
    SETCHANGESCONFIRMED --> END
    REDISPLAYERRORS --> END
    WAITCONFIRM --> END
    LOCKERROR --> END
    UPDATEFAILED --> END
    DATACHANGED --> END
    SAVESUCCESS --> END
    CLEARIDS --> END
    KEEPCONTEXT --> END

rules.rule_name: Determine Next Action Based on Current Screen State
rules.rule_description: The system evaluates the current screen state after input processing to route the transaction to the appropriate next action: fetch data, display details, show errors, await confirmation, save changes, or reset after completion.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Determine Next Action After Input Processing - Based on the current state (details not fetched, details shown, changes validated, changes confirmed, etc.) decide whether to fetch data, show validation errors, prompt for confirmation, or save changes

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted input on the Account Update screen and input processing has completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the current screen state flag
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system routes to one of the following actions based on state: (1) Details-Not-Fetched or PF12 → attempt account data fetch; (2) Show-Details → check for input errors or changes; (3) Changes-Not-OK → re-display with errors; (4) Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed without PF5 → stay on confirmation prompt; (5) Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed with PF5 → attempt save; (6) Changes-Okayed-And-Done → transition to show updated details; (7) Any unexpected state → trigger abnormal termination with code '0001' and message 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO'

rules.rule_name: Validate Account Number Before Fetching Data
rules.rule_description: Before attempting to retrieve account data, the system validates that the entered account number meets all required criteria: it must be present, numeric, 11 digits, and non-zero.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Account Number Valid?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Details Not Fetched' and the user has entered an account number on the search screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system validates the account number field
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the account number is blank or low-values, the system sets an input error, flags the account filter as blank, prompts the user to enter an account number, clears the account ID to zeros, and stays on the search screen; If the account number is supplied but is not numeric or equals zero, the system sets an input error and displays the message 'Account Number if supplied must be a 11 digit Non-Zero Number', clears the account ID to zeros, and stays on the search screen; If the account number is a valid 11-digit non-zero numeric value, the system marks the account filter as valid and proceeds to fetch account data

rules.rule_name: Fetch Account, Customer and Card Cross-Reference Data
rules.rule_description: When a valid account number is provided, the system performs a three-step sequential lookup: first the Card Cross-Reference file to get the Customer ID and Card Number, then the Account Master file for account details, and finally the Customer Master file for customer details.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Fetch Account, Customer and Card Data from Database

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account number has been validated as a valid 11-digit non-zero numeric value
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates the account data retrieval process
acceptance_criteria.Then: Step 1 - The system looks up the Card Cross-Reference file using the account number: if found, the Customer ID and Card Number are retrieved and stored; if not found, an input error is set with message 'Account: [account number] not found in Cross ref file' and the fetch process stops; Step 2 - The system looks up the Account Master file using the account number: if found, account details are loaded and the account-found flag is set; if not found, an input error is set with message 'Account: [account number] not found in Acct Master file' and the fetch process stops; Step 3 - The system looks up the Customer Master file using the Customer ID retrieved in Step 1: if found, customer details are loaded and the customer-found flag is set; if not found, an input error is set with message 'CustId: [customer ID] not found in customer master' and the fetch process stops

rules.rule_name: Store Fetched Account and Customer Data as Original Values
rules.rule_description: After all three data sources are successfully retrieved, the system stores all fetched values as the original 'old' baseline data. This baseline is used later for change detection and concurrent modification checking.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Fetch Account, Customer and Card Data from Database

acceptance_criteria.Given: All three lookups (Card Cross-Reference, Account Master, Customer Master) have completed successfully
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the retrieved data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system stores the following as original 'old' values: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date (year/month/day), Expiry Date (year/month/day), Reissue Date (year/month/day), Group ID, Customer ID, SSN, Date of Birth (year/month/day), FICO Credit Score, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City (Address Line 3), State Code, Country Code, Zip Code, Phone Number 1, Phone Number 2, Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, and Primary Card Holder Indicator; Additionally, the system stores Account ID, Customer ID, Customer full name, Account Status, and Card Number in the shared communication area

rules.rule_name: Set Screen State to Show Account and Customer Details After Successful Fetch
rules.rule_description: After all three data lookups succeed and customer data is confirmed found, the system transitions the screen state to display the full account and customer details for the user to review and edit.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was Customer Data Found? → Set State: Show Account and Customer Details on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully retrieved data from the Card Cross-Reference file, Account Master file, and Customer Master file
acceptance_criteria.When: The customer data is confirmed as found in the Customer Master
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the screen state to 'Show Details' (ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS), which causes the screen to display all retrieved account and customer information in editable fields, and the user is prompted to make changes

rules.rule_name: Stay on Search Screen When Account or Customer Data Is Not Found
rules.rule_description: If any step in the data fetch process fails (account not in cross-reference, account not in master, or customer not found), the system remains on the search screen and displays the appropriate error message without loading any details.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was Customer Data Found? → Stay on Search Screen No Data to Display

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system attempted to fetch account and customer data using the entered account number
acceptance_criteria.When: Any one of the three lookups (Card Cross-Reference, Account Master, or Customer Master) fails to find the record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag, displays the relevant error message identifying which file and which ID was not found, does not load any account or customer details onto the screen, and remains on the search screen with the account number field available for re-entry

rules.rule_name: Check for Input Validation Errors When Details Are Displayed
rules.rule_description: When account details are currently displayed and the user submits changes, the system first checks whether any input validation errors were detected during the edit phase before deciding the next action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Details Currently Displayed on Screen → Are There Input Validation Errors?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Show Details' (account and customer data is currently displayed on screen)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the form and input validation has been performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: If input errors are present, the system takes no further action (stays on the details screen and re-displays with error highlights); If no input errors are present, the system proceeds to check whether any field values were actually changed by the user

rules.rule_name: Detect Whether User Made Any Changes to Displayed Data
rules.rule_description: After confirming no validation errors exist, the system compares every field entered by the user against the originally fetched values to determine if any actual changes were made. The comparison is case-insensitive for text fields.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Were Any Changes Detected?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Show Details', no input validation errors were found, and the user has submitted the form
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the newly entered values against the originally fetched 'old' values for all fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system compares the following account fields (exact match): Account ID, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit; and the following account fields (case-insensitive): Active Status, Group ID; and the following customer fields (case-insensitive, trimmed): Customer ID, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City, State Code, Country Code, Government Issued ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator; and the following customer fields (exact match): Phone Number 1A/1B/1C, Phone Number 2A/2B/2C, SSN, Date of Birth, EFT Account ID, FICO Score; If ALL fields match (no changes), the system stays on the details screen with no action; If ANY field differs, the system flags that a change has occurred and proceeds to set the confirmation state

rules.rule_name: Set State to Prompt User for Confirmation of Validated Changes
rules.rule_description: When changes are detected and all validations pass, the system transitions to a confirmation state where the user must explicitly press PF5 to save the changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set State: Changes Validated Prompt User for Confirmation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Show Details', no input validation errors were found, and at least one field value has been changed by the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines that changes are present and valid
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the screen state to 'Changes OK - Not Confirmed' (ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED), displays the updated values on screen, highlights the PF5 and PF12 function keys, and displays a confirmation prompt message instructing the user to press PF5 to save or PF12 to re-fetch

rules.rule_name: Stay on Details Screen When No Changes Are Detected or Errors Exist
rules.rule_description: When the user submits the details screen but either no changes were made or validation errors exist, the system remains on the details screen without advancing to the confirmation step.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Stay on Details Screen No Action Needed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Show Details' and the user has submitted the form
acceptance_criteria.When: Either input validation errors are present OR no changes are detected between the entered values and the originally fetched values
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears the non-key flags, stays on the details screen, re-displays the original fetched values, and takes no further processing action; the screen state remains as 'Show Details'

rules.rule_name: Re-display Screen with Validation Error Messages
rules.rule_description: When the screen state indicates that changes have been submitted but contain validation errors, the system re-displays the screen with the entered (invalid) values and highlights the fields that failed validation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Changes Have Validation Errors → Re-display Screen with Validation Error Messages

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Changes Not OK' (ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK), indicating that the user submitted changes that failed one or more validation rules
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the current state to determine the display action
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system continues processing without resetting state, re-displays the screen showing the user's entered values (not the original values), highlights all fields with errors in red, displays an asterisk '*' in mandatory fields that were left blank, positions the cursor on the first field in error, and displays the first validation error message in the error message area

rules.rule_name: Remain on Confirmation Prompt When PF5 Has Not Been Pressed
rules.rule_description: When changes have been validated and the screen is in the confirmation-pending state but the user has not pressed PF5, the system simply re-displays the confirmation prompt without taking any save action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Changes Validated PF05 Not Yet Pressed → Stay on Confirmation Prompt Awaiting User to Press PF05

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Changes OK - Not Confirmed' (ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the screen without pressing PF5 (e.g., presses ENTER)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system takes no save action, continues to display the validated changes on screen, keeps the PF5 and PF12 function keys highlighted, and re-displays the confirmation prompt message instructing the user to press PF5 to confirm the save

rules.rule_name: Attempt to Save Account and Customer Changes When PF5 Is Pressed
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF5 to confirm validated changes, the system initiates the save process by locking both the Account and Customer records, verifying no concurrent modifications occurred, and writing the updated data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Changes Validated and PF05 Save Pressed → Attempt to Save Account and Customer Changes

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Changes OK - Not Confirmed' and the user has pressed PF5
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates the write processing routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system attempts to lock the Account Master record for update using the account number; if the account lock succeeds, the system then attempts to lock the Customer Master record for update using the customer ID; if both locks succeed, the system performs a concurrent change check before writing; the outcome of the save attempt determines the next screen state

rules.rule_name: Set Lock Error State When Account or Customer Record Cannot Be Locked
rules.rule_description: If the system cannot obtain an exclusive lock on either the Account Master or Customer Master record during the save attempt, the update is aborted and the screen transitions to a lock error state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set State: Lock Error Could Not Lock Record for Update

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is attempting to save changes and has initiated the record locking process
acceptance_criteria.When: The attempt to lock the Account Master record for update fails OR the attempt to lock the Customer Master record for update fails
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag, sets the state to 'Changes Okayed - Lock Error' (ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR), aborts the save process, and displays a failure message on screen informing the user that the record could not be locked for update

rules.rule_name: Set Update Failed State When Record Write Fails After Locking
rules.rule_description: If both records are successfully locked but the actual write operation fails for either the Account or Customer record, the system sets a failure state. If the Customer write fails, the Account write is also rolled back.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set State: Update Failed Changes Could Not Be Saved

acceptance_criteria.Given: Both the Account Master and Customer Master records have been successfully locked for update and the concurrent change check has passed
acceptance_criteria.When: The write (rewrite) operation to the Account Master file fails OR the write (rewrite) operation to the Customer Master file fails
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Account Master write fails: the system sets the state to 'Locked But Update Failed' (ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED) and stops processing; If the Customer Master write fails: the system sets the state to 'Locked But Update Failed', issues a transaction rollback to undo the Account Master write that already succeeded, and stops processing; In both cases, a failure message is displayed to the user

rules.rule_name: Detect Concurrent Record Modification Before Saving
rules.rule_description: Before writing updates, the system compares the currently locked database values against the values that were originally fetched and displayed to the user. If any field has been changed by another user in the interim, the save is aborted and the screen is refreshed with the latest data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set State: Show Details Record Was Changed by Another User Refresh with Latest Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: Both the Account Master and Customer Master records have been successfully locked for update
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the current database values against the originally fetched 'old' values for all account and customer fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system compares the following account fields (exact match): Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date year/month/day, Expiry Date year/month/day, Reissue Date year/month/day; and account Group ID (case-insensitive); and the following customer fields (case-insensitive): First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City, State Code, Country Code, Government Issued ID; and the following customer fields (exact match): Zip Code, Phone Number 1, Phone Number 2, SSN, Date of Birth year/month/day, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator, FICO Credit Score; If ALL fields match the original values, the save proceeds; If ANY field differs from the original values, the system sets the state to 'Data Was Changed Before Update' (DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE), aborts the save, transitions the screen to 'Show Details' state, and re-fetches and displays the latest data so the user can review the changes made by the other user

rules.rule_name: Write Updated Account and Customer Data to Master Files
rules.rule_description: After all locks are obtained and no concurrent modifications are detected, the system builds and writes the updated Account and Customer records to their respective master files.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt to Save Account and Customer Changes

acceptance_criteria.Given: Both records are locked, the concurrent change check has passed, and the system is ready to write
acceptance_criteria.When: The system builds the update records and performs the write operations
acceptance_criteria.Then: For the Account Master, the system writes: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD), Expiry Date (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD), Reissue Date (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD), and Group ID; For the Customer Master, the system writes: Customer ID, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City (Address Line 3), State Code, Country Code, Zip Code, Phone Number 1 (formatted as (AAA)PPP-LLLL), Phone Number 2 (formatted as (AAA)PPP-LLLL), SSN, Government Issued ID, Date of Birth (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD), EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator, and FICO Credit Score

rules.rule_name: Set Successful Update State and Transition to Show Updated Details
rules.rule_description: When both the Account and Customer records are successfully written, the system sets the success state and transitions to display the updated account and customer details.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set State: Update Successful Changes Saved Successfully

acceptance_criteria.Given: Both the Account Master and Customer Master records have been successfully written with the updated values
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the outcome of the save process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the screen state to 'Changes Okayed and Done' (ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE) and displays a success confirmation message to the user; on the next processing cycle, the state transitions to 'Show Details' to display the newly saved account and customer information

rules.rule_name: Transition to Show Updated Details After Successful Save
rules.rule_description: After a successful update has been completed and acknowledged, the system transitions the screen state to display the updated account and customer details for the user to review.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Previous Update Completed Successfully → Set State: Show Updated Account and Customer Details

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Changes Okayed and Done' (ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE), indicating a previous update completed successfully
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the current state in the next interaction cycle
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the screen state to 'Show Details' (ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS) so that the updated account and customer information is displayed on screen for the user to review

rules.rule_name: Clear Account and Card Context When No Prior Transaction Exists After Successful Update
rules.rule_description: After a successful update, if the program was not called from another transaction (i.e., it was accessed directly), the system clears the account ID, card number, and account status from the shared context to prevent stale data from persisting.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was Program Called from Another Transaction? → Clear Account ID, Card Number and Account Status from Context

acceptance_criteria.Given: The previous update completed successfully and the screen state is transitioning to 'Show Details'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the program was called from another transaction by examining the calling transaction ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the calling transaction ID is blank or low-values (no prior transaction), the system clears the Account ID to zeros, clears the Card Number to zeros, and clears the Account Status to low-values in the shared communication area; If the calling transaction ID is populated (program was called from another transaction), the system retains the existing Account ID, Card Number, and Account Status values in the shared communication area

key_functionalities.description: Determine Next Action After Input Processing

key_functionalities.title: Cancel Changes and Refresh Data
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD

rules.rule_name: PF12 Key Validity Check - Cancel Changes Only Allowed When Account Details Are Displayed
rules.rule_description: PF12 is only a valid action when account details have already been fetched and are currently displayed on screen. If no account details have been fetched yet, PF12 is ignored and treated as the ENTER key.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Are Account Details Currently Displayed on Screen?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF12 and account details have NOT yet been fetched (screen is in initial search state)
acceptance_criteria.Then: PF12 is treated as invalid and the key press is converted to ENTER key action; no cancel or re-read operation is performed

rules.rule_name: PF12 Triggers Account Data Refresh When Details Are On Screen
rules.rule_description: When PF12 is pressed and account details are currently displayed on screen (regardless of whether changes have been made), the system initiates a full re-read of account and customer data from the database to restore original values.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Yes - Changes in Progress

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and account details have been fetched and are currently displayed (state is not ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF12
acceptance_criteria.Then: PF12 is recognized as a valid action and the system proceeds to re-read all account and customer data from the database using the current Account ID

rules.rule_name: Re-Read Card Cross-Reference File to Retrieve Customer ID and Card Number
rules.rule_description: As the first step of the data refresh triggered by PF12, the system looks up the Card Cross-Reference file using the Account ID to retrieve the associated Customer ID and Card Number.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Re-Read Card Cross-Reference File Using Account ID to Retrieve Customer ID and Card Number

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has pressed PF12 on the Account Update screen and the Account ID is available
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates the data refresh process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads the Card Cross-Reference file using the Account ID as the search key; if found, the associated Customer ID and Card Number are retrieved and stored for use in subsequent lookups

rules.rule_name: Account Not Found in Card Cross-Reference - Show Error and Abort Refresh
rules.rule_description: If the Account ID cannot be found in the Card Cross-Reference file during the PF12 data refresh, the operation is aborted and an error message is displayed to the user identifying the account that was not found.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Account Found in Cross-Reference? - Not Found Show Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has pressed PF12 and the system is attempting to re-read the Card Cross-Reference file using the Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag, marks the account filter as invalid, and displays the error message: 'Account: [Account ID] not found in Cross ref file. Resp: [response code] Reas: [reason code]'; the data refresh is aborted and no further file reads are performed

rules.rule_name: Re-Read Account Master File to Retrieve Full Account Details
rules.rule_description: After successfully retrieving the Customer ID from the Cross-Reference file, the system reads the Account Master file using the Account ID to retrieve the full account details including balances, credit limits, dates, and account status.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Re-Read Account Master File Using Account ID to Retrieve Full Account Details: Balances, Limits, Dates, Status

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID was successfully found in the Card Cross-Reference file and the Customer ID has been retrieved
acceptance_criteria.When: The system proceeds to the second step of the data refresh
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads the Account Master file using the Account ID as the search key; if found, the full account record is retrieved including: Account Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date, and Group ID

rules.rule_name: Account Not Found in Account Master File - Show Error and Abort Refresh
rules.rule_description: If the Account ID cannot be found in the Account Master file during the PF12 data refresh, the operation is aborted and an error message is displayed to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Account Found in Master File? - Not Found Show Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID was found in the Cross-Reference file and the system is attempting to read the Account Master file
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID is not found in the Account Master file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag, marks the account filter as invalid, and displays the error message: 'Account: [Account ID] not found in Acct Master file. Resp: [response code] Reas: [reason code]'; the data refresh is aborted and the Customer Master file is not read

rules.rule_name: Re-Read Customer Master File to Retrieve Full Customer Details
rules.rule_description: After successfully retrieving account details, the system reads the Customer Master file using the Customer ID (obtained from the Cross-Reference lookup) to retrieve the full customer profile including name, address, and contact information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Re-Read Customer Master File Using Customer ID to Retrieve Full Customer Details: Name, Address, Contact Info

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID was found in both the Cross-Reference file and the Account Master file, and the Customer ID has been retrieved
acceptance_criteria.When: The system proceeds to the third step of the data refresh
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads the Customer Master file using the Customer ID as the search key; if found, the full customer record is retrieved including: Customer ID, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Lines 1-3, State Code, Country Code, Zip Code, Phone Numbers 1 and 2, SSN, Government Issued ID, Date of Birth, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator, and FICO Credit Score

rules.rule_name: Customer Not Found in Customer Master File - Show Error and Abort Refresh
rules.rule_description: If the Customer ID cannot be found in the Customer Master file during the PF12 data refresh, the operation is aborted and an error message is displayed to the user identifying the customer that was not found.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Customer Found in Master File? - Not Found Show Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID was found in both the Cross-Reference and Account Master files, and the system is attempting to read the Customer Master file using the Customer ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The Customer ID is not found in the Customer Master file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag, marks the customer filter as invalid, and displays the error message: 'CustId: [Customer ID] not found in customer master. Resp: [response code] REAS: [reason code]'; the data refresh is aborted and no data is restored to the screen

rules.rule_name: Restore Original Account and Customer Values After Successful Re-Read
rules.rule_description: After all three file reads succeed, the freshly retrieved account and customer data is stored as the authoritative 'original' values, overwriting any changes the user had entered on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Restore Original Values Overwrite Any User Changes with Freshly Retrieved Account and Customer Data from Database

acceptance_criteria.Given: All three file reads (Cross-Reference, Account Master, Customer Master) have completed successfully
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the freshly retrieved data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system stores the following as the new baseline 'old' values: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date (Year/Month/Day), Expiry Date (Year/Month/Day), Reissue Date (Year/Month/Day), Group ID, Customer ID, SSN, Date of Birth (Year/Month/Day), FICO Credit Score, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City (Address Line 3), State Code, Country Code, Zip Code, Phone Number 1, Phone Number 2, Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, and Primary Card Holder Indicator; additionally, the Account ID, Customer ID, Customer Name, Account Status, and Card Number are stored in the shared session area

rules.rule_name: Discard All Pending Changes and Reset to Show Details Mode
rules.rule_description: After the fresh data has been retrieved and stored, all pending user changes are discarded and the screen state is reset to 'Show Details' mode, ready for the user to make new changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Discard All Pending Changes Reset Change Detection State Back to Show Details Mode

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully re-read and stored fresh account and customer data from the database following a PF12 press
acceptance_criteria.When: The system resets the screen state
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen state is set to ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS (Show Details mode); all non-key flags are cleared; the change detection state is reset so that the freshly retrieved values become the new baseline for comparison; any previously entered but unconfirmed changes are discarded

rules.rule_name: Display Screen with Original Database Values and Prompt for New Changes
rules.rule_description: After discarding pending changes and resetting to Show Details mode, the screen is redisplayed showing the original values from the database with all editable fields unprotected and a prompt for the user to make new changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Screen with Original Database Values All User Changes Cancelled Prompt User to Make New Changes

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully refreshed data from the database and reset the screen state to Show Details mode after a PF12 press
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen is sent to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen displays the original database values for all account fields (Active Status, Current Balance formatted as currency, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date, Group ID) and all customer fields (Customer ID, SSN parts, FICO Score, Date of Birth, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Lines 1-2, City, State, Zip, Country, Phone Numbers 1 and 2, Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator); all editable fields are unprotected for input; the information message area displays 'Prompt for changes' guidance; no error messages are shown

rules.rule_name: Remain in Changes-Not-OK State When Validation Errors Exist
rules.rule_description: After all input field validations are executed, if any validation error was detected, the screen state remains in Changes-Not-OK, preventing the user from proceeding to the save confirmation step. Error messages and red field highlights are retained on screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Remain in Changes-Not-OK State
Display error messages to user
Highlight fields in red

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the account update screen with one or more field values, and the system has completed all field-level validations (account status, dates, financial limits, SSN, FICO score, name, address, phone, EFT account ID, primary card holder indicator)
acceptance_criteria.When: At least one validation error has been flagged (INPUT-ERROR is set to TRUE) — for example, a mandatory field is blank, a numeric field contains non-numeric data, a date is invalid, or a value is out of the allowed range
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen state is set to Changes-Not-OK (ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK remains TRUE); the system does NOT advance to the Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed state; the first error message encountered during validation is displayed in the error message area; all fields with errors are highlighted in red; mandatory fields that were left blank display an asterisk '*' as a placeholder; the cursor is positioned on the first field in error; the user is prompted to correct the errors and resubmit

rules.rule_name: Remain in Show-Details State When No Changes Are Detected
rules.rule_description: After the user submits the screen in Show-Details state, if the system detects that no field values have changed compared to the originally fetched account and customer data, the screen remains in Show-Details state and the user is prompted to make changes before proceeding.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Remain in Show-Details State
Prompt user to make changes

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account and customer details have been successfully fetched and displayed on screen (ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS is TRUE), and the user has pressed ENTER or submitted the screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares all submitted field values against the originally fetched 'old' values using case-insensitive comparison for text fields (account status, group ID, customer ID, all name fields, all address fields, government ID, primary holder indicator, country code, state code) and exact comparison for numeric fields (balances, limits, phone number parts, SSN, date of birth, EFT account ID, FICO score), AND the comparison determines that NO field has changed (NO-CHANGES-DETECTED is TRUE), OR an input validation error exists (INPUT-ERROR is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen state remains in Show-Details (ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS); the system does NOT advance to Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed state; the original fetched values are redisplayed on screen; the user is prompted to make changes to the displayed account or customer data before the save confirmation flow can be triggered

rules.rule_name: Advance to Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed State When Validations Pass and Changes Are Detected
rules.rule_description: When all field-level validations pass without any errors AND at least one field value has changed compared to the originally fetched data, the screen state is advanced to Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed, indicating the changes are valid and ready for the user to confirm and save.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Screen State to
Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed
All validations passed and
changes are ready to save

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account and customer details have been fetched and displayed (ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS is TRUE), the user has modified one or more fields and submitted the screen, and the system has completed all field-level validations
acceptance_criteria.When: No validation errors were found (INPUT-ERROR is FALSE) AND the change comparison determined that at least one field value differs from the originally fetched data (CHANGE-HAS-OCCURRED is TRUE — meaning at least one of: account status, current balance, credit limit, cash credit limit, open date, expiry date, reissue date, current cycle credit, current cycle debit, group ID, customer ID, any name field, any address field, any phone number part, SSN, government ID, date of birth, EFT account ID, primary holder indicator, or FICO score has changed)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen state is set to Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed (ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED is set to TRUE); the system is ready to display the save confirmation prompt to the user

rules.rule_name: Display Save Confirmation Informational Message to User
rules.rule_description: When the screen state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed, the informational message area on the screen is set to prompt the user to press PF05 to confirm and save the validated changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Informational Message
to Prompt for Confirmation
Instruct user to press PF05
to confirm and save changes

acceptance_criteria.Given: All field-level validations have passed, changes have been detected compared to the original data, and the screen state has been set to Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed (ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the informational message area of the screen during the screen setup phase (3250-SETUP-INFOMSG)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message state is set to PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION; the corresponding confirmation guidance message (WS-INFO-MSG) is moved to the screen's information message output field (INFOMSGO of CACTUPAO), instructing the user to press PF05 to confirm and save the changes

rules.rule_name: Visually Activate PF05 Confirm Save Function Key
rules.rule_description: When the screen is in the save confirmation prompt state, the PF05 function key label is visually highlighted (bright/bold attribute) on the screen to draw the user's attention to the confirm-save action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Highlight PF05 Key Label
Visually activate the
Confirm Save function key

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed and the informational message has been set to PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the screen display attributes during the informational message attribute setup phase (3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The display attribute of the PF05 function key label (FKEY05A of CACTUPAI) is set to bright/bold (DFHBMASB), making the PF05 key label visually prominent on the screen to indicate it is the active key for confirming and saving the changes

rules.rule_name: Visually Activate PF12 Cancel Changes Function Key
rules.rule_description: When the screen is in the save confirmation prompt state, the PF12 function key label is also visually highlighted (bright/bold attribute) on the screen, providing the user with a clearly visible option to cancel the pending changes and refresh the original data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Highlight PF12 Key Label
Visually activate the
Cancel Changes function key

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed and the informational message has been set to PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the screen display attributes during the informational message attribute setup phase (3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The display attribute of the PF12 function key label (FKEY12A of CACTUPAI) is set to bright/bold (DFHBMASB), making the PF12 key label visually prominent on the screen to indicate it is the active key for cancelling the pending changes and returning to the original data view

rules.rule_name: PF05 Key Is Only Valid When Changes Are Confirmed-Not-Yet-Saved
rules.rule_description: The PF05 key is only accepted as a valid action when the screen is in the Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed state. Pressing PF05 in any other state is treated as an invalid key and reprocessed as ENTER.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
User Action
PF05 - Confirm Save

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the account update screen and presses the PF05 function key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the validity of the key press against the current screen state
acceptance_criteria.Then: PF05 is accepted as a valid key action ONLY IF the current screen state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed (ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED is TRUE); if the screen is in any other state (e.g., Details-Not-Fetched, Show-Details, Changes-Not-OK), PF05 is treated as an invalid key and the system resets the key action to ENTER, causing the screen to reprocess the current input without triggering the save operation

rules.rule_name: PF12 Key Is Only Valid When Account Details Have Been Fetched
rules.rule_description: The PF12 key (Cancel Changes / Re-fetch) is only accepted as a valid action when account details have already been fetched and displayed. Pressing PF12 before any account data has been loaded is treated as an invalid key.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
User Action
PF12 - Cancel Changes

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the account update screen and presses the PF12 function key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the validity of the key press against the current screen state
acceptance_criteria.Then: PF12 is accepted as a valid key action ONLY IF account details have already been fetched (ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is FALSE — meaning the screen is in Show-Details, Changes-Not-OK, Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed, or a post-update state); if the screen is still in the Details-Not-Fetched state (no account has been looked up yet), PF12 is treated as an invalid key and the system resets the key action to ENTER

rules.rule_name: Invalid or Unsupported Key Press Is Reprocessed as ENTER
rules.rule_description: Any key press that is not in the set of currently valid keys (ENTER, PF3, PF5 when applicable, PF12 when applicable) is treated as invalid and automatically reprocessed as if the user had pressed ENTER, ensuring the screen continues to function predictably.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Other Key
Invalid Key - Reprocess as Enter

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the account update screen and presses any function key or action key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines the pressed key is not in the set of currently valid keys — valid keys are: ENTER (always valid), PF03 (always valid), PF05 (valid only when ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED is TRUE), PF12 (valid only when ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is FALSE); any other key including PF01, PF02, PF04, PF06 through PF11, PA1, PA2, CLEAR, and any key not matching the valid conditions above is considered invalid
acceptance_criteria.Then: The invalid key flag (PFK-INVALID) is set to TRUE; the key action is overridden and set to ENTER (CCARD-AID-ENTER is set to TRUE); the screen processes the current input as if the user had pressed ENTER, without triggering any special navigation or action associated with the originally pressed key

key_functionalities.title: Lock Account Record for Update

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Account ID from Session Context for Update Processing
rules.rule_description: Before attempting to lock the account record for update, the system retrieves the Account ID from the current user session context to use as the key for locating the account master record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Account ID from current session context

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has pressed PF05 to confirm and save changes to an account record, and the system has validated all input changes successfully and the session context holds the current Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates the update write processing sequence
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account ID stored in the current session context is retrieved and set as the record identifier key to be used for locating and locking the account master record in the Account Master File (ACCTDAT)

rules.rule_name: Request Exclusive Lock on Account Master Record
rules.rule_description: The system attempts to acquire an exclusive lock on the account master record using the Account ID as the lookup key, retrieving the record into a work area for subsequent update. This prevents concurrent modifications by other users during the update process.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Request Exclusive Lock on Account Record using Account ID as key

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID has been retrieved from the current session context and the system is ready to begin the update write processing
acceptance_criteria.When: The system requests an exclusive lock on the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) using the Account ID as the record key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system attempts to read and lock the account record exclusively from the Account Master File; if the lock is granted, the account record data is retrieved into the update work area and the system proceeds to lock the customer record; if the lock is denied or the record is unavailable, the system marks the update as failed and informs the user that the account record is unavailable for update at this time

rules.rule_name: Account Record Lock Success - Proceed to Customer Record Lock
rules.rule_description: When the exclusive lock on the account master record is successfully acquired, the system confirms the account record is secured for update and proceeds to the next step of locking the associated customer record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Account Record Locked and Retrieved for Update Proceed to Lock Customer Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has requested an exclusive lock on the account master record using the Account ID as the key
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account Master File (ACCTDAT) grants the exclusive lock and returns the account record successfully
acceptance_criteria.Then: The account record is held exclusively in the update work area, no error condition is set, and the system proceeds immediately to attempt locking the customer master record for update

rules.rule_name: Account Record Lock Failure - Mark Update as Failed and Inform User
rules.rule_description: When the system cannot acquire an exclusive lock on the account master record — because the record is already locked by another process or is otherwise unavailable — the update is marked as failed and the user is informed that the account record cannot be updated at this time.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Update as Failed Could Not Lock Account Record for Update

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has requested an exclusive lock on the account master record using the Account ID as the key
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account Master File (ACCTDAT) denies the lock request or the record is unavailable for any reason
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an input error condition, sets the update status to 'Could Not Lock Account Record for Update', exits the update processing immediately without attempting to lock the customer record or write any data, and the screen is redisplayed to the user with a message indicating the account record is unavailable for update at this time

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Customer ID Associated with Account for Lock Processing
rules.rule_description: Before attempting to lock the Customer Master record for update, the system must identify the correct customer by retrieving the Customer ID that is associated with the account currently being updated. This Customer ID was previously established during the account lookup phase via the Card Cross-Reference file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Retrieve Customer ID
Use Customer ID associated
with the account being updated

acceptance_criteria.Given: An account update has been initiated and the Account Master record has already been successfully locked for update, and the Customer ID associated with the account being updated is available in the session's account/customer cross-reference data (CDEMO-CUST-ID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to lock the Customer Master record for update processing
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the Customer ID from the session's cross-reference data (CDEMO-CUST-ID) and sets it as the key to be used for locating and locking the Customer Master record

rules.rule_name: Attempt Exclusive Lock on Customer Master Record
rules.rule_description: The system must acquire an exclusive lock on the Customer Master record before any update can be applied. This exclusive lock prevents other users or processes from modifying the same customer record simultaneously, ensuring data integrity during the update operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Attempt to Lock Customer Record
Request exclusive access to
Customer Master record
to prevent concurrent updates

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer ID has been identified and set as the record key, and the Account Master record is already locked for update
acceptance_criteria.When: The system requests an exclusive update lock on the Customer Master record (CUSTDAT) using the Customer ID as the record identifier
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system attempts to open the Customer Master record with exclusive update access; the lock request either succeeds granting exclusive access to the customer record, or fails if the record is currently unavailable or locked by another process

rules.rule_name: Handle Customer Record Lock Failure — Abort Update Processing
rules.rule_description: If the system is unable to acquire an exclusive lock on the Customer Master record, the entire update operation must be aborted. The update state is flagged to indicate that the customer record could not be locked, and the user is informed that the update cannot proceed. No changes are written to any file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Lock Failure
Flag update as failed due to
unable to lock customer record
for exclusive update access

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to acquire an exclusive lock on the Customer Master record in the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT)
acceptance_criteria.When: The lock attempt does not return a normal successful response — meaning the Customer Master record is unavailable or currently locked by another process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the transaction as having an input error, sets the update status flag to 'Could Not Lock Customer Record for Update' (COULD-NOT-LOCK-CUST-FOR-UPDATE), and immediately exits the update processing routine without writing any changes to either the Account Master or Customer Master files; the user is informed that the customer record could not be locked for update

rules.rule_name: Customer Record Lock Success — Proceed to Concurrent Change Detection
rules.rule_description: When the exclusive lock on the Customer Master record is successfully acquired, the system confirms that both the Account Master and Customer Master records are now exclusively held for this update session. Processing can safely continue to the next step, which checks whether another user has modified the data since it was originally fetched for this update session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Customer Record Locked
Exclusive lock acquired on
Customer Master record
Ready for concurrent change check

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to acquire an exclusive lock on the Customer Master record in the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT), and the Account Master record is already locked
acceptance_criteria.When: The lock attempt returns a normal successful response, confirming exclusive access to the Customer Master record has been granted
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system continues update processing without setting any error flags, and proceeds to the concurrent change detection step (9700-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC) to verify that neither the account nor customer data has been modified by another user since it was originally retrieved for this update session

key_functionalities.title: Concurrent Change Detection

rules.rule_name: Detect Concurrent Account Record Modification - Active Status
rules.rule_description: Before applying a user's updates, verify that the Account Active Status in the database matches the value originally fetched. If another user has changed this field, the update must be aborted.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Active Status Matches?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has locked the Account record for update and holds the original Active Status value that was fetched and displayed to the user at the start of the update session
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the current Active Status value in the locked Account record against the originally fetched Active Status value
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the current Active Status does NOT match the originally fetched Active Status, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag, aborts the update process, and refreshes the screen with the latest data to notify the user that the record was modified by another user; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the next field (Current Balance)

rules.rule_name: Detect Concurrent Account Record Modification - Current Balance
rules.rule_description: Before applying a user's updates, verify that the Account Current Balance in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched. Any discrepancy indicates a concurrent modification.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Current Balance Matches?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Active Status check has passed and the system holds the original Current Balance value that was fetched and displayed to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the current numeric Current Balance value in the locked Account record against the originally fetched Current Balance value
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the current Current Balance does NOT exactly match the originally fetched Current Balance, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the Credit Limit field

rules.rule_name: Detect Concurrent Account Record Modification - Credit Limit
rules.rule_description: Before applying a user's updates, verify that the Account Credit Limit in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched to detect concurrent modifications.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Credit Limit Matches?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Current Balance check has passed and the system holds the original Credit Limit value that was fetched and displayed to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the current numeric Credit Limit value in the locked Account record against the originally fetched Credit Limit value
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the current Credit Limit does NOT exactly match the originally fetched Credit Limit, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the Cash Credit Limit field

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Current Cycle Debit Matches?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Current Cycle Credit check has passed and the system holds the original Current Cycle Debit value that was fetched and displayed to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the current numeric Current Cycle Debit value in the locked Account record against the originally fetched Current Cycle Debit value
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the current Current Cycle Debit does NOT exactly match the originally fetched Current Cycle Debit, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the Account Open Date

rules.rule_name: Abort Update and Notify User of Concurrent Record Modification
rules.rule_description: When any field mismatch is detected during the concurrent change check, the update must be immediately aborted, the screen refreshed with the latest data from the database, and the user notified so they can review the changes made by another user before deciding how to proceed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Changed by Another User - Stop Update - Refresh screen with latest data and notify user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has detected that one or more fields in either the Account or Customer record have been modified by another user since the current user fetched the data for editing
acceptance_criteria.When: The 'Data Was Changed Before Update' condition is triggered during the concurrent change detection process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system immediately stops the update process without writing any changes, sets the screen state to 'Show Details' so the latest database values are displayed, and the user is returned to the account details screen showing the current (updated by another user) values so they can review the changes and decide whether to re-enter their modifications

key_functionalities.title: Prepare Account Update Record
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Prepare Account Update Record])

    INIT[Clear and initialize\na fresh Account Update Record]

    SETID[Set Account ID\nfrom user-entered Account Number]

    SETSTATUS[Set Account Active Status\nY = Active / N = Inactive]

    SETBAL[Set Current Balance\nwith validated numeric value]

    SETCREDLIMIT[Set Credit Limit\nwith validated numeric value]

    SETCASHLIMIT[Set Cash Credit Limit\nwith validated numeric value]

    SETCYCCREDIT[Set Current Cycle Credit Amount\nwith validated numeric value]

    SETCYCDEBIT[Set Current Cycle Debit Amount\nwith validated numeric value]

    FORMATOPENDATE[Format Account Open Date\nas YYYY-MM-DD\nby combining Year, Month, Day parts]

    FORMATEXPDATE[Format Account Expiry Date\nas YYYY-MM-DD\nby combining Year, Month, Day parts]

    FORMATREISSUEDATE[Format Account Reissue Date\nas YYYY-MM-DD\nby combining Year, Month, Day parts]

    SETGROUPID[Set Group ID\nfrom user-entered Group value]

    END([End: Account Update Record Ready\nfor Saving to Database])

    START --> INIT
    INIT --> SETID
    SETID --> SETSTATUS
    SETSTATUS --> SETBAL
    SETBAL --> SETCREDLIMIT
    SETCREDLIMIT --> SETCASHLIMIT
    SETCASHLIMIT --> SETCYCCREDIT
    SETCYCCREDIT --> SETCYCDEBIT
    SETCYCDEBIT --> FORMATOPENDATE
    FORMATOPENDATE --> FORMATEXPDATE
    FORMATEXPDATE --> FORMATREISSUEDATE
    FORMATREISSUEDATE --> SETGROUPID
    SETGROUPID --> END

rules.rule_name: Initialize Fresh Account Update Record Before Populating
rules.rule_description: Before populating the account update record with new values, the record must be completely cleared and initialized to ensure no residual or stale data from previous operations is carried forward into the database write.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear and initialize a fresh Account Update Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: A confirmed account update request has been received, all input validations have passed, both the Account Master record and Customer Master record have been successfully locked for update, and no concurrent modifications have been detected
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins preparing the account update record for saving to the database
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must completely clear and initialize the Account Update Record to blank/zero values before any new field values are populated, ensuring no stale or residual data from prior operations is present in the record

rules.rule_name: Set Account ID on Update Record from User-Entered Account Number
rules.rule_description: The Account ID field on the account update record must be populated with the validated account number entered by the user, establishing the primary key that identifies which account record in the Account Master file will be updated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Account ID from user-entered Account Number

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Update Record has been initialized and the user has entered a valid 11-digit non-zero numeric Account Number that has been confirmed to exist in the Account Master file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the Account Update Record fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account ID field on the Account Update Record must be set to the user-entered and validated Account Number value (ACUP-NEW-ACCT-ID), which serves as the unique identifier for the account being updated in the Account Master file

rules.rule_name: Set Account Active Status on Update Record
rules.rule_description: The Account Active Status field on the update record must reflect the user's intended active or inactive designation for the account. A value of 'Y' indicates the account is active and a value of 'N' indicates the account is inactive.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Account Active Status Y = Active / N = Inactive

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Update Record is being populated and the user has entered a valid Account Status value that has passed Y/N validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the Account Active Status on the Account Update Record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account Active Status field (ACCT-UPDATE-ACTIVE-STATUS) must be set to the user-entered active status value (ACUP-NEW-ACTIVE-STATUS), where 'Y' designates the account as Active and 'N' designates the account as Inactive

rules.rule_name: Set Current Balance on Account Update Record Using Validated Numeric Value
rules.rule_description: The Current Balance field on the account update record must be populated using the internally validated numeric representation of the balance entered by the user, ensuring the stored value is a precise numeric figure rather than a raw text string.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Current Balance with validated numeric value

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Update Record is being populated and the user-entered Current Balance has passed signed numeric validation (confirmed to be a valid signed number with up to 2 decimal places)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the Current Balance on the Account Update Record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Current Balance field (ACCT-UPDATE-CURR-BAL) must be set to the internally computed numeric value (ACUP-NEW-CURR-BAL-N), which is the validated numeric form of the user-entered current balance, not the raw text input

rules.rule_name: Set Credit Limit on Account Update Record Using Validated Numeric Value
rules.rule_description: The Credit Limit field on the account update record must be populated using the internally validated numeric representation of the credit limit entered by the user, ensuring the stored value is a precise numeric figure.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Credit Limit with validated numeric value

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Update Record is being populated and the user-entered Credit Limit has passed signed numeric validation (confirmed to be a valid signed number with up to 2 decimal places)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the Credit Limit on the Account Update Record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Credit Limit field (ACCT-UPDATE-CREDIT-LIMIT) must be set to the internally computed numeric value (ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-N), which is the validated numeric form of the user-entered credit limit, not the raw text input

rules.rule_name: Set Cash Credit Limit on Account Update Record Using Validated Numeric Value
rules.rule_description: The Cash Credit Limit field on the account update record must be populated using the internally validated numeric representation of the cash credit limit entered by the user, ensuring the stored value is a precise numeric figure.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Cash Credit Limit with validated numeric value

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Update Record is being populated and the user-entered Cash Credit Limit has passed signed numeric validation (confirmed to be a valid signed number with up to 2 decimal places)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the Cash Credit Limit on the Account Update Record
