acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Update screen map reference has been set, all field values (account status, credit limits, balances, dates, customer name, address, phone numbers, SSN, FICO score, EFT account ID, primary cardholder indicator) have been populated, informational and error messages have been set, field protection attributes have been applied, and cursor position has been determined
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the screen transmission to the user's terminal using the identified map (CCARD-NEXT-MAP) and mapset (CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET) with the prepared output data area (CACTUPAO)
acceptance_criteria.Then: All prepared screen content including account data, customer data, error highlights, guidance messages, and field attributes must be delivered to and rendered on the user's terminal in a single transmission

rules.rule_name: Clear Previously Displayed Screen Content Before Showing New Data
rules.rule_description: Before displaying the newly prepared Account Update screen, any previously displayed content on the user's terminal must be completely erased to prevent stale or residual data from being visible alongside the new screen content.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Erase Current Screen Content
Clear any previously displayed
information from the terminal

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user's terminal may currently be displaying a previous version of the Account Update screen or any other screen content from a prior interaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The system transmits the new Account Update screen to the terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must erase all previously displayed content on the terminal screen before rendering the new screen, ensuring that no residual data, old field values, or prior messages remain visible to the user

rules.rule_name: Position Cursor on Appropriate Field Based on Validation Results or Screen State
rules.rule_description: The cursor must be automatically positioned on the most relevant field when the Account Update screen is displayed. The cursor position is determined by validation results (first field in error) or the current screen state (e.g., Account Number field on initial entry), guiding the user directly to the field requiring attention.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Apply Cursor Positioning
Place cursor on the appropriate
field as determined by
validation results or screen state

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen attribute setup has determined cursor placement by setting a cursor length value of -1 on the appropriate field — which is the first field found to be in error (e.g., Account Number field if account filter is invalid or blank, Account Status field if status is invalid, Open Date Year/Month/Day if date is invalid, Credit Limit if invalid, Expiry Date fields if invalid, Cash Credit Limit if invalid, Reissue Date fields if invalid, Current Balance if invalid, Current Cycle Credit/Debit if invalid, SSN parts if invalid, Date of Birth fields if invalid, FICO Score if invalid, First/Middle/Last Name if invalid, Address Line 1 if invalid, State if invalid, Zip Code if invalid, City if invalid, Country if invalid, Phone Number 1 or 2 parts if invalid, EFT Account ID if invalid, Primary Cardholder if invalid) OR the Account Status field if account data was just found OR the Account Number field as default
acceptance_criteria.When: The system transmits the Account Update screen to the terminal with the CURSOR option enabled
acceptance_criteria.Then: The terminal must place the cursor on the field that was designated with a cursor length value of -1 during screen attribute setup, directing the user's attention to the first field requiring input or correction; if no specific field was designated, the cursor defaults to the Account Number field

rules.rule_name: Unlock Terminal Keyboard After Screen Transmission to Allow User Input
rules.rule_description: After the Account Update screen has been transmitted and displayed, the terminal keyboard must be unlocked so the user can interact with the screen — entering an account number to search, modifying account or customer fields, or pressing function keys to confirm changes, exit, or re-fetch data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Unlock Keyboard
Release the terminal keyboard
so the user can enter
or modify data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Update screen has been successfully transmitted to the user's terminal with all field values, messages, and attributes rendered, and the terminal keyboard may be in a locked state from the previous interaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen transmission completes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must release (free) the terminal keyboard so that the user can immediately begin entering data in editable fields or pressing valid function keys (ENTER to submit, PF3 to exit, PF5 to confirm changes, PF12 to fetch account details) without any additional action required to unlock the keyboard

rules.rule_name: Complete Screen Display Sequence Before Returning Control to User
rules.rule_description: The full screen send process must execute as an ordered sequence — screen layout identification, content population, message setup, attribute configuration, and terminal transmission — before control is returned to the user. The session state is preserved in the communication area so the next user interaction can resume from the correct point.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
End: Screen Displayed
User can now view data
and interact with the screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has been triggered to display the Account Update screen as part of processing a user interaction (initial entry, account search, data edit, confirmation request, or update result notification)
acceptance_criteria.When: The complete screen send sequence executes in order: (1) screen initialization with current date and time, (2) screen field values populated based on current state (blank for initial entry, original fetched values for show-details state, or updated values for changes-made state), (3) informational guidance message set based on state (prompt for search key, prompt for changes, prompt for confirmation, update success, or failure notification), (4) field protection attributes applied (all fields protected initially, then selectively unprotected based on state, error fields highlighted in red, blank mandatory fields marked with asterisk), (5) function key attributes set (PF5 and PF12 highlighted when confirmation is pending), and (6) screen transmitted to terminal with erase, cursor positioning, and keyboard unlock
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen is fully rendered on the user's terminal, the current program state and all field values are saved to the session communication area, and the transaction returns control awaiting the next user input with the same transaction identifier so the session can continue

key_functionalities.title: Function Key Availability Highlighting
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Function Key Highlighting\nDetermine which PF keys to activate])

    CHECKSTATE{What is the\nCurrent Screen State?}

    SEARCHMODE[Search Mode /\nNo Changes Made\nUser has not yet made any changes\nto account or customer data]

    CHANGESMODE{Changes Have Been Made\nBut Not Yet Finalized?}

    CONFIRMMODE{System is Prompting\nUser to Confirm Save?}

    HIGHLIGHTPF12[Highlight PF12 - Cancel Changes\nActivate PF12 key label so user\nknows they can cancel and\nrevert to original values]

    HIGHLIGHTBOTH[Highlight PF05 - Confirm Save\nHighlight PF12 - Cancel Changes\nActivate both PF05 and PF12 key labels\nso user knows they can confirm\nthe save or cancel the changes]

    NOHIGHLIGHT[No Function Key Highlighting\nNeither PF05 nor PF12 is highlighted\nUser is in search or view mode only]

    DONE([Screen Displayed to User\nWith Appropriate Function Key\nLabels Activated and Highlighted])

    START --> CHECKSTATE

    CHECKSTATE -->|Changes in Progress| CHANGESMODE
    CHECKSTATE -->|Awaiting Confirmation| CONFIRMMODE
    CHECKSTATE -->|Search or View Mode| SEARCHMODE

    CHANGESMODE -->|Yes - Changes Made\nNot Yet Confirmed or Completed| HIGHLIGHTPF12
    CHANGESMODE -->|No| NOHIGHLIGHT

    CONFIRMMODE -->|Yes - Waiting for\nUser to Press PF05| HIGHLIGHTBOTH
    CONFIRMMODE -->|No| NOHIGHLIGHT

    SEARCHMODE --> NOHIGHLIGHT

    HIGHLIGHTPF12 --> DONE
    HIGHLIGHTBOTH --> DONE
    NOHIGHLIGHT --> DONE

rules.rule_name: No Function Key Highlighting in Search or View Mode
rules.rule_description: When the user is in search mode (no account loaded), view-only mode (account details displayed with no changes), or after a completed update, neither the PF05 (Confirm Save) nor the PF12 (Cancel Changes) function key label is highlighted on the screen, indicating no change-related actions are available.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
No Function Key Highlighting
Neither PF05 nor PF12 is highlighted
User is in search or view mode only

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Update screen is active AND the current processing state is one of: (a) no account details have been fetched yet, (b) account details are displayed but no changes have been made by the user, or (c) changes have already been successfully saved (update completed)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen function key attributes for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: Neither the PF05 (Confirm Save) key label nor the PF12 (Cancel Changes) key label is highlighted or activated on the screen — both remain in their default unactivated visual state, indicating to the user that no change-confirmation or change-cancellation actions are currently applicable

rules.rule_name: Highlight PF12 Cancel Changes Key When Changes Are In Progress
rules.rule_description: When the user has made changes to account or customer data on the screen but those changes have not yet been confirmed or finalized (i.e., changes are in progress — either pending validation or validated but awaiting confirmation), the PF12 (Cancel Changes) function key label is highlighted to visually guide the user that they can cancel and revert to the original values.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Highlight PF12 - Cancel Changes
Activate PF12 key label so user
knows they can cancel and
revert to original values

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Update screen is active AND the current processing state indicates that changes have been made by the user (the screen is in a 'changes made' state, which includes: changes entered but failing validation, changes validated and awaiting confirmation, update lock error, or update failure) AND the update has NOT yet been successfully completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen function key attributes for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The PF12 (Cancel Changes) function key label is highlighted and activated on the screen (displayed in bright/bold style — DFHBMASB attribute), visually signaling to the user that pressing PF12 is a valid action to cancel the in-progress changes; the PF05 (Confirm Save) key label remains in its default unactivated state

rules.rule_name: Highlight Both PF05 Confirm Save and PF12 Cancel Changes Keys When Awaiting User Confirmation
rules.rule_description: When the system has successfully validated all user-entered changes and is now prompting the user to confirm the save (i.e., the screen is in the 'Prompt for Confirmation' state — changes are validated and OK but not yet committed), both the PF05 (Confirm Save) and PF12 (Cancel Changes) function key labels are highlighted simultaneously, giving the user a clear visual choice between committing or discarding the changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Highlight PF05 - Confirm Save
Highlight PF12 - Cancel Changes
Activate both PF05 and PF12 key labels
so user knows they can confirm
the save or cancel the changes

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Update screen is active AND all user-entered changes have passed validation AND the system has set the processing state to 'Prompt for Confirmation' (PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION is TRUE), which occurs when the state is 'Changes OK — Not Confirmed' (ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED), meaning the user has made valid changes that are ready to be saved but have not yet pressed PF05 to commit them
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen function key attributes for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: Both the PF05 (Confirm Save) function key label AND the PF12 (Cancel Changes) function key label are highlighted and activated on the screen (both displayed in bright/bold style — DFHBMASB attribute), visually presenting the user with two available actions: press PF05 to permanently save the validated changes, or press PF12 to cancel and revert to the original values

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user initiates the Account Update transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program starts and the communication area length is zero OR the calling program is the main menu program and the re-entry flag is not set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program initializes all communication areas and working storage to empty values, sets the program state to 'Enter' mode, and sets the account details state to 'Not Fetched'; otherwise, the prior session data is restored from the communication area including both the shared communication area and the program-specific communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Initialization and Session Context Setup
all_rules.Rule_Description: On program entry, working storage and communication areas are initialized. If this is a fresh entry (no prior session) or the user navigated from the main menu without re-entering, the program initializes a clean session state with no account data loaded. Otherwise, the prior session state is restored from the communication area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user presses a key to submit the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the attention identifier from the terminal interface
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The corresponding function key indicator is set: ENTER key sets AID-ENTER, CLEAR sets AID-CLEAR, PA1 sets AID-PA1, PA2 sets AID-PA2, PF1–PF12 set AID-PFK01 through AID-PFK12 respectively, and PF13–PF24 are mapped to AID-PFK01 through AID-PFK12 as shift equivalents

all_rules.Rule_Name: Function Key Capture and Mapping
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program captures the attention identifier (AID) key pressed by the user and maps it to a named function key indicator. PF13–PF24 are treated as equivalents to PF01–PF12 respectively.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user presses a function key on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the key pressed against the current screen state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is considered valid only if it is ENTER, PF03, PF05 when the current state is 'Changes OK Not Confirmed', or PF12 when the current state is not 'Details Not Fetched'; any other key press is treated as ENTER by setting the AID indicator to ENTER

all_rules.Rule_Name: Valid Function Key Enforcement
all_rules.Rule_Description: Only specific function keys are accepted as valid actions. Keys not in the valid set are treated as ENTER. PF5 is only valid when changes have been validated but not yet confirmed. PF12 is only valid when account details have already been fetched.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF03
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a calling transaction ID exists, control is transferred to that transaction; otherwise the main menu transaction ID is used as the destination. If a calling program exists, control is transferred to that program; otherwise the main menu program is used. The current program sets itself as the 'from' program, sets user type to USER, sets program state to ENTER, records the current map and mapset, commits the current unit of work via SYNCPOINT, and transfers control using XCTL to the destination program passing the shared communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Exit and Return to Calling Program via PF03
all_rules.Rule_Description: When PF03 is pressed, the program transfers control back to the calling program or defaults to the main menu if no calling context exists.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is entered fresh (no prior session) or the user has navigated from the main menu without re-entering
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program determines this is a fresh entry state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program-specific communication area is initialized to empty, the screen is sent with all detail fields blank and protected, only the account number field is enabled for input, the program state is set to 'Re-enter', the account details state is set to 'Not Fetched', and the user is prompted to enter a search key (account number)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fresh Entry Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is entered for the first time or navigated from the main menu, a blank account update screen is displayed with only the account number field available for input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current program state is either 'Changes Okayed and Done' or 'Changes Failed'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the current state at the start of a new interaction cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program-specific communication area, miscellaneous storage, and the account ID in the shared communication area are all initialized to empty values; the program state is set to 'Enter'; the screen is sent in fresh state prompting for a new account number; the program state is then set to 'Re-enter' and account details state is set to 'Not Fetched'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Post-Update and Post-Failed-Update Screen Reset
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful update or a failed update attempt, the screen and session state are fully reset to allow the user to begin a new account search.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered data on the Account Update screen and pressed a key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program receives the screen map input
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All entered field values are captured including: Account ID, Account Status, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Balance, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date (year/month/day), Expiry Date (year/month/day), Reissue Date (year/month/day), Group ID, Customer ID, SSN parts 1/2/3, Date of Birth (year/month/day), FICO Score, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Lines 1 and 2, City, State, Country, Zip Code, Phone Number 1 parts A/B/C, Phone Number 2 parts A/B/C, Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, and Primary Card Holder Indicator; any field containing '*' or spaces is stored as LOW-VALUES (blank); numeric fields that are valid numbers are also converted to their numeric equivalents

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Input Data Capture
all_rules.Rule_Description: All user-entered data is received from the screen map into the program's input area. Fields containing asterisk '*' or spaces are treated as blank and stored as LOW-VALUES internally.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered or left blank the account number field on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates the account number
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account number is blank or LOW-VALUES, an input error is flagged, the account filter flag is set to BLANK, the account ID and demo account ID are set to zeroes, and if no prior error message exists the user is prompted to enter an account number; if the account number is supplied but is not numeric or is equal to zero, an input error is flagged, the demo account ID is set to zeroes, and if no prior error message exists the message 'Account Number if supplied must be a 11 digit Non-Zero Number' is displayed; if the account number is valid numeric and non-zero, the account filter flag is set to VALID and the account ID is stored in the demo account ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Number Mandatory and Format Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The account number entered by the user must be supplied, must be a numeric value, and must be a non-zero 11-digit number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid account number has been entered by the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the Card Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX) using the account ID as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account is found, the customer ID and card number are retrieved and stored in the shared communication area; if the account is not found in the cross-reference file, an input error is flagged, the account filter is set to invalid, and if no prior error message exists the message 'Account: [account number] not found in Cross ref file' is displayed with the response details

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Cross-Reference Lookup by Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Card Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX) is read using the account ID to retrieve the associated customer ID and card number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account was found in the Card Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the Account Master file (ACCTDAT) using the account ID as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account is found, the account found flag is set to TRUE and processing continues to customer lookup; if the account is not found in the Account Master file, an input error is flagged, the account filter is set to invalid, and if no prior error message exists the message 'Account: [account number] not found in Acct Master file' is displayed with the response details

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Master Data Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Master file (ACCTDAT) is read using the account ID to retrieve full account details including balances, credit limits, dates, and status.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account was found in the Account Master file and a customer ID was retrieved from the cross-reference
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT) using the customer ID as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the customer is found, the customer found flag is set to TRUE and processing continues to store the fetched data; if the customer is not found in the Customer Master file, an input error is flagged, the customer filter is set to invalid, and if no prior error message exists the message 'CustId: [customer ID] not found in customer master' is displayed with the response details

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Master Data Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Customer Master file (CUSTDAT) is read using the customer ID (retrieved from the cross-reference) to retrieve full customer details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Account data has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master file and customer data from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program stores the fetched data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following account fields are stored as original values: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date (split into year/month/day from positions 1:4, 6:2, 9:2), Expiry Date (split into year/month/day from positions 1:4, 6:2, 9:2), Reissue Date (split into year/month/day from positions 1:4, 6:2, 9:2), and Group ID; the following customer fields are stored as original values: Customer ID, SSN, Date of Birth (split into year/month/day from positions 1:4, 6:2, 9:2), FICO Credit Score, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Lines 1/2/3, State Code, Country Code, Zip Code, Phone Numbers 1 and 2, Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, and Primary Card Holder Indicator; additionally Account ID, Customer ID, customer name parts, account status, and card number are stored in the shared communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Fetched Account and Customer Data as Original Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving account and customer data from all three files, all retrieved values are stored as 'original' (old) values to enable change detection when the user submits edits.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Account and customer details have been fetched and displayed, and the user has submitted the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program compares all new (user-entered) values against all original (fetched) values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The comparison checks the following account fields for equality: Account ID, Active Status (case-insensitive), Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, and Group ID (case-insensitive, trimmed); AND the following customer fields: Customer ID (case-insensitive, trimmed), First Name (case-insensitive, trimmed), Middle Name (case-insensitive, trimmed), Last Name (case-insensitive, trimmed), Address Lines 1/2/3 (case-insensitive, trimmed), State Code (case-insensitive, trimmed), Country Code (case-insensitive, trimmed), Zip Code (case-insensitive, trimmed), Phone Number parts 1A/1B/1C/2A/2B/2C (exact), SSN (exact), Government Issued ID (case-insensitive, trimmed), Date of Birth (exact), EFT Account ID (exact), Primary Card Holder Indicator (case-insensitive, trimmed), and FICO Score (exact); if ALL fields match, the state is set to 'No Changes Detected' and field-level validation is skipped; if ANY field differs, the state is set to 'Change Has Occurred' and field-level validation proceeds

all_rules.Rule_Name: Change Detection Between Original and User-Entered Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before performing field-level validation, the program compares every user-entered value against the originally fetched values to determine if any changes were made. If no changes are detected, validation is skipped.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the account status field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates the account status value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account status is blank, LOW-VALUES, or zero, an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'Account Status must be supplied.' is displayed; if the account status is supplied but is not 'Y' or 'N' (case-insensitive), an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'Account Status must be Y or N.' is displayed; the validated value is stored in the account status edit work field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Status Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The account active status field must be supplied and must contain only 'Y' (active) or 'N' (inactive).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered year, month, and day values for the Open Date, Expiry Date, or Reissue Date
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates each date field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For the Year component: it must be supplied (not blank), must be a 4-digit numeric value, and the century portion must be either the current century (20xx) or the last century (19xx); otherwise an error is flagged with message '[Date Name] : Year must be supplied.' or '[Date Name] must be 4 digit number.' or '[Date Name] : Century is not valid.'; For the Month component: it must be supplied, must be a number between 1 and 12; otherwise an error is flagged with message '[Date Name] : Month must be supplied.' or '[Date Name]: Month must be a number between 1 and 12.'; For the Day component: it must be supplied, must be a number between 1 and 31; otherwise an error is flagged with message '[Date Name] : Day must be supplied.' or '[Date Name]:day must be a number between 1 and 31.'; Cross-validation rules: a month that does not have 31 days cannot have day=31 (error: '[Date Name]:Cannot have 31 days in this month.'); February cannot have day=30 (error: '[Date Name]:Cannot have 30 days in this month.'); February day=29 is only valid if the year is a leap year — if the last two digits of the year are 00 then the year must be divisible by 400, otherwise the year must be divisible by 4 (error: '[Date Name]:Not a leap year.Cannot have 29 days in this month.'); the complete date is also validated using the system date validation utility CSUTLDTC with format 'YYYYMMDD'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Date Field Validation for Open Date, Expiry Date, and Reissue Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each of the three account dates (Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date) must be valid calendar dates. Each date is entered as separate year, month, and day components and validated individually and in combination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a Date of Birth that passes standard date format validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program performs the additional age validation on the Date of Birth
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program converts the entered date and the current system date to integer day numbers using the INTEGER-OF-DATE function; if the current date integer is greater than the entered date integer, the date is valid (it is in the past); if the current date integer is less than or equal to the entered date integer, an input error is flagged on the year, month, and day components and if no prior error message exists the message '[Date Name]:cannot be in the future' is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Date of Birth Past-Date Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: In addition to standard date format validation, the Date of Birth must represent a date in the past — it cannot be today's date or a future date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the credit limit field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates the credit limit value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the credit limit is blank or LOW-VALUES, an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'Credit Limit must be supplied.' is displayed; if the credit limit is supplied but fails the signed numeric format test (TEST-NUMVAL-C), an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'Credit Limit is not valid' is displayed; the validation result flag is stored for use in screen display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Credit Limit Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The credit limit must be supplied and must be a valid signed numeric value (may include currency sign indicators).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the cash credit limit field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates the cash credit limit value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the cash credit limit is blank or LOW-VALUES, an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'Cash Credit Limit must be supplied.' is displayed; if the cash credit limit is supplied but fails the signed numeric format test (TEST-NUMVAL-C), an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'Cash Credit Limit is not valid' is displayed; the validation result flag is stored for use in screen display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cash Credit Limit Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The cash credit limit must be supplied and must be a valid signed numeric value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the current balance field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates the current balance value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current balance is blank or LOW-VALUES, an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'Current Balance must be supplied.' is displayed; if the current balance is supplied but fails the signed numeric format test (TEST-NUMVAL-C), an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'Current Balance is not valid' is displayed; the validation result flag is stored for use in screen display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Current Balance Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current balance must be supplied and must be a valid signed numeric value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the current cycle credit field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates the current cycle credit value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current cycle credit is blank or LOW-VALUES, an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'Current Cycle Credit Limit must be supplied.' is displayed; if the current cycle credit is supplied but fails the signed numeric format test (TEST-NUMVAL-C), an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'Current Cycle Credit Limit is not valid' is displayed; the validation result flag is stored for use in screen display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Current Cycle Credit Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current cycle credit must be supplied and must be a valid signed numeric value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the current cycle debit field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates the current cycle debit value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current cycle debit is blank or LOW-VALUES, an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'Current Cycle Debit Limit must be supplied.' is displayed; if the current cycle debit is supplied but fails the signed numeric format test (TEST-NUMVAL-C), an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'Current Cycle Debit Limit is not valid' is displayed; the validation result flag is stored for use in screen display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Current Cycle Debit Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current cycle debit must be supplied and must be a valid signed numeric value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered the SSN in three parts on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates each SSN part
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For SSN Part 1 (first 3 digits): it must be supplied (not blank), must be numeric, must be non-zero, and must NOT be 000, 666, or any value between 900 and 999; if blank the error message is 'SSN: First 3 chars must be supplied.'; if non-numeric the error message is 'SSN: First 3 chars must be all numeric.'; if zero the error message is 'SSN: First 3 chars must not be zero.'; if in the invalid range the error message is 'SSN: First 3 chars: should not be 000, 666, or between 900 and 999'; For SSN Part 2 (4th and 5th digits): it must be supplied, must be numeric, and must be non-zero; error messages follow the same pattern with label 'SSN 4th & 5th chars'; For SSN Part 3 (last 4 digits): it must be supplied, must be numeric, and must be non-zero; error messages follow the same pattern with label 'SSN Last 4 chars'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Social Security Number (SSN) Three-Part Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The SSN is entered in three separate parts and each part is validated for format, numeric content, non-zero value, and range restrictions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the FICO score field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates the FICO score value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The field is first validated as a required 3-character numeric non-zero value: if blank the message is 'FICO Score must be supplied.'; if non-numeric the message is 'FICO Score must be all numeric.'; if zero the message is 'FICO Score must not be zero.'; if the numeric validation passes, the value is further checked to be within the range 300 to 850 inclusive; if outside this range, an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'FICO Score: should be between 300 and 850' is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: FICO Credit Score Range Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The FICO credit score must be supplied, must be a 3-digit numeric value, must be non-zero, and must fall within the valid FICO score range of 300 to 850.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the customer name fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates the First Name, Middle Name, and Last Name fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For First Name (up to 25 characters): it must be supplied; if blank the message is 'First Name must be supplied.'; if supplied but contains non-alphabetic characters the message is 'First Name can have alphabets only.'; For Middle Name (up to 25 characters): it is optional; if blank it is accepted as valid; if supplied but contains non-alphabetic characters the message is 'Middle Name can have alphabets only.'; For Last Name (up to 25 characters): it must be supplied; if blank the message is 'Last Name must be supplied.'; if supplied but contains non-alphabetic characters the message is 'Last Name can have alphabets only.'; alphabetic validation is performed by converting all known alphabetic characters to spaces and checking if the result is entirely spaces

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Name Fields Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: First Name and Last Name are mandatory and must contain only alphabetic characters. Middle Name is optional but if provided must also contain only alphabetic characters.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or left blank the Address Line 1 field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates Address Line 1 (up to 50 characters)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If Address Line 1 is blank, LOW-VALUES, or has zero trimmed length, an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'Address Line 1 must be supplied.' is displayed; if the field is supplied with any non-blank content, it is accepted as valid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Address Line 1 Mandatory Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Address Line 1 is a mandatory field and must be supplied by the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the state code field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates the state code (2 characters)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the state code is blank the message is 'State must be supplied.'; if supplied but contains non-alphabetic characters the message is 'State can have alphabets only.'; if the state code passes alphabetic validation, it is further checked against the list of valid US state codes; if it is not a valid US state code, an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'State: is not a valid state code' is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: US State Code Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The state code must be supplied, must be exactly 2 alphabetic characters, and must be a valid US state code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the zip code field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates the zip code (5 characters)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the zip code is blank the message is 'Zip must be supplied.'; if supplied but not all numeric the message is 'Zip must be all numeric.'; if numeric but equal to zero the message is 'Zip must not be zero.'; if all validations pass the zip code is accepted as valid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Zip Code Numeric and Non-Zero Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The zip code must be supplied, must be exactly 5 numeric digits, and must be non-zero.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the state code and zip code have individually passed their respective validations
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program performs the state and zip code cross-validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The state code is concatenated with the first 2 digits of the zip code to form a 4-character lookup key; this key is checked against the valid US state and zip code prefix combination table; if the combination is not valid, an input error is flagged, both the state flag and zip code flag are set to invalid, and if no prior error message exists the message 'Invalid zip code for state' is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: State and Zip Code Combination Cross-Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When both the state code and zip code individually pass validation, the combination of the state code and the first two digits of the zip code must represent a valid USPS state-to-zip assignment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the city field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates the city field (up to 50 characters)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the city is blank the message is 'City must be supplied.'; if supplied but contains non-alphabetic characters the message is 'City can have alphabets only.'; if the city contains only alphabetic characters it is accepted as valid

all_rules.Rule_Name: City Field Alphabetic Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The city field is mandatory and must contain only alphabetic characters.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the country code field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates the country code (3 characters)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the country code is blank the message is 'Country must be supplied.'; if supplied but contains non-alphabetic characters the message is 'Country can have alphabets only.'; if the country code contains only alphabetic characters it is accepted as valid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Country Code Alphabetic Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The country code is mandatory, must be exactly 3 alphabetic characters.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or left blank the phone number fields (Phone 1 and Phone 2, each with parts A, B, C)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates each phone number
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If all three parts (A, B, C) of a phone number are blank or LOW-VALUES, the phone number is considered not provided and is accepted as valid; if any part is provided, all parts are validated as follows: Area Code (Part A, 3 digits) must be supplied (error: '[Phone Name]: Area code must be supplied.'), must be a 3-digit numeric value (error: '[Phone Name]: Area code must be A 3 digit number.'), must be non-zero (error: '[Phone Name]: Area code cannot be zero'), and must be a valid North American general purpose area code (error: '[Phone Name]: Not valid North America general purpose area code'); Prefix (Part B, 3 digits) must be supplied (error: '[Phone Name]: Prefix code must be supplied.'), must be a 3-digit numeric value (error: '[Phone Name]: Prefix code must be A 3 digit number.'), and must be non-zero (error: '[Phone Name]: Prefix code cannot be zero'); Line Number (Part C, 4 digits) must be supplied (error: '[Phone Name]: Line number code must be supplied.'), must be a 4-digit numeric value (error: '[Phone Name]: Line number code must be A 4 digit number.'), and must be non-zero (error: '[Phone Name]: Line number code cannot be zero')

all_rules.Rule_Name: US Phone Number Format Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Both phone numbers are optional. However, if any part of a phone number is provided, all three parts (area code, prefix, line number) must be provided and valid. Each phone number is validated for US North American format.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the EFT Account ID field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates the EFT Account ID (10 characters)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the EFT Account ID is blank the message is 'EFT Account Id must be supplied.'; if supplied but not all numeric the message is 'EFT Account Id must be all numeric.'; if numeric but equal to zero the message is 'EFT Account Id must not be zero.'; if all validations pass the EFT Account ID is accepted as valid

all_rules.Rule_Name: EFT Account ID Numeric Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The EFT Account ID must be supplied, must be exactly 10 numeric digits, and must be non-zero.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the Primary Card Holder Indicator field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates the Primary Card Holder Indicator
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the indicator is blank, LOW-VALUES, or zero, an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'Primary Card Holder must be supplied.' is displayed; if the indicator is supplied but is not 'Y' or 'N' (case-insensitive), an input error is flagged and if no prior error message exists the message 'Primary Card Holder must be Y or N.' is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Primary Card Holder Indicator Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Primary Card Holder Indicator must be supplied and must be either 'Y' (yes, primary holder) or 'N' (no, not primary holder).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Input processing and validation have completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the current state to determine the next action
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the state is 'Details Not Fetched' or PF12 was pressed AND the account filter is valid, the program reads account data from the database and if the customer is found sets the state to 'Show Details'; if the state is 'Show Details' and there are no input errors and changes were detected, the state is set to 'Changes OK Not Confirmed'; if the state is 'Changes Not OK', processing continues (screen will show errors); if the state is 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' and PF05 was pressed, the update write processing is triggered; if the state is 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' without PF05, processing continues (screen will prompt for confirmation); if the state is 'Changes Okayed and Done', the state is set back to 'Show Details' and if the session came from another transaction the account ID, card number, and account status in the shared communication area are cleared; any unexpected state triggers an abend with code '0001' and message 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Next Action Determination After Input Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: After input processing and validation, the program determines the appropriate next action based on the current state and validation results.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Account details have been fetched and the user has made changes on screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF12 (which is valid only when details have been fetched)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program re-reads the Card Cross-Reference file, Account Master file, and Customer Master file to retrieve the current database values; the fetched data is stored as the new original values; the screen is redisplayed showing the current database values with all user changes discarded

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cancel Changes and Refresh Data from Database
all_rules.Rule_Description: When PF12 is pressed after account details have been fetched, the program re-reads the account and customer data from the database and redisplays the original values, discarding any user-entered changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All field-level validations have passed with no errors
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program determines the next action after successful validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The state is set to 'Changes OK Not Confirmed'; the screen is redisplayed showing the user-entered values; the informational message area displays a confirmation prompt; the PF05 function key label is highlighted to indicate it is available for confirming the save; the PF12 function key label is also highlighted; all detail fields remain protected (read-only) in this state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prompt User for Save Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all validations pass with no errors, the screen state is set to prompt the user to confirm the changes by pressing PF05 before the update is committed to the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has confirmed the changes by pressing PF05 and the state is 'Changes OK Not Confirmed'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to acquire an exclusive lock on the Account Master record (ACCTDAT) using the account ID as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the lock is acquired successfully, processing continues to lock the customer record; if the lock cannot be acquired, an input error is flagged, the state is set to indicate a lock error (cannot update), and the screen is redisplayed with a failure message informing the user that the record could not be locked for update

all_rules.Rule_Name: Lock Account Record for Exclusive Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before writing updates, the Account Master record must be locked exclusively to prevent concurrent modifications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master record has been successfully locked for update
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to acquire an exclusive lock on the Customer Master record (CUSTDAT) using the customer ID as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the lock is acquired successfully, processing continues to the concurrent change check; if the lock cannot be acquired, an input error is flagged, the state is set to indicate a lock error (cannot update), and the screen is redisplayed with a failure message informing the user that the record could not be locked for update

all_rules.Rule_Name: Lock Customer Record for Exclusive Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully locking the Account Master record, the Customer Master record must also be locked exclusively before writing updates.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the Account Master and Customer Master records have been locked for update
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program compares the currently locked database record values against the original values that were fetched and stored when the account was first displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For the Account record, the following fields are compared: Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date (year at positions 1:4, month at 6:2, day at 9:2), Expiry Date (year at 1:4, month at 6:2, day at 9:2), Reissue Date (year at 1:4, month at 6:2, day at 9:2), and Group ID (case-insensitive); for the Customer record, the following fields are compared: First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Lines 1/2/3, State Code, Country Code (all case-insensitive), Zip Code, Phone Numbers 1 and 2, SSN, Government Issued ID (case-insensitive), Date of Birth (year at 1:4, month at 6:2, day at 9:2), EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator, and FICO Credit Score; if any field has changed, the state is set to 'Data Was Changed Before Update', the update is aborted, and the screen is refreshed with the newly changed database values so the user can review and re-enter their changes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Concurrent Modification Detection Before Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: After locking both records, the program verifies that neither record has been modified by another user since the data was originally fetched for display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: No concurrent modifications were detected and the update is safe to proceed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program builds the account update record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account update record is initialized and populated with: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance (numeric), Credit Limit (numeric), Cash Credit Limit (numeric), Current Cycle Credit (numeric), Current Cycle Debit (numeric), Open Date formatted as 'YYYY-MM-DD' by concatenating the year, '-', month, '-', day components, Expiry Date formatted as 'YYYY-MM-DD' by concatenating the year, '-', month, '-', day components, Reissue Date formatted as 'YYYY-MM-DD' by concatenating the year, '-', month, '-', day components, and Group ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Account Update Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The account update record is built from the validated user-entered values, with dates formatted as YYYY-MM-DD strings.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account update record has been prepared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program builds the customer update record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The customer update record is initialized and populated with: Customer ID, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, Address Line 3 (City), State Code, Country Code, Zip Code, Phone Number 1 formatted as '(AAA)PPP-LLLL' by concatenating '(', area code part A, ')', prefix part B, '-', line number part C, Phone Number 2 formatted as '(AAA)PPP-LLLL' using the same pattern, SSN (combined from three parts), Government Issued ID, Date of Birth formatted as 'YYYY-MM-DD' by concatenating the year, '-', month, '-', day components, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator, and FICO Credit Score (numeric)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Customer Update Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer update record is built from the validated user-entered values, with phone numbers formatted in standard US format and date of birth formatted as YYYY-MM-DD.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account update record has been prepared with all new values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program writes the updated account record to the Account Master file (ACCTDAT) using the REWRITE operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the write is successful, processing continues to save the customer record; if the write fails, the state is set to 'Locked But Update Failed' and the screen is redisplayed with a failure message informing the user that the update failed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Account Changes to Account Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The prepared account update record is written back to the Account Master file (ACCTDAT) to persist the changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account record has been successfully updated in the Account Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program writes the updated customer record to the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT) using the REWRITE operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the write is successful, the state is set to 'Changes Okayed and Done' and the screen is redisplayed with a success confirmation message; if the write fails, a SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK is issued to undo the account record update, the state is set to 'Locked But Update Failed', and the screen is redisplayed with a failure message informing the user that the update failed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Customer Changes to Customer Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The prepared customer update record is written back to the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT). If this write fails, the account update is rolled back to maintain data consistency.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is about to send the screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen initialization routine executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen output area is set to LOW-VALUES; the current system date and time are retrieved; the screen header is populated with: the standard title lines from the application title constants, the current transaction ID, the current program name, the current date formatted as MM/DD/YY, and the current time formatted as HH:MM:SS

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Header Initialization with Current Date and Time
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before sending the screen to the user, the screen output area is initialized and the header fields are populated with the current date, time, transaction ID, program name, and standard titles.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Account and customer data has been successfully fetched from the database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program populates the screen with original values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If account data was found, the following account fields are displayed: Active Status, Current Balance (formatted as currency with 2 decimal places), Credit Limit (formatted as currency), Cash Credit Limit (formatted as currency), Current Cycle Credit (formatted as currency), Current Cycle Debit (formatted as currency), Open Date year/month/day, Expiry Date year/month/day, Reissue Date year/month/day, and Group ID; if customer data was found, the following customer fields are displayed: Customer ID, SSN Part 1 (characters 1-3), SSN Part 2 (characters 4-5), SSN Part 3 (characters 6-9), FICO Score, Date of Birth year/month/day, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Lines 1 and 2, City, State Code, Zip Code, Country Code, Phone 1 area code (characters 2-4), Phone 1 prefix (characters 6-8), Phone 1 line number (characters 10-13), Phone 2 area code (characters 2-4), Phone 2 prefix (characters 6-8), Phone 2 line number (characters 10-13), Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, and Primary Card Holder Indicator; the screen state is set to 'Prompt for Changes'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Original Account and Customer Data on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account details have been successfully fetched or when showing original values, all account and customer fields are populated on the screen with the originally retrieved database values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Validation has been performed and one or more fields have errors
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program populates the screen with the user-entered (new) values for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All user-entered values are displayed as entered; for numeric fields that passed validation, the formatted numeric value is shown; for numeric fields that failed validation, the raw entered text is shown; all date component fields (open, expiry, reissue, DOB) show the entered year/month/day values; all name, address, phone, and other fields show the entered values; fields with validation errors are highlighted in red; fields that were left blank when mandatory are shown with an asterisk '*' placeholder and highlighted in red; the cursor is positioned on the first field in error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Updated Values with Validation Error Highlighting
all_rules.Rule_Description: When validation errors exist, the screen is redisplayed with the user-entered values retained and invalid fields highlighted in red with asterisks for blank mandatory fields.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is preparing to send the screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets up the informational message based on the current state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message displayed corresponds to the current state as follows: if the state is 'Program Enter' or 'Details Not Fetched', the message prompts the user to enter search keys; if the state is 'Show Details' or 'Changes Not OK', the message prompts the user to make changes; if the state is 'Changes OK Not Confirmed', the message prompts the user to confirm the changes; if the state is 'Changes Okayed and Done', the message confirms the update was successful; if the state is 'Changes Okayed Lock Error' or 'Changes Okayed But Failed', the message informs the user of the failure; the error message from validation (if any) is also displayed in the error message area of the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Context-Sensitive Informational Message Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: The informational message area on the screen displays guidance messages appropriate to the current processing state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is preparing to send the screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets field protection attributes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All fields are first set to protected (read-only) including: Account ID, Account Status, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Balance, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date parts, Expiry Date parts, Reissue Date parts, Group ID, Customer Number, SSN parts, FICO Score, DOB parts, First/Middle/Last Name, Address Lines 1 and 2, City, State, Zip, Country, Phone 1 and 2 parts, Government ID, EFT Account ID, Primary Holder Indicator, and Info Message; then based on state: if 'Details Not Fetched', only the Account ID field is made editable; if 'Show Details' or 'Changes Not OK', the following fields are made editable: Account Status, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Balance, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date parts, Expiry Date parts, Reissue Date parts, DOB parts, Group ID, SSN parts, FICO Score, First/Middle/Last Name, Address Lines 1 and 2, City, State, Zip, Phone 1 and 2 parts, Government ID, EFT Account ID, Primary Holder Indicator; Customer Number and Country Code remain protected in all states; if 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' or 'Changes Okayed and Done', all fields remain protected

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Field Protection Based on Processing State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Screen field protection attributes are set based on the current processing state. All fields are protected by default, then specific fields are selectively unprotected for editing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is preparing to send the screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets the cursor position based on validation results and current state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If account data was found or no changes were detected, the cursor is placed on the Account Status field; if the account filter is invalid or blank, the cursor is placed on the Account ID field; otherwise the cursor is placed on the first field in error in the following priority order: Account Status, Open Date Year, Open Date Month, Open Date Day, Credit Limit, Expiry Date Year, Expiry Date Month, Expiry Date Day, Cash Credit Limit, Reissue Date Year, Reissue Date Month, Reissue Date Day, Current Balance, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, SSN Part 1, SSN Part 2, SSN Part 3, DOB Year, DOB Month, DOB Day, FICO Score, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, State, Zip Code, City, Country, Phone 1 Area Code, Phone 1 Prefix, Phone 1 Line Number, Phone 2 Area Code, Phone 2 Prefix, Phone 2 Line Number, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder; if none of the above apply, the cursor defaults to the Account ID field; cursor is set by moving -1 to the length attribute of the target field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cursor Positioning on First Error Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: The cursor is positioned on the first field that has a validation error, or on the appropriate starting field based on the current state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is preparing to send the screen and validation has been performed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets color attributes for screen fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the user navigated from the Account List screen (CCLISTMAPSET), the Account ID field is displayed in the default color; if the account filter is invalid, the Account ID field is displayed in red; if the account filter is blank and the program is in re-entry mode, the Account ID field shows '*' and is displayed in red; for each field that has a validation error (not-ok or blank flag set) and the program is in re-entry mode, the field is displayed in red; additionally, if the field was blank (mandatory but not supplied), an asterisk '*' is placed in the output field as a visual indicator; this applies to all validated fields: Account Status, Open Date parts, Credit Limit, Expiry Date parts, Cash Credit Limit, Reissue Date parts, Current Balance, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, SSN parts, DOB parts, FICO Score, First/Middle/Last Name, Address Line 1, State, Address Line 2, Zip Code, City, Country, Phone 1 and 2 parts, Primary Card Holder, and EFT Account ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Field Color Highlighting
all_rules.Rule_Description: Fields with validation errors are highlighted in red on the screen. Blank mandatory fields additionally show an asterisk placeholder. Fields navigated from the account list screen are shown in a distinct default color.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is preparing to send the screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets function key label attributes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the informational message area has no message, it is displayed in dark (non-highlighted) color; otherwise it is displayed in bright (highlighted) color; if the current state indicates changes have been made (any 'changes made' state) AND the update has not yet been completed, the PF12 function key label is highlighted (bright); if the current state is 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' (awaiting confirmation), both the PF05 and PF12 function key labels are highlighted (bright) to draw the user's attention to the available confirmation action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Function Key Availability Highlighting
all_rules.Rule_Description: The PF05 and PF12 function key labels on the screen are highlighted to indicate their availability based on the current processing state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen has been fully initialized with data, attributes, messages, and cursor position
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sends the screen to the user terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen map is sent using the current map name and mapset name; the screen is sent with the CURSOR option to position the cursor as specified, the ERASE option to clear the terminal screen before display, and the FREEKB option to unlock the keyboard for user input; the next map and mapset names are recorded in the card control area for session continuity

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Formatted Screen to User Terminal
all_rules.Rule_Description: The fully prepared screen with all data, field attributes, colors, cursor position, and function key labels is transmitted to the user's terminal.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update program has been invoked and is beginning execution
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program starts its main processing routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card work area (CC-WORK-AREA) and all miscellaneous working storage variables (WS-MISC-STORAGE) must be reset to their initial empty/default values, ensuring no stale data from any previous execution remains in working storage

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Working Storage on Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: All working storage variables and temporary storage areas used during account update processing must be cleared to their initial default values each time the program begins execution, ensuring no residual data from prior executions affects the current session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update program has been invoked and working storage has been initialized
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins its initialization sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The working storage communication area (WS-COMMAREA) must be cleared to its initial empty/default state before any session data is loaded or restored

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Communication Area on Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: The communication area (COMMAREA) used to pass data between transactions must be cleared at the start of each program execution to ensure a clean state before session data is selectively restored or initialized.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update program has initialized its working storage and communication areas
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets up its transaction context
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) must be stored in the working storage transaction ID field (WS-TRANID), and the return message flag must be set to OFF (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF) so that the first error encountered during processing will be captured as the displayed error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Transaction Identity
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must record its own transaction identifier in working storage at startup so that the transaction context is available throughout processing for navigation, return routing, and session management.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update program has completed its initial storage setup
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the session context
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the communication area length (EIBCALEN) equals zero — meaning no prior session data exists — OR if the calling program is the Main Menu program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM equals LIT-MENUPGM) AND the program re-entry flag is NOT set (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is false), then the session is treated as a fresh entry and the program proceeds to full initialization; otherwise the session is treated as a returning session and prior session data is restored

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Whether This is a Fresh Program Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must determine whether the current invocation is a completely new session or a return from a prior interaction. A fresh entry occurs either when there is no prior session data at all, or when the user has navigated here directly from the Main Menu for the first time (not a re-entry).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has determined this is a fresh entry — either no prior session data exists or the user has arrived from the Main Menu for the first time
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The fresh entry initialization path is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entire CardDemo shared communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) must be initialized to its default empty values, clearing all shared cross-program data fields including account ID, customer ID, card number, program routing fields, and user type indicators

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Shared CardDemo Communication Area for Fresh Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is entered fresh (no prior session or first entry from Main Menu), the shared CardDemo communication area that carries data across all programs in the CardDemo application suite must be fully cleared to ensure no cross-program data contamination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has determined this is a fresh entry and the shared CardDemo communication area has been initialized
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The fresh entry initialization path continues
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) must be initialized to its default empty values, clearing all local account update state flags, previously fetched account details, and any pending change data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Program-Specific Communication Area for Fresh Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is entered fresh, the program-specific communication area that holds local account update state and data must be fully cleared, ensuring the account update screen starts with no pre-loaded account or customer data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has determined this is a fresh entry and both communication areas have been initialized
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets its operational state flags
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program entry state flag must be set to ENTER mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER set to TRUE), indicating to all downstream processing that this is a first-time entry and the program should present the initial account search screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Program State to Fresh Entry Mode
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is entered fresh, the program state flag must be set to indicate this is a first-time entry so that subsequent processing logic correctly presents an empty search screen rather than attempting to display or process account details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has determined this is a fresh entry, communication areas have been initialized, and the program state has been set to ENTER mode
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program finalizes its fresh entry initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account details fetch state flag must be set to NOT FETCHED (ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED set to TRUE), indicating that no account data has been loaded and the user must first enter and submit a valid account number before any account or customer details can be displayed or edited

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Account Details as Not Yet Fetched on Fresh Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is entered fresh, the account details state must be explicitly marked as not yet fetched so that the screen correctly shows only the account number search field and does not attempt to display or validate account/customer detail fields.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has determined this is a returning session — prior session data exists (EIBCALEN is greater than zero) AND the entry is not a first-time arrival from the Main Menu
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The returning session restoration path is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The CardDemo shared communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) must be populated by copying the first portion of the passed communication area (DFHCOMMAREA) with a length equal to the size of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, restoring all shared cross-program data fields to their values from the previous interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Restore Shared CardDemo Communication Area for Returning Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is re-entered from a prior interaction (not a fresh start), the shared CardDemo communication area must be restored from the passed communication area data so that cross-program context such as account ID, customer ID, card number, and navigation routing are preserved from the previous interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has determined this is a returning session and the shared CardDemo communication area has been restored from the passed communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The returning session restoration path continues
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) must be populated by copying the second portion of the passed communication area (DFHCOMMAREA), starting at the position immediately after the CardDemo communication area (offset = LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1) and with a length equal to the size of WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, restoring all local account update state flags, previously fetched account data, and pending change information

all_rules.Rule_Name: Restore Program-Specific Communication Area for Returning Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is re-entered from a prior interaction, the program-specific communication area must be restored from the passed communication area data so that the account update state, previously fetched account details, and any pending changes are preserved exactly as they were at the end of the previous interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and presses any key on the terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system receives the key press input from the terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies and records the key pressed as one of the following logical key indicators: Enter key, Clear key, PA1 key, PA2 key, PF01 through PF12. Extended keys PF13 through PF24 are mapped to their base equivalents: PF13 maps to PF01, PF14 maps to PF02, PF15 maps to PF03, PF16 maps to PF04, PF17 maps to PF05, PF18 maps to PF06, PF19 maps to PF07, PF20 maps to PF08, PF21 maps to PF09, PF22 maps to PF10, PF23 maps to PF11, PF24 maps to PF12. Exactly one key indicator is set to active for use in subsequent processing.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture and Identify User Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses any key on the terminal, the system must identify and record which specific key was pressed so that subsequent processing can determine the appropriate action. Extended PF keys (PF13-PF24) are treated as their base equivalents (PF01-PF12).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed a key on the Account Update screen and the key has been identified
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the key against the current screen state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is marked as valid if it is the Enter key (always valid), OR it is PF03 (always valid), OR it is PF05 AND the current state is 'Changes Validated but Not Yet Confirmed', OR it is PF12 AND the current state is NOT 'Account Details Not Yet Fetched' (i.e., account details have already been loaded and displayed). If none of these conditions are met, the key is marked as invalid.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Overall Key Validity in Current Context
all_rules.Rule_Description: After identifying which key was pressed, the system evaluates whether that key is valid given the current state of the Account Update screen. Only specific keys are permitted under specific conditions; all others are considered invalid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen in any state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is recognized as valid and the system proceeds to process the user's screen input without any state-based restriction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enter Key Is Always a Valid Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Enter key is unconditionally valid on the Account Update screen regardless of the current screen state. Pressing Enter always triggers standard input processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen in any state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF03 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is recognized as valid and the system proceeds to exit the Account Update screen and return control to the calling program or main menu, without any state-based restriction

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF03 Key Is Always Valid for Exit
all_rules.Rule_Description: The PF03 key (Exit) is unconditionally valid on the Account Update screen regardless of the current screen state. Pressing PF03 always initiates the exit and return-to-menu process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and presses PF05
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the current screen state is 'Changes Validated but Not Yet Confirmed' (i.e., all field-level validations have passed and the system is prompting the user to confirm the update)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current state IS 'Changes Validated but Not Yet Confirmed', PF05 is marked as valid and the system proceeds to execute the save and update process. If the current state is NOT 'Changes Validated but Not Yet Confirmed' (for example, no account has been fetched, details are just being displayed, or changes have validation errors), PF05 is marked as invalid and is overridden to be treated as the Enter key.

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF05 Key Valid Only When Changes Are Validated and Awaiting Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The PF05 key (Save/Confirm) is a context-sensitive key that is only valid when the user has made changes to account or customer data, those changes have passed all validations, and the system is waiting for the user to explicitly confirm the save. PF05 is not valid at any other point in the workflow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and the current state is NOT 'Changes Validated but Not Yet Confirmed' (e.g., no account has been fetched, account details are displayed but no changes made, or changes have failed validation)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF05
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: PF05 is treated as an invalid key press. The system overrides the PF05 action and processes the interaction as if the Enter key had been pressed, continuing with standard input processing.

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF05 Not Valid Outside of Confirmation State
all_rules.Rule_Description: When PF05 is pressed but the screen is not in the 'Changes Validated but Not Yet Confirmed' state, the key press is considered invalid because there are no confirmed-valid changes ready to be saved.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and presses PF12
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the current screen state indicates that account details have already been fetched and displayed (i.e., the state is NOT 'Account Details Not Yet Fetched')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If account details HAVE been fetched and are displayed, PF12 is marked as valid and the system proceeds to refresh the screen with the original fetched data, cancelling any unsaved changes. If account details have NOT yet been fetched (the screen is in initial/search state), PF12 is marked as invalid and is overridden to be treated as the Enter key.

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF12 Key Valid Only When Account Details Have Been Fetched
