all_rules.Rule_Description: The PF12 key (Refresh/Cancel Changes) is a context-sensitive key that is only valid when account and customer details have already been retrieved and are currently displayed on the screen. PF12 is not valid when the screen is in its initial state with no account data loaded.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and the current state is 'Account Details Not Yet Fetched' (the screen is in its initial state, waiting for the user to enter an account number)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF12
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: PF12 is treated as an invalid key press. The system overrides the PF12 action and processes the interaction as if the Enter key had been pressed, continuing with standard input processing.

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF12 Not Valid When No Account Details Are Displayed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When PF12 is pressed but no account details have been fetched and displayed yet, the key press is considered invalid because there is no loaded account data to refresh or cancel changes against.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen in any state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key that is not Enter, PF03, a contextually valid PF05, or a contextually valid PF12 — including but not limited to PF01, PF02, PF04, PF06, PF07, PF08, PF09, PF10, PF11, CLEAR, PA1, or PA2
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is marked as invalid. The system overrides the key action and substitutes it with the Enter key action, so that the screen input is processed as a standard Enter key submission. No error message is displayed to the user for the invalid key — processing continues silently as Enter.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Any Unrecognized or Unsupported Key Is Treated as Enter
all_rules.Rule_Description: Any key press that is not explicitly supported by the Account Update screen (including PF01, PF02, PF04, PF06 through PF11, CLEAR, PA1, PA2, and any other unsupported keys) is treated as an invalid action and automatically overridden to behave as the Enter key, ensuring the screen continues to process normally.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A key has been pressed on the Account Update screen and has been evaluated as invalid (either an unsupported key type, or a context-sensitive key pressed outside its valid state)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines the key is invalid (the invalid key flag is active)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the active key indicator to Enter key, effectively replacing the invalid key action with Enter key processing. All subsequent processing proceeds as if the user had pressed the Enter key. This override applies to: unsupported keys (PF01, PF02, PF04, PF06-PF11, CLEAR, PA1, PA2), PF05 pressed when changes are not in 'validated but unconfirmed' state, and PF12 pressed when account details have not yet been fetched.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Key Override to Enter Key Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When any key is determined to be invalid in the current context, the system enforces a fallback mechanism that substitutes the invalid key with the Enter key, ensuring uninterrupted screen processing flow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Account Update screen and the communication area contains a previously recorded calling transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) that is not blank and not empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF03 to exit the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination transaction ID (CDEMO-TO-TRANID) to the calling transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) that was stored in the communication area, so control will be returned to the originating transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Return Destination Transaction When Calling Transaction Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF03 to exit, the system checks whether a calling transaction ID was recorded in the communication area. If a valid calling transaction ID exists, it is used as the return destination; otherwise, the system defaults to the main menu transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Account Update screen and the communication area does not contain a valid calling transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID is blank or empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF03 to exit the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination transaction ID (CDEMO-TO-TRANID) to the predefined main menu transaction ID (LIT-MENUTRANID), so control will be returned to the main menu

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Return Destination to Main Menu When No Calling Transaction Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF03 to exit and no calling transaction ID is recorded in the communication area (the program was entered directly or from the main menu), the system defaults the return destination to the main menu transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Account Update screen and the communication area contains a previously recorded calling program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) that is not blank and not empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF03 to exit the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program name (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) to the calling program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) that was stored in the communication area, so control will be returned to the originating program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Return Destination Program When Calling Program Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF03 to exit, the system checks whether a calling program name was recorded in the communication area. If a valid calling program name exists, it is used as the return destination program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Account Update screen and the communication area does not contain a valid calling program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is blank or empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF03 to exit the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program name (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) to the predefined main menu program name (LIT-MENUPGM), so control will be returned to the main menu program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Return Destination to Main Menu Program When No Calling Program Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF03 to exit and no calling program name is recorded in the communication area, the system defaults the return destination to the main menu program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF03 and the destination program and transaction have been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the communication area for the transfer of control
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the current Account Update transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) into the 'from transaction' field (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) and the current Account Update program name (LIT-THISPGM) into the 'from program' field (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the communication area, and also records the current map set name (LIT-THISMAPSET) into CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET and the current map name (LIT-THISMAP) into CDEMO-LAST-MAP

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Program as Originator in Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control, the system updates the communication area to record the Account Update program and its transaction as the originating source, so the destination program knows where it was called from.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF03 and the communication area is being prepared for transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the user context before transferring control
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the user type indicator (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER) to 'Standard User' in the communication area, indicating the receiving program should treat this as a regular user session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set User Type to Standard User on Exit
all_rules.Rule_Description: When exiting via PF03, the system sets the user type context to standard user (non-administrative) in the communication area, ensuring the destination program receives the correct user role context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF03 and the communication area is being prepared for transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the entry mode context before transferring control
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the program entry mode flag (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) to 'Enter' (fresh entry) in the communication area, so the destination program will initialize itself as a new entry rather than treating it as a screen re-entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Program Entry Mode to Fresh Entry on Exit
all_rules.Rule_Description: When exiting via PF03, the system sets the program entry mode to 'fresh entry' in the communication area, ensuring the destination program initializes itself as if being entered for the first time rather than as a re-entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination program name (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) has been determined (either the calling program or the main menu program), the user type is set to Standard User, the entry mode is set to Fresh Entry, and the communication area has been updated with the current program as the originator
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the transfer of control
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers control directly to the destination program identified by CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, passing the complete updated communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) to that program, and the destination program begins execution with the provided context

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Destination Program with Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all context has been set, the system transfers control directly to the determined destination program, passing the fully updated communication area so the destination program has all necessary session context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update program is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Either (a) there is no existing session communication area (first-time launch), OR (b) the calling program is the Main Menu program AND the program re-entry flag is NOT set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program is treated as a fresh entry: all communication area data and program working storage are fully reset to empty/initial values, the program state is set to 'Enter' mode, and the account details state is set to 'Details Not Fetched'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Fresh Program Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determine whether the current invocation is a fresh entry into the Account Update program — either the very first time it is launched (no prior session data exists) or when the user navigates to it directly from the Main Menu without having previously re-entered the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has been identified as a fresh entry (first launch or navigation from Main Menu without re-entry)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The fresh entry initialization logic executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The shared communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is fully initialized to empty values, the program-specific working area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is fully initialized to empty values, the program state flag is set to 'Program Enter', and the account details availability flag is set to 'Details Not Fetched'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset All Session Data on Fresh Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a fresh entry is detected, all previously held session data — including the shared communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) and the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) — must be completely cleared to prevent stale data from a prior session from appearing on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update screen is about to be sent to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen initialization routine (3100-SCREEN-INIT) executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen output area is cleared to low values; Screen Title Line 1 is populated from the standard title definition (CCDA-TITLE01); Screen Title Line 2 is populated from the standard title definition (CCDA-TITLE02); the Transaction Name field is set to the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID); the Program Name field is set to the current program name (LIT-THISPGM); the Current Date field is formatted as MM/DD/YY using the system current date; and the Current Time field is formatted as HH:MM:SS using the system current time

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Screen Header with Current Date and Time
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying any screen, the screen header area must be populated with static identification information (screen titles, transaction ID, program name) and dynamic runtime information (current system date and current system time) so the user can identify the screen context and when it was rendered.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen variable setup routine (3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS) is executing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program state flag is set to 'Program Enter' (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All account and customer data field population steps are bypassed entirely — no account number, no account details, no customer details are moved to the screen output fields; the routine exits without populating any data fields

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Account and Customer Data Population on Fresh Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in 'Enter' mode (fresh entry), the screen variable setup routine must skip all account and customer data field population entirely. No account details, customer details, balances, dates, names, or address information should be moved to the screen output area during a fresh entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen variable setup routine is determining what values to display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account details state is 'Details Not Fetched' OR the account number is zero/empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All of the following screen output fields are set to blank (low values): Account Status, Credit Limit, Current Balance, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date Year/Month/Day, Expiry Date Year/Month/Day, Reissue Date Year/Month/Day, Group ID, Customer Number, SSN Part 1/Part 2/Part 3, FICO Score, Date of Birth Year/Month/Day, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City, State, Zip Code, Country, Phone 1 Area Code/Prefix/Line Number, Phone 2 Area Code/Prefix/Line Number, Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, and Primary Cardholder Flag

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display All Account and Customer Fields as Blank
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account details have not yet been fetched (initial state), all account and customer detail fields on the screen must be set to blank (low values) so the user sees a completely empty form. This covers all data fields including account status, all financial limits and balances, all date fields, group ID, customer number, SSN parts, FICO score, date of birth, customer name fields, all address fields, both phone numbers, government ID, EFT account ID, and primary cardholder flag.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The informational message setup routine (3250-SETUP-INFOMSG) is executing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program state is 'Program Enter' (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) OR the account details state is 'Details Not Fetched' (ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED) OR there is no informational message currently set (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message flag is set to 'Prompt for Search Keys' (PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS), and the corresponding search key prompt message text is moved to the informational message output field (INFOMSGO) on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Search Key Prompt Message on Fresh Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in fresh entry mode or account details have not yet been fetched, the informational message area on the screen must display a prompt instructing the user to enter an Account Number to begin a search. This guides the user on the required first action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen attribute setup routine (3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS) is executing and calls the protect-all routine (3310-PROTECT-ALL-ATTRS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The protect-all-attributes routine executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All of the following screen input fields are set to protected (read-only) mode using the DFHBMPRF attribute: Account Number, Account Status, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Balance, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date Year/Month/Day, Expiry Date Year/Month/Day, Reissue Date Year/Month/Day, Group ID, Customer Number, SSN Part 1/Part 2/Part 3, FICO Score, Date of Birth Year/Month/Day, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City, State, Zip Code, Country, Phone 1 Area Code/Prefix/Line Number, Phone 2 Area Code/Prefix/Line Number, Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, Primary Cardholder Flag, and the Informational Message field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Protect All Screen Fields by Default
all_rules.Rule_Description: As the first step in setting screen field protection attributes, all input fields on the Account Update screen must be set to protected (read-only) mode. This is the default baseline protection applied before selectively unprotecting specific fields based on the current program state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All screen fields have been set to protected mode and the screen attribute setup routine is evaluating the current program state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account details state is 'Details Not Fetched' (ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Number input field attribute (ACCTSIDA) is set to 'field select enabled' (DFHBMFSE), making it the only editable field on the screen; all other fields remain protected

all_rules.Rule_Name: Make Only Account Number Field Editable on Fresh Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account details have not yet been fetched (fresh entry state), only the Account Number entry field should be made editable so the user can enter a search value. All other fields remain protected. The Account Number field is unprotected by setting it to 'field select enabled' (DFHBMFSE) attribute.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen attribute setup routine is setting cursor position based on the current state and validation flags
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account filter flag is 'Not OK' (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK) OR the account filter flag is 'Blank' (FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK) OR no other specific field error flag is set (falls to OTHERWISE condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor length attribute for the Account Number field (ACCTSIDL) is set to -1, which instructs the terminal to position the cursor on the Account Number input field when the screen is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Position Cursor on Account Number Field for Fresh Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no account data has been fetched and the screen is in fresh entry state, the cursor must be automatically positioned on the Account Number field so the user can immediately begin typing the account number without manually navigating to the field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The informational message attribute setup routine (3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS) is executing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account update state is NOT 'Changes Made' (ACUP-CHANGES-MADE is FALSE) AND the informational message state is NOT 'Prompt for Confirmation' (PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION is FALSE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Neither the PF5 key attribute (FKEY05A) nor the PF12 key attribute (FKEY12A) is set to the highlighted/bright attribute (DFHBMASB); both action keys remain in their default non-highlighted display state, indicating they are not currently active

all_rules.Rule_Name: Suppress Action Key Highlighting When No Data is Loaded
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen is in fresh entry state with no account data loaded, the PF5 (Confirm/Save) and PF12 (Re-fetch) action keys must not be visually highlighted or activated. These keys are only highlighted when there is data to act upon — PF5 when changes are pending confirmation, and PF12 when changes have been made.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen output area (CACTUPAO) has been fully prepared with blank data fields, the search key prompt message, all fields protected except Account Number, and no action keys highlighted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen send routine (3400-SEND-SCREEN) executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen map (LIT-THISMAP) from the map set (LIT-THISMAPSET) is sent to the terminal using the prepared output area (CACTUPAO) with the following settings: cursor is automatically positioned on the designated field (CURSOR option active), the terminal screen is fully erased before the new screen is displayed (ERASE option), and the keyboard is freed/unlocked so the user can immediately type (FREEKB option); the next map and mapset are recorded in the session navigation fields (CCARD-NEXT-MAP and CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Blank Account Update Screen to User
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all screen fields, messages, and attributes have been prepared for a fresh entry, the completed blank screen must be transmitted to the user's terminal. The screen is sent with cursor positioning enabled, the terminal screen is erased before display, and the keyboard is unlocked so the user can immediately begin entering data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account update process has completed and the program state is either 'Changes Okayed and Done' (successful update) or 'Changes Failed' (failed update attempt)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the current program state in the main processing decision block
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds with the post-update screen reset workflow for both successful and failed update outcomes, treating both outcomes identically for the purpose of resetting the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Post-Update Outcome to Trigger Screen Reset
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the update processing completes, the system evaluates whether the outcome was a successful update or a failed update attempt, and in both cases triggers the same screen reset workflow to allow a new account search.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account update process has completed with either a successful update (ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE) or a failed update (ACUP-CHANGES-FAILED)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the post-update reset sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program-specific working area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is fully initialized to remove all intermediate processing data, flags, and state information from the previous update session; and the miscellaneous storage area (WS-MISC-STORAGE) is also fully initialized to clear any temporary working values

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Program Working Area After Update Outcome
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful or failed update, all intermediate program working data, processing flags, and the program-specific communication area are cleared to remove any residual state from the previous account update session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account update process has completed with either a successful or failed update outcome, and the shared session context (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) still holds the account number from the previous search
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the post-update reset sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID stored in the shared session communication area (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) is set to zeroes, effectively removing the previously searched account number from the active session context

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Previously Searched Account ID from Context
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful or failed update, the account number that was previously searched and used in the update session is removed from the shared session context so that no stale account reference persists into the next user interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program working area and account ID have been cleared following a successful or failed update
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to display the blank account update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program entry state flag (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) is set to TRUE, marking the program as being in fresh entry mode so that the screen setup routines render an initial blank screen with only the account number field available for input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Program State to Fresh Entry Mode Before Displaying Blank Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before sending the blank reset screen, the program state is temporarily set to 'fresh entry' mode so that the screen rendering logic treats the upcoming display as an initial program entry, resulting in a fully blank and unprotected account search screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program state has been set to fresh entry mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is TRUE) and all working areas have been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the send-map routine (3000-SEND-MAP)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is initialized with current date and time; all account and customer detail fields (Account Status, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Balance, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date, Group ID, Customer Number, SSN parts, FICO Score, Date of Birth, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Lines 1 and 2, City, State, Zip, Country, Phone Numbers 1 and 2, Government ID, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder flag) are set to blank/empty; the information message area displays a prompt for the user to enter a search key (account number); all fields except the account number entry field are protected from input; and the screen is sent to the terminal with the keyboard unlocked and the screen erased

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Blank Account Update Screen for New Search
all_rules.Rule_Description: After resetting the program state to fresh entry mode, a blank account update screen is sent to the user. All account and customer detail fields are empty and protected, and only the account number search field is available for input, prompting the user to begin a new account search.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The blank account update screen has been successfully sent to the user following a post-update reset
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes the screen send operation and prepares to return control to await the next user input
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is set to TRUE, marking that the screen has been displayed and the next interaction will be treated as a re-entry to the program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Program State to Re-Entry Mode After Blank Screen is Sent
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the blank account update screen has been sent to the user, the program state is updated to re-entry mode to indicate that the screen has already been displayed once. This ensures that on the next user interaction, the system correctly identifies this as a re-entry rather than a first-time entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The blank account update screen has been sent and the program state has been set to re-entry mode
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the post-update reset sequence before returning control to await the next user input
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account details status flag (ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED) is set to TRUE, indicating that no account data is currently loaded; on the next user interaction, the system will treat any input as a new account search request rather than an attempt to edit previously loaded account details

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Account Details as Not Fetched After Screen Reset
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the blank screen is sent and the program is placed in re-entry mode, the account details status is explicitly set to 'not fetched' to indicate that no account data is currently loaded in the session. This ensures the next user interaction correctly routes to the account search flow rather than the account edit flow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The post-update reset sequence is complete: working areas cleared, account ID cleared, program state set to re-entry mode, account details marked as not fetched, and blank screen sent to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the common return routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Any pending return message is moved to the screen error message area; the current shared session state (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) and program-specific state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) are saved together into the return communication area; control is returned to the CICS environment specifying the same transaction ID to be re-invoked when the user next presses a key, with the saved communication area passed along so the session state is fully restored on the next interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Control to Await Next User Input After Reset
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all reset steps are complete, the system saves the current session state and returns control to the terminal, waiting for the user to enter a new account number. The session state is preserved in the communication area so it can be restored on the next interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account update screen has been submitted by the user and the system is about to capture the entered data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins the screen input receive process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All fields in the new account and customer details working area (ACUP-NEW-DETAILS) are initialized to empty/default values before any screen field values are read, ensuring a clean slate for the current input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize New Input Data Area Before Capturing Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before capturing any user-entered data from the account update screen, all previously held new/pending input values must be cleared to ensure no stale data from a prior interaction contaminates the current input capture cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the account update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Account ID field (ACCTSIDI) from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Account ID field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, both the working Account ID (CC-ACCT-ID) and the new Account ID input field (ACUP-NEW-ACCT-ID-X) are cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered Account ID value is stored in both CC-ACCT-ID and ACUP-NEW-ACCT-ID-X

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Account ID from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account ID entered by the user on the account update screen must be captured and stored. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank (spaces), the Account ID is treated as not provided and cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored as the working Account ID for subsequent processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the account update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that the screen is currently in Search Mode, meaning account details have not yet been fetched (ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system stops capturing screen input immediately after reading the Account ID field and exits the input capture process; no account status, financial limits, balances, dates, customer details, or any other fields are read from the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Restrict Full Field Capture to Edit Mode Only
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen is in Search Mode (no account details have been fetched and displayed yet), only the Account ID field is relevant. All other account and customer detail fields on the screen are ignored and not captured, because the user has not yet retrieved an account to edit.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Account Status field (ACSTTUSI) from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Account Status field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new Account Active Status (ACUP-NEW-ACTIVE-STATUS) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in ACUP-NEW-ACTIVE-STATUS

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Account Active Status from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Active Status field entered by the user must be captured. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the status is treated as not provided and cleared. Otherwise, the entered value (expected to be Y or N) is stored for subsequent validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Credit Limit field (ACRDLIMI) from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Credit Limit field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new Credit Limit text field (ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-X) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); if a value is entered, it is stored in ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-X, and additionally, if the entered text passes a signed numeric format check (TEST-NUMVAL-C returns 0), the numeric equivalent is computed using NUMVAL-C and stored in ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-N; if the text is not a valid signed number, the numeric field is left unchanged

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Credit Limit from Screen Input with Numeric Conversion
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Credit Limit entered by the user must be captured as text. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the Credit Limit is cleared. If a value is entered, it is stored as text and, if it is a valid signed numeric value, it is also converted to a numeric form for subsequent financial calculations and comparisons.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Cash Credit Limit field (ACSHLIMI) from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Cash Credit Limit field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new Cash Credit Limit text field (ACUP-NEW-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-X) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); if a value is entered, it is stored in ACUP-NEW-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-X, and additionally, if the entered text passes a signed numeric format check (TEST-NUMVAL-C returns 0), the numeric equivalent is computed using NUMVAL-C and stored in ACUP-NEW-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-N; if the text is not a valid signed number, the numeric field is left unchanged

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Cash Credit Limit from Screen Input with Numeric Conversion
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Cash Credit Limit entered by the user must be captured as text. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the Cash Credit Limit is cleared. If a value is entered, it is stored as text and, if it is a valid signed numeric value, it is also converted to a numeric form for subsequent financial calculations and comparisons.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Current Balance field (ACURBALI) from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Current Balance field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new Current Balance text field (ACUP-NEW-CURR-BAL-X) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); if a value is entered, it is stored in ACUP-NEW-CURR-BAL-X, and additionally, if the entered text passes a signed numeric format check (TEST-NUMVAL-C returns 0), the numeric equivalent is computed using NUMVAL-C and stored in ACUP-NEW-CURR-BAL-N; if the text is not a valid signed number, the numeric field is left unchanged

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Current Balance from Screen Input with Numeric Conversion
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Current Balance entered by the user must be captured as text. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the Current Balance is cleared. If a value is entered, it is stored as text and, if it is a valid signed numeric value, it is also converted to a numeric form for subsequent financial calculations and comparisons.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Current Cycle Credit field (ACRCYCRI) from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Current Cycle Credit field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new Current Cycle Credit text field (ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-X) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); if a value is entered, it is stored in ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-X, and additionally, if the entered text passes a signed numeric format check (TEST-NUMVAL-C returns 0), the numeric equivalent is computed using NUMVAL-C and stored in ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-N; if the text is not a valid signed number, the numeric field is left unchanged

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Current Cycle Credit from Screen Input with Numeric Conversion
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Current Cycle Credit entered by the user must be captured as text. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the Current Cycle Credit is cleared. If a value is entered, it is stored as text and, if it is a valid signed numeric value, it is also converted to a numeric form for subsequent financial calculations and comparisons.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Current Cycle Debit field (ACRCYDBI) from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Current Cycle Debit field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new Current Cycle Debit text field (ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-X) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); if a value is entered, it is stored in ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-X, and additionally, if the entered text passes a signed numeric format check (TEST-NUMVAL-C returns 0), the numeric equivalent is computed using NUMVAL-C and stored in ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-N; if the text is not a valid signed number, the numeric field is left unchanged

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Current Cycle Debit from Screen Input with Numeric Conversion
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Current Cycle Debit entered by the user must be captured as text. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the Current Cycle Debit is cleared. If a value is entered, it is stored as text and, if it is a valid signed numeric value, it is also converted to a numeric form for subsequent financial calculations and comparisons.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Open Date Year (OPNYEARI), Open Date Month (OPNMONI), and Open Date Day (OPNDAYI) fields from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each of the three Open Date components independently: if the field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the corresponding new value (ACUP-NEW-OPEN-YEAR, ACUP-NEW-OPEN-MON, ACUP-NEW-OPEN-DAY respectively) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in the corresponding new field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Account Open Date Components from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Open Date is entered by the user as three separate fields: Year, Month, and Day. Each component must be individually captured. If any component contains an asterisk '*' or is blank, that specific component is cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent date validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Expiry Date Year (EXPYEARI), Expiry Date Month (EXPMONI), and Expiry Date Day (EXPDAYI) fields from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each of the three Expiry Date components independently: if the field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the corresponding new value (ACUP-NEW-EXP-YEAR, ACUP-NEW-EXP-MON, ACUP-NEW-EXP-DAY respectively) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in the corresponding new field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Account Expiry Date Components from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Expiry Date is entered by the user as three separate fields: Year, Month, and Day. Each component must be individually captured. If any component contains an asterisk '*' or is blank, that specific component is cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent date validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Reissue Date Year (RISYEARI), Reissue Date Month (RISMONI), and Reissue Date Day (RISDAYI) fields from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each of the three Reissue Date components independently: if the field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the corresponding new value (ACUP-NEW-REISSUE-YEAR, ACUP-NEW-REISSUE-MON, ACUP-NEW-REISSUE-DAY respectively) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in the corresponding new field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Account Reissue Date Components from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Reissue Date is entered by the user as three separate fields: Year, Month, and Day. Each component must be individually captured. If any component contains an asterisk '*' or is blank, that specific component is cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent date validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Group ID field (AADDGRPI) from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Group ID field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new Group ID (ACUP-NEW-GROUP-ID) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in ACUP-NEW-GROUP-ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Account Group ID from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Group ID entered by the user must be captured. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the Group ID is treated as not provided and cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Customer ID field (ACSTNUMI) from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Customer ID field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new Customer ID text field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-ID-X) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in ACUP-NEW-CUST-ID-X

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Customer ID from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Customer ID displayed on the account update screen must be captured. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the Customer ID is treated as not provided and cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the SSN Part 1 (ACTSSN1I - first 3 digits), SSN Part 2 (ACTSSN2I - middle 2 digits), and SSN Part 3 (ACTSSN3I - last 4 digits) fields from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each of the three SSN parts independently: if the field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the corresponding new SSN part (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-1, ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-2, ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-3 respectively) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in the corresponding new SSN part field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Social Security Number Parts from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's Social Security Number (SSN) is entered as three separate parts: the first 3 digits, the middle 2 digits, and the last 4 digits. Each part must be individually captured. If any part contains an asterisk '*' or is blank, that specific part is cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent SSN validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Date of Birth Year (DOBYEARI), Date of Birth Month (DOBMONI), and Date of Birth Day (DOBDAYI) fields from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each of the three Date of Birth components independently: if the field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the corresponding new value (ACUP-NEW-CUST-DOB-YEAR, ACUP-NEW-CUST-DOB-MON, ACUP-NEW-CUST-DOB-DAY respectively) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in the corresponding new field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Customer Date of Birth Components from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's Date of Birth is entered as three separate fields: Year, Month, and Day. Each component must be individually captured. If any component contains an asterisk '*' or is blank, that specific component is cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent date of birth validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the FICO Score field (ACSTFCOI) from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the FICO Score field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new FICO Score text field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-FICO-SCORE-X) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in ACUP-NEW-CUST-FICO-SCORE-X

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Customer FICO Credit Score from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's FICO Credit Score entered by the user must be captured. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the FICO Score is treated as not provided and cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent FICO score range validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the First Name (ACSFNAMI), Middle Name (ACSMNAMI), and Last Name (ACSLNAMI) fields from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each name field independently: if the field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the corresponding new name field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-FIRST-NAME, ACUP-NEW-CUST-MIDDLE-NAME, ACUP-NEW-CUST-LAST-NAME respectively) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in the corresponding new name field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Customer Name Fields from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's First Name, Middle Name, and Last Name are entered as separate fields. Each name field must be individually captured. If any name field contains an asterisk '*' or is blank, that specific field is cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent name validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Address Line 1 (ACSADL1I), Address Line 2 (ACSADL2I), and City (ACSCITYI) fields from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each address field independently: if the field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the corresponding new address field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-LINE-1, ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-LINE-2, ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-LINE-3 respectively) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in the corresponding new address field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Customer Address Lines and City from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's Address Line 1, Address Line 2, and City are entered as separate fields. Each address field must be individually captured. If any address field contains an asterisk '*' or is blank, that specific field is cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent address validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the State Code field (ACSSTTEI) from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the State Code field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new State Code (ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Customer State Code from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's State Code entered by the user must be captured. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the State Code is treated as not provided and cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent US state code validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Country Code field (ACSCTRYI) from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Country Code field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new Country Code (ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Customer Country Code from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's Country Code entered by the user must be captured. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the Country Code is treated as not provided and cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent country code validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Zip Code field (ACSZIPCI) from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Zip Code field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new Zip Code (ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-ZIP) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-ZIP

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Customer Zip Code from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's Zip Code entered by the user must be captured. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the Zip Code is treated as not provided and cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent zip code validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Primary Phone Area Code (ACSPH1AI), Primary Phone Prefix (ACSPH1BI), and Primary Phone Line Number (ACSPH1CI) fields from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each of the three Primary Phone Number parts independently: if the field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the corresponding new phone part (ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1A, ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1B, ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1C respectively) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in the corresponding new phone part field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Primary Phone Number Parts from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's Primary Phone Number is entered as three separate parts: Area Code (3 digits), Prefix (3 digits), and Line Number (4 digits). Each part must be individually captured. If any part contains an asterisk '*' or is blank, that specific part is cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent phone number validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Secondary Phone Area Code (ACSPH2AI), Secondary Phone Prefix (ACSPH2BI), and Secondary Phone Line Number (ACSPH2CI) fields from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each of the three Secondary Phone Number parts independently: if the field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the corresponding new phone part (ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2A, ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2B, ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2C respectively) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in the corresponding new phone part field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Secondary Phone Number Parts from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's Secondary Phone Number is entered as three separate parts: Area Code (3 digits), Prefix (3 digits), and Line Number (4 digits). Each part must be individually captured. If any part contains an asterisk '*' or is blank, that specific part is cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent phone number validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Government Issued ID field (ACSGOVTI) from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Government Issued ID field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new Government Issued ID (ACUP-NEW-CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in ACUP-NEW-CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Customer Government Issued ID from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's Government Issued ID entered by the user must be captured. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the Government Issued ID is treated as not provided and cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the EFT Account ID field (ACSEFTCI) from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the EFT Account ID field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new EFT Account ID (ACUP-NEW-CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in ACUP-NEW-CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Customer EFT Account ID from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) Account ID entered by the user must be captured. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the EFT Account ID is treated as not provided and cleared. Otherwise, the entered value is stored for subsequent EFT account ID validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Edit Mode with account details already fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Primary Card Holder Indicator field (ACSPFLGI) from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Primary Card Holder Indicator field contains an asterisk '*' or spaces, the new Primary Card Holder Indicator (ACUP-NEW-CUST-PRI-HOLDER-IND) is cleared to empty (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the entered value is stored in ACUP-NEW-CUST-PRI-HOLDER-IND

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Primary Card Holder Indicator from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Primary Card Holder Indicator entered by the user must be captured. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank, the indicator is treated as not provided and cleared. Otherwise, the entered value (expected to be Y or N) is stored for subsequent validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has submitted the form with the Account Number field left blank, containing only spaces, or containing no value (empty/low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs account number validation on the submitted Account Number field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) mark the account number filter status as 'Blank' (invalid), (2) set the overall input status to 'Error', (3) display a prompt message asking the user to enter an account number, (4) reset both the session Account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) and the new Account ID working field (ACUP-NEW-ACCT-ID) to zero, and (5) stop further account number validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Number Blank or Empty Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the user has entered an account number before any further processing. If the account number field is left blank or empty, the system must prompt the user to provide one and reset the account identifier to zero.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a non-blank value in the Account Number field on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the entered Account Number consists entirely of numeric digits
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Account Number contains any non-numeric characters, the system must: (1) set the overall input status to 'Error', (2) display the error message 'Account Number if supplied must be a 11 digit Non-Zero Number', (3) reset the session Account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) to zero, and (4) stop further account number validation. If the Account Number is fully numeric, processing continues to the zero-value check

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Number Must Be Numeric
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the account number entered by the user contains only numeric digits. If the account number contains any non-numeric characters, it is rejected with a specific error message indicating the required format.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a numeric value in the Account Number field on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the numeric Account Number has a value equal to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Account Number equals zero, the system must: (1) set the overall input status to 'Error', (2) display the error message 'Account Number if supplied must be a 11 digit Non-Zero Number', (3) reset the session Account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) to zero, and (4) stop further account number validation. If the Account Number is non-zero, processing continues to mark the account number as valid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Number Must Be Non-Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the account number entered by the user is not zero. An account number of all zeros is not a valid account identifier and must be rejected with the same format error message as a non-numeric entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered an Account Number that is non-blank, fully numeric, and non-zero on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account number successfully passes all validation checks (blank check, numeric check, and zero check)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) copy the validated Account Number into the session Account ID field (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) for use in subsequent account lookup operations, (2) mark the account number filter status as 'Valid' (FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID), and (3) allow processing to continue to the account data retrieval step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Number Valid - Store for Further Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the account number passes all validation checks (non-blank, numeric, and non-zero), it is accepted as a valid 11-digit account number and stored in the session context for subsequent account lookup and processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid 11-digit non-zero Account ID has been entered and confirmed as the search key for account data retrieval
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the account data lookup process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system searches the Card Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX) using the Account ID as the unique search key to locate the associated customer ID and card number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initiate Card Cross-Reference Lookup by Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account data lookup is triggered, the system must search the Card Cross-Reference file using the provided Account ID as the search key to locate the associated customer and card details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched the Card Cross-Reference file using the Account ID as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID is found in the Card Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts the Customer ID (XREF-CUST-ID) and stores it in the session communication area (CDEMO-CUST-ID), and extracts the Card Number (XREF-CARD-NUM) and stores it in the session communication area (CDEMO-CARD-NUM), making both values available for subsequent account and customer master data retrieval

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Cross-Reference Lookup - Extract Customer ID and Card Number
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account ID is found in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system must extract and store the associated Customer ID and Card Number for use in subsequent lookups.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched the Card Cross-Reference file using the provided Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the account filter as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK), sets an input error condition, and if no prior error message has been set, constructs and displays the error message: 'Account: [Account ID] not found in Cross ref file. Resp: [response code] Reas: [reason code]', and the account data lookup process is terminated without proceeding to the Account Master or Customer Master lookups

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Not Found in Card Cross-Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the provided Account ID does not exist in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system must mark the account search as invalid and display a descriptive error message identifying the account number and the file where it was not found.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to search the Card Cross-Reference file using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The lookup results in an unexpected outcome that is neither a successful find nor a standard 'not found' response
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the account filter as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK), sets an input error condition, records the operation name as 'READ', records the file name (LIT-CARDXREFNAME-ACCT-PATH), captures the response and reason codes, and sets the standard file error message; the account data lookup process is terminated without proceeding to further lookups

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unexpected Failure During Cross-Reference Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected issue occurs during the Card Cross-Reference file lookup (neither a successful read nor a 'not found' response), the system must mark the account as invalid and record a system-level error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Cross-Reference lookup has completed successfully and both Customer ID and Card Number have been stored in the session communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The cross-reference lookup step ends with a successful outcome
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to the next step in the account data lookup sequence, which is reading the Account Master file (9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT) using the same Account ID to retrieve full account details

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Account Master Retrieval After Successful Cross-Reference
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving the Customer ID and Card Number from the Card Cross-Reference file, the system must continue the account data lookup by proceeding to retrieve account details from the Account Master file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Cross-Reference file lookup has failed, either because the account was not found or due to an unexpected issue, and the account filter flag has been set to invalid
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks the account filter validity flag after the cross-reference lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system exits the account data lookup process immediately (GO TO 9000-READ-ACCT-EXIT) without performing any further lookups (Account Master or Customer Master), and the error message previously set is displayed to the user on the account update screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Account Lookup and Return Error to Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card Cross-Reference lookup fails for any reason (account not found or unexpected issue), the account data lookup process must be terminated immediately and the user must be returned to the screen with an appropriate error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid Account ID has been provided and the Cross-Reference lookup has already succeeded in the prior step
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a lookup of the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) using the Account ID as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the full account record containing Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date, and Group ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Account Master File by Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account lookup is initiated, the system retrieves the full account record from the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) using the Account ID as the unique search key. This is the primary data retrieval step to obtain all account-level details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup of the Account Master File using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account record is found successfully in the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the account as found (FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER = TRUE) and the following account details become available for use: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date (Year/Month/Day), Expiry Date (Year/Month/Day), Reissue Date (Year/Month/Day), and Group ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Successfully Found in Account Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Master File lookup returns a successful result, the system marks the account as found and makes all retrieved account details available for display and further processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup of the Account Master File using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No account record matching the provided Account ID is found in the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag (INPUT-ERROR = TRUE), marks the account filter as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK = TRUE), and if no prior error message has been set, prepares the error message: 'Account: [Account ID] not found in Acct Master file'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Not Found in Account Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Master File lookup finds no matching record for the provided Account ID, the system flags an input error and prepares a descriptive error message to inform the user that the account does not exist in the Account Master File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup of the Account Master File using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Master File lookup fails due to an unexpected error (not a not-found condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag (INPUT-ERROR = TRUE), marks the account filter as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK = TRUE), and prepares a standard file error message indicating the operation was a READ on the Account Master File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Master File Lookup Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Master File lookup encounters an unexpected failure (other than a simple not-found condition), the system flags an input error and prepares a generic file error message to inform the user that the account lookup could not be completed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master File lookup has resulted in either a not-found condition or an unexpected error
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the result of the Account Master File lookup and determines the account was not successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system immediately halts the account data retrieval process (exits 9000-READ-ACCT), does not proceed to Customer Data Retrieval, and returns the error condition and message to the screen display for the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stop Processing and Return Error When Account Not Retrieved
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Master File lookup fails for any reason (not found or unexpected error), the system immediately stops the account data retrieval process and returns control to the screen display with the error message, without proceeding to Customer Data Retrieval.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master File lookup has completed successfully and the account record has been marked as found
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the account lookup result and confirms the account was found
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to the next step in the retrieval sequence — Customer Data Retrieval — using the Customer ID (CDEMO-CUST-ID) that was obtained from the Card Cross-Reference lookup

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Customer Data Retrieval After Successful Account Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Master File lookup succeeds, the system continues the data retrieval sequence by proceeding to retrieve the associated customer details using the Customer ID obtained from the earlier Cross-Reference lookup.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master File lookup has succeeded and the account record is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched account data as original reference values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system saves the following account fields as original 'old' values for change-detection purposes: Account ID (ACUP-OLD-ACCT-ID), Active Status (ACUP-OLD-ACTIVE-STATUS), Current Balance (ACUP-OLD-CURR-BAL-N), Credit Limit (ACUP-OLD-CREDIT-LIMIT-N), Cash Credit Limit (ACUP-OLD-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-N), Current Cycle Credit (ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-N), Current Cycle Debit (ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-N), Open Date split into Year (ACUP-OLD-OPEN-YEAR), Month (ACUP-OLD-OPEN-MON), Day (ACUP-OLD-OPEN-DAY), Expiry Date split into Year (ACUP-OLD-EXP-YEAR), Month (ACUP-OLD-EXP-MON), Day (ACUP-OLD-EXP-DAY), Reissue Date split into Year (ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-YEAR), Month (ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-MON), Day (ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-DAY), and Group ID (ACUP-OLD-GROUP-ID)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Retrieved Account Details as Original Reference Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all three lookups (Cross-Reference, Account Master, Customer Master) succeed, the system stores all retrieved account field values as the original 'old' reference values. These stored values are later used to detect whether the user has made any changes and to detect concurrent modifications by other users before saving updates.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid Customer ID has been retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference file during the account lookup process
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to read the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT) using the Customer ID as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer Master file is accessed using the Customer ID to locate the matching customer record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Customer Record from Customer Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system uses the Customer ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference lookup to read the Customer Master file and retrieve the full customer profile.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has submitted a read request to the Customer Master file using a Customer ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A matching customer record is found in the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the customer as successfully found, and the following customer data fields become available: First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City (Address Line 3), State Code, Zip Code, Country Code, Primary Phone Number, Secondary Phone Number, Social Security Number, Date of Birth, FICO Credit Score, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator, and Government Issued ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Record Successfully Found in Customer Master
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Customer Master file contains a record matching the provided Customer ID, the system marks the customer as found and makes the full customer profile available for display and editing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has submitted a read request to the Customer Master file using a Customer ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No matching customer record is found in the Customer Master file for the provided Customer ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag, sets the customer filter status to 'not found', and displays the error message: 'CustId: [Customer ID] not found in customer master' along with the response and reason codes from the file system

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Record Not Found in Customer Master
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no customer record exists in the Customer Master file for the given Customer ID, the system sets an error condition and generates an appropriate error message to be displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched customer data as original values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following customer identity fields are stored as original values: Customer ID, Social Security Number (full), Date of Birth Year, Date of Birth Month, Date of Birth Day, FICO Credit Score, First Name, Middle Name, and Last Name

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Customer Personal Identity Data as Original Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving the customer record, the system stores the customer's personal identity information as the original baseline values to enable change detection when the user submits edits.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched customer address data as original values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following customer address fields are stored as original values: Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City (Address Line 3), State Code, Country Code, and Zip Code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Customer Address Data as Original Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving the customer record, the system stores the customer's full address information as the original baseline values to enable change detection when the user submits edits.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched customer contact and financial data as original values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following customer contact and financial fields are stored as original values: Primary Phone Number, Secondary Phone Number, Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Customer Contact and Financial Data as Original Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving the customer record, the system stores the customer's contact details and financial profile data as the original baseline values to enable change detection when the user submits edits.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched data into the session context
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer ID, First Name, Middle Name, and Last Name are copied into the session-level communication area (CDEMO) so they are accessible throughout the current user session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Propagate Customer Name to Session Context
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving the customer record, the system copies the customer's name and identifiers into the active session communication area so they are available across the application for display and reference.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system attempted to read the Customer Master file and the customer record was not found
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The customer not-found error condition is detected
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account data retrieval process exits immediately without storing any fetched data, and the error message is passed back to the screen display for the user to see; no account or customer data is presented for editing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Exit Account Retrieval Process on Customer Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the customer record cannot be found in the Customer Master file, the account retrieval process is immediately terminated and control is returned to the screen display with the error condition set, preventing any further data processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully retrieved account and customer data from the Account Master, Customer Master, and Card Cross-Reference files for a given Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The process to store fetched data as original values begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entire original details storage area (ACUP-OLD-DETAILS) is cleared and initialized to its default empty state before any new values are written into it, ensuring a clean baseline for subsequent change detection

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Original Details Storage Before Saving Fetched Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before storing any retrieved account or customer data as original values, the original details storage area must be fully cleared to ensure no stale data from a previous session or lookup contaminates the new comparison baseline.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master file record has been successfully read for the requested Account ID, providing the Account ID and Account Active Status
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched account data as original values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID from the Account Master record is saved as the Original Account ID (ACUP-OLD-ACCT-ID), and the Account Active Status from the Account Master record is saved as the Original Account Active Status (ACUP-OLD-ACTIVE-STATUS)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Account Identity and Status as Original Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account ID retrieved from the Account Master file and the Account Active Status must be preserved as the original (baseline) values so that any user modifications to these fields can be detected during the change comparison step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master file record has been successfully read, providing the five financial values: Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit amount, and Current Cycle Debit amount
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched account financial data as original values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Each financial value is saved individually as its corresponding original numeric value: Current Balance is saved as ACUP-OLD-CURR-BAL-N, Credit Limit is saved as ACUP-OLD-CREDIT-LIMIT-N, Cash Credit Limit is saved as ACUP-OLD-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-N, Current Cycle Credit is saved as ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-N, and Current Cycle Debit is saved as ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-N

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Account Financial Values as Original Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: All five account financial values retrieved from the Account Master file must be preserved as original (baseline) numeric values so that any user modifications to these financial fields can be accurately detected during the change comparison step.
