Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master file record has been successfully read, providing three dates in YYYY-MM-DD format: Account Open Date (ACCT-OPEN-DATE), Account Expiry Date (ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE), and Account Reissue Date (ACCT-REISSUE-DATE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched account date data as original values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Each date is split into three components using fixed character positions: positions 1-4 (Year), positions 6-7 (Month), and positions 9-10 (Day). Account Open Date Year is saved to ACUP-OLD-OPEN-YEAR, Month to ACUP-OLD-OPEN-MON, Day to ACUP-OLD-OPEN-DAY. Account Expiry Date Year is saved to ACUP-OLD-EXP-YEAR, Month to ACUP-OLD-EXP-MON, Day to ACUP-OLD-EXP-DAY. Account Reissue Date Year is saved to ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-YEAR, Month to ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-MON, Day to ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-DAY

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Account Dates as Original Values by Splitting into Year, Month, and Day Components
all_rules.Rule_Description: The three account dates stored in the Account Master file in YYYY-MM-DD format must each be decomposed into separate Year, Month, and Day components and stored individually as original values. This decomposition enables field-level change detection and screen display of individual date parts.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master file record has been successfully read, providing the Account Group ID (ACCT-GROUP-ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched account group data as original values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Group ID from the Account Master record is saved as the Original Group ID (ACUP-OLD-GROUP-ID)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Account Group ID as Original Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Group ID retrieved from the Account Master file must be preserved as the original (baseline) value so that any user modification to this field can be detected during the change comparison step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Master file record has been successfully read using the Customer ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference lookup, providing the Customer ID (CUST-ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched customer identity data as original values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer ID from the Customer Master record is saved as the Original Customer ID (ACUP-OLD-CUST-ID)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Customer ID as Original Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Customer ID retrieved from the Customer Master file must be preserved as the original (baseline) value to establish the customer identity link for the account being updated and to support change detection.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Master file record has been successfully read, providing the customer's SSN (CUST-SSN), Date of Birth in YYYY-MM-DD format (CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD), and FICO Credit Score (CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched customer personal data as original values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The SSN is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-SSN. The Date of Birth is split using fixed character positions: positions 1-4 (Year) saved to ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-YEAR, positions 6-7 (Month) saved to ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-MON, and positions 9-10 (Day) saved to ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-DAY. The FICO Credit Score is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-FICO-SCORE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Customer Personal Details as Original Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's Social Security Number, Date of Birth, and FICO Credit Score retrieved from the Customer Master file must be preserved as original values. The Date of Birth is decomposed into separate Year, Month, and Day components. These values serve as the baseline for detecting any user modifications during the change comparison step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Master file record has been successfully read, providing the customer's First Name (CUST-FIRST-NAME), Middle Name (CUST-MIDDLE-NAME), and Last Name (CUST-LAST-NAME)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched customer name data as original values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The First Name is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-FIRST-NAME, the Middle Name is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-MIDDLE-NAME, and the Last Name is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-LAST-NAME

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Customer Name Details as Original Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's full name components — First Name, Middle Name, and Last Name — retrieved from the Customer Master file must be preserved as original (baseline) values so that any user modifications to name fields can be detected during the change comparison step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Master file record has been successfully read, providing the customer's Address Line 1 (CUST-ADDR-LINE-1), Address Line 2 (CUST-ADDR-LINE-2), City stored as Address Line 3 (CUST-ADDR-LINE-3), State Code (CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD), Country Code (CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD), and Zip Code (CUST-ADDR-ZIP)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched customer address data as original values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Address Line 1 is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-1, Address Line 2 is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-2, City (Address Line 3) is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-3, State Code is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD, Country Code is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD, and Zip Code is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-ZIP

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Customer Address Details as Original Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: All six components of the customer's mailing address retrieved from the Customer Master file must be preserved as original (baseline) values so that any user modifications to address fields can be detected during the change comparison step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Master file record has been successfully read, providing the customer's Primary Phone Number (CUST-PHONE-NUM-1), Secondary Phone Number (CUST-PHONE-NUM-2), Government Issued ID (CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID), EFT Account ID (CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID), and Primary Card Holder Indicator (CUST-PRI-CARD-HOLDER-IND)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched customer contact and identity data as original values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Primary Phone Number is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1, Secondary Phone Number is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2, Government Issued ID is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID, EFT Account ID is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID, and Primary Card Holder Indicator is saved as ACUP-OLD-CUST-PRI-HOLDER-IND

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Customer Contact and Identity Details as Original Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's contact and identity details — Primary Phone Number, Secondary Phone Number, Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, and Primary Card Holder Indicator — retrieved from the Customer Master file must be preserved as original (baseline) values so that any user modifications to these fields can be detected during the change comparison step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master, Customer Master, and Card Cross-Reference records have all been successfully read and their data stored as original values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the storage of fetched data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The session communication area (CDEMO) is updated with the following values: Account ID (ACCT-ID) is stored in CDEMO-ACCT-ID, Customer ID (CUST-ID) is stored in CDEMO-CUST-ID, Customer First Name (CUST-FIRST-NAME) is stored in CDEMO-CUST-FNAME, Customer Middle Name (CUST-MIDDLE-NAME) is stored in CDEMO-CUST-MNAME, Customer Last Name (CUST-LAST-NAME) is stored in CDEMO-CUST-LNAME, Account Active Status (ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS) is stored in CDEMO-ACCT-STATUS, and the Card Number from the Cross-Reference record (XREF-CARD-NUM) is stored in CDEMO-CARD-NUM

all_rules.Rule_Name: Update Session Communication Area with Account and Customer Context
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all original values are stored, the shared session communication area must be updated with key account and customer identifiers so that other programs and screens in the session can access the current account context without re-reading the files.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the account update screen after account details have already been fetched and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The change detection process begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the internal state to 'No Changes Found' as the starting baseline before any field comparisons are performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Change Detection State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before comparing any field values, the change detection process initializes its state to indicate that no changes have been found. This baseline state is updated if any field comparison reveals a difference.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account details have been fetched and displayed, and the user has submitted the screen with entered values for Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, and Cash Credit Limit
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the new (user-entered) values against the original fetched values for: Account ID (exact match), Active Status (case-insensitive match), Current Balance (numeric value match), Credit Limit (numeric value match), and Cash Credit Limit (numeric value match)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If any of these five fields differ between the new and original values, the system immediately flags the state as 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process; if all five fields match, the system proceeds to compare account date fields

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compare Core Account Fields for Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the user-entered values for core account fields against the originally fetched values. Active Status comparison is case-insensitive. Numeric fields are compared by value. If any difference is found, the process immediately flags a change and stops further comparison.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The core account fields (Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit) have all matched between new and original values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the new (user-entered) values against the original fetched values for: Open Date (exact match), Expiry Date (exact match), and Reissue Date (exact match)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If any of these three date fields differ between the new and original values, the system immediately flags the state as 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process; if all three date fields match, the system proceeds to compare other account fields

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compare Account Date Fields for Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the user-entered date values for Open Date, Expiry Date, and Reissue Date against the originally fetched values. Each date is compared as a complete date value. If any difference is found, the process immediately flags a change.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The core account fields and account date fields have all matched between new and original values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the new (user-entered) values against the original fetched values for: Current Cycle Credit (numeric value match), Current Cycle Debit (numeric value match), and Group ID (case-insensitive match after trimming leading and trailing spaces)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If any of these three fields differ between the new and original values, the system immediately flags the state as 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process; if all three fields match, the system proceeds to compare customer name fields

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compare Other Account Fields for Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the user-entered values for Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, and Group ID against the originally fetched values. Group ID comparison is case-insensitive and ignores leading/trailing spaces. If any difference is found, the process immediately flags a change.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All account-level fields (core fields, dates, and other account fields) have matched between new and original values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the new (user-entered) values against the original fetched values for: Customer ID (case-insensitive, trimmed), First Name (case-insensitive, trimmed), Middle Name (case-insensitive, trimmed), and Last Name (case-insensitive, trimmed)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If any of these four fields differ between the new and original values, the system immediately flags the state as 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process; if all four fields match, the system proceeds to compare customer address fields

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compare Customer Name Fields for Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the user-entered customer name values and Customer ID against the originally fetched values. All comparisons are case-insensitive and ignore leading/trailing spaces. Customer ID is also included in this comparison group. If any difference is found, the process immediately flags a change.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All account-level fields and customer name fields have matched between new and original values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the new (user-entered) values against the original fetched values for: Address Line 1 (case-insensitive, trimmed), Address Line 2 (case-insensitive, trimmed), City/Address Line 3 (case-insensitive, trimmed), State Code (case-insensitive, trimmed), Country Code (case-insensitive, trimmed), and Zip Code (case-insensitive, trimmed)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If any of these six address fields differ between the new and original values, the system immediately flags the state as 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process; if all six address fields match, the system proceeds to compare customer phone number fields

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compare Customer Address Fields for Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the user-entered customer address values against the originally fetched values. All text field comparisons are case-insensitive and ignore leading/trailing spaces. Zip Code is compared case-insensitively and trimmed. If any difference is found, the process immediately flags a change.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All account-level fields, customer name fields, and customer address fields have matched between new and original values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the new (user-entered) values against the original fetched values for all six phone number parts: Phone Number 1 Area Code (exact match), Phone Number 1 Prefix (exact match), Phone Number 1 Line Number (exact match), Phone Number 2 Area Code (exact match), Phone Number 2 Prefix (exact match), and Phone Number 2 Line Number (exact match)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If any of these six phone number parts differ between the new and original values, the system immediately flags the state as 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process; if all six phone number parts match, the system proceeds to compare other customer fields

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compare Customer Phone Number Fields for Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the user-entered phone number values against the originally fetched values. Each phone number is stored in three separate parts (Area Code, Prefix, Line Number) and each part is compared individually using an exact match. If any part of either phone number differs, the process immediately flags a change.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All account-level fields, customer name fields, customer address fields, and customer phone number fields have matched between new and original values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the new (user-entered) values against the original fetched values for: SSN (exact match of full SSN value), Government Issued ID (case-insensitive, trimmed), Date of Birth (exact match), EFT Account ID (exact match), Primary Card Holder Indicator (case-insensitive, trimmed), and FICO Score (exact match)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If any of these six fields differ between the new and original values, the system flags the state as 'Change Has Occurred'; if all six fields match, the system flags the state as 'No Changes Detected', indicating the user has not modified any data and no update is required

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compare Other Customer Fields for Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the remaining user-entered customer fields against the originally fetched values. Government Issued ID and Primary Card Holder Indicator comparisons are case-insensitive and trimmed. SSN, Date of Birth, EFT Account ID, and FICO Score are compared by exact value. This is the final comparison group — if all match, no changes are detected.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The change detection process is comparing new (user-entered) values against original fetched values across account and customer fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A difference is detected in any compared field at any point during the comparison sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system immediately sets the state to 'Change Has Occurred', exits the change detection process without performing any further comparisons, and the subsequent action is to proceed with full input validation of all submitted field values

all_rules.Rule_Name: Flag Change Has Occurred - Proceed to Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When any field comparison during change detection reveals a difference between the user-entered value and the originally fetched value, the system immediately flags that a change has occurred and exits the comparison process. This flag triggers the full field-by-field validation process to run on the submitted data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The change detection process has completed comparisons across all account fields (Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Group ID) and all customer fields (Customer ID, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Lines 1-3, State, Country, Zip, Phone 1 all parts, Phone 2 all parts, SSN, Government Issued ID, Date of Birth, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator, FICO Score)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Every single field comparison shows that the new (user-entered) value matches the original fetched value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the state to 'No Changes Detected', no field validation is performed, no update to account or customer records is initiated, and the screen is redisplayed showing the original values with a message indicating no changes were found

all_rules.Rule_Name: Flag No Changes Detected - Skip Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all field comparisons across all account and customer fields show that the user-entered values match the originally fetched values, the system flags that no changes have been detected. This means no update to the account or customer records is required, and the screen is redisplayed with the original values without triggering any validation or update processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the account update screen with a value entered (or left blank) in the Account Status field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to validate the Account Status field by loading the user-entered value from the screen input area (ACUP-NEW-ACTIVE-STATUS) into the Yes/No validation working field, and sets the field label to 'Account Status'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Status value entered by the user is available in the validation working area, the field label 'Account Status' is set for use in any error messages, and the Y/N validation routine is invoked to perform the actual checks

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Account Active Status for Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before validating the account active status, the system retrieves the value entered by the user on the account update screen and prepares it for the Y/N validation routine. This rule ensures the correct field value and field label ('Account Status') are loaded into the validation working area prior to any checks being performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the account update screen and the Account Status field has been loaded into the validation working area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Status value is blank (spaces), empty (low-values), or zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The overall input is marked as invalid (INPUT-ERROR), the Account Status field is specifically flagged as blank (FLG-YES-NO-BLANK), and if no prior error message has already been set, the error message 'Account Status must be supplied.' is recorded; validation of the Account Status field ends immediately without checking the Y/N value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Status Mandatory Presence Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Active Status field is mandatory on the account update screen. If the user leaves the field blank, empty, or submits a zero value, the system must reject the input and inform the user that the field must be supplied. Only the first error message encountered during the entire screen validation is displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the account update screen, the Account Status field is not blank, and the value has been loaded into the validation working area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Status value is evaluated and it does NOT equal 'Y' or 'N' (i.e., FLG-YES-NO-ISVALID is not set, meaning the value is not a valid Y/N indicator)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The overall input is marked as invalid (INPUT-ERROR), the Account Status field is specifically flagged as containing an invalid value (FLG-YES-NO-NOT-OK), and if no prior error message has already been set, the error message 'Account Status must be Y or N.' is recorded; validation of the Account Status field ends immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Status Y or N Value Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Active Status field is not blank, the system must verify that the value entered is either 'Y' (Yes/Active) or 'N' (No/Inactive). Any other value is considered invalid. This enforces the business rule that an account's active status can only be one of two defined states.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the account update screen with a value in the Account Status field that is not blank and equals either 'Y' or 'N'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Both the blank check and the Y/N value check pass successfully (FLG-YES-NO-ISVALID is confirmed as true)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: No error is raised for the Account Status field, the validated Account Status value is stored in the account status edit result area (WS-EDIT-ACCT-STATUS), and the validation process proceeds to the next field (Open Date validation)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Status Successfully Validated
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Active Status field passes both the mandatory presence check and the Y/N value check, it is marked as valid and the validation result is stored. Processing continues to the next field validation in the account update workflow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Status field has failed validation (either blank or contains a value other than Y or N) during the account update screen submission
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to record the Account Status error message ('Account Status must be supplied.' or 'Account Status must be Y or N.')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message is written to the screen error message area ONLY IF no prior error message has already been set (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is true); if a prior error message already exists, the Account Status error message is suppressed and the existing message is preserved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Single Error Message Display Policy for Account Status
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Status field fails validation (either blank or invalid value), an error message is only recorded if no other error message has already been captured during the current screen validation pass. This ensures that only the first error encountered across all fields is shown to the user at one time, preventing message overwriting.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the account update screen with values entered for Account Open Date, Account Expiry Date, Account Reissue Date, and Customer Date of Birth, and changes have been detected compared to the originally fetched values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the submitted input fields for date validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must validate Account Open Date first, then Account Expiry Date, then Account Reissue Date, and finally Customer Date of Birth — each using the common CCYYMMDD date validation routine; for Customer Date of Birth only, if the date passes common validation, an additional check is performed to ensure the date is in the past; validation results (pass/fail flags) are stored separately for each date field as Open Date flags, Expiry Date flags, Reissue Date flags, and Date of Birth flags respectively

all_rules.Rule_Name: Date Field Validation Invocation for Account and Customer Dates
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system applies date validation to four specific date fields on the account update screen: Account Open Date, Account Expiry Date, Account Reissue Date, and Customer Date of Birth. Each date is validated in sequence using a common date validation routine. Date of Birth has an additional future-date check applied only after it passes the common validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A date field (Account Open Date, Account Expiry Date, Account Reissue Date, or Customer Date of Birth) is being validated and the year portion of the date has been submitted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The year value is blank (spaces) or contains no data (low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must mark the year as missing by setting the Year-Blank error flag, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name] : Year must be supplied'; the system then proceeds to validate the month component without further year checks

all_rules.Rule_Name: Year Must Be Supplied for Date Fields
all_rules.Rule_Description: When validating any date field (Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date, or Date of Birth), the year component is mandatory and must not be blank or empty.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A date field year component has been supplied (is not blank) and is being validated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The year value is not numeric (contains non-numeric characters)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must mark the year as invalid by setting the Year-Not-OK error flag, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name] must be 4 digit number'; the system then proceeds to validate the month component without further year checks

all_rules.Rule_Name: Year Must Be a 4-Digit Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a year value has been supplied for any date field, it must be a valid 4-digit numeric value to be accepted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A date field year component has been supplied and confirmed to be numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The year value does not fall within the 1900s (last century) or the 2000s (current century)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must mark the year as invalid by setting the Year-Not-OK error flag, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name] : Century is not valid'; the system then proceeds to validate the month component; if the year is within the 1900s or 2000s, the year is marked as valid and month validation proceeds

all_rules.Rule_Name: Year Century Must Be 1900s or 2000s
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a year value is numeric, it must belong to either the 20th century (1900–1999) or the 21st century (2000–2099). Years outside these two centuries are not accepted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A date field (Account Open Date, Account Expiry Date, Account Reissue Date, or Customer Date of Birth) is being validated and the month portion has been submitted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The month value is blank (spaces) or contains no data (low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must mark the month as missing by setting the Month-Blank error flag, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name] : Month must be supplied'; the system then proceeds to validate the day component without further month checks

all_rules.Rule_Name: Month Must Be Supplied for Date Fields
all_rules.Rule_Description: When validating any date field, the month component is mandatory and must not be blank or empty, regardless of whether the year was valid or not.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A date field month component has been supplied (is not blank) and is being validated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The month value is not a valid calendar month number (not between 1 and 12 inclusive, or is not numeric)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must mark the month as invalid by setting the Month-Not-OK error flag, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name]: Month must be a number between 1 and 12'; the system then proceeds to validate the day component; if the month is valid (1–12), the month is marked as valid and day validation proceeds

all_rules.Rule_Name: Month Must Be a Number Between 1 and 12
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a month value has been supplied for any date field, it must represent a valid calendar month — a number between 1 (January) and 12 (December).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A date field (Account Open Date, Account Expiry Date, Account Reissue Date, or Customer Date of Birth) is being validated and the day portion has been submitted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The day value is blank (spaces) or contains no data (low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must mark the day as missing by setting the Day-Blank error flag, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name] : Day must be supplied'; the system then proceeds to the month-day cross-validation checks without further day checks

all_rules.Rule_Name: Day Must Be Supplied for Date Fields
all_rules.Rule_Description: When validating any date field, the day component is mandatory and must not be blank or empty, regardless of whether the year or month were valid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A date field day component has been supplied (is not blank) and is being validated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The day value is not numeric (contains non-numeric characters)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must mark the day as invalid by setting the Day-Not-OK error flag, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name]:day must be a number between 1 and 31'; the system then proceeds to the month-day cross-validation checks without further day range checks

all_rules.Rule_Name: Day Must Be a Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a day value has been supplied for any date field, it must be a numeric value before range checking can be applied.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A date field day component has been supplied and confirmed to be numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The numeric day value is less than 1 or greater than 31
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must mark the day as invalid by setting the Day-Not-OK error flag, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name]:day must be a number between 1 and 31'; the system then proceeds to the month-day cross-validation checks; if the day is between 1 and 31 inclusive, the day is marked as valid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Day Must Be Between 1 and 31
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a day value is confirmed to be numeric, it must fall within the general calendar day range of 1 to 31 inclusive.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A date field has passed individual year, month, and day format checks and is undergoing month-day cross-validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered day value is 31 AND the entered month is one that does not allow 31 days (i.e., the month is not January, March, May, July, August, October, or December)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must mark both the day and the month as invalid by setting the Day-Not-OK and Month-Not-OK error flags, set the overall input as invalid, set the error message to '[Date Field Name]:Cannot have 31 days in this month', and stop further cross-validation for this date field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Day 31 Is Not Valid for Months That Have Fewer Than 31 Days
all_rules.Rule_Description: Not all calendar months have 31 days. When a user enters day 31, the system must verify that the specified month actually has 31 days. Months with only 28, 29, or 30 days cannot have a 31st day.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A date field has passed the 31-day month check and is undergoing further month-day cross-validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered month is February (month 2) AND the entered day value is 30
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must mark both the day and the month as invalid by setting the Day-Not-OK and Month-Not-OK error flags, set the overall input as invalid, set the error message to '[Date Field Name]:Cannot have 30 days in this month', and stop further cross-validation for this date field

all_rules.Rule_Name: February Cannot Have 30 Days
all_rules.Rule_Description: February never has 30 days regardless of whether it is a leap year or not. When a user enters February (month 2) with day 30, this is always invalid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A date field has passed the February-30 check and is undergoing further month-day cross-validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered month is February (month 2) AND the entered day value is 29, and the leap year check is performed: if the year ends in '00' (century year), the year must be divisible by 400; otherwise the year must be divisible by 4; if the year does not satisfy the applicable divisibility rule, it is not a leap year
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the year is NOT a leap year: the system must mark the day, month, and year all as invalid by setting Day-Not-OK, Month-Not-OK, and Year-Not-OK error flags, set the overall input as invalid, set the error message to '[Date Field Name]:Not a leap year.Cannot have 29 days in this month', and stop further cross-validation for this date field; if the year IS a leap year (remainder is zero after division), the date February 29 is accepted as valid

all_rules.Rule_Name: February 29 Is Only Valid in a Leap Year
all_rules.Rule_Description: February 29 (the leap day) only exists in leap years. A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, except for century years (years ending in 00) which must be divisible by 400. If the year is not a leap year, February 29 is an invalid date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Date of Birth field has passed all standard date format validations (year, month, day, and calendar cross-checks) and is undergoing the additional birth date check
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered Date of Birth, when converted to an integer date value, is greater than or equal to today's current system date converted to an integer date value (i.e., the date is today or in the future)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must mark the day, month, and year all as invalid by setting Day-Not-OK, Month-Not-OK, and Year-Not-OK error flags, set the overall input as invalid, and set the error message to '[Date Field Name]:cannot be in the future'; if the Date of Birth is strictly before today's date, the date of birth is accepted as valid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Date of Birth Must Not Be a Future Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: A customer's date of birth must represent a date that has already occurred. A date of birth that is today's date or any future date is not a valid birth date. This check is applied exclusively to the Date of Birth field after it has passed all standard date format validations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a Date of Birth on the account update screen and the basic date format validation (year, month, day structure, leap year checks) has been performed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The basic date format validation result flag (WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-ISVALID) indicates the date format is valid
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to invoke the Date of Birth age validation routine (EDIT-DATE-OF-BIRTH) to check whether the date represents a past date, and the resulting date validation flags (WS-EDIT-DATE-FLGS) are stored as the Date of Birth validation outcome (WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-FLGS); if the basic format validation did not pass, the age validation is skipped entirely

all_rules.Rule_Name: Conditional Trigger of DOB Age Validation Based on Prior Format Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Date of Birth age validation (checking whether the date is in the past) is only invoked when the basic date format validation has already passed successfully. If the basic format check failed, the age check is skipped entirely.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Date of Birth age validation routine has been triggered because the basic date format validation passed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The age validation routine begins execution
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures the current system date (WS-CURRENT-DATE-YYYYMMDD) using the system's current date function, which will serve as the reference point for all subsequent date comparison logic

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Current System Date as Reference Point for DOB Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before comparing the entered Date of Birth against today's date, the system retrieves the current system date to use as the reference point for determining whether the date of birth is in the past.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date has been captured and the Date of Birth (WS-EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD-N) has passed basic format validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares for the date comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system computes a numeric integer value (WS-EDIT-DATE-BINARY) from the Date of Birth using the INTEGER-OF-DATE function applied to the date value (WS-EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD-N), producing a single comparable integer that represents the absolute day count of the Date of Birth

all_rules.Rule_Name: Convert Date of Birth to Numeric Integer for Date Comparison
all_rules.Rule_Description: The entered Date of Birth (in CCYYMMDD format) is converted to a numeric integer representation so that it can be arithmetically compared against today's date to determine whether it falls before the current date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date (WS-CURRENT-DATE-YYYYMMDD) has been captured and the Date of Birth integer (WS-EDIT-DATE-BINARY) has been computed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares for the date comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system computes a numeric integer value (WS-CURRENT-DATE-BINARY) from today's date using the INTEGER-OF-DATE function applied to the current date value (WS-CURRENT-DATE-YYYYMMDD-N), producing a single comparable integer that represents the absolute day count of today's date

all_rules.Rule_Name: Convert Today's Date to Numeric Integer for Date Comparison
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current system date is converted to a numeric integer representation so that it can be arithmetically compared against the entered Date of Birth to determine whether the Date of Birth falls strictly before today.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the Date of Birth (WS-EDIT-DATE-BINARY) and today's date (WS-CURRENT-DATE-BINARY) have been converted to numeric integer values for comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the two integer date values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If today's date integer (WS-CURRENT-DATE-BINARY) is strictly greater than the Date of Birth integer (WS-EDIT-DATE-BINARY), the Date of Birth is considered valid and the validation passes; if today's date integer is equal to or less than the Date of Birth integer (meaning the DOB is today or in the future), the Date of Birth is considered invalid and the validation fails

all_rules.Rule_Name: Date of Birth Must Be Strictly Before Today's Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: The core age validation rule: the Date of Birth must represent a date that is strictly in the past — it cannot be today's date or any future date. The comparison is performed using the integer representations of both dates.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Date of Birth integer value (WS-EDIT-DATE-BINARY) and today's date integer value (WS-CURRENT-DATE-BINARY) have been computed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Today's date integer (WS-CURRENT-DATE-BINARY) is strictly greater than the Date of Birth integer (WS-EDIT-DATE-BINARY)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system takes no error action (CONTINUE), the Date of Birth age validation passes, no error flags are set for Day, Month, or Year, no error message is generated, and processing proceeds normally to the end of the Date of Birth validation routine

all_rules.Rule_Name: Date of Birth Accepted as Valid When It Represents a Past Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Date of Birth is confirmed to be strictly before today's date, the date is accepted as a valid birth date and no error is raised for the age check. Processing continues to any remaining field validations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Date of Birth integer value (WS-EDIT-DATE-BINARY) has been compared against today's date integer value (WS-CURRENT-DATE-BINARY)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Today's date integer (WS-CURRENT-DATE-BINARY) is NOT strictly greater than the Date of Birth integer (WS-EDIT-DATE-BINARY), meaning the Date of Birth is today or in the future
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the overall input error indicator (INPUT-ERROR) to TRUE, sets the Day field error flag (FLG-DAY-NOT-OK) to TRUE, sets the Month field error flag (FLG-MONTH-NOT-OK) to TRUE, and sets the Year field error flag (FLG-YEAR-NOT-OK) to TRUE, marking all three date components as invalid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark All Date of Birth Component Fields as Invalid When DOB Is Not in the Past
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Date of Birth is today or in the future, all three date component fields (Day, Month, and Year) are simultaneously marked as invalid. This ensures the user is clearly directed to correct the entire date entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Date of Birth has been determined to be invalid because it is today or in the future, and all three date component error flags (Day, Month, Year) have been set to TRUE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether an error message has already been set (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is TRUE, meaning no prior message exists)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system constructs and stores an error message by concatenating the field name label (from WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME, trimmed of trailing spaces) with the text ':cannot be in the future', and stores this combined message in the error message area (WS-RETURN-MSG); if a prior error message already exists (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is FALSE), the existing message is preserved and no new message is written

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Error Message When Date of Birth Is in the Future
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Date of Birth fails the age validation because it is today or in the future, a specific error message is generated to inform the user that the date of birth cannot be a future date. The message is only set if no prior error message has already been recorded.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account update screen is being prepared for display after a Date of Birth validation failure, and the program is in re-entry mode (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen attributes are being set up (3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS) and any of the following conditions are true: the Year field is invalid (FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-YEAR-NOT-OK) or blank (FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-YEAR-BLANK); the Month field is invalid (FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-MONTH-NOT-OK) or blank (FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-MONTH-BLANK); the Day field is invalid (FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-DAY-NOT-OK) or blank (FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-DAY-BLANK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each Date of Birth component field that is in error or blank: the field's color attribute is set to RED (DFHRED) on the screen output map (CACTUPAO); additionally, if the specific component field was blank (FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-YEAR-BLANK, FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-MONTH-BLANK, or FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-DAY-BLANK respectively), an asterisk character '*' is placed in that field's output value (DOBYEARO, DOBMONO, or DOBDAYO) as a visual placeholder indicating the field was left empty

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight Date of Birth Fields in Red on Screen When Validation Fails
all_rules.Rule_Description: When any Date of Birth component field (Year, Month, or Day) has a validation error or is blank, that field is highlighted in red on the screen to visually direct the user to the fields requiring correction. Additionally, if a mandatory date component was left blank, an asterisk placeholder is displayed in that field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has made changes to account details, and the Credit Limit field (ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-X) is part of the update form
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the form and the Credit Limit field contains only blank spaces or is completely empty (LOW-VALUES or SPACES)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the overall input as invalid (INPUT-ERROR), sets the Credit Limit field status to 'Blank/Missing' (FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-BLANK), records the error message 'Credit Limit must be supplied.' as the first error message (only if no prior error message has been set), the Credit Limit field is highlighted in red on the screen, an asterisk '*' is displayed in the Credit Limit field to indicate it is missing, and the cursor is positioned on the Credit Limit field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Credit Limit Field Must Be Supplied
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Credit Limit field has been entered by the user and is not left blank or empty before any further validation is performed. This is a mandatory field on the account update screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, has made changes to account details, and the Credit Limit field (ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-X) has been supplied with a non-blank value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the entered Credit Limit value passes the signed numeric currency validation (NUMVAL-C test, which accepts values like 1234.56, -500.00, or currency-formatted numbers) and the value fails this check
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the overall input as invalid (INPUT-ERROR), sets the Credit Limit field status to 'Invalid' (FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-NOT-OK), records the error message 'Credit Limit is not valid' as the first error message (only if no prior error message has been set), the Credit Limit field is highlighted in red on the screen, and the cursor is positioned on the Credit Limit field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Credit Limit Must Be a Valid Signed Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Credit Limit value entered by the user is a properly formatted signed numeric value (e.g., 1234.56 or -500.00), allowing for currency-style input including signs and decimal points. This check is only performed after confirming the field is not blank.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has entered a value in the Credit Limit field (ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-X)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Credit Limit value is non-blank AND passes the signed numeric currency format validation (NUMVAL-C test returns 0, confirming it is a valid signed numeric value such as 1234.56 or -500.00)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the Credit Limit field status as valid (FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-ISVALID), the validated numeric value is computed and stored internally (ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-N) using NUMVAL-C conversion, no error message is generated for this field, the field result flag (WS-EDIT-CREDIT-LIMIT) is updated to reflect successful validation, and processing continues to the next field validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Credit Limit Successfully Validated
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Credit Limit field passes both the mandatory presence check and the signed numeric format check, it is marked as successfully validated, allowing the update process to proceed to the next field validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Credit Limit field has failed validation — either it was not supplied (FLG-CRED-LIMIT-BLANK) or it contained an invalid value (FLG-CRED-LIMIT-NOT-OK), and the program is in re-entry mode (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen attributes for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Credit Limit field (ACRDLIMC) is highlighted in red (DFHRED) on the screen; if the field was blank (FLG-CRED-LIMIT-BLANK), an asterisk '*' is placed in the Credit Limit output field (ACRDLIMO) to indicate the missing value; the cursor is positioned on the Credit Limit field (ACRDLIML set to -1) to direct the user's attention to the error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Credit Limit Error Field Screen Highlighting
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Credit Limit field fails validation (either missing or invalid), the screen display is updated to visually indicate the error to the user by highlighting the field in red and placing the cursor on it, and showing an asterisk if the field was left blank.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has fetched account details, and changes have been detected between the original and newly entered values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen and the Cash Credit Limit field is blank, empty, or contains only spaces or low-values (i.e., no value has been entered)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Cash Credit Limit field is marked as invalid with a blank indicator, the overall input is flagged as containing an error, the error message 'Cash Credit Limit must be supplied.' is set (only if no prior error message has already been recorded), and validation for this field stops immediately without proceeding to the numeric format check

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cash Credit Limit - Mandatory Field Presence Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Ensures that the Cash Credit Limit field is not left empty when a user submits account update details. The field is mandatory and must contain a value before any further validation is performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, has fetched account details, changes have been detected, and the Cash Credit Limit field has been supplied with a non-blank value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the supplied Cash Credit Limit value is a valid signed numeric number (using currency-aware numeric validation that accepts signs and decimal points)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the value is NOT a valid signed numeric number, the Cash Credit Limit field is marked as invalid, the overall input is flagged as containing an error, and the error message 'Cash Credit Limit is not valid' is set (only if no prior error message has already been recorded), and validation for this field stops; if the value IS a valid signed numeric number, processing continues to mark the field as valid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cash Credit Limit - Signed Numeric Format Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Ensures that the Cash Credit Limit value entered by the user is a properly formatted signed numeric value (e.g., may include currency signs or positive/negative indicators). This check only runs when a value has been supplied.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, has fetched account details, changes have been detected, the Cash Credit Limit field has been supplied with a non-blank value, and the value has passed the signed numeric format check
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All validation checks for the Cash Credit Limit field have been completed without any errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Cash Credit Limit field validation flag is set to valid, indicating the field has passed all checks, and processing proceeds to the next field validation (Reissue Date)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cash Credit Limit - Mark Field as Successfully Validated
all_rules.Rule_Description: Records the successful outcome of Cash Credit Limit validation so that downstream processing (such as update confirmation and screen display) can correctly identify this field as having passed all validation checks.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account update screen is displayed and the user has interacted with the Current Balance field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen input is received and the Current Balance field contains either an asterisk '*' or spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Balance value is cleared (set to empty/low-values) internally, indicating no value was supplied by the user; otherwise, the entered value is captured as-is for further validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Current Balance Input Capture and Blank Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters a value in the Current Balance field on the account update screen, the system captures the input. If the user enters an asterisk '*' or leaves the field blank (spaces), the Current Balance is treated as not supplied and cleared internally.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account update screen has been submitted with account details already fetched, and changes have been detected between the original and newly entered values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Current Balance field is empty, blank (spaces), or was not supplied by the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the Current Balance field with a 'blank' error status, sets the overall input error flag to true, and displays the error message 'Current Balance must be supplied.' — provided no prior error message has already been set in the session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Current Balance Mandatory Field Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Current Balance field is mandatory on the account update screen. If the user does not supply a value, the system must flag the field as blank, set an input error, and display an appropriate error message. Only the first error message encountered during the session is displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Current Balance field has been supplied with a non-blank value on the account update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered Current Balance value fails the signed numeric format check (i.e., it cannot be interpreted as a valid signed currency/numeric amount)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the Current Balance field with an 'invalid' error status, sets the overall input error flag to true, and displays the error message 'Current Balance is not valid' — provided no prior error message has already been set in the session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Current Balance Signed Numeric Format Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a value is supplied for Current Balance, it must be a valid signed numeric value (i.e., it may include a sign indicator such as '+' or '-' and decimal notation). Values that cannot be interpreted as a signed numeric amount are rejected.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Current Balance field has been supplied with a non-blank value on the account update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered Current Balance value passes the signed numeric format validation (i.e., it is a valid signed numeric amount)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system converts the text value of Current Balance into its numeric equivalent and stores it as the new Current Balance numeric value for further processing; the Current Balance field is marked as valid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Current Balance Numeric Value Storage on Successful Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Current Balance passes the signed numeric format check, the system converts the text representation of the balance into its internal numeric form for use in subsequent processing such as change detection, update record preparation, and screen display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Account details have been fetched and displayed on screen, and the user has submitted changes where at least one field differs from the originally fetched values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs the full input validation sequence for all editable fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Balance validation routine is invoked with the entered Current Balance value; upon completion, the resulting validation status flag (valid, blank, or invalid) is stored against the Current Balance field and used to control error highlighting and cursor positioning on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Current Balance Validation Orchestration
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Current Balance validation is invoked as part of the full field-by-field edit process, which occurs only when account details have already been fetched and actual changes have been detected between the original and newly entered values. The validation result flag is stored for use in screen attribute setup and error highlighting.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account details on the Account Update screen and the Current Cycle Credit amount field is part of the editable fields being validated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Current Cycle Credit amount field is left blank, contains only spaces, or contains no value (low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Cycle Credit amount is marked as invalid with a blank indicator, the overall input is flagged as containing an error, and the error message 'Current Cycle Credit Limit must be supplied.' is recorded as the active error message (only if no prior error message has already been set), and validation ends for this field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Current Cycle Credit Amount - Mandatory Field Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Current Cycle Credit amount has been provided by the user before any format checks are performed. This is a mandatory field on the account update screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account details on the Account Update screen and the Current Cycle Credit amount field has been provided with a non-blank value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The provided Current Cycle Credit amount value fails the signed numeric currency validation check (i.e., it is not a valid signed numeric value such as containing invalid characters or improper formatting)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Cycle Credit amount is marked as invalid with a not-valid indicator, the overall input is flagged as containing an error, and the error message 'Current Cycle Credit Limit is not valid' is recorded as the active error message (only if no prior error message has already been set), and validation ends for this field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Current Cycle Credit Amount - Valid Signed Numeric Format Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Current Cycle Credit amount, when provided, is a properly formatted signed numeric value (allowing currency signs and decimal notation). This ensures the value can be correctly stored as a financial amount.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account details on the Account Update screen and the Current Cycle Credit amount field has been provided with a non-blank value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Current Cycle Credit amount passes both the mandatory presence check and the signed numeric format validation check
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Cycle Credit amount is marked as valid, indicating it is acceptable for use in the account update, and no error is raised for this field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Current Cycle Credit Amount - Mark as Valid
all_rules.Rule_Description: Confirms that the Current Cycle Credit amount has passed all validation checks — it is present and is a properly formatted signed numeric value — and marks it as valid for further processing and update.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has fetched account details, and changes have been detected between the original and newly entered values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen and the Current Cycle Debit amount field is blank or contains no value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Cycle Debit amount is marked as invalid, the overall input is flagged as containing an error, and the error message 'Current Cycle Debit Limit must be supplied.' is recorded as the first error message (only if no prior error message has already been set)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Current Cycle Debit Amount - Mandatory Field Presence Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Ensures that the Current Cycle Debit amount field is not left empty when a user submits account update details. The field is mandatory and must contain a value before any further validation is performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, the Current Cycle Debit amount field has been supplied with a non-blank value, and changes have been detected between the original and newly entered values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen and the value entered in the Current Cycle Debit amount field is not a valid signed numeric currency value (e.g., contains letters, special characters, or is otherwise not parseable as a signed number)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Cycle Debit amount is marked as invalid, the overall input is flagged as containing an error, and the error message 'Current Cycle Debit Limit is not valid' is recorded as the first error message (only if no prior error message has already been set)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Current Cycle Debit Amount - Signed Numeric Format Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Ensures that the Current Cycle Debit amount, when supplied, is a properly formatted signed numeric value that can represent a monetary amount, including support for positive and negative values with up to two decimal places.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, the Current Cycle Debit amount field has been supplied with a non-blank value, and changes have been detected between the original and newly entered values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Current Cycle Debit amount passes both the mandatory presence check and the signed numeric format check
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Cycle Debit amount is marked as valid, and the validated numeric value is stored internally for use in the account update record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Current Cycle Debit Amount - Successful Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Confirms that the Current Cycle Debit amount has passed all validation checks — it is present and is a valid signed numeric currency value — and marks it as valid so that the update process may proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a value (or left blank) in the Current Cycle Debit amount field on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen input is received by the system
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the entered value is an asterisk '*' or spaces, the Current Cycle Debit amount is treated as blank and cleared internally; if a non-blank value is entered and it is a valid signed numeric currency value, it is stored both as a text value and converted to its numeric equivalent for processing; if the value is non-blank but not a valid signed numeric, only the text value is stored and the numeric conversion is skipped

all_rules.Rule_Name: Current Cycle Debit Amount - Input Capture and Numeric Conversion
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines how the Current Cycle Debit amount is captured from the user's screen input before validation begins. An asterisk '*' or blank entry is treated as a cleared/empty field. If a value is present and is a valid signed numeric, it is also converted to its internal numeric representation for downstream processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Current Cycle Debit amount field has failed validation (either blank or invalid format) and the screen is being re-displayed to the user after a submission attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen attributes for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor is positioned on the Current Cycle Debit amount field; the field is highlighted in red to indicate an error; if the field was blank (not supplied), an asterisk '*' is displayed in the field as a visual indicator that input is required

all_rules.Rule_Name: Current Cycle Debit Amount - Error Field Highlighting on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines how the screen visually communicates a Current Cycle Debit validation error to the user by highlighting the field in red and placing the cursor on it. If the field was blank, an asterisk placeholder is also shown to indicate the field requires input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer information on the Account Update screen, and the SSN first 3 digits field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-1) is being validated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The first 3 digits of the SSN are blank, contain only spaces, or have zero trimmed length (i.e., nothing was entered)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as invalid by setting INPUT-ERROR to TRUE and FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK to TRUE for SSN Part 1; the validation flags are stored in WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1-FLGS; if no prior error message has been set, the error message 'SSN: First 3 chars must be supplied.' is recorded; validation of the first 3 digits stops immediately and processing continues with the middle 2 digits validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: SSN First 3 Digits - Presence Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the first 3 digits of the Social Security Number have been entered by the user and are not blank or missing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer information on the Account Update screen, and the SSN first 3 digits field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-1) has been supplied (is not blank)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The first 3 digits of the SSN contain any non-numeric characters
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as invalid by setting INPUT-ERROR to TRUE and FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK to TRUE for SSN Part 1; the validation flags are stored in WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1-FLGS; if no prior error message has been set, the error message 'SSN: First 3 chars must be all numeric.' is recorded; validation of the first 3 digits stops immediately and processing continues with the middle 2 digits validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: SSN First 3 Digits - Numeric Format Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the first 3 digits of the Social Security Number contain only numeric characters.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer information on the Account Update screen, and the SSN first 3 digits field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-1) has been supplied and confirmed as numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The numeric value of the first 3 digits of the SSN equals zero (i.e., '000')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as invalid by setting INPUT-ERROR to TRUE and FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK to TRUE for SSN Part 1; the validation flags are stored in WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1-FLGS; if no prior error message has been set, the error message 'SSN: First 3 chars must not be zero.' is recorded; validation of the first 3 digits stops immediately and processing continues with the middle 2 digits validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: SSN First 3 Digits - Non-Zero Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the first 3 digits of the Social Security Number are not all zeros.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer information on the Account Update screen, and the SSN first 3 digits field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-1) has passed the presence, numeric, and non-zero checks (FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1-ISVALID is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The first 3 digits of the SSN match any of the restricted values: 000, 666, or any value between 900 and 999 inclusive (as determined by the INVALID-SSN-PART1 condition evaluated against WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as invalid by setting INPUT-ERROR to TRUE and FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1-NOT-OK to TRUE; if no prior error message has been set, the error message 'SSN: First 3 chars: should not be 000, 666, or between 900 and 999' is recorded; processing continues with the middle 2 digits validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: SSN First 3 Digits - Restricted Range Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the first 3 digits of the Social Security Number do not fall within federally restricted SSN prefix ranges. The values 000, 666, and the range 900-999 are not valid SSN prefixes per US Social Security Administration rules.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer information on the Account Update screen, and the SSN first 3 digits field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-1) is being validated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The first 3 digits are supplied, all numeric, non-zero, and do not fall within the restricted ranges (000, 666, 900-999)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID to TRUE for SSN Part 1, and the validation flags are stored in WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1-FLGS; processing continues to validate the middle 2 digits of the SSN

all_rules.Rule_Name: SSN First 3 Digits - Valid
all_rules.Rule_Description: Confirms that the first 3 digits of the SSN have passed all validation checks and are marked as valid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer information on the Account Update screen, and the SSN middle 2 digits field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-2) is being validated after completion of Part 1 validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The middle 2 digits of the SSN are blank, contain only spaces, or have zero trimmed length (i.e., nothing was entered)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as invalid by setting INPUT-ERROR to TRUE and FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK to TRUE for SSN Part 2; the validation flags are stored in WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART2-FLGS; if no prior error message has been set, the error message 'SSN 4th & 5th chars must be supplied.' is recorded; validation of the middle 2 digits stops immediately and processing continues with the last 4 digits validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: SSN Middle 2 Digits - Presence Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the middle 2 digits (4th and 5th characters) of the Social Security Number have been entered by the user and are not blank or missing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer information on the Account Update screen, and the SSN middle 2 digits field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-2) has been supplied (is not blank)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The middle 2 digits of the SSN contain any non-numeric characters
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as invalid by setting INPUT-ERROR to TRUE and FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK to TRUE for SSN Part 2; the validation flags are stored in WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART2-FLGS; if no prior error message has been set, the error message 'SSN 4th & 5th chars must be all numeric.' is recorded; validation of the middle 2 digits stops immediately and processing continues with the last 4 digits validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: SSN Middle 2 Digits - Numeric Format Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the middle 2 digits (4th and 5th characters) of the Social Security Number contain only numeric characters.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer information on the Account Update screen, and the SSN middle 2 digits field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-2) has been supplied and confirmed as numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The numeric value of the middle 2 digits of the SSN equals zero (i.e., '00')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as invalid by setting INPUT-ERROR to TRUE and FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK to TRUE for SSN Part 2; the validation flags are stored in WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART2-FLGS; if no prior error message has been set, the error message 'SSN 4th & 5th chars must not be zero.' is recorded; validation of the middle 2 digits stops immediately and processing continues with the last 4 digits validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: SSN Middle 2 Digits - Non-Zero Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the middle 2 digits (4th and 5th characters) of the Social Security Number are not all zeros.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer information on the Account Update screen, and the SSN middle 2 digits field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-2) is being validated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The middle 2 digits are supplied, all numeric, and non-zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID to TRUE for SSN Part 2, and the validation flags are stored in WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART2-FLGS; processing continues to validate the last 4 digits of the SSN

all_rules.Rule_Name: SSN Middle 2 Digits - Valid
all_rules.Rule_Description: Confirms that the middle 2 digits of the SSN have passed all validation checks and are marked as valid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer information on the Account Update screen, and the SSN last 4 digits field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-3) is being validated after completion of Part 1 and Part 2 validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The last 4 digits of the SSN are blank, contain only spaces, or have zero trimmed length (i.e., nothing was entered)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as invalid by setting INPUT-ERROR to TRUE and FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK to TRUE for SSN Part 3; the validation flags are stored in WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3-FLGS; if no prior error message has been set, the error message 'SSN Last 4 chars must be supplied.' is recorded; SSN validation ends and validation flags for all three parts are returned

all_rules.Rule_Name: SSN Last 4 Digits - Presence Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the last 4 digits of the Social Security Number have been entered by the user and are not blank or missing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer information on the Account Update screen, and the SSN last 4 digits field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-3) has been supplied (is not blank)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The last 4 digits of the SSN contain any non-numeric characters
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as invalid by setting INPUT-ERROR to TRUE and FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK to TRUE for SSN Part 3; the validation flags are stored in WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3-FLGS; if no prior error message has been set, the error message 'SSN Last 4 chars must be all numeric.' is recorded; SSN validation ends and validation flags for all three parts are returned

all_rules.Rule_Name: SSN Last 4 Digits - Numeric Format Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the last 4 digits of the Social Security Number contain only numeric characters.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer information on the Account Update screen, and the SSN last 4 digits field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-3) has been supplied and confirmed as numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The numeric value of the last 4 digits of the SSN equals zero (i.e., '0000')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as invalid by setting INPUT-ERROR to TRUE and FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK to TRUE for SSN Part 3; the validation flags are stored in WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3-FLGS; if no prior error message has been set, the error message 'SSN Last 4 chars must not be zero.' is recorded; SSN validation ends and validation flags for all three parts are returned

all_rules.Rule_Name: SSN Last 4 Digits - Non-Zero Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the last 4 digits of the Social Security Number are not all zeros.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer information on the Account Update screen, and the SSN last 4 digits field (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-3) is being validated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The last 4 digits are supplied, all numeric, and non-zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID to TRUE for SSN Part 3, and the validation flags are stored in WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3-FLGS; SSN validation ends and validation flags for all three parts are returned to the calling validation process

all_rules.Rule_Name: SSN Last 4 Digits - Valid
all_rules.Rule_Description: Confirms that the last 4 digits of the SSN have passed all validation checks and are marked as valid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer information on the Account Update screen and has entered values in the SSN fields (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-1, ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-2, ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-3)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The SSN validation routine (1265-EDIT-US-SSN) is invoked from the field-level edit process (1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS) with the field label set to 'SSN'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system validates all three SSN parts sequentially and independently — Part 1 (first 3 digits, field label 'SSN: First 3 chars'), Part 2 (middle 2 digits, field label 'SSN 4th & 5th chars'), and Part 3 (last 4 digits, field label 'SSN Last 4 chars') — even if earlier parts have errors; upon completion, the individual validation flags (WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1-FLGS, WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART2-FLGS, WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3-FLGS) are all set and returned to the calling process for use in screen error highlighting and update eligibility determination

all_rules.Rule_Name: SSN Validation - Sequential Three-Part Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines the overall SSN validation process as a sequential three-part validation where all three parts are always evaluated independently, regardless of errors found in earlier parts, and all validation flags are returned to the caller.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account details on the Account Update screen and the FICO Score field is part of the editable customer information
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the form with the FICO Score field left blank, containing only spaces, or containing no meaningful characters
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the FICO Score field as invalid, sets an input error condition, records the error message 'FICO Score must be supplied.' (only if no prior error message has been recorded in the session), and flags the FICO Score field to be highlighted in red on the screen; processing of the FICO Score validation stops immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: FICO Score Must Be Supplied
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the FICO credit score field is not left blank or empty when a user submits account update details. The FICO Score is a mandatory field and must contain a value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account details on the Account Update screen and has supplied a non-blank value in the FICO Score field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The supplied FICO Score value contains any non-numeric characters (letters, symbols, or mixed content) within its 3-character length
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the FICO Score field as invalid, sets an input error condition, records the error message 'FICO Score must be all numeric.' (only if no prior error message has been recorded in the session), and flags the FICO Score field to be highlighted in red on the screen; processing of the FICO Score validation stops immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: FICO Score Must Be All Numeric
