all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the FICO credit score contains only numeric digits. Non-numeric characters such as letters or special symbols are not permitted in the FICO Score field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account details on the Account Update screen and has supplied a numeric value in the FICO Score field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The numeric value of the FICO Score evaluates to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the FICO Score field as invalid, sets an input error condition, records the error message 'FICO Score must not be zero.' (only if no prior error message has been recorded in the session), and flags the FICO Score field to be highlighted in red on the screen; processing of the FICO Score validation stops immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: FICO Score Must Be Non-Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the FICO credit score is not zero. A FICO Score of zero is not a valid credit score and must be rejected.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account details on the Account Update screen and has supplied a FICO Score value that has already passed the mandatory, numeric, and non-zero checks
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The numeric FICO Score value is outside the valid range — that is, it is less than 300 or greater than 850
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the FICO Score field as invalid, sets an input error condition, records the error message 'FICO Score: should be between 300 and 850' (only if no prior error message has been recorded in the session), and flags the FICO Score field to be highlighted in red on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: FICO Score Must Fall Within Valid Range of 300 to 850
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the FICO credit score falls within the industry-standard valid range of 300 to 850 inclusive. This range check is only performed after the score has passed the numeric and non-zero checks.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account details on the Account Update screen and has supplied a value in the FICO Score field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The FICO Score value is non-blank, is entirely numeric, is non-zero, and falls within the range of 300 to 850 inclusive
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the FICO Score field as valid (FLG-FICO-SCORE-ISVALID), no error condition is set for this field, no error message is generated for this field, and the validation process continues to the next field on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: FICO Score Is Valid — Proceed to Next Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Confirms that the FICO credit score has passed all validation checks — it is supplied, numeric, non-zero, and within the range of 300 to 850 — and the validation process proceeds to the next field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account details on the Account Update screen and the FICO Score field has been submitted for validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The FICO Score has passed the mandatory, numeric, and non-zero checks and is flagged as valid (FLG-FICO-SCORE-ISVALID is set to TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system invokes the FICO Score range validation routine to check whether the score falls between 300 and 850; if the FICO Score did not pass the prior checks, the range validation routine is not invoked and the field remains flagged as invalid

all_rules.Rule_Name: FICO Score Range Validation Is Conditionally Invoked
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines the conditional action rule that the FICO Score range check (300–850) is only invoked when the FICO Score has already been confirmed as valid through the prior numeric and non-zero checks. The range validation is skipped entirely if earlier checks have already failed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has fetched account details, and changes have been detected requiring validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the form with the First Name field left blank, containing only spaces, or containing no meaningful characters (empty after trimming)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The First Name field is marked as invalid, an input error state is set, and the error message 'First Name must be supplied.' is displayed to the user (only if no prior error message has already been set)

all_rules.Rule_Name: First Name Mandatory Presence Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the customer First Name field is not left blank or empty when submitting account update details. First Name is a required field and must be supplied by the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, has fetched account details, changes have been detected, and the First Name field has been supplied with a non-blank value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the form and the First Name value (up to 25 characters) contains any characters that are not alphabetic letters or spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The First Name field is marked as invalid, an input error state is set, and the error message 'First Name can have alphabets only.' is displayed to the user (only if no prior error message has already been set)

all_rules.Rule_Name: First Name Alphabetic Character Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the customer First Name field contains only alphabetic characters (A-Z, a-z) and spaces. No numeric digits or special characters are permitted in the First Name field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has fetched account details with changes detected requiring validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The First Name field is supplied with a non-blank value of up to 25 characters that contains only alphabetic letters and spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The First Name field is marked as valid and no error is raised for this field; processing continues to the Middle Name validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: First Name Valid Acceptance
all_rules.Rule_Description: Confirms that the customer First Name field passes all validation checks — it is non-blank and contains only alphabetic characters and spaces — and is accepted as a valid input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has fetched account details with changes detected requiring validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the form with the Middle Name field left blank, containing only spaces, or containing no meaningful characters (empty after trimming)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Middle Name field is marked as valid without any error, and processing continues directly to Last Name validation without checking the content of the Middle Name field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Middle Name Optional Field Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the Middle Name field has been provided. Middle Name is an optional field; if it is left blank or empty, it is automatically accepted as valid and no further validation is performed on it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, has fetched account details, changes have been detected, and the Middle Name field has been supplied with a non-blank value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the form and the Middle Name value (up to 25 characters) contains any characters that are not alphabetic letters or spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Middle Name field is marked as invalid, an input error state is set, and the error message 'Middle Name can have alphabets only.' is displayed to the user (only if no prior error message has already been set)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Middle Name Alphabetic Character Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the customer Middle Name field, when provided, contains only alphabetic characters (A-Z, a-z) and spaces. No numeric digits or special characters are permitted if a Middle Name value is entered.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, has fetched account details, changes have been detected, and the Middle Name field has been supplied with a non-blank value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Middle Name value (up to 25 characters) contains only alphabetic letters and spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Middle Name field is marked as valid and no error is raised for this field; processing continues to the Last Name validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Middle Name Valid Acceptance
all_rules.Rule_Description: Confirms that the customer Middle Name field, when provided, passes the alphabetic character validation and is accepted as a valid input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has fetched account details with changes detected requiring validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the form with the Last Name field left blank, containing only spaces, or containing no meaningful characters (empty after trimming)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Last Name field is marked as invalid, an input error state is set, and the error message 'Last Name must be supplied.' is displayed to the user (only if no prior error message has already been set)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Last Name Mandatory Presence Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the customer Last Name field is not left blank or empty when submitting account update details. Last Name is a required field and must be supplied by the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, has fetched account details, changes have been detected, and the Last Name field has been supplied with a non-blank value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the form and the Last Name value (up to 25 characters) contains any characters that are not alphabetic letters or spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Last Name field is marked as invalid, an input error state is set, and the error message 'Last Name can have alphabets only.' is displayed to the user (only if no prior error message has already been set)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Last Name Alphabetic Character Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the customer Last Name field contains only alphabetic characters (A-Z, a-z) and spaces. No numeric digits or special characters are permitted in the Last Name field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has fetched account details with changes detected requiring validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Last Name field is supplied with a non-blank value of up to 25 characters that contains only alphabetic letters and spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Last Name field is marked as valid, no error is raised for this field, and name field validation is complete; processing continues to the next validation group

all_rules.Rule_Name: Last Name Valid Acceptance
all_rules.Rule_Description: Confirms that the customer Last Name field passes all validation checks — it is non-blank and contains only alphabetic characters and spaces — and is accepted as a valid input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has fetched an existing account and customer record, changes have been detected between the original and newly entered values, and the Address Line 1 field (maximum 50 characters) is being validated as part of the full field validation sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Address Line 1 field submitted by the user is entirely blank (spaces), contains only low-value characters, or has a trimmed length of zero (i.e., no meaningful content is present)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The overall input is marked as invalid (INPUT-ERROR), the Address Line 1 field is specifically flagged as blank (FLG-ADDRESS-LINE-1-BLANK), and if no prior error message has already been set, the error message 'Address Line 1 must be supplied.' is recorded; validation for this field ends immediately and Address Line 1 is not marked as valid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Address Line 1 Mandatory Field Presence Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the customer Address Line 1 field is mandatory and must contain a non-blank, non-empty value before the account update can proceed. This rule is triggered only after account details have been fetched and changes have been detected.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has fetched an existing account and customer record, changes have been detected between the original and newly entered values, and the Address Line 1 field (maximum 50 characters) is being validated as part of the full field validation sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Address Line 1 field submitted by the user contains at least one non-blank, non-low-value character (i.e., the trimmed length is greater than zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Address Line 1 field is marked as valid (FLG-ADDRESS-LINE-1-ISVALID / FLG-MANDATORY-ISVALID), no error is raised for this field, and the validation result flag (WS-EDIT-ADDRESS-LINE-1-FLGS) is updated to reflect the valid status so that subsequent processing and screen attribute setup can proceed correctly

all_rules.Rule_Name: Address Line 1 Successful Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Confirms that the customer Address Line 1 field passes the mandatory presence check and is marked as valid, allowing the overall account update validation to continue to subsequent fields.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Address Line 1 field has been determined to be blank or empty (validation has failed), and the system is about to set the error message for the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A prior error message has already been set during the current validation pass (i.e., the return message flag is no longer in the 'off' / unset state, meaning WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is FALSE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message 'Address Line 1 must be supplied.' is NOT written to the return message area, preserving the earlier error message; the field is still flagged as blank and input is still marked as invalid regardless of message suppression

all_rules.Rule_Name: Address Line 1 Error Message Suppression When Prior Error Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: Enforces the rule that only the first validation error message encountered during the full field validation sequence is displayed to the user. If a prior error message has already been set for another field, the Address Line 1 error message is suppressed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account and its associated customer record have been successfully fetched and displayed on the account update screen, and the user has submitted changes that differ from the originally fetched values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the full field validation sequence (1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS) and reaches the Address Line 1 validation step, passing the entered Address Line 1 value (up to 50 characters) and the field label 'Address Line 1' to the mandatory field validation routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The mandatory validation routine (1215-EDIT-MANDATORY) is executed for Address Line 1, the resulting validation status flags are stored in WS-EDIT-ADDRESS-LINE-1-FLGS, and the outcome (valid or blank/invalid) is available for subsequent screen attribute setup and error highlighting

all_rules.Rule_Name: Address Line 1 Validation Invocation as Part of Account Update Edit Sequence
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines the process rule that Address Line 1 validation is invoked as a specific step within the full account update field validation sequence, only when account details have already been fetched and user-entered changes have been detected.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has fetched account details and is on the Account Update screen with the State Code field available for editing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen with the State Code field left blank, containing only spaces, or containing no meaningful characters (zero-length after trimming)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The State Code field is marked as invalid; an input error is raised; the error message 'State must be supplied.' is set and displayed (only if no prior error message has been set); the State Code field is highlighted in Red on the screen; and if the field was blank, an asterisk '*' is placed in the State Code display field

all_rules.Rule_Name: State Code Mandatory Supply Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the State Code field is not left blank or empty when the user submits account update details. The State Code is a required field and must be provided.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has fetched account details and is on the Account Update screen, and the State Code field has been supplied with a non-blank value of up to 2 characters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen and the State Code value contains one or more non-alphabetic characters (digits, symbols, or special characters)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The State Code field is marked as invalid; an input error is raised; the error message 'State can have alphabets only.' is set and displayed (only if no prior error message has been set); and the State Code field is highlighted in Red on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: State Code Alphabetic Characters Only Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the State Code field contains only alphabetic characters. No numeric digits or special characters are permitted in a US State Code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has fetched account details and is on the Account Update screen, and the State Code field has been supplied with a non-blank, 2-character alphabetic value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen and the State Code value does not match any entry in the valid US State Code reference list
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The State Code field is marked as invalid; an input error is raised; the error message 'State: is not a valid state code' is set and displayed (only if no prior error message has been set); and the State Code field is highlighted in Red on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: State Code Valid US State Code Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the supplied 2-character alphabetic State Code corresponds to a recognized and valid US State Code from the approved list of US state codes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has fetched account details and is on the Account Update screen with a State Code value entered
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The State Code is non-blank, contains only alphabetic characters, and matches a valid US State Code from the approved reference list
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The State Code field is marked as valid; no error is raised for the State Code field; and the validation process proceeds to the State and Zip Code cross-validation (checking that the first 2 digits of the Zip Code are valid for the given State)

all_rules.Rule_Name: State Code Successfully Validated
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the State Code passes all individual validations (non-blank, alphabetic only, and valid US state code), it is marked as valid and the process proceeds to the State and Zip Code cross-validation check.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Account Update screen with a value (or blank) in the State Code field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins the State Code validation process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The State Code value from the screen input (ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD) is moved into the alphanumeric validation work area; the validation field length is set to 2 characters; and the State Code is initially marked as invalid pending successful completion of all validation checks

all_rules.Rule_Name: State Code Field Setup and Length Configuration
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any validation is performed, the State Code value entered by the user is transferred from the screen input area into the validation work area, and the expected field length is set to 2 characters for all subsequent validation checks.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has fetched account details, and the Zip Code field is left blank, contains only spaces, or contains low values (i.e., no value is entered)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen for processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as invalid, sets the Zip Code field flag to 'Blank', and displays the error message 'Zip must be supplied.' The Zip Code field is highlighted in red on the screen with an asterisk '*' shown as a placeholder, and no further Zip Code validation is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Zip Code Must Be Supplied
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Zip Code field is not left blank or empty when the user submits the account update screen. The Zip Code is a mandatory field and must contain a value before any further validation can proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, the Zip Code field has been supplied with a value (not blank), and the entered value contains one or more non-numeric characters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen for processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as invalid, sets the Zip Code field flag to 'Not OK', and displays the error message 'Zip must be all numeric.' The Zip Code field is highlighted in red on the screen, and no further Zip Code validation is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Zip Code Must Be All Numeric
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Zip Code field contains only numeric digits. A Zip Code that contains alphabetic or special characters is not acceptable and must be rejected.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, the Zip Code field has been supplied with a numeric value, and the numeric value evaluates to zero (e.g., '00000')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen for processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as invalid, sets the Zip Code field flag to 'Not OK', and displays the error message 'Zip must not be zero.' The Zip Code field is highlighted in red on the screen, and no further Zip Code validation is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Zip Code Must Not Be Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Zip Code field does not contain an all-zero value. Even if the Zip Code is numeric, a value of zero (e.g., '00000') is not a valid Zip Code and must be rejected.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, the Zip Code field has been supplied with a value that is all numeric and non-zero, and the State Code field has also independently passed its own validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes individual Zip Code validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the Zip Code validity flag to 'Valid', and subsequently triggers the State-Zip cross-validation check to verify that the combination of the State Code and the first two digits of the Zip Code represents a valid geographic pairing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Zip Code Marked Valid for Cross-Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Zip Code passes all individual validations (supplied, all numeric, non-zero), it is marked as valid. This valid flag is then used as a prerequisite condition to trigger the State and Zip Code cross-validation check, which verifies that the first two digits of the Zip Code are consistent with the entered State Code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the account update screen with a State Code and/or Zip Code value, AND at least one of those fields has already failed its individual field-level validation (i.e., State Code is not a valid 2-character alphabetic US state code, OR Zip Code is not a valid 5-digit non-zero numeric value)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether to perform the State and Zip Code cross-validation check
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips the State-Zip cross-validation entirely and does not generate any additional cross-validation error message, since field-level errors for State Code and/or Zip Code have already been flagged

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip State-Zip Cross-Validation When Individual Field Errors Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before performing the State and Zip Code cross-validation, the system checks whether both the State Code and Zip Code fields have individually passed their own field-level validations. If either field already has an error, the cross-validation is bypassed entirely, since field-level errors have already been reported to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the account update screen with a State Code and a Zip Code value, AND the State Code has passed individual validation (is a valid 2-character alphabetic US state code), AND the Zip Code has passed individual validation (is a valid 5-digit non-zero numeric value)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether to perform the State and Zip Code cross-validation check
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to execute the State and Zip Code cross-validation by combining the State Code with the first 2 digits of the Zip Code and checking the combination against USPS-based rules

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to State-Zip Cross-Validation When Both Fields Are Individually Valid
all_rules.Rule_Description: The State and Zip Code cross-validation is only triggered when both the State Code and the Zip Code have each independently passed their own field-level validations. This ensures the cross-validation operates only on clean, well-formed input values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the State Code (2-character alphabetic, e.g., 'NY') and the Zip Code (5-digit numeric, e.g., '10001') have individually passed their field-level validations
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the cross-validation lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system concatenates the full State Code (2 characters) with the first 2 digits of the Zip Code (e.g., '10') to form a single 4-character composite lookup value (e.g., 'NY10'), which is then used to check against the USPS-based State and Zip Code combination rules

all_rules.Rule_Name: Combine State Code and Zip Code Prefix for Cross-Validation Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: To perform the State and Zip Code cross-validation, the system constructs a composite lookup key by concatenating the 2-character State Code with the first 2 digits of the 5-digit Zip Code. This combined 4-character value is then used to look up whether the zip code prefix is geographically consistent with the given state according to USPS-based rules.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has constructed a composite lookup value by combining the State Code with the first 2 digits of the Zip Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks the composite value against the USPS-based valid State and Zip Code prefix combination table
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the combination is found in the valid combinations table, both the State Code and Zip Code are considered geographically consistent and the cross-validation passes with no error generated; If the combination is NOT found in the valid combinations table, the system marks both the State Code field and the Zip Code field as invalid, sets the error message to 'Invalid zip code for state', and flags the overall input as containing an error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate State and Zip Code Prefix Combination Against USPS-Based Rules
all_rules.Rule_Description: After constructing the composite State Code and Zip Code prefix lookup value, the system validates it against a predefined table of valid USPS-based State and Zip Code prefix combinations. This ensures that the zip code entered is geographically consistent with the state provided — for example, a zip code starting with '10' is valid for New York ('NY') but not for California ('CA').

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The State Code and Zip Code have each individually passed their own field-level validations, AND the system has determined that the combination of the State Code and the first 2 digits of the Zip Code does not match any valid USPS-based State and Zip Code prefix combination
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the cross-validation failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system simultaneously marks the State Code field as invalid (FLG-STATE-NOT-OK), marks the Zip Code field as invalid (FLG-ZIPCODE-NOT-OK), sets the overall input error flag to indicate the screen contains errors, and sets the error message to 'Invalid zip code for state' — both fields will be highlighted in red on the screen when re-displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Both State and Zip Fields Invalid on Cross-Validation Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the State Code and Zip Code prefix combination fails the USPS-based cross-validation, both fields are simultaneously marked as invalid. This dual-field invalidation signals to the user that the error is a geographic inconsistency between the two fields, not an error in either field individually. Both fields will be highlighted in red on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The State Code and Zip Code cross-validation has failed because the combination of the State Code and the first 2 digits of the Zip Code is not a valid USPS-based combination, AND no prior error message has been set during this screen interaction (the error message field is currently empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the error message for the cross-validation failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error message to exactly 'Invalid zip code for state', which will be displayed in the error message area of the account update screen; if a prior error message was already set from an earlier validation failure in the same screen interaction, the message is not overwritten and the existing message is preserved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Error Message for Invalid State and Zip Code Combination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the State and Zip Code cross-validation fails, a specific business error message is generated to inform the user that the zip code entered is not valid for the state they have specified. The message is only set if no prior error message has already been recorded for this screen interaction, ensuring the first error encountered is the one displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has fetched account details, and the City field (mapped from customer address line 3) is available for editing with a maximum length of 50 characters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the form with the City field left blank, containing only spaces, containing only low-values, or where the trimmed length of the City value equals zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The City field is marked as invalid with a blank indicator, an input error flag is set for the overall form, and the error message 'City must be supplied.' is recorded as the return message (only if no prior error message has already been set), and processing of the City field ends immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: City Field Must Be Supplied
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the City field is not left blank or empty when a user submits account/customer update details. City is a mandatory field and must contain a value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, the City field has been supplied with a non-blank value of up to 50 characters, and the mandatory presence check has already passed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system inspects each character in the City field by converting all valid alphabetic characters (A–Z, a–z) and spaces to spaces, and then checks if any non-space characters remain after the conversion — meaning non-alphabetic characters were present in the original input
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If non-alphabetic characters are found (i.e., the trimmed result of the converted field is not empty/zero length), the City field is marked as invalid with a not-ok indicator, an input error flag is set for the overall form, and the error message 'City can have alphabets only.' is recorded as the return message (only if no prior error message has already been set), and processing of the City field ends immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: City Field Must Contain Alphabetic Characters Only
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the City field, when supplied, contains only alphabetic characters and spaces. Numeric digits, special characters, or any non-alphabetic characters are not permitted in the City field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, the City field has been supplied with a non-blank value of up to 50 characters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The City field is non-blank AND all characters in the City field are alphabetic characters or spaces (no numeric or special characters present)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The City field is marked as valid with a valid indicator flag, no input error is set for the City field, and no error message is generated for City — allowing the overall form submission to proceed past the City validation step

all_rules.Rule_Name: City Field Marked as Valid When All Checks Pass
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the City field passes both the mandatory presence check and the alphabetic-only character check, the City field is confirmed as valid and no error is raised.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and has fetched account details, and changes have been detected requiring full field validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen with the Country Code field left blank, containing only spaces, or containing no meaningful characters after trimming
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Country Code field is marked as invalid with a blank flag, an input error is raised, the error message 'Country must be supplied.' is set (only if no prior error message has already been recorded), and the Country Code validation ends without proceeding to the alphabetic character check

all_rules.Rule_Name: Country Code Mandatory Supply Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Country Code field is not left blank or empty when a user submits account/customer update details. The Country Code is a required field and must contain a value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen, the Country Code field has been supplied with a non-blank value, and the mandatory supply check has passed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system inspects the Country Code value by converting all valid alphabetic characters to spaces and checks whether any non-alphabetic characters remain after the conversion
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If non-alphabetic characters are found (i.e., the trimmed result is not empty after removing all alphabetic characters), the Country Code is marked as invalid, an input error is raised, and the error message 'Country can have alphabets only.' is set (only if no prior error message has already been recorded); if all characters are alphabetic, the Country Code is marked as valid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Country Code Alphabetic Characters Only Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Country Code field, when supplied, contains only alphabetic characters (A–Z, a–z). No numeric digits or special characters are permitted in the Country Code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and is entering or modifying the Country Code for the customer's address
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Country Code value is received from the screen input and prepared for validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The validation is applied to exactly the first 3 characters of the Country Code field; the field label 'Country' is used in all associated error messages

all_rules.Rule_Name: Country Code Field Length Constraint
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines the expected length of the Country Code field. The Country Code must be exactly 3 characters in length when submitted for validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Country Code field has completed its validation process (either passed or failed)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The validation routine for alphabetic required fields returns its result flags
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The validation outcome flags (valid, blank, or not-ok) are transferred to the Country Code-specific flag area (WS-EDIT-COUNTRY-FLGS) so that subsequent screen attribute setup can correctly highlight the field in red or mark it with an asterisk if invalid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Country Code Validation Result Stored for Screen Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: After Country Code validation completes, the resulting validation status flags are stored so that the screen display logic can use them to determine field highlighting and cursor positioning.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Country Code validation has failed (field is either blank or contains non-alphabetic characters) and the program is in re-entry mode (the screen has been previously submitted)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen attributes are being set up for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Country Code field is highlighted in red on the screen; additionally, if the failure reason is that the field was blank, an asterisk '*' is placed in the Country Code output field as a visual prompt to the user that the field must be filled in

all_rules.Rule_Name: Country Code Error Screen Highlighting
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Country Code field fails validation (either blank or contains non-alphabetic characters), the field is visually highlighted in red on the screen to alert the user. If the field was left blank, an asterisk placeholder is displayed in the field to indicate it requires input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer information on the Account Update screen, and both Phone Number 1 and Phone Number 2 fields are available for input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All three parts of a phone number (Area Code, Prefix, and Line Number) are left blank or empty for Phone Number 1 or Phone Number 2
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The phone number is treated as not provided, marked as valid, and no validation errors are raised for that phone number; processing continues to the next validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Phone Number Is Optional When All Parts Are Blank
all_rules.Rule_Description: Both Phone Number 1 and Phone Number 2 are optional fields. If all three parts (Area Code, Prefix, and Line Number) of a phone number are blank or empty, the phone number is considered not provided and is automatically marked as valid without any further validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is entering a phone number on the Account Update screen, and at least one part of the phone number (Prefix or Line Number) has been entered, making it a partial entry
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Area Code field is left blank or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An input error is raised, the Area Code field is flagged as blank, and the error message '[Phone Number field name]: Area code must be supplied.' is displayed; validation continues to check the Prefix

all_rules.Rule_Name: Phone Number Area Code Must Be Supplied When Phone Number Is Partially Entered
all_rules.Rule_Description: If at least one part of a phone number has been entered (making it a partial entry), the Area Code portion is mandatory and must be provided. This rule applies to both Phone Number 1 and Phone Number 2.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has supplied an Area Code for a phone number on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Area Code contains non-numeric characters (letters, symbols, or special characters)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An input error is raised, the Area Code field is flagged as invalid, and the error message '[Phone Number field name]: Area code must be A 3 digit number.' is displayed; validation continues to check the Prefix

all_rules.Rule_Name: Phone Number Area Code Must Be a 3-Digit Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an Area Code is supplied for a phone number, it must consist entirely of numeric digits. Non-numeric characters are not permitted in the Area Code. This rule applies to both Phone Number 1 and Phone Number 2.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has supplied a numeric Area Code for a phone number on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The numeric value of the Area Code equals zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An input error is raised, the Area Code field is flagged as invalid, and the error message '[Phone Number field name]: Area code cannot be zero' is displayed; validation continues to check the Prefix

all_rules.Rule_Name: Phone Number Area Code Must Be Non-Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an Area Code is supplied and is numeric, it must not be zero. An Area Code of all zeros is not a valid phone area code. This rule applies to both Phone Number 1 and Phone Number 2.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has supplied a numeric, non-zero Area Code for a phone number on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Area Code does not match any valid North America general purpose area code in the reference list
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An input error is raised, the Area Code field is flagged as invalid, and the error message '[Phone Number field name]: Not valid North America general purpose area code' is displayed; validation continues to check the Prefix

all_rules.Rule_Name: Phone Number Area Code Must Be a Valid North America General Purpose Area Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an Area Code is supplied, numeric, and non-zero, it must be a recognized valid North America general purpose area code. Special-purpose, reserved, or non-existent area codes are not accepted. This rule applies to both Phone Number 1 and Phone Number 2.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is entering a phone number on the Account Update screen, and at least one part of the phone number has been entered
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Prefix field is left blank or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An input error is raised, the Prefix field is flagged as blank, and the error message '[Phone Number field name]: Prefix code must be supplied.' is displayed; validation continues to check the Line Number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Phone Number Prefix Must Be Supplied When Phone Number Is Partially Entered
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a phone number has been partially entered (at least one part provided), the Prefix (middle 3 digits) is mandatory and must be provided. This rule applies to both Phone Number 1 and Phone Number 2, and is checked regardless of whether the Area Code passed or failed validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has supplied a Prefix for a phone number on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Prefix contains non-numeric characters (letters, symbols, or special characters)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An input error is raised, the Prefix field is flagged as invalid, and the error message '[Phone Number field name]: Prefix code must be A 3 digit number.' is displayed; validation continues to check the Line Number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Phone Number Prefix Must Be a 3-Digit Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Prefix is supplied for a phone number, it must consist entirely of numeric digits. Non-numeric characters are not permitted in the Prefix. This rule applies to both Phone Number 1 and Phone Number 2.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has supplied a numeric Prefix for a phone number on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The numeric value of the Prefix equals zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An input error is raised, the Prefix field is flagged as invalid, and the error message '[Phone Number field name]: Prefix code cannot be zero' is displayed; validation continues to check the Line Number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Phone Number Prefix Must Be Non-Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Prefix is supplied and is numeric, it must not be zero. A Prefix of all zeros is not a valid phone prefix. This rule applies to both Phone Number 1 and Phone Number 2.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is entering a phone number on the Account Update screen, and at least one part of the phone number has been entered
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Line Number field is left blank or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An input error is raised, the Line Number field is flagged as blank, and the error message '[Phone Number field name]: Line number code must be supplied.' is displayed; phone number validation ends and processing moves to the next phone number or next validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Phone Number Line Number Must Be Supplied When Phone Number Is Partially Entered
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a phone number has been partially entered (at least one part provided), the Line Number (last 4 digits) is mandatory and must be provided. This rule applies to both Phone Number 1 and Phone Number 2, and is checked regardless of whether the Area Code or Prefix passed or failed validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has supplied a Line Number for a phone number on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Line Number contains non-numeric characters (letters, symbols, or special characters)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An input error is raised, the Line Number field is flagged as invalid, and the error message '[Phone Number field name]: Line number code must be A 4 digit number.' is displayed; phone number validation ends and processing moves to the next phone number or next validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Phone Number Line Number Must Be a 4-Digit Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Line Number is supplied for a phone number, it must consist entirely of numeric digits. Non-numeric characters are not permitted in the Line Number. This rule applies to both Phone Number 1 and Phone Number 2.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has supplied a numeric Line Number for a phone number on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The numeric value of the Line Number equals zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An input error is raised, the Line Number field is flagged as invalid, and the error message '[Phone Number field name]: Line number code cannot be zero' is displayed; phone number validation ends and processing moves to the next phone number or next validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Phone Number Line Number Must Be Non-Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Line Number is supplied and is numeric, it must not be zero. A Line Number of all zeros is not a valid phone line number. This rule applies to both Phone Number 1 and Phone Number 2.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered all three parts of a phone number on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Area Code is supplied, numeric, non-zero, and a valid North America general purpose area code; AND the Prefix is supplied, numeric, and non-zero; AND the Line Number is supplied, numeric, and non-zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The phone number is marked as fully valid with no errors raised, and processing continues to validate the next phone number or the next field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Phone Number Is Fully Valid When All Three Parts Pass All Checks
all_rules.Rule_Description: A phone number is considered fully valid only when all three parts — Area Code, Prefix, and Line Number — have each individually passed all their respective validation checks (supplied, numeric, non-zero, and for Area Code also a valid North America general purpose code). This applies to both Phone Number 1 and Phone Number 2.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is submitting account and customer updates on the Account Update screen, and both Phone Number 1 and Phone Number 2 fields are present
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The phone number validation process is triggered as part of the full field validation sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Phone Number 1 is validated first (Area Code, then Prefix, then Line Number), and upon completion — whether valid, optional, or containing errors — Phone Number 2 is validated next using the identical validation rules; validation results for each phone number are stored independently as Phone Number 1 flags and Phone Number 2 flags respectively

all_rules.Rule_Name: Phone Number Validation Is Invoked Sequentially for Both Phone Numbers
all_rules.Rule_Description: The phone number validation process is applied to both Phone Number 1 (primary) and Phone Number 2 (secondary) in sequence. Phone Number 1 is validated first, and regardless of its outcome (valid, optional, or errors), Phone Number 2 is always validated next using the same set of rules.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating customer account details and the EFT Account ID field is part of the update form with a required length of 10 characters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the form with the EFT Account ID field left blank, containing only spaces, or containing no meaningful value (empty after trimming)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the EFT Account ID field as invalid with a blank error flag, sets the overall input to an error state, and displays the error message 'EFT Account Id must be supplied.' — no further validation of the EFT Account ID is performed for this submission

all_rules.Rule_Name: EFT Account ID - Mandatory Field Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the EFT Account ID field has been supplied by the user and is not left blank or empty before any further validation is performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating customer account details and has supplied a value in the EFT Account ID field (10-character field, not blank)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The submitted EFT Account ID value contains one or more non-numeric characters (letters, symbols, or mixed content)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the EFT Account ID field as invalid with a not-ok error flag, sets the overall input to an error state, and displays the error message 'EFT Account Id must be all numeric.' — no further validation of the EFT Account ID is performed for this submission

all_rules.Rule_Name: EFT Account ID - Numeric Format Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the EFT Account ID, when supplied, consists entirely of numeric digits with a length of 10 characters, ensuring no alphabetic or special characters are present.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating customer account details and has supplied a value in the EFT Account ID field that has already passed the mandatory and numeric format checks
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The numeric value of the submitted EFT Account ID evaluates to zero (e.g., '0000000000')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the EFT Account ID field as invalid with a not-ok error flag, sets the overall input to an error state, and displays the error message 'EFT Account Id must not be zero.' — the EFT Account ID is not accepted

all_rules.Rule_Name: EFT Account ID - Non-Zero Value Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the EFT Account ID, after passing the numeric format check, contains a meaningful non-zero value, preventing the submission of an all-zeros EFT Account ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating customer account details and has supplied a value in the EFT Account ID field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The EFT Account ID is not blank, consists entirely of numeric digits across its 10-character length, and its numeric value is greater than zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the EFT Account ID field as valid, clears any error flags for this field, and allows the overall account update validation process to continue to the next field

all_rules.Rule_Name: EFT Account ID - Successful Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Confirms that the EFT Account ID has passed all validation checks — it is supplied, all numeric, and non-zero — and marks it as valid so the update process can proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer details on the Account Update screen, and the Primary Card Holder Indicator field is available for input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen without entering a value in the Primary Card Holder Indicator field, leaving it blank, empty (spaces), or as zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the Primary Card Holder Indicator field as blank/missing, sets an overall input error condition on the screen, and displays the error message 'Primary Card Holder must be supplied.' The validation stops immediately for this field and no further value checks are performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Primary Card Holder Indicator - Mandatory Field Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Primary Card Holder Indicator field has been supplied by the user before any value check is performed. This is a mandatory field and cannot be left blank, empty, or zero.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer details on the Account Update screen, and the Primary Card Holder Indicator field has been supplied with a non-blank value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user enters a value in the Primary Card Holder Indicator field that is neither 'Y' nor 'N'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the Primary Card Holder Indicator field as invalid, sets an overall input error condition on the screen, and displays the error message 'Primary Card Holder must be Y or N.' The validation fails for this field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Primary Card Holder Indicator - Allowed Value Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Primary Card Holder Indicator field contains only an accepted value of 'Y' (Yes) or 'N' (No). Any other non-blank value is considered invalid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is updating account and customer details on the Account Update screen, and the Primary Card Holder Indicator field has been supplied with a value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered value is either 'Y' or 'N'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the Primary Card Holder Indicator field as valid, no error condition is set for this field, and no error message is generated. Processing continues to the next validation step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Primary Card Holder Indicator - Successful Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Confirms that the Primary Card Holder Indicator field has passed all validation checks — it was supplied and contains a valid value of 'Y' or 'N'. The field is marked as valid and no error is raised.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Account Update screen with changes to account and customer details, and the system has determined that changes have been made and full field validation is required
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins validation of the Primary Card Holder Indicator field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the Primary Card Holder Indicator value entered by the user from the screen input, sets the field context name to 'Primary Card Holder' for use in any error messages, and invokes the Yes/No validation routine to check the value. The validated result is stored back as the Primary Card Holder field status

all_rules.Rule_Name: Primary Card Holder Indicator - Retrieve and Prepare for Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines the process of retrieving the Primary Card Holder Indicator value entered by the user from the screen input and preparing it for validation. The field label 'Primary Card Holder' is set as the context for any error messages generated during validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted input on the Account Update screen and input processing has completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the current screen state flag
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system routes to one of the following actions based on state: (1) Details-Not-Fetched or PF12 → attempt account data fetch; (2) Show-Details → check for input errors or changes; (3) Changes-Not-OK → re-display with errors; (4) Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed without PF5 → stay on confirmation prompt; (5) Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed with PF5 → attempt save; (6) Changes-Okayed-And-Done → transition to show updated details; (7) Any unexpected state → trigger abnormal termination with code '0001' and message 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Next Action Based on Current Screen State
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system evaluates the current screen state after input processing to route the transaction to the appropriate next action: fetch data, display details, show errors, await confirmation, save changes, or reset after completion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Details Not Fetched' and the user has entered an account number on the search screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system validates the account number field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account number is blank or low-values, the system sets an input error, flags the account filter as blank, prompts the user to enter an account number, clears the account ID to zeros, and stays on the search screen; If the account number is supplied but is not numeric or equals zero, the system sets an input error and displays the message 'Account Number if supplied must be a 11 digit Non-Zero Number', clears the account ID to zeros, and stays on the search screen; If the account number is a valid 11-digit non-zero numeric value, the system marks the account filter as valid and proceeds to fetch account data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Account Number Before Fetching Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before attempting to retrieve account data, the system validates that the entered account number meets all required criteria: it must be present, numeric, 11 digits, and non-zero.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account number has been validated as a valid 11-digit non-zero numeric value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the account data retrieval process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Step 1 - The system looks up the Card Cross-Reference file using the account number: if found, the Customer ID and Card Number are retrieved and stored; if not found, an input error is set with message 'Account: [account number] not found in Cross ref file' and the fetch process stops; Step 2 - The system looks up the Account Master file using the account number: if found, account details are loaded and the account-found flag is set; if not found, an input error is set with message 'Account: [account number] not found in Acct Master file' and the fetch process stops; Step 3 - The system looks up the Customer Master file using the Customer ID retrieved in Step 1: if found, customer details are loaded and the customer-found flag is set; if not found, an input error is set with message 'CustId: [customer ID] not found in customer master' and the fetch process stops

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fetch Account, Customer and Card Cross-Reference Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid account number is provided, the system performs a three-step sequential lookup: first the Card Cross-Reference file to get the Customer ID and Card Number, then the Account Master file for account details, and finally the Customer Master file for customer details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All three lookups (Card Cross-Reference, Account Master, Customer Master) have completed successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the retrieved data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system stores the following as original 'old' values: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date (year/month/day), Expiry Date (year/month/day), Reissue Date (year/month/day), Group ID, Customer ID, SSN, Date of Birth (year/month/day), FICO Credit Score, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City (Address Line 3), State Code, Country Code, Zip Code, Phone Number 1, Phone Number 2, Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, and Primary Card Holder Indicator; Additionally, the system stores Account ID, Customer ID, Customer full name, Account Status, and Card Number in the shared communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Fetched Account and Customer Data as Original Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all three data sources are successfully retrieved, the system stores all fetched values as the original 'old' baseline data. This baseline is used later for change detection and concurrent modification checking.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully retrieved data from the Card Cross-Reference file, Account Master file, and Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The customer data is confirmed as found in the Customer Master
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the screen state to 'Show Details' (ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS), which causes the screen to display all retrieved account and customer information in editable fields, and the user is prompted to make changes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Screen State to Show Account and Customer Details After Successful Fetch
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all three data lookups succeed and customer data is confirmed found, the system transitions the screen state to display the full account and customer details for the user to review and edit.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system attempted to fetch account and customer data using the entered account number
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Any one of the three lookups (Card Cross-Reference, Account Master, or Customer Master) fails to find the record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag, displays the relevant error message identifying which file and which ID was not found, does not load any account or customer details onto the screen, and remains on the search screen with the account number field available for re-entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stay on Search Screen When Account or Customer Data Is Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: If any step in the data fetch process fails (account not in cross-reference, account not in master, or customer not found), the system remains on the search screen and displays the appropriate error message without loading any details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Show Details' (account and customer data is currently displayed on screen)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the form and input validation has been performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If input errors are present, the system takes no further action (stays on the details screen and re-displays with error highlights); If no input errors are present, the system proceeds to check whether any field values were actually changed by the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Check for Input Validation Errors When Details Are Displayed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account details are currently displayed and the user submits changes, the system first checks whether any input validation errors were detected during the edit phase before deciding the next action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Show Details', no input validation errors were found, and the user has submitted the form
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the newly entered values against the originally fetched 'old' values for all fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system compares the following account fields (exact match): Account ID, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit; and the following account fields (case-insensitive): Active Status, Group ID; and the following customer fields (case-insensitive, trimmed): Customer ID, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City, State Code, Country Code, Government Issued ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator; and the following customer fields (exact match): Phone Number 1A/1B/1C, Phone Number 2A/2B/2C, SSN, Date of Birth, EFT Account ID, FICO Score; If ALL fields match (no changes), the system stays on the details screen with no action; If ANY field differs, the system flags that a change has occurred and proceeds to set the confirmation state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Whether User Made Any Changes to Displayed Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: After confirming no validation errors exist, the system compares every field entered by the user against the originally fetched values to determine if any actual changes were made. The comparison is case-insensitive for text fields.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Show Details', no input validation errors were found, and at least one field value has been changed by the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that changes are present and valid
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the screen state to 'Changes OK - Not Confirmed' (ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED), displays the updated values on screen, highlights the PF5 and PF12 function keys, and displays a confirmation prompt message instructing the user to press PF5 to save or PF12 to re-fetch

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set State to Prompt User for Confirmation of Validated Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: When changes are detected and all validations pass, the system transitions to a confirmation state where the user must explicitly press PF5 to save the changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Show Details' and the user has submitted the form
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Either input validation errors are present OR no changes are detected between the entered values and the originally fetched values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears the non-key flags, stays on the details screen, re-displays the original fetched values, and takes no further processing action; the screen state remains as 'Show Details'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stay on Details Screen When No Changes Are Detected or Errors Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user submits the details screen but either no changes were made or validation errors exist, the system remains on the details screen without advancing to the confirmation step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Changes Not OK' (ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK), indicating that the user submitted changes that failed one or more validation rules
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the current state to determine the display action
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system continues processing without resetting state, re-displays the screen showing the user's entered values (not the original values), highlights all fields with errors in red, displays an asterisk '*' in mandatory fields that were left blank, positions the cursor on the first field in error, and displays the first validation error message in the error message area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Re-display Screen with Validation Error Messages
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen state indicates that changes have been submitted but contain validation errors, the system re-displays the screen with the entered (invalid) values and highlights the fields that failed validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Changes OK - Not Confirmed' (ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen without pressing PF5 (e.g., presses ENTER)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system takes no save action, continues to display the validated changes on screen, keeps the PF5 and PF12 function keys highlighted, and re-displays the confirmation prompt message instructing the user to press PF5 to confirm the save

all_rules.Rule_Name: Remain on Confirmation Prompt When PF5 Has Not Been Pressed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When changes have been validated and the screen is in the confirmation-pending state but the user has not pressed PF5, the system simply re-displays the confirmation prompt without taking any save action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Changes OK - Not Confirmed' and the user has pressed PF5
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the write processing routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system attempts to lock the Account Master record for update using the account number; if the account lock succeeds, the system then attempts to lock the Customer Master record for update using the customer ID; if both locks succeed, the system performs a concurrent change check before writing; the outcome of the save attempt determines the next screen state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Attempt to Save Account and Customer Changes When PF5 Is Pressed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF5 to confirm validated changes, the system initiates the save process by locking both the Account and Customer records, verifying no concurrent modifications occurred, and writing the updated data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is attempting to save changes and has initiated the record locking process
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The attempt to lock the Account Master record for update fails OR the attempt to lock the Customer Master record for update fails
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag, sets the state to 'Changes Okayed - Lock Error' (ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR), aborts the save process, and displays a failure message on screen informing the user that the record could not be locked for update

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Lock Error State When Account or Customer Record Cannot Be Locked
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the system cannot obtain an exclusive lock on either the Account Master or Customer Master record during the save attempt, the update is aborted and the screen transitions to a lock error state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the Account Master and Customer Master records have been successfully locked for update and the concurrent change check has passed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write (rewrite) operation to the Account Master file fails OR the write (rewrite) operation to the Customer Master file fails
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Account Master write fails: the system sets the state to 'Locked But Update Failed' (ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED) and stops processing; If the Customer Master write fails: the system sets the state to 'Locked But Update Failed', issues a transaction rollback to undo the Account Master write that already succeeded, and stops processing; In both cases, a failure message is displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Update Failed State When Record Write Fails After Locking
all_rules.Rule_Description: If both records are successfully locked but the actual write operation fails for either the Account or Customer record, the system sets a failure state. If the Customer write fails, the Account write is also rolled back.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the Account Master and Customer Master records have been successfully locked for update
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current database values against the originally fetched 'old' values for all account and customer fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system compares the following account fields (exact match): Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date year/month/day, Expiry Date year/month/day, Reissue Date year/month/day; and account Group ID (case-insensitive); and the following customer fields (case-insensitive): First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City, State Code, Country Code, Government Issued ID; and the following customer fields (exact match): Zip Code, Phone Number 1, Phone Number 2, SSN, Date of Birth year/month/day, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator, FICO Credit Score; If ALL fields match the original values, the save proceeds; If ANY field differs from the original values, the system sets the state to 'Data Was Changed Before Update' (DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE), aborts the save, transitions the screen to 'Show Details' state, and re-fetches and displays the latest data so the user can review the changes made by the other user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Record Modification Before Saving
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before writing updates, the system compares the currently locked database values against the values that were originally fetched and displayed to the user. If any field has been changed by another user in the interim, the save is aborted and the screen is refreshed with the latest data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both records are locked, the concurrent change check has passed, and the system is ready to write
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system builds the update records and performs the write operations
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For the Account Master, the system writes: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD), Expiry Date (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD), Reissue Date (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD), and Group ID; For the Customer Master, the system writes: Customer ID, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City (Address Line 3), State Code, Country Code, Zip Code, Phone Number 1 (formatted as (AAA)PPP-LLLL), Phone Number 2 (formatted as (AAA)PPP-LLLL), SSN, Government Issued ID, Date of Birth (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD), EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator, and FICO Credit Score

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Updated Account and Customer Data to Master Files
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all locks are obtained and no concurrent modifications are detected, the system builds and writes the updated Account and Customer records to their respective master files.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the Account Master and Customer Master records have been successfully written with the updated values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the outcome of the save process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the screen state to 'Changes Okayed and Done' (ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE) and displays a success confirmation message to the user; on the next processing cycle, the state transitions to 'Show Details' to display the newly saved account and customer information

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Successful Update State and Transition to Show Updated Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When both the Account and Customer records are successfully written, the system sets the success state and transitions to display the updated account and customer details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen state is 'Changes Okayed and Done' (ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE), indicating a previous update completed successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the current state in the next interaction cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the screen state to 'Show Details' (ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS) so that the updated account and customer information is displayed on screen for the user to review

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transition to Show Updated Details After Successful Save
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful update has been completed and acknowledged, the system transitions the screen state to display the updated account and customer details for the user to review.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The previous update completed successfully and the screen state is transitioning to 'Show Details'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the program was called from another transaction by examining the calling transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the calling transaction ID is blank or low-values (no prior transaction), the system clears the Account ID to zeros, clears the Card Number to zeros, and clears the Account Status to low-values in the shared communication area; If the calling transaction ID is populated (program was called from another transaction), the system retains the existing Account ID, Card Number, and Account Status values in the shared communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Account and Card Context When No Prior Transaction Exists After Successful Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful update, if the program was not called from another transaction (i.e., it was accessed directly), the system clears the account ID, card number, and account status from the shared context to prevent stale data from persisting.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF12 and account details have NOT yet been fetched (screen is in initial search state)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: PF12 is treated as invalid and the key press is converted to ENTER key action; no cancel or re-read operation is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF12 Key Validity Check - Cancel Changes Only Allowed When Account Details Are Displayed
all_rules.Rule_Description: PF12 is only a valid action when account details have already been fetched and are currently displayed on screen. If no account details have been fetched yet, PF12 is ignored and treated as the ENTER key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account Update screen and account details have been fetched and are currently displayed (state is not ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF12
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: PF12 is recognized as a valid action and the system proceeds to re-read all account and customer data from the database using the current Account ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF12 Triggers Account Data Refresh When Details Are On Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When PF12 is pressed and account details are currently displayed on screen (regardless of whether changes have been made), the system initiates a full re-read of account and customer data from the database to restore original values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed PF12 on the Account Update screen and the Account ID is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the data refresh process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads the Card Cross-Reference file using the Account ID as the search key; if found, the associated Customer ID and Card Number are retrieved and stored for use in subsequent lookups

all_rules.Rule_Name: Re-Read Card Cross-Reference File to Retrieve Customer ID and Card Number
all_rules.Rule_Description: As the first step of the data refresh triggered by PF12, the system looks up the Card Cross-Reference file using the Account ID to retrieve the associated Customer ID and Card Number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed PF12 and the system is attempting to re-read the Card Cross-Reference file using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag, marks the account filter as invalid, and displays the error message: 'Account: [Account ID] not found in Cross ref file. Resp: [response code] Reas: [reason code]'; the data refresh is aborted and no further file reads are performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Not Found in Card Cross-Reference - Show Error and Abort Refresh
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Account ID cannot be found in the Card Cross-Reference file during the PF12 data refresh, the operation is aborted and an error message is displayed to the user identifying the account that was not found.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID was successfully found in the Card Cross-Reference file and the Customer ID has been retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to the second step of the data refresh
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads the Account Master file using the Account ID as the search key; if found, the full account record is retrieved including: Account Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date, and Group ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Re-Read Account Master File to Retrieve Full Account Details
