all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving the Customer ID from the Cross-Reference file, the system reads the Account Master file using the Account ID to retrieve the full account details including balances, credit limits, dates, and account status.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID was found in the Cross-Reference file and the system is attempting to read the Account Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID is not found in the Account Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag, marks the account filter as invalid, and displays the error message: 'Account: [Account ID] not found in Acct Master file. Resp: [response code] Reas: [reason code]'; the data refresh is aborted and the Customer Master file is not read

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Not Found in Account Master File - Show Error and Abort Refresh
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Account ID cannot be found in the Account Master file during the PF12 data refresh, the operation is aborted and an error message is displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID was found in both the Cross-Reference file and the Account Master file, and the Customer ID has been retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to the third step of the data refresh
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads the Customer Master file using the Customer ID as the search key; if found, the full customer record is retrieved including: Customer ID, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Lines 1-3, State Code, Country Code, Zip Code, Phone Numbers 1 and 2, SSN, Government Issued ID, Date of Birth, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator, and FICO Credit Score

all_rules.Rule_Name: Re-Read Customer Master File to Retrieve Full Customer Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving account details, the system reads the Customer Master file using the Customer ID (obtained from the Cross-Reference lookup) to retrieve the full customer profile including name, address, and contact information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID was found in both the Cross-Reference and Account Master files, and the system is attempting to read the Customer Master file using the Customer ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer ID is not found in the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag, marks the customer filter as invalid, and displays the error message: 'CustId: [Customer ID] not found in customer master. Resp: [response code] REAS: [reason code]'; the data refresh is aborted and no data is restored to the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Not Found in Customer Master File - Show Error and Abort Refresh
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Customer ID cannot be found in the Customer Master file during the PF12 data refresh, the operation is aborted and an error message is displayed to the user identifying the customer that was not found.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All three file reads (Cross-Reference, Account Master, Customer Master) have completed successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the freshly retrieved data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system stores the following as the new baseline 'old' values: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date (Year/Month/Day), Expiry Date (Year/Month/Day), Reissue Date (Year/Month/Day), Group ID, Customer ID, SSN, Date of Birth (Year/Month/Day), FICO Credit Score, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City (Address Line 3), State Code, Country Code, Zip Code, Phone Number 1, Phone Number 2, Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, and Primary Card Holder Indicator; additionally, the Account ID, Customer ID, Customer Name, Account Status, and Card Number are stored in the shared session area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Restore Original Account and Customer Values After Successful Re-Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all three file reads succeed, the freshly retrieved account and customer data is stored as the authoritative 'original' values, overwriting any changes the user had entered on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully re-read and stored fresh account and customer data from the database following a PF12 press
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system resets the screen state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen state is set to ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS (Show Details mode); all non-key flags are cleared; the change detection state is reset so that the freshly retrieved values become the new baseline for comparison; any previously entered but unconfirmed changes are discarded

all_rules.Rule_Name: Discard All Pending Changes and Reset to Show Details Mode
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the fresh data has been retrieved and stored, all pending user changes are discarded and the screen state is reset to 'Show Details' mode, ready for the user to make new changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully refreshed data from the database and reset the screen state to Show Details mode after a PF12 press
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is sent to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen displays the original database values for all account fields (Active Status, Current Balance formatted as currency, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date, Group ID) and all customer fields (Customer ID, SSN parts, FICO Score, Date of Birth, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Lines 1-2, City, State, Zip, Country, Phone Numbers 1 and 2, Government Issued ID, EFT Account ID, Primary Card Holder Indicator); all editable fields are unprotected for input; the information message area displays 'Prompt for changes' guidance; no error messages are shown

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Screen with Original Database Values and Prompt for New Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: After discarding pending changes and resetting to Show Details mode, the screen is redisplayed showing the original values from the database with all editable fields unprotected and a prompt for the user to make new changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the account update screen with one or more field values, and the system has completed all field-level validations (account status, dates, financial limits, SSN, FICO score, name, address, phone, EFT account ID, primary card holder indicator)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: At least one validation error has been flagged (INPUT-ERROR is set to TRUE) — for example, a mandatory field is blank, a numeric field contains non-numeric data, a date is invalid, or a value is out of the allowed range
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen state is set to Changes-Not-OK (ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK remains TRUE); the system does NOT advance to the Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed state; the first error message encountered during validation is displayed in the error message area; all fields with errors are highlighted in red; mandatory fields that were left blank display an asterisk '*' as a placeholder; the cursor is positioned on the first field in error; the user is prompted to correct the errors and resubmit

all_rules.Rule_Name: Remain in Changes-Not-OK State When Validation Errors Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all input field validations are executed, if any validation error was detected, the screen state remains in Changes-Not-OK, preventing the user from proceeding to the save confirmation step. Error messages and red field highlights are retained on screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account and customer details have been successfully fetched and displayed on screen (ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS is TRUE), and the user has pressed ENTER or submitted the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares all submitted field values against the originally fetched 'old' values using case-insensitive comparison for text fields (account status, group ID, customer ID, all name fields, all address fields, government ID, primary holder indicator, country code, state code) and exact comparison for numeric fields (balances, limits, phone number parts, SSN, date of birth, EFT account ID, FICO score), AND the comparison determines that NO field has changed (NO-CHANGES-DETECTED is TRUE), OR an input validation error exists (INPUT-ERROR is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen state remains in Show-Details (ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS); the system does NOT advance to Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed state; the original fetched values are redisplayed on screen; the user is prompted to make changes to the displayed account or customer data before the save confirmation flow can be triggered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Remain in Show-Details State When No Changes Are Detected
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the user submits the screen in Show-Details state, if the system detects that no field values have changed compared to the originally fetched account and customer data, the screen remains in Show-Details state and the user is prompted to make changes before proceeding.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account and customer details have been fetched and displayed (ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS is TRUE), the user has modified one or more fields and submitted the screen, and the system has completed all field-level validations
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No validation errors were found (INPUT-ERROR is FALSE) AND the change comparison determined that at least one field value differs from the originally fetched data (CHANGE-HAS-OCCURRED is TRUE — meaning at least one of: account status, current balance, credit limit, cash credit limit, open date, expiry date, reissue date, current cycle credit, current cycle debit, group ID, customer ID, any name field, any address field, any phone number part, SSN, government ID, date of birth, EFT account ID, primary holder indicator, or FICO score has changed)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen state is set to Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed (ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED is set to TRUE); the system is ready to display the save confirmation prompt to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Advance to Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed State When Validations Pass and Changes Are Detected
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all field-level validations pass without any errors AND at least one field value has changed compared to the originally fetched data, the screen state is advanced to Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed, indicating the changes are valid and ready for the user to confirm and save.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All field-level validations have passed, changes have been detected compared to the original data, and the screen state has been set to Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed (ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the informational message area of the screen during the screen setup phase (3250-SETUP-INFOMSG)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message state is set to PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION; the corresponding confirmation guidance message (WS-INFO-MSG) is moved to the screen's information message output field (INFOMSGO of CACTUPAO), instructing the user to press PF05 to confirm and save the changes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Save Confirmation Informational Message to User
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed, the informational message area on the screen is set to prompt the user to press PF05 to confirm and save the validated changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed and the informational message has been set to PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the screen display attributes during the informational message attribute setup phase (3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The display attribute of the PF05 function key label (FKEY05A of CACTUPAI) is set to bright/bold (DFHBMASB), making the PF05 key label visually prominent on the screen to indicate it is the active key for confirming and saving the changes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Visually Activate PF05 Confirm Save Function Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen is in the save confirmation prompt state, the PF05 function key label is visually highlighted (bright/bold attribute) on the screen to draw the user's attention to the confirm-save action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed and the informational message has been set to PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the screen display attributes during the informational message attribute setup phase (3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The display attribute of the PF12 function key label (FKEY12A of CACTUPAI) is set to bright/bold (DFHBMASB), making the PF12 key label visually prominent on the screen to indicate it is the active key for cancelling the pending changes and returning to the original data view

all_rules.Rule_Name: Visually Activate PF12 Cancel Changes Function Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen is in the save confirmation prompt state, the PF12 function key label is also visually highlighted (bright/bold attribute) on the screen, providing the user with a clearly visible option to cancel the pending changes and refresh the original data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the account update screen and presses the PF05 function key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the validity of the key press against the current screen state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: PF05 is accepted as a valid key action ONLY IF the current screen state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed (ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED is TRUE); if the screen is in any other state (e.g., Details-Not-Fetched, Show-Details, Changes-Not-OK), PF05 is treated as an invalid key and the system resets the key action to ENTER, causing the screen to reprocess the current input without triggering the save operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF05 Key Is Only Valid When Changes Are Confirmed-Not-Yet-Saved
all_rules.Rule_Description: The PF05 key is only accepted as a valid action when the screen is in the Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed state. Pressing PF05 in any other state is treated as an invalid key and reprocessed as ENTER.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the account update screen and presses the PF12 function key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the validity of the key press against the current screen state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: PF12 is accepted as a valid key action ONLY IF account details have already been fetched (ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is FALSE — meaning the screen is in Show-Details, Changes-Not-OK, Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed, or a post-update state); if the screen is still in the Details-Not-Fetched state (no account has been looked up yet), PF12 is treated as an invalid key and the system resets the key action to ENTER

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF12 Key Is Only Valid When Account Details Have Been Fetched
all_rules.Rule_Description: The PF12 key (Cancel Changes / Re-fetch) is only accepted as a valid action when account details have already been fetched and displayed. Pressing PF12 before any account data has been loaded is treated as an invalid key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the account update screen and presses any function key or action key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines the pressed key is not in the set of currently valid keys — valid keys are: ENTER (always valid), PF03 (always valid), PF05 (valid only when ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED is TRUE), PF12 (valid only when ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is FALSE); any other key including PF01, PF02, PF04, PF06 through PF11, PA1, PA2, CLEAR, and any key not matching the valid conditions above is considered invalid
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The invalid key flag (PFK-INVALID) is set to TRUE; the key action is overridden and set to ENTER (CCARD-AID-ENTER is set to TRUE); the screen processes the current input as if the user had pressed ENTER, without triggering any special navigation or action associated with the originally pressed key

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid or Unsupported Key Press Is Reprocessed as ENTER
all_rules.Rule_Description: Any key press that is not in the set of currently valid keys (ENTER, PF3, PF5 when applicable, PF12 when applicable) is treated as invalid and automatically reprocessed as if the user had pressed ENTER, ensuring the screen continues to function predictably.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed PF05 to confirm and save changes to an account record, and the system has validated all input changes successfully and the session context holds the current Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the update write processing sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID stored in the current session context is retrieved and set as the record identifier key to be used for locating and locking the account master record in the Account Master File (ACCTDAT)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Account ID from Session Context for Update Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before attempting to lock the account record for update, the system retrieves the Account ID from the current user session context to use as the key for locating the account master record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID has been retrieved from the current session context and the system is ready to begin the update write processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system requests an exclusive lock on the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) using the Account ID as the record key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system attempts to read and lock the account record exclusively from the Account Master File; if the lock is granted, the account record data is retrieved into the update work area and the system proceeds to lock the customer record; if the lock is denied or the record is unavailable, the system marks the update as failed and informs the user that the account record is unavailable for update at this time

all_rules.Rule_Name: Request Exclusive Lock on Account Master Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system attempts to acquire an exclusive lock on the account master record using the Account ID as the lookup key, retrieving the record into a work area for subsequent update. This prevents concurrent modifications by other users during the update process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has requested an exclusive lock on the account master record using the Account ID as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Master File (ACCTDAT) grants the exclusive lock and returns the account record successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account record is held exclusively in the update work area, no error condition is set, and the system proceeds immediately to attempt locking the customer master record for update

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Record Lock Success - Proceed to Customer Record Lock
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the exclusive lock on the account master record is successfully acquired, the system confirms the account record is secured for update and proceeds to the next step of locking the associated customer record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has requested an exclusive lock on the account master record using the Account ID as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Master File (ACCTDAT) denies the lock request or the record is unavailable for any reason
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an input error condition, sets the update status to 'Could Not Lock Account Record for Update', exits the update processing immediately without attempting to lock the customer record or write any data, and the screen is redisplayed to the user with a message indicating the account record is unavailable for update at this time

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Record Lock Failure - Mark Update as Failed and Inform User
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system cannot acquire an exclusive lock on the account master record — because the record is already locked by another process or is otherwise unavailable — the update is marked as failed and the user is informed that the account record cannot be updated at this time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account update has been initiated and the Account Master record has already been successfully locked for update, and the Customer ID associated with the account being updated is available in the session's account/customer cross-reference data (CDEMO-CUST-ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to lock the Customer Master record for update processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the Customer ID from the session's cross-reference data (CDEMO-CUST-ID) and sets it as the key to be used for locating and locking the Customer Master record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Customer ID Associated with Account for Lock Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before attempting to lock the Customer Master record for update, the system must identify the correct customer by retrieving the Customer ID that is associated with the account currently being updated. This Customer ID was previously established during the account lookup phase via the Card Cross-Reference file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer ID has been identified and set as the record key, and the Account Master record is already locked for update
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system requests an exclusive update lock on the Customer Master record (CUSTDAT) using the Customer ID as the record identifier
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system attempts to open the Customer Master record with exclusive update access; the lock request either succeeds granting exclusive access to the customer record, or fails if the record is currently unavailable or locked by another process

all_rules.Rule_Name: Attempt Exclusive Lock on Customer Master Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must acquire an exclusive lock on the Customer Master record before any update can be applied. This exclusive lock prevents other users or processes from modifying the same customer record simultaneously, ensuring data integrity during the update operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to acquire an exclusive lock on the Customer Master record in the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The lock attempt does not return a normal successful response — meaning the Customer Master record is unavailable or currently locked by another process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the transaction as having an input error, sets the update status flag to 'Could Not Lock Customer Record for Update' (COULD-NOT-LOCK-CUST-FOR-UPDATE), and immediately exits the update processing routine without writing any changes to either the Account Master or Customer Master files; the user is informed that the customer record could not be locked for update

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Customer Record Lock Failure — Abort Update Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the system is unable to acquire an exclusive lock on the Customer Master record, the entire update operation must be aborted. The update state is flagged to indicate that the customer record could not be locked, and the user is informed that the update cannot proceed. No changes are written to any file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to acquire an exclusive lock on the Customer Master record in the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT), and the Account Master record is already locked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The lock attempt returns a normal successful response, confirming exclusive access to the Customer Master record has been granted
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system continues update processing without setting any error flags, and proceeds to the concurrent change detection step (9700-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC) to verify that neither the account nor customer data has been modified by another user since it was originally retrieved for this update session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Record Lock Success — Proceed to Concurrent Change Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the exclusive lock on the Customer Master record is successfully acquired, the system confirms that both the Account Master and Customer Master records are now exclusively held for this update session. Processing can safely continue to the next step, which checks whether another user has modified the data since it was originally fetched for this update session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has locked the Account record for update and holds the original Active Status value that was fetched and displayed to the user at the start of the update session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Active Status value in the locked Account record against the originally fetched Active Status value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Active Status does NOT match the originally fetched Active Status, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag, aborts the update process, and refreshes the screen with the latest data to notify the user that the record was modified by another user; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the next field (Current Balance)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Account Record Modification - Active Status
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before applying a user's updates, verify that the Account Active Status in the database matches the value originally fetched. If another user has changed this field, the update must be aborted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Active Status check has passed and the system holds the original Current Balance value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current numeric Current Balance value in the locked Account record against the originally fetched Current Balance value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Current Balance does NOT exactly match the originally fetched Current Balance, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the Credit Limit field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Account Record Modification - Current Balance
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before applying a user's updates, verify that the Account Current Balance in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched. Any discrepancy indicates a concurrent modification.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Current Balance check has passed and the system holds the original Credit Limit value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current numeric Credit Limit value in the locked Account record against the originally fetched Credit Limit value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Credit Limit does NOT exactly match the originally fetched Credit Limit, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the Cash Credit Limit field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Account Record Modification - Credit Limit
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before applying a user's updates, verify that the Account Credit Limit in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched to detect concurrent modifications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Credit Limit check has passed and the system holds the original Cash Credit Limit value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current numeric Cash Credit Limit value in the locked Account record against the originally fetched Cash Credit Limit value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Cash Credit Limit does NOT exactly match the originally fetched Cash Credit Limit, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the Current Cycle Credit field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Account Record Modification - Cash Credit Limit
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before applying a user's updates, verify that the Account Cash Credit Limit in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched to detect concurrent modifications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Cash Credit Limit check has passed and the system holds the original Current Cycle Credit value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current numeric Current Cycle Credit value in the locked Account record against the originally fetched Current Cycle Credit value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Current Cycle Credit does NOT exactly match the originally fetched Current Cycle Credit, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the Current Cycle Debit field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Account Record Modification - Current Cycle Credit
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before applying a user's updates, verify that the Account Current Cycle Credit in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched to detect concurrent modifications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Current Cycle Credit check has passed and the system holds the original Current Cycle Debit value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current numeric Current Cycle Debit value in the locked Account record against the originally fetched Current Cycle Debit value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Current Cycle Debit does NOT exactly match the originally fetched Current Cycle Debit, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the Account Open Date

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Account Record Modification - Current Cycle Debit
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before applying a user's updates, verify that the Account Current Cycle Debit in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched to detect concurrent modifications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Current Cycle Debit check has passed and the system holds the original Account Open Date (stored as separate Year, Month, Day components) that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the Year (characters 1-4), Month (characters 6-7), and Day (characters 9-10) of the current Account Open Date in the locked record against the originally fetched Open Year, Open Month, and Open Day values respectively
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If any component of the Account Open Date (Year, Month, or Day) does NOT match the originally fetched value, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if all three components match, the system proceeds to check the Account Expiry Date

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Account Record Modification - Account Open Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before applying a user's updates, verify that the Account Open Date (Year, Month, and Day components) in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched to detect concurrent modifications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Open Date check has passed and the system holds the original Account Expiry Date (stored as separate Year, Month, Day components) that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the Year (characters 1-4), Month (characters 6-7), and Day (characters 9-10) of the current Account Expiry Date in the locked record against the originally fetched Expiry Year, Expiry Month, and Expiry Day values respectively
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If any component of the Account Expiry Date (Year, Month, or Day) does NOT match the originally fetched value, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if all three components match, the system proceeds to check the Account Reissue Date

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Account Record Modification - Account Expiry Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before applying a user's updates, verify that the Account Expiry Date (Year, Month, and Day components) in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched to detect concurrent modifications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Expiry Date check has passed and the system holds the original Account Reissue Date (stored as separate Year, Month, Day components) that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the Year (characters 1-4), Month (characters 6-7), and Day (characters 9-10) of the current Account Reissue Date in the locked record against the originally fetched Reissue Year, Reissue Month, and Reissue Day values respectively
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If any component of the Account Reissue Date (Year, Month, or Day) does NOT match the originally fetched value, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if all three components match, the system proceeds to check the Group ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Account Record Modification - Account Reissue Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before applying a user's updates, verify that the Account Reissue Date (Year, Month, and Day components) in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched to detect concurrent modifications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Reissue Date check has passed and the system holds the original Group ID value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Group ID value in the locked Account record against the originally fetched Group ID value using a case-insensitive comparison (both values converted to lowercase before comparing)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Group ID does NOT match the originally fetched Group ID (case-insensitive), the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, all Account fields are confirmed unchanged and the system proceeds to compare Customer record fields

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Account Record Modification - Group ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before applying a user's updates, verify that the Account Group ID in the database matches the value originally fetched. The comparison is case-insensitive to avoid false mismatches due to letter casing differences.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All Account record fields have been confirmed unchanged and the system holds the original Customer First Name value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Customer First Name in the locked Customer record against the originally fetched Customer First Name using a case-insensitive comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Customer First Name does NOT match the originally fetched value (case-insensitive), the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the Customer Middle Name

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - First Name
all_rules.Rule_Description: After confirming no concurrent changes to the Account record, verify that the Customer First Name in the database matches the value originally fetched. The comparison is case-insensitive.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer First Name check has passed and the system holds the original Customer Middle Name value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Customer Middle Name in the locked Customer record against the originally fetched Customer Middle Name using a case-insensitive comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Customer Middle Name does NOT match the originally fetched value (case-insensitive), the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the Customer Last Name

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - Middle Name
all_rules.Rule_Description: Verify that the Customer Middle Name in the database matches the value originally fetched. The comparison is case-insensitive.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Middle Name check has passed and the system holds the original Customer Last Name value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Customer Last Name in the locked Customer record against the originally fetched Customer Last Name using a case-insensitive comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Customer Last Name does NOT match the originally fetched value (case-insensitive), the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check Address Line 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - Last Name
all_rules.Rule_Description: Verify that the Customer Last Name in the database matches the value originally fetched. The comparison is case-insensitive.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Last Name check has passed and the system holds the original Customer Address Line 1 value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Customer Address Line 1 in the locked Customer record against the originally fetched Address Line 1 using a case-insensitive comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Address Line 1 does NOT match the originally fetched value (case-insensitive), the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check Address Line 2

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - Address Line 1
all_rules.Rule_Description: Verify that the Customer Address Line 1 in the database matches the value originally fetched. The comparison is case-insensitive.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Address Line 1 check has passed and the system holds the original Customer Address Line 2 value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Customer Address Line 2 in the locked Customer record against the originally fetched Address Line 2 using a case-insensitive comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Address Line 2 does NOT match the originally fetched value (case-insensitive), the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the City

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - Address Line 2
all_rules.Rule_Description: Verify that the Customer Address Line 2 in the database matches the value originally fetched. The comparison is case-insensitive.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Address Line 2 check has passed and the system holds the original Customer City value (stored as Address Line 3) that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Customer City (Address Line 3) in the locked Customer record against the originally fetched City value using a case-insensitive comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current City does NOT match the originally fetched value (case-insensitive), the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the State Code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - City
all_rules.Rule_Description: Verify that the Customer City (stored as Address Line 3) in the database matches the value originally fetched. The comparison is case-insensitive.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The City check has passed and the system holds the original Customer State Code value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Customer State Code in the locked Customer record against the originally fetched State Code using a case-insensitive comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current State Code does NOT match the originally fetched value (case-insensitive), the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the Country Code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - State Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: Verify that the Customer State Code in the database matches the value originally fetched. The comparison is case-insensitive.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The State Code check has passed and the system holds the original Customer Country Code value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Customer Country Code in the locked Customer record against the originally fetched Country Code using a case-insensitive comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Country Code does NOT match the originally fetched value (case-insensitive), the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the Zip Code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - Country Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: Verify that the Customer Country Code in the database matches the value originally fetched. The comparison is case-insensitive.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Country Code check has passed and the system holds the original Customer Zip Code value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Customer Zip Code in the locked Customer record against the originally fetched Zip Code using an exact comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Zip Code does NOT exactly match the originally fetched Zip Code, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check Primary Phone Number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - Zip Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: Verify that the Customer Zip Code in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched. The comparison is exact (not case-insensitive) for this numeric field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Zip Code check has passed and the system holds the original Customer Primary Phone Number value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Customer Primary Phone Number in the locked Customer record against the originally fetched Primary Phone Number using an exact comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Primary Phone Number does NOT exactly match the originally fetched value, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the Secondary Phone Number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - Primary Phone Number
all_rules.Rule_Description: Verify that the Customer Primary Phone Number in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched. The full phone number (including formatting) is compared as a single value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Primary Phone Number check has passed and the system holds the original Customer Secondary Phone Number value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Customer Secondary Phone Number in the locked Customer record against the originally fetched Secondary Phone Number using an exact comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Secondary Phone Number does NOT exactly match the originally fetched value, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the SSN

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - Secondary Phone Number
all_rules.Rule_Description: Verify that the Customer Secondary Phone Number in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Secondary Phone Number check has passed and the system holds the original Customer SSN value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Customer SSN in the locked Customer record against the originally fetched SSN using an exact comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current SSN does NOT exactly match the originally fetched SSN, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the Government Issued ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - Social Security Number
all_rules.Rule_Description: Verify that the Customer Social Security Number (SSN) in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SSN check has passed and the system holds the original Customer Government Issued ID value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Customer Government Issued ID in the locked Customer record against the originally fetched Government Issued ID using a case-insensitive comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Government Issued ID does NOT match the originally fetched value (case-insensitive), the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the Date of Birth

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - Government Issued ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: Verify that the Customer Government Issued ID in the database matches the value originally fetched. The comparison is case-insensitive.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Government Issued ID check has passed and the system holds the original Customer Date of Birth (stored in YYYY-MM-DD format) that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the Date of Birth from the locked Customer record against the originally fetched Date of Birth by checking: Year (characters 1-4 of database value against characters 1-4 of stored value), Month (characters 6-7 of database value against characters 5-6 of stored value), and Day (characters 9-10 of database value against characters 7-8 of stored value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If any component of the Date of Birth (Year, Month, or Day) does NOT match the originally fetched value, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if all three components match, the system proceeds to check the EFT Account ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - Date of Birth
all_rules.Rule_Description: Verify that the Customer Date of Birth (Year, Month, and Day components) in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched. The date is stored in YYYY-MM-DD format and each component is compared individually using specific character positions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Date of Birth check has passed and the system holds the original Customer EFT Account ID value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Customer EFT Account ID in the locked Customer record against the originally fetched EFT Account ID using an exact comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current EFT Account ID does NOT exactly match the originally fetched EFT Account ID, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the Primary Card Holder Indicator

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - EFT Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: Verify that the Customer EFT Account ID in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The EFT Account ID check has passed and the system holds the original Customer Primary Card Holder Indicator value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Customer Primary Card Holder Indicator in the locked Customer record against the originally fetched Primary Card Holder Indicator using a case-insensitive comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current Primary Card Holder Indicator does NOT match the originally fetched value (case-insensitive), the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, the system proceeds to check the FICO Score

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - Primary Card Holder Indicator
all_rules.Rule_Description: Verify that the Customer Primary Card Holder Indicator in the database matches the value originally fetched. The comparison is case-insensitive.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Primary Card Holder Indicator check has passed and the system holds the original Customer FICO Credit Score value that was fetched and displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current Customer FICO Credit Score in the locked Customer record against the originally fetched FICO Credit Score using an exact comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current FICO Score does NOT exactly match the originally fetched FICO Score, the system sets the 'Data Was Changed Before Update' flag and aborts the update; if the values match, all Customer fields are confirmed unchanged, no concurrent modifications have been detected across all Account and Customer fields, and the system marks it safe to proceed with writing the user's updates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Concurrent Customer Record Modification - FICO Score
all_rules.Rule_Description: Verify that the Customer FICO Credit Score in the database exactly matches the value originally fetched. This is the final field check; if it passes, the system confirms no concurrent changes have occurred and the update may safely proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has detected that one or more fields in either the Account or Customer record have been modified by another user since the current user fetched the data for editing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The 'Data Was Changed Before Update' condition is triggered during the concurrent change detection process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system immediately stops the update process without writing any changes, sets the screen state to 'Show Details' so the latest database values are displayed, and the user is returned to the account details screen showing the current (updated by another user) values so they can review the changes and decide whether to re-enter their modifications

all_rules.Rule_Name: Abort Update and Notify User of Concurrent Record Modification
all_rules.Rule_Description: When any field mismatch is detected during the concurrent change check, the update must be immediately aborted, the screen refreshed with the latest data from the database, and the user notified so they can review the changes made by another user before deciding how to proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A confirmed account update request has been received, all input validations have passed, both the Account Master record and Customer Master record have been successfully locked for update, and no concurrent modifications have been detected
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins preparing the account update record for saving to the database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must completely clear and initialize the Account Update Record to blank/zero values before any new field values are populated, ensuring no stale or residual data from prior operations is present in the record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Fresh Account Update Record Before Populating
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the account update record with new values, the record must be completely cleared and initialized to ensure no residual or stale data from previous operations is carried forward into the database write.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update Record has been initialized and the user has entered a valid 11-digit non-zero numeric Account Number that has been confirmed to exist in the Account Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account Update Record fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID field on the Account Update Record must be set to the user-entered and validated Account Number value (ACUP-NEW-ACCT-ID), which serves as the unique identifier for the account being updated in the Account Master file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Account ID on Update Record from User-Entered Account Number
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account ID field on the account update record must be populated with the validated account number entered by the user, establishing the primary key that identifies which account record in the Account Master file will be updated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update Record is being populated and the user has entered a valid Account Status value that has passed Y/N validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the Account Active Status on the Account Update Record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Active Status field (ACCT-UPDATE-ACTIVE-STATUS) must be set to the user-entered active status value (ACUP-NEW-ACTIVE-STATUS), where 'Y' designates the account as Active and 'N' designates the account as Inactive

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Account Active Status on Update Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Active Status field on the update record must reflect the user's intended active or inactive designation for the account. A value of 'Y' indicates the account is active and a value of 'N' indicates the account is inactive.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update Record is being populated and the user-entered Current Balance has passed signed numeric validation (confirmed to be a valid signed number with up to 2 decimal places)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the Current Balance on the Account Update Record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Balance field (ACCT-UPDATE-CURR-BAL) must be set to the internally computed numeric value (ACUP-NEW-CURR-BAL-N), which is the validated numeric form of the user-entered current balance, not the raw text input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Current Balance on Account Update Record Using Validated Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Current Balance field on the account update record must be populated using the internally validated numeric representation of the balance entered by the user, ensuring the stored value is a precise numeric figure rather than a raw text string.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update Record is being populated and the user-entered Credit Limit has passed signed numeric validation (confirmed to be a valid signed number with up to 2 decimal places)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the Credit Limit on the Account Update Record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Credit Limit field (ACCT-UPDATE-CREDIT-LIMIT) must be set to the internally computed numeric value (ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-N), which is the validated numeric form of the user-entered credit limit, not the raw text input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Credit Limit on Account Update Record Using Validated Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Credit Limit field on the account update record must be populated using the internally validated numeric representation of the credit limit entered by the user, ensuring the stored value is a precise numeric figure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update Record is being populated and the user-entered Cash Credit Limit has passed signed numeric validation (confirmed to be a valid signed number with up to 2 decimal places)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the Cash Credit Limit on the Account Update Record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Cash Credit Limit field (ACCT-UPDATE-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT) must be set to the internally computed numeric value (ACUP-NEW-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-N), which is the validated numeric form of the user-entered cash credit limit, not the raw text input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Cash Credit Limit on Account Update Record Using Validated Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Cash Credit Limit field on the account update record must be populated using the internally validated numeric representation of the cash credit limit entered by the user, ensuring the stored value is a precise numeric figure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update Record is being populated and the user-entered Current Cycle Credit amount has passed signed numeric validation (confirmed to be a valid signed number with up to 2 decimal places)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the Current Cycle Credit on the Account Update Record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Cycle Credit field (ACCT-UPDATE-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) must be set to the internally computed numeric value (ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-N), which is the validated numeric form of the user-entered current cycle credit amount, not the raw text input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Current Cycle Credit Amount on Account Update Record Using Validated Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Current Cycle Credit field on the account update record must be populated using the internally validated numeric representation of the cycle credit amount entered by the user, ensuring the stored value is a precise numeric figure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update Record is being populated and the user-entered Current Cycle Debit amount has passed signed numeric validation (confirmed to be a valid signed number with up to 2 decimal places)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the Current Cycle Debit on the Account Update Record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Cycle Debit field (ACCT-UPDATE-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) must be set to the internally computed numeric value (ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-N), which is the validated numeric form of the user-entered current cycle debit amount, not the raw text input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Current Cycle Debit Amount on Account Update Record Using Validated Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Current Cycle Debit field on the account update record must be populated using the internally validated numeric representation of the cycle debit amount entered by the user, ensuring the stored value is a precise numeric figure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update Record is being populated and the user has entered the Account Open Date as three separate components — a 4-digit Year (ACUP-NEW-OPEN-YEAR), a 2-digit Month (ACUP-NEW-OPEN-MON), and a 2-digit Day (ACUP-NEW-OPEN-DAY) — all of which have passed individual date component validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats and sets the Account Open Date on the Account Update Record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Open Date field (ACCT-UPDATE-OPEN-DATE) must be set by concatenating the Year, a hyphen '-', the Month, a hyphen '-', and the Day to produce a date string in the format YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., 2024-03-15)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Set Account Open Date as YYYY-MM-DD by Combining Separate Year, Month, and Day Parts
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Open Date must be stored in the database in the standard YYYY-MM-DD format. Since the user enters the year, month, and day as three separate fields on the screen, the system must combine these three parts with hyphen separators to form the correctly formatted date string before saving.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update Record is being populated and the user has entered the Account Expiry Date as three separate components — a 4-digit Year (ACUP-NEW-EXP-YEAR), a 2-digit Month (ACUP-NEW-EXP-MON), and a 2-digit Day (ACUP-NEW-EXP-DAY) — all of which have passed individual date component validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats and sets the Account Expiry Date on the Account Update Record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Expiry Date field (ACCT-UPDATE-EXPIRAION-DATE) must be set by concatenating the Year, a hyphen '-', the Month, a hyphen '-', and the Day to produce a date string in the format YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., 2026-12-31)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Set Account Expiry Date as YYYY-MM-DD by Combining Separate Year, Month, and Day Parts
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Expiry Date must be stored in the database in the standard YYYY-MM-DD format. Since the user enters the year, month, and day as three separate fields on the screen, the system must combine these three parts with hyphen separators to form the correctly formatted date string before saving.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update Record is being populated and the user has entered the Account Reissue Date as three separate components — a 4-digit Year (ACUP-NEW-REISSUE-YEAR), a 2-digit Month (ACUP-NEW-REISSUE-MON), and a 2-digit Day (ACUP-NEW-REISSUE-DAY) — all of which have passed individual date component validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats and sets the Account Reissue Date on the Account Update Record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Reissue Date field (ACCT-UPDATE-REISSUE-DATE) must be set by concatenating the Year, a hyphen '-', the Month, a hyphen '-', and the Day to produce a date string in the format YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., 2025-06-01)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Set Account Reissue Date as YYYY-MM-DD by Combining Separate Year, Month, and Day Parts
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Reissue Date must be stored in the database in the standard YYYY-MM-DD format. Since the user enters the year, month, and day as three separate fields on the screen, the system must combine these three parts with hyphen separators to form the correctly formatted date string before saving.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update Record is being populated and the user has entered a Group ID value (ACUP-NEW-GROUP-ID) on the account update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the Group ID on the Account Update Record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Group ID field (ACCT-UPDATE-GROUP-ID) must be set to the user-entered Group ID value (ACUP-NEW-GROUP-ID) exactly as entered, completing the population of all account-level fields on the Account Update Record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Group ID on Account Update Record from User-Entered Group Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Group ID field on the account update record must be populated with the group identifier entered by the user, which categorizes or associates the account with a specific business group or portfolio segment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A confirmed account and customer update has been requested by the user after passing all validations, and the system is preparing to write the new customer data to the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins building the customer update record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All fields in the customer update record (CUST-UPDATE-RECORD) are cleared and reset to their initial empty state before any new values are copied into it

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Customer Update Record Before Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the customer update record with new values, all fields in the record must be cleared to ensure no residual or stale data from a previous operation is carried forward into the update.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer update record has been initialized and the new customer ID (ACUP-NEW-CUST-ID) is available from the validated input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the customer update record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer ID field (CUST-UPDATE-ID) in the update record is set to the value of the new customer ID (ACUP-NEW-CUST-ID)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Customer ID in Update Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Customer ID that was originally fetched and associated with the account must be carried forward unchanged into the customer update record to ensure the correct customer record is updated in the Customer Master file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer update record has been initialized, and the validated new first name (ACUP-NEW-CUST-FIRST-NAME), middle name (ACUP-NEW-CUST-MIDDLE-NAME), and last name (ACUP-NEW-CUST-LAST-NAME) are available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the name fields in the customer update record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The first name field (CUST-UPDATE-FIRST-NAME) is set to ACUP-NEW-CUST-FIRST-NAME, the middle name field (CUST-UPDATE-MIDDLE-NAME) is set to ACUP-NEW-CUST-MIDDLE-NAME, and the last name field (CUST-UPDATE-LAST-NAME) is set to ACUP-NEW-CUST-LAST-NAME

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Customer Name Fields in Update Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's full name — comprising first name, middle name, and last name — as entered and validated by the user must be written to the customer update record. All three name components are individually copied to their respective fields.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer update record has been initialized, and the validated new address line 1 (ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-LINE-1), address line 2 (ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-LINE-2), and city/address line 3 (ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-LINE-3) are available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the address fields in the customer update record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The address line 1 field (CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-LINE-1) is set to ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-LINE-1, the address line 2 field (CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-LINE-2) is set to ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-LINE-2, and the city field (CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-LINE-3) is set to ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-LINE-3

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Customer Address Fields in Update Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's address details — comprising address line 1, address line 2, and city (stored as address line 3) — as entered and validated by the user must be written to the customer update record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer update record has been initialized, and the validated new state code (ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD) and zip code (ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-ZIP) are available; the country code field is protected on the screen and cannot be modified by the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the geographic location fields in the customer update record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The state code field (CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-STATE-CD) is set to ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD, the zip code field (CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-ZIP) is set to ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-ZIP, and the country code field (CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD) is set to ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD as carried from the validated input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set State and Zip Code in Update Record — Country Code is Read-Only and Not Updated
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's state code and zip code as entered and validated by the user are written to the customer update record. The country code field is protected on the screen and is not editable by the user; therefore, it is not included in the update record population.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer update record has been initialized, and the validated primary phone number parts are available: area code (ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1A), prefix (ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1B), and line number (ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1C)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats and populates the primary phone number field in the customer update record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The primary phone number field (CUST-UPDATE-PHONE-NUM-1) is built by concatenating: opening parenthesis '(', area code (ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1A), closing parenthesis ')', prefix (ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1B), hyphen '-', and line number (ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1C), resulting in the format (NNN)NNN-NNNN

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Set Primary Phone Number in Update Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The primary phone number is entered by the user in three separate parts — area code (3 digits), prefix (3 digits), and line number (4 digits). Before storing in the Customer Master file, these three parts must be combined and formatted into the standard North American phone number format: (NNN)NNN-NNNN.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer update record has been initialized, and the validated secondary phone number parts are available: area code (ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2A), prefix (ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2B), and line number (ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2C)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats and populates the secondary phone number field in the customer update record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The secondary phone number field (CUST-UPDATE-PHONE-NUM-2) is built by concatenating: opening parenthesis '(', area code (ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2A), closing parenthesis ')', prefix (ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2B), hyphen '-', and line number (ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2C), resulting in the format (NNN)NNN-NNNN

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Set Secondary Phone Number in Update Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The secondary phone number is entered by the user in three separate parts — area code (3 digits), prefix (3 digits), and line number (4 digits). Before storing in the Customer Master file, these three parts must be combined and formatted into the standard North American phone number format: (NNN)NNN-NNNN.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer update record has been initialized, and the validated combined Social Security Number (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN) is available from the validated input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the SSN field in the customer update record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The SSN field (CUST-UPDATE-SSN) in the update record is set to the combined SSN value (ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Social Security Number in Update Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's Social Security Number, which was validated in three separate parts (first 3 digits, 4th and 5th digits, last 4 digits), is stored as a combined value and must be copied to the customer update record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer update record has been initialized, and the new government issued ID (ACUP-NEW-CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID) is available from the validated input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the government issued ID field in the customer update record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The government issued ID field (CUST-UPDATE-GOVT-ISSUED-ID) in the update record is set to the value of ACUP-NEW-CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Government Issued ID in Update Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's government-issued identification number as entered by the user must be copied to the customer update record for storage in the Customer Master file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer update record has been initialized, and the validated date of birth parts are available: year (ACUP-NEW-CUST-DOB-YEAR), month (ACUP-NEW-CUST-DOB-MON), and day (ACUP-NEW-CUST-DOB-DAY)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats and populates the date of birth field in the customer update record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The date of birth field (CUST-UPDATE-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD) is built by concatenating: year (ACUP-NEW-CUST-DOB-YEAR), hyphen '-', month (ACUP-NEW-CUST-DOB-MON), hyphen '-', and day (ACUP-NEW-CUST-DOB-DAY), resulting in the format YYYY-MM-DD

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Set Date of Birth in Update Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's date of birth is entered by the user in three separate parts — year (4 digits), month (2 digits), and day (2 digits). Before storing in the Customer Master file, these three parts must be combined and formatted into the standard date format: YYYY-MM-DD.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer update record has been initialized, and the validated new EFT account ID (ACUP-NEW-CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID) is available from the validated input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the EFT account ID field in the customer update record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The EFT account ID field (CUST-UPDATE-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID) in the update record is set to the value of ACUP-NEW-CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set EFT Account ID in Update Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) account identifier, which links the customer to their bank account for electronic payments, must be copied to the customer update record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer update record has been initialized, and the validated new primary card holder indicator (ACUP-NEW-CUST-PRI-HOLDER-IND) with a value of 'Y' or 'N' is available from the validated input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the primary card holder indicator field in the customer update record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The primary card holder indicator field (CUST-UPDATE-PRI-CARD-IND) in the update record is set to the value of ACUP-NEW-CUST-PRI-HOLDER-IND, which is either 'Y' (is primary holder) or 'N' (is not primary holder)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Primary Card Holder Indicator in Update Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The primary card holder indicator flag, which designates whether the customer is the primary holder of the credit card (Y) or not (N), must be copied to the customer update record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer update record has been initialized, and the validated new FICO credit score (ACUP-NEW-CUST-FICO-SCORE) is available from the validated input with a value between 300 and 850
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the FICO credit score field in the customer update record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The FICO credit score field (CUST-UPDATE-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE) in the update record is set to the value of ACUP-NEW-CUST-FICO-SCORE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set FICO Credit Score in Update Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's FICO credit score, which is a 3-digit numeric value between 300 and 850 representing the customer's creditworthiness, must be copied to the customer update record for storage in the Customer Master file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has confirmed account changes that have passed all validations, both the Account and Customer records have been successfully locked for update, and no concurrent modifications have been detected
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assembles the account update record prior to writing it to the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account update record must be initialized (cleared) and then populated with the following new values: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit amount, Current Cycle Debit amount, Open Date formatted as YYYY-MM-DD, Expiry Date formatted as YYYY-MM-DD, Reissue Date formatted as YYYY-MM-DD, and Group ID — all sourced from the user-entered and validated new data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assemble Account Update Record with All New Field Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before saving to the Account Master File, a complete account update record must be assembled by populating all required fields with the user-entered and validated new values. Date fields (Open Date, Expiry Date, Reissue Date) must be formatted as YYYY-MM-DD before being stored.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered valid Year, Month, and Day values separately for the Open Date, Expiry Date, and Reissue Date fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assembles the account update record for saving
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Each date field must be concatenated into a single value in the format YYYY-MM-DD (Year + '-' + Month + '-' + Day) for Open Date, Expiry Date, and Reissue Date respectively before being stored in the account update record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Account Date Fields as YYYY-MM-DD Before Saving
all_rules.Rule_Description: The three account date fields — Open Date, Expiry Date, and Reissue Date — are entered by the user as separate Year, Month, and Day components. Before writing to the Account Master File, each date must be assembled into a single string in the standard YYYY-MM-DD format with hyphen separators.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account update record has been fully assembled with all new field values including formatted dates, and the account record is currently locked for update
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to save the updated account record to the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must write the complete assembled account update record to the Account Master File, replacing the previously locked record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Updated Account Record to Account Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the account update record has been fully assembled with all new values, the system must write (rewrite) the updated record to the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) to persist the changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write the updated account record to the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the result of the account record save operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account record was saved successfully, the system must proceed to save the customer record changes; if the account record save failed for any reason, the system must mark the overall update as failed (Update Failed status) and immediately stop all further update processing — no attempt is made to save customer record changes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Outcome After Account Record Save Attempt
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to write the updated account record to the Account Master File, the system must evaluate whether the save was successful. A successful save allows processing to continue to the customer record update. A failed save halts all further update processing immediately.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write the updated account record to the Account Master File and the save operation did not complete successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects that the account record save has failed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the update status to 'Update Failed' (LOCKED-BUT-UPDATE-FAILED), immediately exit the update processing routine without attempting to save any customer record changes, and return control so that the screen can display an appropriate failure message to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Update as Failed When Account Record Cannot Be Saved
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the account record cannot be successfully written to the Account Master File, the system must flag the entire update operation as failed. This prevents any partial updates and ensures the user is informed that their account changes were not saved.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The updated account record has been successfully written to the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the account record save was successful
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must continue processing and proceed to assemble and save the updated customer record to the Customer Master File, maintaining the integrity of the combined account and customer update operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Customer Record Save After Successful Account Save
all_rules.Rule_Description: A successful save of the account record to the Account Master File is a prerequisite for proceeding to save the associated customer record changes. The two updates are treated as a sequential dependent process — customer changes are only attempted if the account changes were saved successfully.
