Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed all screen content preparation including field values, informational messages, error highlights, and field protection attributes for the Account Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is ready to transmit the Account Update screen to the user's terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the screen map reference to the Account Update screen map name (LIT-THISMAP) and the corresponding mapset name (LIT-THISMAPSET), storing them as the next map and mapset to be displayed, so that the correct screen layout is used for rendering all account and customer data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify Account Update Screen Layout for Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transmitting any content to the user's terminal, the system must identify and register the correct Account Update screen layout (map and mapset) that will be used to render all account and customer data fields.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update screen map reference has been set, all field values (account status, credit limits, balances, dates, customer name, address, phone numbers, SSN, FICO score, EFT account ID, primary cardholder indicator) have been populated, informational and error messages have been set, field protection attributes have been applied, and cursor position has been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the screen transmission to the user's terminal using the identified map (CCARD-NEXT-MAP) and mapset (CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET) with the prepared output data area (CACTUPAO)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All prepared screen content including account data, customer data, error highlights, guidance messages, and field attributes must be delivered to and rendered on the user's terminal in a single transmission

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transmit Prepared Account Update Screen Content to Terminal
all_rules.Rule_Description: The fully prepared Account Update screen — containing all account details, customer information, field values, error messages, guidance messages, and field attributes — must be transmitted to the user's terminal as a single atomic operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user's terminal may currently be displaying a previous version of the Account Update screen or any other screen content from a prior interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system transmits the new Account Update screen to the terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must erase all previously displayed content on the terminal screen before rendering the new screen, ensuring that no residual data, old field values, or prior messages remain visible to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Previously Displayed Screen Content Before Showing New Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the newly prepared Account Update screen, any previously displayed content on the user's terminal must be completely erased to prevent stale or residual data from being visible alongside the new screen content.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen attribute setup has determined cursor placement by setting a cursor length value of -1 on the appropriate field — which is the first field found to be in error (e.g., Account Number field if account filter is invalid or blank, Account Status field if status is invalid, Open Date Year/Month/Day if date is invalid, Credit Limit if invalid, Expiry Date fields if invalid, Cash Credit Limit if invalid, Reissue Date fields if invalid, Current Balance if invalid, Current Cycle Credit/Debit if invalid, SSN parts if invalid, Date of Birth fields if invalid, FICO Score if invalid, First/Middle/Last Name if invalid, Address Line 1 if invalid, State if invalid, Zip Code if invalid, City if invalid, Country if invalid, Phone Number 1 or 2 parts if invalid, EFT Account ID if invalid, Primary Cardholder if invalid) OR the Account Status field if account data was just found OR the Account Number field as default
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system transmits the Account Update screen to the terminal with the CURSOR option enabled
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The terminal must place the cursor on the field that was designated with a cursor length value of -1 during screen attribute setup, directing the user's attention to the first field requiring input or correction; if no specific field was designated, the cursor defaults to the Account Number field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Position Cursor on Appropriate Field Based on Validation Results or Screen State
all_rules.Rule_Description: The cursor must be automatically positioned on the most relevant field when the Account Update screen is displayed. The cursor position is determined by validation results (first field in error) or the current screen state (e.g., Account Number field on initial entry), guiding the user directly to the field requiring attention.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update screen has been successfully transmitted to the user's terminal with all field values, messages, and attributes rendered, and the terminal keyboard may be in a locked state from the previous interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen transmission completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must release (free) the terminal keyboard so that the user can immediately begin entering data in editable fields or pressing valid function keys (ENTER to submit, PF3 to exit, PF5 to confirm changes, PF12 to fetch account details) without any additional action required to unlock the keyboard

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unlock Terminal Keyboard After Screen Transmission to Allow User Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Account Update screen has been transmitted and displayed, the terminal keyboard must be unlocked so the user can interact with the screen — entering an account number to search, modifying account or customer fields, or pressing function keys to confirm changes, exit, or re-fetch data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has been triggered to display the Account Update screen as part of processing a user interaction (initial entry, account search, data edit, confirmation request, or update result notification)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The complete screen send sequence executes in order: (1) screen initialization with current date and time, (2) screen field values populated based on current state (blank for initial entry, original fetched values for show-details state, or updated values for changes-made state), (3) informational guidance message set based on state (prompt for search key, prompt for changes, prompt for confirmation, update success, or failure notification), (4) field protection attributes applied (all fields protected initially, then selectively unprotected based on state, error fields highlighted in red, blank mandatory fields marked with asterisk), (5) function key attributes set (PF5 and PF12 highlighted when confirmation is pending), and (6) screen transmitted to terminal with erase, cursor positioning, and keyboard unlock
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is fully rendered on the user's terminal, the current program state and all field values are saved to the session communication area, and the transaction returns control awaiting the next user input with the same transaction identifier so the session can continue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Complete Screen Display Sequence Before Returning Control to User
all_rules.Rule_Description: The full screen send process must execute as an ordered sequence — screen layout identification, content population, message setup, attribute configuration, and terminal transmission — before control is returned to the user. The session state is preserved in the communication area so the next user interaction can resume from the correct point.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update screen is active AND the current processing state is one of: (a) no account details have been fetched yet, (b) account details are displayed but no changes have been made by the user, or (c) changes have already been successfully saved (update completed)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen function key attributes for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Neither the PF05 (Confirm Save) key label nor the PF12 (Cancel Changes) key label is highlighted or activated on the screen — both remain in their default unactivated visual state, indicating to the user that no change-confirmation or change-cancellation actions are currently applicable

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Function Key Highlighting in Search or View Mode
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user is in search mode (no account loaded), view-only mode (account details displayed with no changes), or after a completed update, neither the PF05 (Confirm Save) nor the PF12 (Cancel Changes) function key label is highlighted on the screen, indicating no change-related actions are available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update screen is active AND the current processing state indicates that changes have been made by the user (the screen is in a 'changes made' state, which includes: changes entered but failing validation, changes validated and awaiting confirmation, update lock error, or update failure) AND the update has NOT yet been successfully completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen function key attributes for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The PF12 (Cancel Changes) function key label is highlighted and activated on the screen (displayed in bright/bold style — DFHBMASB attribute), visually signaling to the user that pressing PF12 is a valid action to cancel the in-progress changes; the PF05 (Confirm Save) key label remains in its default unactivated state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight PF12 Cancel Changes Key When Changes Are In Progress
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user has made changes to account or customer data on the screen but those changes have not yet been confirmed or finalized (i.e., changes are in progress — either pending validation or validated but awaiting confirmation), the PF12 (Cancel Changes) function key label is highlighted to visually guide the user that they can cancel and revert to the original values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Update screen is active AND all user-entered changes have passed validation AND the system has set the processing state to 'Prompt for Confirmation' (PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION is TRUE), which occurs when the state is 'Changes OK — Not Confirmed' (ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED), meaning the user has made valid changes that are ready to be saved but have not yet pressed PF05 to commit them
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen function key attributes for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Both the PF05 (Confirm Save) function key label AND the PF12 (Cancel Changes) function key label are highlighted and activated on the screen (both displayed in bright/bold style — DFHBMASB attribute), visually presenting the user with two available actions: press PF05 to permanently save the validated changes, or press PF12 to cancel and revert to the original values

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight Both PF05 Confirm Save and PF12 Cancel Changes Keys When Awaiting User Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system has successfully validated all user-entered changes and is now prompting the user to confirm the save (i.e., the screen is in the 'Prompt for Confirmation' state — changes are validated and OK but not yet committed), both the PF05 (Confirm Save) and PF12 (Cancel Changes) function key labels are highlighted simultaneously, giving the user a clear visual choice between committing or discarding the changes.

description:
COACTUPC is an online CICS program that handles the Account Update business function, allowing users to search for an account by account number, view the associated account and customer details, make changes to both account and customer information, validate all inputs, and commit the updates to the underlying data files. The program manages the full update lifecycle including data retrieval, field-level validation, change detection, user confirmation, and concurrent update conflict checking before writing changes to the account and customer master files.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: VSAM/CICS Files - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Initialize working storage areas, communication areas, and set up transaction context when the program starts or is entered fresh from the main menu 2: PF Key Validation - Validate the function key pressed by the user (PF03 for exit, Enter for processing, PF05 for save confirmation, PF12 for cancel/refresh) and determine if the key is valid in the current context 3: Exit and Return to Calling Program - When user presses PF03, transfer control back to the calling program or main menu, passing the communication area with updated context 4: Fresh Entry Screen Display - On first entry into the program, display a blank account update screen prompting the user to enter an account number to search 5: Post-Update Screen Reset - After a successful update or failed update, reset the screen and communication area to allow the user to start a new account search 6: Receive Screen Input - Capture all user-entered data from the account update screen including account ID, account details (status, limits, balances, dates), and customer details (name, address, SSN, DOB, FICO score, phone numbers, EFT, primary holder indicator) 7: Account Number Validation - Validate that the account number entered by the user is non-blank, numeric, and non-zero (11-digit number) 8: Account Data Lookup - Read the card cross-reference file using the account ID to retrieve the associated customer ID and card number 9: Account Master Data Retrieval - Read the account master file using the account ID to retrieve full account details including balances, limits, dates, and status 10: Customer Master Data Retrieval - Read the customer master file using the customer ID to retrieve full customer details including personal information, address, and contact details 11: Store Fetched Data as Original Values - Save the retrieved account and customer data as the original (old) values in the communication area for later comparison and change detection 12: Change Detection - Compare all new (user-entered) field values against the original fetched values to determine if any changes have been made by the user 13: Account Status Validation - Validate that the account active status field contains only 'Y' or 'N' 14: Date Field Validation - Validate account open date, expiry date, reissue date, and customer date of birth as valid calendar dates in CCYYMMDD format 15: Date of Birth Age Validation - Perform additional validation on the date of birth to ensure it represents a valid birth date 16: Credit Limit Validation - Validate that the credit limit is supplied and is a valid signed numeric value 17: Cash Credit Limit Validation - Validate that the cash credit limit is supplied and is a valid signed numeric value 18: Current Balance Validation - Validate that the current balance is supplied and is a valid signed numeric value 19: Current Cycle Credit Validation - Validate that the current cycle credit amount is supplied and is a valid signed numeric value 20: Current Cycle Debit Validation - Validate that the current cycle debit amount is supplied and is a valid signed numeric value 21: SSN Validation - Validate the Social Security Number in three parts: first 3 digits must be numeric, non-zero, and not 000/666/900-999; middle 2 digits must be numeric and non-zero; last 4 digits must be numeric and non-zero 22: FICO Score Validation - Validate that the FICO credit score is numeric, non-zero, and falls within the valid range of 300 to 850 23: Name Field Validation - Validate that first name and last name are supplied and contain only alphabetic characters and spaces; middle name is optional but must be alphabetic if provided 24: Address Line 1 Validation - Validate that address line 1 is mandatory and supplied 25: State Code Validation - Validate that the state code is supplied, alphabetic, and is a valid US state code 26: Zip Code Validation - Validate that the zip code is supplied and is all numeric 27: State and Zip Code Cross-Validation - Validate that the zip code prefix is consistent with the provided state code using USPS-based rules 28: City Validation - Validate that the city field is supplied and contains only alphabetic characters 29: Country Code Validation - Validate that the country code is supplied and contains only alphabetic characters 30: Phone Number Validation - Validate both phone numbers (primary and secondary) for valid US format: area code must be a valid 3-digit North America general purpose area code, prefix must be a non-zero 3-digit number, and line number must be a non-zero 4-digit number; phone numbers are optional but if partially entered all parts must be valid 31: EFT Account ID Validation - Validate that the EFT account ID is supplied and is all numeric 32: Primary Card Holder Indicator Validation - Validate that the primary card holder indicator is supplied and contains only 'Y' or 'N' 33: Determine Next Action After Input Processing - Based on the current state (details not fetched, details shown, changes validated, changes confirmed, etc.) decide whether to fetch data, show validation errors, prompt for confirmation, or save changes 34: Cancel Changes and Refresh Data - When user presses PF12 while changes are in progress, re-read the account and customer data from the database and redisplay the original values 35: Prompt for Save Confirmation - When all input validations pass and changes are detected, set the screen state to prompt the user to press PF05 to confirm and save the changes 36: Lock Account Record for Update - Attempt to acquire an exclusive lock on the account master record for update processing 37: Lock Customer Record for Update - Attempt to acquire an exclusive lock on the customer master record for update processing 38: Concurrent Change Detection - Before applying updates, compare the currently locked database records against the original values fetched earlier to detect if another user has modified the records in the meantime 39: Prepare Account Update Record - Build the account update record with all new values including active status, balances, credit limits, dates (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD), and group ID 40: Prepare Customer Update Record - Build the customer update record with all new values including name, address, phone numbers (formatted as (NNN)NNN-NNNN), SSN, date of birth, EFT account ID, primary holder indicator, and FICO score 41: Save Account Changes to Database - Write the updated account record back to the account master file 42: Save Customer Changes to Database - Write the updated customer record back to the customer master file; if this fails, roll back the account update as well 43: Screen Initialization - Set up screen header information including titles, transaction ID, program name, current date, and current time 44: Display Initial Empty Screen - Show the account update screen with all data fields blank when no account has been searched yet 45: Display Original Account and Customer Data - Populate the screen with the original fetched account and customer data formatted for display (currency values formatted with commas and decimals) 46: Display Updated Values with Validation Results - Populate the screen with the user-entered values, showing formatted values for valid fields and raw input for invalid fields 47: Set Up Informational Messages - Display context-appropriate messages to guide the user: prompt for account search, prompt for changes, prompt for confirmation, confirm success, or inform of failure 48: Set Screen Field Protection - Protect all screen fields by default, then selectively unprotect editable fields based on the current processing state (search mode vs. edit mode) 49: Set Cursor Position - Position the screen cursor on the first field that has an error or on the appropriate starting field based on the current processing state 50: Set Field Color Attributes - Apply color highlighting to fields based on validation status (red for errors, default for normal fields) 51: Send Screen to User - Transmit the formatted screen with all data, attributes, and cursor positioning to the user's terminal 52: Function Key Availability Highlighting - Activate and highlight the PF05 (confirm save) and PF12 (cancel changes) function key labels on the screen based on the current processing state, so users are visually guided on which action keys are available to them at each step
